<dd> Set metadata information of the next output file from <i>infile</i>. Note that those are file indices (zero-based), not filenames. Optional <i>metadata_spec_in/out</i> parameters specify, which metadata to copy. A metadata specifier can have the following forms:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><i>g</i>
<dd> global metadata, i.e. metadata that applies to the whole file
<dt><i>s</i><b>[:</b><i>stream_spec</i><b>]</b>
<dd> per-stream metadata. <i>stream_spec</i> is a stream specifier as described in the <b>Stream specifiers</b> chapter. In an input metadata specifier, the first matching stream is copied from. In an output metadata specifier, all matching streams are copied to.
<dt><i>c</i><b>:</b><i>chapter_index</i>
<dd> per-chapter metadata. <i>chapter_index</i> is the zero-based chapter index.
<dt><i>p</i><b>:</b><i>program_index</i>
<dd> per-program metadata. <i>program_index</i> is the zero-based program index.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 If metadata specifier is omitted, it defaults to global. 

 By default, global metadata is copied from the first input file, per-stream and per-chapter metadata is copied along with streams/chapters. These default mappings are disabled by creating any mapping of the relevant type. A negative file index can be used to create a dummy mapping that just disables automatic copying. 

 For example to copy metadata from the first stream of the input file to global metadata of the output file: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.ogg -map_metadata 0:s:0 out.mp3
</pre> 

 To do the reverse, i.e. copy global metadata to all audio streams: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map_metadata:s:a 0:g out.mkv
</pre> 

 Note that simple <tt>0</tt> would work as well in this example, since global metadata is assumed by default.</dl>

<dt><b>-map_chapters</b> <i>input_file_index</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Copy chapters from input file with index <i>input_file_index</i> to the next output file. If no chapter mapping is specified, then chapters are copied from the first input file with at least one chapter. Use a negative file index to disable any chapter copying.
<dt><b>-benchmark (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Show benchmarking information at the end of an encode. Shows real, system and user time used and maximum memory consumption. Maximum memory consumption is not supported on all systems, it will usually display as 0 if not supported.
<dt><b>-benchmark_all (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Show benchmarking information during the encode. Shows real, system and user time used in various steps (audio/video encode/decode).
<dt><b>-timelimit</b> <i>duration</i> <b>(</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Exit after ffmpeg has been running for <i>duration</i> seconds in <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> user time.
<dt><b>-dump (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Dump each input packet to stderr.
<dt><b>-hex (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> When dumping packets, also dump the payload.
<dt><b>-re (</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Read input at native frame rate. Mainly used to simulate a grab device, or live input stream (e.g. when reading from a file). Should not be used with actual grab devices or live input streams (where it can cause packet loss). By default <b>ffmpeg</b> attempts to read the input(s) as fast as possible. This option will slow down the reading of the input(s) to the native frame rate of the input(s). It is useful for real-time output (e.g. live streaming).
<dt><b>-vsync</b> <i>parameter</i>
<dd> Video sync method. For compatibility reasons old values can be specified as numbers. Newly added values will have to be specified as strings always.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0, passthrough</b>
<dd> Each frame is passed with its timestamp from the demuxer to the muxer.
<dt><b>1, cfr</b>
<dd> Frames will be duplicated and dropped to achieve exactly the requested constant frame rate.
<dt><b>2, vfr</b>
<dd> Frames are passed through with their timestamp or dropped so as to prevent 2 frames from having the same timestamp.
<dt><b>drop</b>
<dd> As passthrough but destroys all timestamps, making the muxer generate fresh timestamps based on frame-rate.
<dt><b>-1, auto</b>
<dd> Chooses between 1 and 2 depending on muxer capabilities. This is the default method.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Note that the timestamps may be further modified by the muxer, after this. For example, in the case that the format option <b>avoid_negative_ts</b> is enabled. 

 With -map you can select from which stream the timestamps should be taken. You can leave either video or audio unchanged and sync the remaining stream(s) to the unchanged one.</dl>

<dt><b>-frame_drop_threshold</b> <i>parameter</i>
<dd> Frame drop threshold, which specifies how much behind video frames can be before they are dropped. In frame rate units, so 1.0 is one frame. The default is -1.1. One possible usecase is to avoid framedrops in case of noisy timestamps or to increase frame drop precision in case of exact timestamps.
<dt><b>-async</b> <i>samples_per_second</i>
<dd> Audio sync method. ``Stretches/squeezes'' the audio stream to match the timestamps, the parameter is the maximum samples per second by which the audio is changed. -async 1 is a special case where only the start of the audio stream is corrected without any later correction. 

 Note that the timestamps may be further modified by the muxer, after this. For example, in the case that the format option <b>avoid_negative_ts</b> is enabled. 

 This option has been deprecated. Use the <tt>&quot;aresample&quot;</tt> audio filter instead.
<dt><b>-adrift_threshold</b> <i>time</i>
<dd> Set the minimum difference between timestamps and audio data (in seconds) to trigger adding/dropping samples to make it match the timestamps. This option effectively is a threshold to select between hard (add/drop) and soft (squeeze/stretch) compensation. <tt>&quot;-async&quot;</tt> must be set to a positive value.
<dt><b>-apad</b> <i>parameters</i> <b>(</b><i>output,per-stream</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Pad the output audio stream(s). This is the same as applying <tt>&quot;-af apad&quot;</tt>. Argument is a string of filter parameters composed the same as with the <tt>&quot;apad&quot;</tt> filter. <tt>&quot;-shortest&quot;</tt> must be set for this output for the option to take effect.
<dt><b>-copyts</b>
<dd> Do not process input timestamps, but keep their values without trying to sanitize them. In particular, do not remove the initial start time offset value. 

 Note that, depending on the <b>vsync</b> option or on specific muxer processing (e.g. in case the format option <b>avoid_negative_ts</b> is enabled) the output timestamps may mismatch with the input timestamps even when this option is selected.
<dt><b>-start_at_zero</b>
<dd> When used with <b>copyts</b>, shift input timestamps so they start at zero. 

 This means that using e.g. <tt>&quot;-ss 50&quot;</tt> will make output timestamps start at 50 seconds, regardless of what timestamp the input file started at.
<dt><b>-copytb</b> <i>mode</i>
<dd> Specify how to set the encoder timebase when stream copying. <i>mode</i> is an integer numeric value, and can assume one of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd> Use the demuxer timebase. 

 The time base is copied to the output encoder from the corresponding input demuxer. This is sometimes required to avoid non monotonically increasing timestamps when copying video streams with variable frame rate.
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd> Use the decoder timebase. 

 The time base is copied to the output encoder from the corresponding input decoder.
<dt><b>-1</b>
<dd> Try to make the choice automatically, in order to generate a sane output.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is -1.</dl>

<dt><b>-enc_time_base[:</b><i>stream_specifier</i><b>]</b> <i>timebase</i> <b>(</b><i>output,per-stream</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the encoder timebase. <i>timebase</i> is a floating point number, and can assume one of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd> Assign a default value according to the media type. 

 For video - use 1/framerate, for audio - use 1/samplerate.
<dt><b>-1</b>
<dd> Use the input stream timebase when possible. 

 If an input stream is not available, the default timebase will be used.
<dt><b>&gt;0</b>
<dd> Use the provided number as the timebase. 

 This field can be provided as a ratio of two integers (e.g. 1:24, 1:48000) or as a floating point number (e.g. 0.04166, 2.0833e-5)</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is 0.</dl>

<dt><b>-bitexact (</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable bitexact mode for (de)muxer and (de/en)coder
<dt><b>-shortest (</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Finish encoding when the shortest input stream ends.
<dt><b>-dts_delta_threshold</b>
<dd> Timestamp discontinuity delta threshold.
<dt><b>-dts_error_threshold</b> <i>seconds</i>
<dd> Timestamp error delta threshold. This threshold use to discard crazy/damaged timestamps and the default is 30 hours which is arbitrarily picked and quite conservative.
<dt><b>-muxdelay</b> <i>seconds</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the maximum demux-decode delay.
<dt><b>-muxpreload</b> <i>seconds</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the initial demux-decode delay.
<dt><b>-streamid</b> <i>output-stream-index</i><b>:</b><i>new-value</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Assign a new stream-id value to an output stream. This option should be specified prior to the output filename to which it applies. For the situation where multiple output files exist, a streamid may be reassigned to a different value. 

 For example, to set the stream 0 <font SIZE="-1">PID</font> to 33 and the stream 1 <font SIZE="-1">PID</font> to 36 for an output mpegts file: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i inurl -streamid 0:33 -streamid 1:36 out.ts
</pre>
<dt><b>-bsf[:</b><i>stream_specifier</i><b>]</b> <i>bitstream_filters</i> <b>(</b><i>output,per-stream</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set bitstream filters for matching streams. <i>bitstream_filters</i> is a comma-separated list of bitstream filters. Use the <tt>&quot;-bsfs&quot;</tt> option to get the list of bitstream filters. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i h264.mp4 -c:v copy -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb -an out.h264
        
        ffmpeg -i file.mov -an -vn -bsf:s mov2textsub -c:s copy -f rawvideo sub.txt
</pre>
<dt><b>-tag[:</b><i>stream_specifier</i><b>]</b> <i>codec_tag</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output,per-stream</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Force a tag/fourcc for matching streams.
<dt><b>-timecode</b> <i>hh</i><b>:</b><i>mm</i><b>:</b><i>ss</i><font SIZE="-1"><b>SEP</b></font><i>ff</i>
<dd> Specify Timecode for writing. <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SEP</i></font><i></i> is ':' for non drop timecode and ';' (or '.') for drop. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.mpg -timecode 01:02:03.04 -r 30000/1001 -s ntsc output.mpg
</pre>
<dt><b>-filter_complex</b> <i>filtergraph</i> <b>(</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Define a complex filtergraph, i.e. one with arbitrary number of inputs and/or outputs. For simple graphs --- those with one input and one output of the same type --- see the <b>-filter</b> options. <i>filtergraph</i> is a description of the filtergraph, as described in the ``Filtergraph syntax'' section of the ffmpeg-filters manual. 

 Input link labels must refer to input streams using the <tt>&quot;[file_index:stream_specifier]&quot;</tt> syntax (i.e. the same as <b>-map</b> uses). If <i>stream_specifier</i> matches multiple streams, the first one will be used. An unlabeled input will be connected to the first unused input stream of the matching type. 

 Output link labels are referred to with <b>-map</b>. Unlabeled outputs are added to the first output file. 

 Note that with this option it is possible to use only lavfi sources without normal input files. 

 For example, to overlay an image over video 

 
ffmpeg - i video.mkv - i image.png - filter_complex '[0:v][1:v]overlay[out]' - map '[out]' out.mkv
 

 Here <tt>&quot;[0:v]&quot;</tt> refers to the first video stream in the first input file, which is linked to the first (main) input of the overlay filter. Similarly the first video stream in the second input is linked to the second (overlay) input of overlay. 

 Assuming there is only one video stream in each input file, we can omit input labels, so the above is equivalent to 

 
ffmpeg - i video.mkv - i image.png - filter_complex 'overlay[out]' - map '[out]' out.mkv
 

 Furthermore we can omit the output label and the single output from the filter graph will be added to the output file automatically, so we can simply write 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i video.mkv -i image.png -filter_complex 'overlay' out.mkv
</pre> 

 As a special exception, you can use a bitmap subtitle stream as input: it will be converted into a video with the same size as the largest video in the file, or 720x576 if no video is present. Note that this is an experimental and temporary solution. It will be removed once libavfilter has proper support for subtitles. 

 For example, to hardcode subtitles on top of a DVB-T recording stored in MPEG-TS format, delaying the subtitles by 1 second: 

 
ffmpeg - i input.ts - filter_complex '[#0x2ef] setpts=PTS+1/TB [sub] ; [#0x2d0] [sub] overlay' - sn - map '#0x2dc' output.mkv
 

 (0x2d0, 0x2dc and 0x2ef are the MPEG-TS PIDs of respectively the video, audio and subtitles streams; 0:0, 0:3 and 0:7 would have worked too) 

 To generate 5 seconds of pure red video using lavfi <tt>&quot;color&quot;</tt> source: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -filter_complex 'color=c=red' -t 5 out.mkv
</pre>
<dt><b>-filter_complex_threads</b> <i>nb_threads</i> <b>(</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Defines how many threads are used to process a filter_complex graph. Similar to filter_threads but used for <tt>&quot;-filter_complex&quot;</tt> graphs only. The default is the number of available CPUs.
<dt><b>-lavfi</b> <i>filtergraph</i> <b>(</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Define a complex filtergraph, i.e. one with arbitrary number of inputs and/or outputs. Equivalent to <b>-filter_complex</b>.
<dt><b>-filter_complex_script</b> <i>filename</i> <b>(</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> This option is similar to <b>-filter_complex</b>, the only difference is that its argument is the name of the file from which a complex filtergraph description is to be read.
<dt><b>-accurate_seek (</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> This option enables or disables accurate seeking in input files with the <b>-ss</b> option. It is enabled by default, so seeking is accurate when transcoding. Use <b>-noaccurate_seek</b> to disable it, which may be useful e.g. when copying some streams and transcoding the others.
<dt><b>-seek_timestamp (</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> This option enables or disables seeking by timestamp in input files with the <b>-ss</b> option. It is disabled by default. If enabled, the argument to the <b>-ss</b> option is considered an actual timestamp, and is not offset by the start time of the file. This matters only for files which do not start from timestamp 0, such as transport streams.
<dt><b>-thread_queue_size</b> <i>size</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> This option sets the maximum number of queued packets when reading from the file or device. With low latency / high rate live streams, packets may be discarded if they are not read in a timely manner; setting this value can force ffmpeg to use a separate input thread and read packets as soon as they arrive. By default ffmpeg only do this if multiple inputs are specified.
<dt><b>-sdp_file</b> <i>file</i> <b>(</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Print sdp information for an output stream to <i>file</i>. This allows dumping sdp information when at least one output isn't an rtp stream. (Requires at least one of the output formats to be rtp).
<dt><b>-discard (</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Allows discarding specific streams or frames from streams. Any input stream can be fully discarded, using value <tt>&quot;all&quot;</tt> whereas selective discarding of frames from a stream occurs at the demuxer and is not supported by all demuxers.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Discard no frame.
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd> Default, which discards no frames.
<dt><b>noref</b>
<dd> Discard all non-reference frames.
<dt><b>bidir</b>
<dd> Discard all bidirectional frames.
<dt><b>nokey</b>
<dd> Discard all frames excepts keyframes.
<dt><b>all</b>
<dd> Discard all frames.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>-abort_on</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Stop and abort on various conditions. The following flags are available:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>empty_output</b>
<dd> No packets were passed to the muxer, the output is empty.
<dt><b>empty_output_stream</b>
<dd> No packets were passed to the muxer in some of the output streams.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>-max_error_rate (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set fraction of decoding frame failures across all inputs which when crossed ffmpeg will return exit code 69. Crossing this threshold does not terminate processing. Range is a floating-point number between 0 to 1. Default is 2/3.
<dt><b>-xerror (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Stop and exit on error
<dt><b>-max_muxing_queue_size</b> <i>packets</i> <b>(</b><i>output,per-stream</i><b>)</b>
<dd> When transcoding audio and/or video streams, ffmpeg will not begin writing into the output until it has one packet for each such stream. While waiting for that to happen, packets for other streams are buffered. This option sets the size of this buffer, in packets, for the matching output stream. 

 The default value of this option should be high enough for most uses, so only touch this option if you are sure that you need it.
<dt><b>-muxing_queue_data_threshold</b> <i>bytes</i> <b>(</b><i>output,per-stream</i><b>)</b>
<dd> This is a minimum threshold until which the muxing queue size is not taken into account. Defaults to 50 megabytes per stream, and is based on the overall size of packets passed to the muxer.
<dt><b>-auto_conversion_filters (</b><i>global</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable automatically inserting format conversion filters in all filter graphs, including those defined by <b>-vf</b>, <b>-af</b>, <b>-filter_complex</b> and <b>-lavfi</b>. If filter format negotiation requires a conversion, the initialization of the filters will fail. Conversions can still be performed by inserting the relevant conversion filter (scale, aresample) in the graph. On by default, to explicitly disable it you need to specify <tt>&quot;-noauto_conversion_filters&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<h3>Preset files</h3>

 A preset file contains a sequence of <i>option</i>=<i>value</i> pairs, one for each line, specifying a sequence of options which would be awkward to specify on the command line. Lines starting with the hash ('#') character are ignored and are used to provide comments. Check the <i>presets</i> directory in the FFmpeg source tree for examples. 

 There are two types of preset files: ffpreset and avpreset files. 

 <i>ffpreset files</i> 

 ffpreset files are specified with the <tt>&quot;vpre&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;apre&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;spre&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;fpre&quot;</tt> options. The <tt>&quot;fpre&quot;</tt> option takes the filename of the preset instead of a preset name as input and can be used for any kind of codec. For the <tt>&quot;vpre&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;apre&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;spre&quot;</tt> options, the options specified in a preset file are applied to the currently selected codec of the same type as the preset option. 

 The argument passed to the <tt>&quot;vpre&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;apre&quot;</tt>, and <tt>&quot;spre&quot;</tt> preset options identifies the preset file to use according to the following rules: 

 First ffmpeg searches for a file named <i>arg</i>.ffpreset in the directories <i></i>$FFMPEG_DATADIR<i></i> (if set), and <i></i>$HOME<i>/.ffmpeg</i>, and in the datadir defined at configuration time (usually <i>PREFIX/share/ffmpeg</i>) or in a <i>ffpresets</i> folder along the executable on win32, in that order. For example, if the argument is <tt>&quot;libvpx-1080p&quot;</tt>, it will search for the file <i>libvpx-1080p.ffpreset</i>. 

 If no such file is found, then ffmpeg will search for a file named <i>codec_name</i>-<i>arg</i>.ffpreset in the above-mentioned directories, where <i>codec_name</i> is the name of the codec to which the preset file options will be applied. For example, if you select the video codec with <tt>&quot;-vcodec libvpx&quot;</tt> and use <tt>&quot;-vpre 1080p&quot;</tt>, then it will search for the file <i>libvpx-1080p.ffpreset</i>. 

 <i>avpreset files</i> 

 avpreset files are specified with the <tt>&quot;pre&quot;</tt> option. They work similar to ffpreset files, but they only allow encoder- specific options. Therefore, an <i>option</i>=<i>value</i> pair specifying an encoder cannot be used. 

 When the <tt>&quot;pre&quot;</tt> option is specified, ffmpeg will look for files with the suffix .avpreset in the directories <i></i>$AVCONV_DATADIR<i></i> (if set), and <i></i>$HOME<i>/.avconv</i>, and in the datadir defined at configuration time (usually <i>PREFIX/share/ffmpeg</i>), in that order. 

 First ffmpeg searches for a file named <i>codec_name</i>-<i>arg</i>.avpreset in the above-mentioned directories, where <i>codec_name</i> is the name of the codec to which the preset file options will be applied. For example, if you select the video codec with <tt>&quot;-vcodec libvpx&quot;</tt> and use <tt>&quot;-pre 1080p&quot;</tt>, then it will search for the file <i>libvpx-1080p.avpreset</i>. 

 If no such file is found, then ffmpeg will search for a file named <i>arg</i>.avpreset in the same directories.

<h2>EXAMPLES</h2>

<h3>Video and Audio grabbing</h3>

 If you specify the input format and device then ffmpeg can grab video and audio directly. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f oss -i /dev/dsp -f video4linux2 -i /dev/video0 /tmp/out.mpg
</pre> 

 Or with an <font SIZE="-1">ALSA</font> audio source (mono input, card id 1) instead of <font SIZE="-1">OSS:</font> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f alsa -ac 1 -i hw:1 -f video4linux2 -i /dev/video0 /tmp/out.mpg
</pre> 

 Note that you must activate the right video source and channel before launching ffmpeg with any <font SIZE="-1">TV</font> viewer such as &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://linux.bytesex.org/xawtv/">http://linux.bytesex.org/xawtv/</a></b>&gt; by Gerd Knorr. You also have to set the audio recording levels correctly with a standard mixer.

<h3>X11 grabbing</h3>

 Grab the X11 display with ffmpeg via 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f x11grab -video_size cif -framerate 25 -i :0.0 /tmp/out.mpg
</pre> 

 0.0 is display.screen number of your X11 server, same as the <font SIZE="-1">DISPLAY</font> environment variable. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f x11grab -video_size cif -framerate 25 -i :0.0+10,20 /tmp/out.mpg
</pre> 

 0.0 is display.screen number of your X11 server, same as the <font SIZE="-1">DISPLAY</font> environment variable. 10 is the x-offset and 20 the y-offset for the grabbing.

<h3>Video and Audio file format conversion</h3>

 Any supported file format and protocol can serve as input to ffmpeg: 

 Examples:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can use <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> files as input: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i /tmp/test%d.Y /tmp/out.mpg
</pre> 

 It will use the files: 

 <pre>
        /tmp/test0.Y, /tmp/test0.U, /tmp/test0.V,
        /tmp/test1.Y, /tmp/test1.U, /tmp/test1.V, etc...
</pre> 

 The Y files use twice the resolution of the U and V files. They are raw files, without header. They can be generated by all decent video decoders. You must specify the size of the image with the <b>-s</b> option if ffmpeg cannot guess it.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can input from a raw <font SIZE="-1">YUV420P</font> file: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i /tmp/test.yuv /tmp/out.avi
</pre> 

 test.yuv is a file containing raw <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> planar data. Each frame is composed of the Y plane followed by the U and V planes at half vertical and horizontal resolution.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can output to a raw <font SIZE="-1">YUV420P</font> file: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i mydivx.avi hugefile.yuv
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can set several input files and output files: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i /tmp/a.wav -s 640x480 -i /tmp/a.yuv /tmp/a.mpg
</pre> 

 Converts the audio file a.wav and the raw <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> video file a.yuv to <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> file a.mpg.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can also do audio and video conversions at the same time: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i /tmp/a.wav -ar 22050 /tmp/a.mp2
</pre> 

 Converts a.wav to <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> audio at 22050 Hz sample rate.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can encode to several formats at the same time and define a mapping from input stream to output streams: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i /tmp/a.wav -map 0:a -b:a 64k /tmp/a.mp2 -map 0:a -b:a 128k /tmp/b.mp2
</pre> 

 Converts a.wav to a.mp2 at 64 kbits and to b.mp2 at 128 kbits. '-map file:index' specifies which input stream is used for each output stream, in the order of the definition of output streams.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can transcode decrypted VOBs: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i snatch_1.vob -f avi -c:v mpeg4 -b:v 800k -g 300 -bf 2 -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 128k snatch.avi
</pre> 

 This is a typical <font SIZE="-1">DVD</font> ripping example; the input is a <font SIZE="-1">VOB</font> file, the output an <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> file with <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> video and <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> audio. Note that in this command we use B-frames so the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> stream is DivX5 compatible, and <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size is 300 which means one intra frame every 10 seconds for 29.97fps input video. Furthermore, the audio stream is MP3-encoded so you need to enable <font SIZE="-1">LAME</font> support by passing <tt>&quot;--enable-libmp3lame&quot;</tt> to configure. The mapping is particularly useful for <font SIZE="-1">DVD</font> transcoding to get the desired audio language. 

 <font SIZE="-1">NOTE:</font> To see the supported input formats, use <tt>&quot;ffmpeg -demuxers&quot;</tt>.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can extract images from a video, or create a video from many images: 

 For extracting images from a video: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i foo.avi -r 1 -s WxH -f image2 foo-%03d.jpeg
</pre> 

 This will extract one video frame per second from the video and will output them in files named <i>foo-001.jpeg</i>, <i>foo-002.jpeg</i>, etc. Images will be rescaled to fit the new WxH values. 

 If you want to extract just a limited number of frames, you can use the above command in combination with the <tt>&quot;-frames:v&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;-t&quot;</tt> option, or in combination with -ss to start extracting from a certain point in time. 

 For creating a video from many images: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f image2 -framerate 12 -i foo-%03d.jpeg -s WxH foo.avi
</pre> 

 The syntax <tt>&quot;foo-%03d.jpeg&quot;</tt> specifies to use a decimal number composed of three digits padded with zeroes to express the sequence number. It is the same syntax supported by the C printf function, but only formats accepting a normal integer are suitable. 

 When importing an image sequence, -i also supports expanding shell-like wildcard patterns (globbing) internally, by selecting the image2-specific <tt>&quot;-pattern_type glob&quot;</tt> option. 

 For example, for creating a video from filenames matching the glob pattern <tt>&quot;foo-*.jpeg&quot;</tt>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f image2 -pattern_type glob -framerate 12 -i 'foo-*.jpeg' -s WxH foo.avi
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> You can put many streams of the same type in the output: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i test1.avi -i test2.avi -map 1:1 -map 1:0 -map 0:1 -map 0:0 -c copy -y test12.nut
</pre> 

 The resulting output file <i>test12.nut</i> will contain the first four streams from the input files in reverse order.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> To force <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> video output: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i myfile.avi -b 4000k -minrate 4000k -maxrate 4000k -bufsize 1835k out.m2v
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> The four options lmin, lmax, mblmin and mblmax use 'lambda' units, but you may use the <font SIZE="-1">QP2LAMBDA</font> constant to easily convert from 'q' units: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i src.ext -lmax 21*QP2LAMBDA dst.ext
</pre></dl>

<h2>SYNTAX</h2>

 This section documents the syntax and formats employed by the FFmpeg libraries and tools.

<h3>Quoting and escaping</h3>

 FFmpeg adopts the following quoting and escaping mechanism, unless explicitly specified. The following rules are applied:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>'</b> and <b>\</b> are special characters (respectively used for quoting and escaping). In addition to them, there might be other special characters depending on the specific syntax where the escaping and quoting are employed.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A special character is escaped by prefixing it with a <b>\</b>.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> All characters enclosed between <b>''</b> are included literally in the parsed string. The quote character <b>'</b> itself cannot be quoted, so you may need to close the quote and escape it.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Leading and trailing whitespaces, unless escaped or quoted, are removed from the parsed string.</dl>
 

 Note that you may need to add a second level of escaping when using the command line or a script, which depends on the syntax of the adopted shell language. 

 The function <tt>&quot;av_get_token&quot;</tt> defined in <i>libavutil/avstring.h</i> can be used to parse a token quoted or escaped according to the rules defined above. 

 The tool <i>tools/ffescape</i> in the FFmpeg source tree can be used to automatically quote or escape a string in a script. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Escape the string <tt>&quot;Crime d'Amour&quot;</tt> containing the <tt>&quot;'&quot;</tt> special character: 

 <pre>
        Crime d\'Amour
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> The string above contains a quote, so the <tt>&quot;'&quot;</tt> needs to be escaped when quoting it: 

 <pre>
        'Crime d'\''Amour'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Include leading or trailing whitespaces using quoting: 

 <pre>
        '  this string starts and ends with whitespaces  '
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Escaping and quoting can be mixed together: 

 <pre>
        ' The string '\'string\'' is a string '
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> To include a literal <b>\</b> you can use either escaping or quoting: 

 <pre>
        'c:\foo' can be written as c:\\foo
</pre></dl>

<h3>Date</h3>

 The accepted syntax is: 

 
        [(YYYY-MM-DD|YYYYMMDD)[T|t| ]]((HH:MM:SS[.m...]]])|(HHMMSS[.m...]]]))[Z]
        now
 

 If the value is ``now'' it takes the current time. 

 Time is local time unless Z is appended, in which case it is interpreted as <font SIZE="-1">UTC.</font> If the year-month-day part is not specified it takes the current year-month-day.

<h3>Time duration</h3>

 There are two accepted syntaxes for expressing time duration. 

 
[-] [&lt;HH&gt;:]&lt;MM&gt; : &lt;SS&gt;[.&lt;m&gt;...]
 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>HH</i></font><i></i> expresses the number of hours, <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>MM</i></font><i></i> the number of minutes for a maximum of 2 digits, and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SS</i></font><i></i> the number of seconds for a maximum of 2 digits. The <i>m</i> at the end expresses decimal value for <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>SS</i></font><i></i>. 

 <i>or</i> 

 
[-]&lt;S&gt; + [.&lt;m&gt;...][s | ms | us]
 

 <i>S</i> expresses the number of seconds, with the optional decimal part <i>m</i>. The optional literal suffixes <b>s</b>, <b>ms</b> or <b>us</b> indicate to interpret the value as seconds, milliseconds or microseconds, respectively. 

 In both expressions, the optional <b>-</b> indicates negative duration. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 The following examples are all valid time duration:
<dl>
<dt><b>55</b>
<dd> 55 seconds
<dt><b>0.2</b>
<dd> 0.2 seconds
<dt><b>200ms</b>
<dd> 200 milliseconds, that's 0.2s
<dt><b>200000us</b>
<dd> 200000 microseconds, that's 0.2s
<dt><b>12:03:45</b>
<dd> 12 hours, 03 minutes and 45 seconds
<dt><b>23.189</b>
<dd> 23.189 seconds</dl>

<h3>Video rate</h3>

 Specify the frame rate of a video, expressed as the number of frames generated per second. It has to be a string in the format <i>frame_rate_num</i>/<i>frame_rate_den</i>, an integer number, a float number or a valid video frame rate abbreviation. 

 The following abbreviations are recognized:
<dl>
<dt><b>ntsc</b>
<dd> 30000/1001
<dt><b>pal</b>
<dd> 25/1
<dt><b>qntsc</b>
<dd> 30000/1001
<dt><b>qpal</b>
<dd> 25/1
<dt><b>sntsc</b>
<dd> 30000/1001
<dt><b>spal</b>
<dd> 25/1
<dt><b>film</b>
<dd> 24/1
<dt><b>ntsc-film</b>
<dd> 24000/1001</dl>

<h3>Ratio</h3>

 A ratio can be expressed as an expression, or in the form <i>numerator</i>:<i>denominator</i>. 

 Note that a ratio with infinite (1/0) or negative value is considered valid, so you should check on the returned value if you want to exclude those values. 

 The undefined value can be expressed using the ``0:0'' string.

<h3>Color</h3>

 It can be the name of a color as defined below (case insensitive match) or a <tt>&quot;[0x|#]RRGGBB[AA]&quot;</tt> sequence, possibly followed by @ and a string representing the alpha component. 

 The alpha component may be a string composed by ``0x'' followed by an hexadecimal number or a decimal number between 0.0 and 1.0, which represents the opacity value (<b>0x00</b> or <b>0.0</b> means completely transparent, <b>0xff</b> or <b>1.0</b> completely opaque). If the alpha component is not specified then <b>0xff</b> is assumed. 

 The string <b>random</b> will result in a random color. 

 The following names of colors are recognized:
<dl>
<dt><b>AliceBlue</b>

<dd> 0x00FFFF

<dd> 0xF0FFFF

<dd> 0xF5F5DC
<dt><b>Bisque</b>
<dd> 0xFFE4C4
<dt><b>Black</b>
<dd> 0x000000
<dt><b>BlanchedAlmond</b>
<dd> 0xFFEBCD
<dt><b>Blue</b>
<dd> 0x0000FF
<dt><b>BlueViolet</b>
<dd> 0x8A2BE2
<dt><b>Brown</b>
<dd> 0xA52A2A
<dt><b>BurlyWood</b>
<dd> 0xDEB887
<dt><b>CadetBlue</b>

<h3>Channel Layout</h3>

 A channel layout specifies the spatial disposition of the channels in a multi-channel audio stream. To specify a channel layout, FFmpeg makes use of a special syntax. 

 Individual channels are identified by an id, as given by the table below:
<dl>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FL</b></font>
<dd> front left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FR</b></font>
<dd> front right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FC</b></font>
<dd> front center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>LFE</b></font>
<dd> low frequency
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>BL</b></font>
<dd> back left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>BR</b></font>
<dd> back right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FLC</b></font>
<dd> front left-of-center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>FRC</b></font>
<dd> front right-of-center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>BC</b></font>
<dd> back center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SL</b></font>
<dd> side left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SR</b></font>
<dd> side right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TC</b></font>
<dd> top center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TFL</b></font>
<dd> top front left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TFC</b></font>
<dd> top front center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TFR</b></font>
<dd> top front right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TBL</b></font>
<dd> top back left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TBC</b></font>
<dd> top back center
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TBR</b></font>
<dd> top back right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>DL</b></font>
<dd> downmix left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>DR</b></font>
<dd> downmix right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>WL</b></font>
<dd> wide left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>WR</b></font>
<dd> wide right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SDL</b></font>
<dd> surround direct left
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SDR</b></font>
<dd> surround direct right
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>LFE2</b></font>
<dd> low frequency 2</dl>
 

 Standard channel layout compositions can be specified by using the following identifiers:
<dl>
<dt><b>mono</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FC</font>
<dt><b>stereo</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR</font>
<dt><b>2.1</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+LFE</font>
<dt><b>3.0</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC</font>
<dt><b>3.0(back)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+BC</font>
<dt><b>4.0</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BC</font>
<dt><b>quad</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+BL+BR</font>
<dt><b>quad(side)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>3.1</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE</font>
<dt><b>5.0</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR</font>
<dt><b>5.0(side)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>4.1</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BC</font>
<dt><b>5.1</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR</font>
<dt><b>5.1(side)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>6.0</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>6.0(front)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>hexagonal</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR+BC</font>
<dt><b>6.1</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>6.1</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR+BC</font>
<dt><b>6.1(front)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+LFE+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.0</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.0(front)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.1</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>7.1(wide)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR+FLC+FRC</font>
<dt><b>7.1(wide-side)</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+LFE+FLC+FRC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>octagonal</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR+BC+SL+SR</font>
<dt><b>hexadecagonal</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FL+FR+FC+BL+BR+BC+SL+SR+WL+WR+TBL+TBR+TBC+TFC+TFL+TFR</font>
<dt><b>downmix</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">DL+DR</font></dl>
 

 A custom channel layout can be specified as a sequence of terms, separated by '+' or '|'. Each term can be:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> the name of a standard channel layout (e.g. <b>mono</b>, <b>stereo</b>, <b>4.0</b>, <b>quad</b>, <b>5.0</b>, etc.)
<dt>&bull;
<dd> the name of a single channel (e.g. <font SIZE="-1"><b>FL</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>FR</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>FC</b></font>, <font SIZE="-1"><b>LFE</b></font>, etc.)
<dt>&bull;
<dd> a number of channels, in decimal, followed by 'c', yielding the default channel layout for that number of channels (see the function <tt>&quot;av_get_default_channel_layout&quot;</tt>). Note that not all channel counts have a default layout.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> a number of channels, in decimal, followed by 'C', yielding an unknown channel layout with the specified number of channels. Note that not all channel layout specification strings support unknown channel layouts.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> a channel layout mask, in hexadecimal starting with ``0x'' (see the <tt>&quot;AV_CH_*&quot;</tt> macros in <i>libavutil/channel_layout.h</i>.</dl>
 

 Before libavutil version 53 the trailing character ``c'' to specify a number of channels was optional, but now it is required, while a channel layout mask can also be specified as a decimal number (if and only if not followed by ``c'' or ``C''). 

 See also the function <tt>&quot;av_get_channel_layout&quot;</tt> defined in <i>libavutil/channel_layout.h</i>.

<h2>EXPRESSION EVALUATION</h2>

 When evaluating an arithmetic expression, FFmpeg uses an internal formula evaluator, implemented through the <i>libavutil/eval.h</i> interface. 

 An expression may contain unary, binary operators, constants, and functions. 

 Two expressions <i>expr1</i> and <i>expr2</i> can be combined to form another expression &quot;<i>expr1</i>;<i>expr2</i>&quot;. <i>expr1</i> and <i>expr2</i> are evaluated in turn, and the new expression evaluates to the value of <i>expr2</i>. 

 The following binary operators are available: <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;-&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;*&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;/&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;^&quot;</tt>. 

 The following unary operators are available: <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;-&quot;</tt>. 

 The following functions are available:
<dl>
<dt><b>abs(x)</b>
<dd> Compute absolute value of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>acos(x)</b>
<dd> Compute arccosine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>asin(x)</b>
<dd> Compute arcsine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>atan(x)</b>
<dd> Compute arctangent of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>atan2(x, y)</b>
<dd> Compute principal value of the arc tangent of <i>y</i>/<i>x</i>.
<dt><b>between(x, min, max)</b>
<dd> Return 1 if <i>x</i> is greater than or equal to <i>min</i> and lesser than or equal to <i>max</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>bitand(x, y)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bitor(x, y)</b>
<dd> Compute bitwise and/or operation on <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>. 

 The results of the evaluation of <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are converted to integers before executing the bitwise operation. 

 Note that both the conversion to integer and the conversion back to floating point can lose precision. Beware of unexpected results for large numbers (usually 2^53 and larger).
<dt><b>ceil(expr)</b>
<dd> Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> upwards to the nearest integer. For example, ``ceil(1.5)'' is ``2.0''.
<dt><b>clip(x, min, max)</b>
<dd> Return the value of <i>x</i> clipped between <i>min</i> and <i>max</i>.
<dt><b>cos(x)</b>
<dd> Compute cosine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>cosh(x)</b>
<dd> Compute hyperbolic cosine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>eq(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return 1 if <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are equivalent, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>exp(x)</b>
<dd> Compute exponential of <i>x</i> (with base <tt>&quot;e&quot;</tt>, the Euler's number).
<dt><b>floor(expr)</b>
<dd> Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> downwards to the nearest integer. For example, ``floor(-1.5)'' is ``-2.0''.
<dt><b>gauss(x)</b>
<dd> Compute Gauss function of <i>x</i>, corresponding to <tt>&quot;exp(-x*x/2) / sqrt(2*PI)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>gcd(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return the greatest common divisor of <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>. If both <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> are 0 or either or both are less than zero then behavior is undefined.
<dt><b>gt(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return 1 if <i>x</i> is greater than <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>gte(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return 1 if <i>x</i> is greater than or equal to <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>hypot(x, y)</b>
<dd> This function is similar to the C function with the same name; it returns &quot;sqrt(<i>x</i>*<i>x</i> + <i>y</i>*<i>y</i>)&quot;, the length of the hypotenuse of a right triangle with sides of length <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>, or the distance of the point (<i>x</i>, <i>y</i>) from the origin.
<dt><b>if(x, y)</b>
<dd> Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is non-zero return the result of the evaluation of <i>y</i>, return 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>if(x, y, z)</b>
<dd> Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is non-zero return the evaluation result of <i>y</i>, otherwise the evaluation result of <i>z</i>.
<dt><b>ifnot(x, y)</b>
<dd> Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is zero return the result of the evaluation of <i>y</i>, return 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>ifnot(x, y, z)</b>
<dd> Evaluate <i>x</i>, and if the result is zero return the evaluation result of <i>y</i>, otherwise the evaluation result of <i>z</i>.
<dt><b>isinf(x)</b>
<dd> Return 1.0 if <i>x</i> is +/-INFINITY, 0.0 otherwise.
<dt><b>isnan(x)</b>
<dd> Return 1.0 if <i>x</i> is <font SIZE="-1">NAN, 0.0</font> otherwise.
<dt><b>ld(var)</b>
<dd> Load the value of the internal variable with number <i>var</i>, which was previously stored with st(<i>var</i>, <i>expr</i>). The function returns the loaded value.
<dt><b>lerp(x, y, z)</b>
<dd> Return linear interpolation between <i>x</i> and <i>y</i> by amount of <i>z</i>.
<dt><b>log(x)</b>
<dd> Compute natural logarithm of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>lt(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return 1 if <i>x</i> is lesser than <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>lte(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return 1 if <i>x</i> is lesser than or equal to <i>y</i>, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>max(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return the maximum between <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>.
<dt><b>min(x, y)</b>
<dd> Return the minimum between <i>x</i> and <i>y</i>.
<dt><b>mod(x, y)</b>
<dd> Compute the remainder of division of <i>x</i> by <i>y</i>.
<dt><b>not(expr)</b>
<dd> Return 1.0 if <i>expr</i> is zero, 0.0 otherwise.
<dt><b>pow(x, y)</b>
<dd> Compute the power of <i>x</i> elevated <i>y</i>, it is equivalent to &quot;(<i>x</i>)^(<i>y</i>)&quot;.
<dt><b>print(t)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>print(t, l)</b>
<dd> Print the value of expression <i>t</i> with loglevel <i>l</i>. If <i>l</i> is not specified then a default log level is used. Returns the value of the expression printed. 

 Prints t with loglevel l
<dt><b>random(x)</b>
<dd> Return a pseudo random value between 0.0 and 1.0. <i>x</i> is the index of the internal variable which will be used to save the seed/state.
<dt><b>root(expr, max)</b>
<dd> Find an input value for which the function represented by <i>expr</i> with argument <i></i>ld<i>(0)</i> is 0 in the interval 0..<i>max</i>. 

 The expression in <i>expr</i> must denote a continuous function or the result is undefined. 

 <i></i>ld<i>(0)</i> is used to represent the function input value, which means that the given expression will be evaluated multiple times with various input values that the expression can access through <tt>ld(0)</tt>. When the expression evaluates to 0 then the corresponding input value will be returned.
<dt><b>round(expr)</b>
<dd> Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> to the nearest integer. For example, ``round(1.5)'' is ``2.0''.
<dt><b>sgn(x)</b>
<dd> Compute sign of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>sin(x)</b>
<dd> Compute sine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>sinh(x)</b>
<dd> Compute hyperbolic sine of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>sqrt(expr)</b>
<dd> Compute the square root of <i>expr</i>. This is equivalent to &quot;(<i>expr</i>)^.5&quot;.
<dt><b>squish(x)</b>
<dd> Compute expression <tt>&quot;1/(1 + exp(4*x))&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>st(var, expr)</b>
<dd> Store the value of the expression <i>expr</i> in an internal variable. <i>var</i> specifies the number of the variable where to store the value, and it is a value ranging from 0 to 9. The function returns the value stored in the internal variable. Note, Variables are currently not shared between expressions.
<dt><b>tan(x)</b>
<dd> Compute tangent of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>tanh(x)</b>
<dd> Compute hyperbolic tangent of <i>x</i>.
<dt><b>taylor(expr, x)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>taylor(expr, x, id)</b>
<dd> Evaluate a Taylor series at <i>x</i>, given an expression representing the <tt>&quot;ld(id)&quot;</tt>-th derivative of a function at 0. 

 When the series does not converge the result is undefined. 

 <i>ld(id)</i> is used to represent the derivative order in <i>expr</i>, which means that the given expression will be evaluated multiple times with various input values that the expression can access through <tt>&quot;ld(id)&quot;</tt>. If <i>id</i> is not specified then 0 is assumed. 

 Note, when you have the derivatives at y instead of 0, <tt>&quot;taylor(expr, x-y)&quot;</tt> can be used.
<dt><b>time(0)</b>
<dd> Return the current (wallclock) time in seconds.
<dt><b>trunc(expr)</b>
<dd> Round the value of expression <i>expr</i> towards zero to the nearest integer. For example, ``trunc(-1.5)'' is ``-1.0''.
<dt><b>while(cond, expr)</b>
<dd> Evaluate expression <i>expr</i> while the expression <i>cond</i> is non-zero, and returns the value of the last <i>expr</i> evaluation, or <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if <i>cond</i> was always false.</dl>
 

 The following constants are available:
<dl>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PI</b></font>
<dd> area of the unit disc, approximately 3.14
<dt><b>E</b>
<dd> <b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-exp/">exp</a></b>(1) (Euler's number), approximately 2.718
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PHI</b></font>
<dd> golden ratio (1+<b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/5-sqrt/">sqrt</a></b>(5))/2, approximately 1.618</dl>
 

 Assuming that an expression is considered ``true'' if it has a non-zero value, note that: 

 <tt>&quot;*&quot;</tt> works like <font SIZE="-1">AND</font> 

 <tt>&quot;+&quot;</tt> works like <font SIZE="-1">OR</font> 

 For example the construct: 

 <pre>
        if (A AND B) then C
</pre> 

 is equivalent to: 

 <pre>
        if(A*B, C)
</pre> 

 In your C code, you can extend the list of unary and binary functions, and define recognized constants, so that they are available for your expressions. 

 The evaluator also recognizes the International System unit prefixes. If 'i' is appended after the prefix, binary prefixes are used, which are based on powers of 1024 instead of powers of 1000. The 'B' postfix multiplies the value by 8, and can be appended after a unit prefix or used alone. This allows using for example '<font SIZE="-1">KB</font>', 'MiB', 'G' and 'B' as number postfix. 

 The list of available International System prefixes follows, with indication of the corresponding powers of 10 and of 2.
<dl>
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd> 10^-24 / 2^-80
<dt><b>z</b>
<dd> 10^-21 / 2^-70
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd> 10^-18 / 2^-60
<dt><b>f</b>
<dd> 10^-15 / 2^-50
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd> 10^-12 / 2^-40
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> 10^-9 / 2^-30
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd> 10^-6 / 2^-20
<dt><b>m</b>
<dd> 10^-3 / 2^-10
<dt><b>c</b>
<dd> 10^-2
<dt><b>d</b>
<dd> 10^-1
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> 10^2
<dt><b>k</b>
<dd> 10^3 / 2^10
<dt><b>K</b>
<dd> 10^3 / 2^10
<dt><b>M</b>
<dd> 10^6 / 2^20
<dt><b>G</b>
<dd> 10^9 / 2^30
<dt><b>T</b>
<dd> 10^12 / 2^40
<dt><b>P</b>
<dd> 10^15 / 2^40
<dt><b>E</b>
<dd> 10^18 / 2^50
<dt><b>Z</b>
<dd> 10^21 / 2^60
<dt><b>Y</b>
<dd> 10^24 / 2^70</dl>

<h2>CODEC OPTIONS</h2>

 libavcodec provides some generic global options, which can be set on all the encoders and decoders. In addition each codec may support so-called private options, which are specific for a given codec. 

 Sometimes, a global option may only affect a specific kind of codec, and may be nonsensical or ignored by another, so you need to be aware of the meaning of the specified options. Also some options are meant only for decoding or encoding. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, or by setting the value explicitly in the <tt>&quot;AVCodecContext&quot;</tt> options or using the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API</font> for programmatic use. 

 The list of supported options follow:
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set bitrate in bits/s. Default value is 200K.
<dt><b>ab</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set audio bitrate (in bits/s). Default value is 128K.
<dt><b>bt</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set video bitrate tolerance (in bits/s). In 1-pass mode, bitrate tolerance specifies how far ratecontrol is willing to deviate from the target average bitrate value. This is not related to min/max bitrate. Lowering tolerance too much has an adverse effect on quality.
<dt><b>flags</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio,video,subtitles</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set generic flags. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>mv4</b>
<dd> Use four motion vector by macroblock (mpeg4).
<dt><b>qpel</b>
<dd> Use 1/4 pel motion compensation.
<dt><b>loop</b>
<dd> Use loop filter.
<dt><b>qscale</b>
<dd> Use fixed qscale.
<dt><b>pass1</b>
<dd> Use internal 2pass ratecontrol in first pass mode.
<dt><b>pass2</b>
<dd> Use internal 2pass ratecontrol in second pass mode.
<dt><b>gray</b>
<dd> Only decode/encode grayscale.
<dt><b>psnr</b>
<dd> Set error[?] variables during encoding.
<dt><b>truncated</b>
<dd> Input bitstream might be randomly truncated.
<dt><b>drop_changed</b>
<dd> Don't output frames whose parameters differ from first decoded frame in stream. Error <font SIZE="-1">AVERROR_INPUT_CHANGED</font> is returned when a frame is dropped.
<dt><b>ildct</b>
<dd> Use interlaced <font SIZE="-1">DCT.</font>
<dt><b>low_delay</b>
<dd> Force low delay.
<dt><b>global_header</b>
<dd> Place global headers in extradata instead of every keyframe.
<dt><b>bitexact</b>
<dd> Only write platform-, build- and time-independent data. (except (I)DCT). This ensures that file and data checksums are reproducible and match between platforms. Its primary use is for regression testing.
<dt><b>aic</b>
<dd> Apply H263 advanced intra coding / mpeg4 ac prediction.
<dt><b>ilme</b>
<dd> Apply interlaced motion estimation.
<dt><b>cgop</b>
<dd> Use closed gop.
<dt><b>output_corrupt</b>
<dd> Output even potentially corrupted frames.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>time_base</b> <i>rational number</i>
<dd> Set codec time base. 

 It is the fundamental unit of time (in seconds) in terms of which frame timestamps are represented. For fixed-fps content, timebase should be <tt>&quot;1 / frame_rate&quot;</tt> and timestamp increments should be identically 1.
<dt><b>g</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the group of picture (<font SIZE="-1">GOP</font>) size. Default value is 12.
<dt><b>ar</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set audio sampling rate (in Hz).
<dt><b>ac</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set number of audio channels.
<dt><b>cutoff</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set cutoff bandwidth. (Supported only by selected encoders, see their respective documentation sections.)
<dt><b>frame_size</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set audio frame size. 

 Each submitted frame except the last must contain exactly frame_size samples per channel. May be 0 when the codec has <font SIZE="-1">CODEC_CAP_VARIABLE_FRAME_SIZE</font> set, in that case the frame size is not restricted. It is set by some decoders to indicate constant frame size.
<dt><b>frame_number</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set the frame number.
<dt><b>delay</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>qcomp</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set video quantizer scale compression (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>). It is used as a constant in the ratecontrol equation. Recommended range for default rc_eq: 0.0-1.0.
<dt><b>qblur</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set video quantizer scale blur (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>).
<dt><b>qmin</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set min video quantizer scale (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>). Must be included between -1 and 69, default value is 2.
<dt><b>qmax</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set max video quantizer scale (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>). Must be included between -1 and 1024, default value is 31.
<dt><b>qdiff</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set max difference between the quantizer scale (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>).
<dt><b>bf</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set max number of B frames between non-B-frames. 

 Must be an integer between -1 and 16. 0 means that B-frames are disabled. If a value of -1 is used, it will choose an automatic value depending on the encoder. 

 Default value is 0.
<dt><b>b_qfactor</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set qp factor between P and B frames.
<dt><b>b_strategy</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set strategy to choose between I/P/B-frames.
<dt><b>ps</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> payload size in bytes.
<dt><b>mv_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>header_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>i_tex_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>p_tex_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>i_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>p_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>skip_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>misc_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>frame_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>codec_tag</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>bug</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Workaround not auto detected encoder bugs. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>autodetect</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>xvid_ilace</b>
<dd> Xvid interlacing bug (autodetected if fourcc==XVIX)
<dt><b>ump4</b>
<dd> (autodetected if fourcc==UMP4)
<dt><b>no_padding</b>
<dd> padding bug (autodetected)
<dt><b>amv</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>qpel_chroma</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>std_qpel</b>
<dd> old standard qpel (autodetected per fourcc/version)
<dt><b>qpel_chroma2</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>direct_blocksize</b>
<dd> direct-qpel-blocksize bug (autodetected per fourcc/version)
<dt><b>edge</b>
<dd> edge padding bug (autodetected per fourcc/version)
<dt><b>hpel_chroma</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dc_clip</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ms</b>
<dd> Workaround various bugs in microsoft broken decoders.
<dt><b>trunc</b>
<dd> trancated frames</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>strict</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Specify how strictly to follow the standards. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>very</b>
<dd> strictly conform to an older more strict version of the spec or reference software
<dt><b>strict</b>
<dd> strictly conform to all the things in the spec no matter what consequences
<dt><b>normal</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>unofficial</b>
<dd> allow unofficial extensions
<dt><b>experimental</b>
<dd> allow non standardized experimental things, experimental (unfinished/work in progress/not well tested) decoders and encoders. Note: experimental decoders can pose a security risk, do not use this for decoding untrusted input.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>b_qoffset</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> offset between P and B frames.
<dt><b>err_detect</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set error detection flags. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>crccheck</b>
<dd> verify embedded CRCs
<dt><b>bitstream</b>
<dd> detect bitstream specification deviations
<dt><b>buffer</b>
<dd> detect improper bitstream length
<dt><b>explode</b>
<dd> abort decoding on minor error detection
<dt><b>ignore_err</b>
<dd> ignore decoding errors, and continue decoding. This is useful if you want to analyze the content of a video and thus want everything to be decoded no matter what. This option will not result in a video that is pleasing to watch in case of errors.
<dt><b>careful</b>
<dd> consider things that violate the spec and have not been seen in the wild as errors
<dt><b>compliant</b>
<dd> consider all spec non compliancies as errors
<dt><b>aggressive</b>
<dd> consider things that a sane encoder should not do as an error</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>has_b_frames</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>block_align</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>mpeg_quant</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> quantizers instead of H.263.
<dt><b>rc_override_count</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd>
<dt><b>maxrate</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>

<dt><b>minrate</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set min bitrate tolerance (in bits/s). Most useful in setting up a <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> encode. It is of little use elsewise.
<dt><b>bufsize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,audio,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set ratecontrol buffer size (in bits).
<dt><b>i_qfactor</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> factor between P and I frames.
<dt><b>i_qoffset</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> offset between P and I frames.
<dt><b>dct</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">DCT</font> algorithm. 

 Possible values:
<dl>

<dd>

<dd> autoselect a good one (default)

<dd>

<dl>

<dt><b>lumi_mask</b> <i>float</i> <b>(</b><i>encoding,video</i><b>)</b>

 Possible values:

<dd> Set noise reduction.

<dd> Set number of bits which should be loaded into the rc buffer before decoding starts.
<dt><b>flags2</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio,video,subtitles</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>fast</b>
<dd> Allow non spec compliant speedup tricks.
<dt><b>noout</b>
<dd> Skip bitstream encoding.
<dt><b>ignorecrop</b>
<dd> Ignore cropping information from sps.
<dt><b>local_header</b>
<dd> Place global headers at every keyframe instead of in extradata.
<dt><b>chunks</b>
<dd> Frame data might be split into multiple chunks.
<dt><b>showall</b>
<dd> Show all frames before the first keyframe.
<dt><b>export_mvs</b>
<dd> Export motion vectors into frame side-data (see <tt>&quot;AV_FRAME_DATA_MOTION_VECTORS&quot;</tt>) for codecs that support it. See also <i>doc/examples/export_mvs.c</i>.
<dt><b>skip_manual</b>
<dd> Do not skip samples and export skip information as frame side data.
<dt><b>ass_ro_flush_noop</b>
<dd> Do not reset <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> ReadOrder field on flush.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>export_side_data</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding/encoding,audio,video,subtitles</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>mvs</b>
<dd> Export motion vectors into frame side-data (see <tt>&quot;AV_FRAME_DATA_MOTION_VECTORS&quot;</tt>) for codecs that support it. See also <i>doc/examples/export_mvs.c</i>.
<dt><b>prft</b>
<dd> Export encoder Producer Reference Time into packet side-data (see <tt>&quot;AV_PKT_DATA_PRFT&quot;</tt>) for codecs that support it.
<dt><b>venc_params</b>
<dd> Export video encoding parameters through frame side data (see <tt>&quot;AV_FRAME_DATA_VIDEO_ENC_PARAMS&quot;</tt>) for codecs that support it. At present, those are H.264 and <font SIZE="-1">VP9.</font>
<dt><b>film_grain</b>
<dd> Export film grain parameters through frame side data (see <tt>&quot;AV_FRAME_DATA_FILM_GRAIN_PARAMS&quot;</tt>). Supported at present by <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> decoders.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dd> Set max macroblock lagrange factor (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>).

<dd>
<dt><b>skip_idct</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>skip_frame</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>decoding,video</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Make decoder discard processing depending on the frame type selected by the option value. 

 <b>skip_loop_filter</b> skips frame loop filtering, <b>skip_idct</b> skips frame IDCT/dequantization, <b>skip_frame</b> skips decoding. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Discard no frame.
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd> Discard useless frames like 0-sized frames.
<dt><b>noref</b>
<dd> Discard all non-reference frames.
<dt><b>bidir</b>
<dd> Discard all bidirectional frames.
<dt><b>nokey</b>
<dd> Discard all frames excepts keyframes.
<dt><b>nointra</b>
<dd> Discard all frames except I frames.
<dt><b>all</b>
<dd> Discard all frames.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>default</b>.</dl>
