<h3>libvorbis</h3>

 libvorbis encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libvorbisenc headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libvorbis&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libvorbis wrapper. The <b>oggenc</b>-equivalent of the options are listed in parentheses. 

 To get a more accurate and extensive documentation of the libvorbis options, consult the libvorbisenc's and <b>oggenc</b>'s documentations. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://xiph.org/vorbis/">http://xiph.org/vorbis/</a></b>&gt;, &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://wiki.xiph.org/Vorbis-tools">http://wiki.xiph.org/Vorbis-tools</a></b>&gt;, and <b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-oggenc/">oggenc</a></b>(1).
<dl>
<dt><b>b (</b><i>-b</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set bitrate expressed in bits/s for <font SIZE="-1">ABR.</font> <b>oggenc</b> <b>-b</b> is expressed in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>q (</b><i>-q</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set constant quality setting for <font SIZE="-1">VBR.</font> The value should be a float number in the range of -1.0 to 10.0. The higher the value, the better the quality. The default value is <b>3.0</b>. 

 This option is valid only using the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. For library interface users, use <b>global_quality</b>.
<dt><b>cutoff (</b><i>--advanced-encode-option lowpass_frequency=N</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set cutoff bandwidth in Hz, a value of 0 disables cutoff. <b>oggenc</b>'s related option is expressed in kHz. The default value is <b>0</b> (cutoff disabled).
<dt><b>minrate (</b><i>-m</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set minimum bitrate expressed in bits/s. <b>oggenc</b> <b>-m</b> is expressed in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>maxrate (</b><i>-M</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set maximum bitrate expressed in bits/s. <b>oggenc</b> <b>-M</b> is expressed in kilobits/s. This only has effect on <font SIZE="-1">ABR</font> mode.
<dt><b>iblock (</b><i>--advanced-encode-option impulse_noisetune=N</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set noise floor bias for impulse blocks. The value is a float number from -15.0 to 0.0. A negative bias instructs the encoder to pay special attention to the crispness of transients in the encoded audio. The tradeoff for better transient response is a higher bitrate.</dl>

<h3>mjpeg</h3>

 Motion <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> encoder. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>huffman</b>
<dd> Set the huffman encoding strategy. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd> Use the default huffman tables. This is the default strategy.
<dt><b>optimal</b>
<dd> Compute and use optimal huffman tables.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>wavpack</h3>

 WavPack lossless audio encoder. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The equivalent options for <b>wavpack</b> command line utility are listed in parentheses. 

 Shared options 

 The following shared options are effective for this encoder. Only special notes about this particular encoder will be documented here. For the general meaning of the options, see <b>the Codec Options chapter</b>.
<dl>
<dt><b>frame_size (</b><i>--blocksize</i><b>)</b>
<dd> For this encoder, the range for this option is between 128 and 131072. Default is automatically decided based on sample rate and number of channel. 

 For the complete formula of calculating default, see <i>libavcodec/wavpackenc.c</i>.
<dt><b>compression_level (</b><i>-f</i><b>,</b> <i>-h</i><b>,</b> <i>-hh</i><b>, and</b> <i>-x</i><b>)</b>
<dd></dl>
 

 Private options
<dl>
<dt><b>joint_stereo (</b><i>-j</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set whether to enable joint stereo. Valid values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>on (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Force mid/side audio encoding.
<dt><b>off (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Force left/right audio encoding.
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> Let the encoder decide automatically.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>optimize_mono</b>
<dd> Set whether to enable optimization for mono. This option is only effective for non-mono streams. Available values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>on</b>
<dd> enabled
<dt><b>off</b>
<dd> disabled</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h2>VIDEO ENCODERS</h2>

 A description of some of the currently available video encoders follows.

<h3><font SIZE="-1">GIF</font></h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> image/animation encoder. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>gifflags</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Sets the flags used for <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> encoding.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>offsetting</b>
<dd> Enables picture offsetting. 

 Default is enabled.
<dt><b>transdiff</b>
<dd> Enables transparency detection between frames. 

 Default is enabled.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>gifimage</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Enables encoding one full <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> image per frame, rather than an animated <font SIZE="-1">GIF.</font> 

 Default value is <b>0</b>.
<dt><b>global_palette</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Writes a palette to the global <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> header where feasible. 

 If disabled, every frame will always have a palette written, even if there is a global palette supplied. 

 Default value is <b>1</b>.</dl>

<h3>Hap</h3>

 Vidvox Hap video encoder. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>format</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Specifies the Hap format to encode.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>hap</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hap_alpha</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hap_q</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>hap</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>chunks</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Specifies the number of chunks to split frames into, between 1 and 64. This permits multithreaded decoding of large frames, potentially at the cost of data-rate. The encoder may modify this value to divide frames evenly. 

 Default value is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>compressor</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Specifies the second-stage compressor to use. If set to <b>none</b>, <b>chunks</b> will be limited to 1, as chunked uncompressed frames offer no benefit.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>snappy</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>snappy</b>.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>jpeg2000</h3>

 The native jpeg 2000 encoder is lossy by default, the <tt>&quot;-q:v&quot;</tt> option can be used to set the encoding quality. Lossless encoding can be selected with <tt>&quot;-pred 1&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>format</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Can be set to either <tt>&quot;j2k&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;jp2&quot;</tt> (the default) that makes it possible to store non-rgb pix_fmts.
<dt><b>tile_width</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Sets tile width. Range is 1 to 1073741824. Default is 256.
<dt><b>tile_height</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Sets tile height. Range is 1 to 1073741824. Default is 256.
<dt><b>pred</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Allows setting the discrete wavelet transform (<font SIZE="-1">DWT</font>) type
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>dwt97int (Lossy)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dwt53 (Lossless)</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;dwt97int&quot;</tt></dl>

<dt><b>sop</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Enable this to add <font SIZE="-1">SOP</font> marker at the start of each packet. Disabled by default.
<dt><b>eph</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Enable this to add <font SIZE="-1">EPH</font> marker at the end of each packet header. Disabled by default.
<dt><b>prog</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Sets the progression order to be used by the encoder. Possible values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lrcp</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>rlcp</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>rpcl</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>pcrl</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cprl</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Set to <tt>&quot;lrcp&quot;</tt> by default.</dl>

<dt><b>layer_rates</b> <i>string</i>
<dd> By default, when this option is not used, compression is done using the quality metric. This option allows for compression using compression ratio. The compression ratio for each level could be specified. The compression ratio of a layer <tt>&quot;l&quot;</tt> species the what ratio of total file size is contained in the first <tt>&quot;l&quot;</tt> layers. 

 Example usage: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.bmp -c:v jpeg2000 -layer_rates &quot;100,10,1&quot; output.j2k
</pre> 

 This would compress the image to contain 3 layers, where the data contained in the first layer would be compressed by 1000 times, compressed by 100 in the first two layers, and shall contain all data while using all 3 layers.</dl>

<h3>librav1e</h3>

 rav1e <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the rav1e headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-librav1e&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>qmax</b>
<dd> Sets the maximum quantizer to use when using bitrate mode.
<dt><b>qmin</b>
<dd> Sets the minimum quantizer to use when using bitrate mode.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd> Uses quantizer mode to encode at the given quantizer (0-255).
<dt><b>speed</b>
<dd> Selects the speed preset (0-10) to encode with.
<dt><b>tiles</b>
<dd> Selects how many tiles to encode with.
<dt><b>tile-rows</b>
<dd> Selects how many rows of tiles to encode with.
<dt><b>tile-columns</b>
<dd> Selects how many columns of tiles to encode with.
<dt><b>rav1e-params</b>
<dd> Set rav1e options using a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> pairs separated by ``:''. See <b>rav1e --help</b> for a list of options. 

 For example to specify librav1e encoding options with <b>-rav1e-params</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input -c:v librav1e -b:v 500K -rav1e-params speed=5:low_latency=true output.mp4
</pre></dl>

<h3>libaom-av1</h3>

 libaom <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libaom headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libaom&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The wrapper supports the following standard libavcodec options:
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> Set bitrate target in bits/second. By default this will use variable-bitrate mode. If <b>maxrate</b> and <b>minrate</b> are also set to the same value then it will use constant-bitrate mode, otherwise if <b>crf</b> is set as well then it will use constrained-quality mode.
<dt><b>g keyint_min</b>
<dd> Set key frame placement. The <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size sets the maximum distance between key frames; if zero the output stream will be intra-only. The minimum distance is ignored unless it is the same as the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size, in which case key frames will always appear at a fixed interval. Not set by default, so without this option the library has completely free choice about where to place key frames.
<dt><b>qmin qmax</b>
<dd> Set minimum/maximum quantisation values. Valid range is from 0 to 63 (warning: this does not match the quantiser values actually used by <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> - divide by four to map real quantiser values to this range). Defaults to min/max (no constraint).
<dt><b>minrate maxrate bufsize rc_init_occupancy</b>
<dd> Set rate control buffering parameters. Not used if not set - defaults to unconstrained variable bitrate.
<dt><b>threads</b>
<dd> Set the number of threads to use while encoding. This may require the <b>tiles</b> or <b>row-mt</b> options to also be set to actually use the specified number of threads fully. Defaults to the number of hardware threads supported by the host machine.
<dt><b>profile</b>
<dd> Set the encoding profile. Defaults to using the profile which matches the bit depth and chroma subsampling of the input.</dl>
 

 The wrapper also has some specific options:
<dl>
<dt><b>cpu-used</b>
<dd> Set the quality/encoding speed tradeoff. Valid range is from 0 to 8, higher numbers indicating greater speed and lower quality. The default value is 1, which will be slow and high quality.
<dt><b>auto-alt-ref</b>
<dd> Enable use of alternate reference frames. Defaults to the internal default of the library.
<dt><b>arnr-max-frames (</b><i>frames</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set altref noise reduction max frame count. Default is -1.
<dt><b>arnr-strength (</b><i>strength</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set altref noise reduction filter strength. Range is -1 to 6. Default is -1.
<dt><b>aq-mode (</b><i>aq-mode</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set adaptive quantization mode. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Disabled.
<dt><b>variance (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Variance-based.
<dt><b>complexity (</b><i>2</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Complexity-based.
<dt><b>cyclic (</b><i>3</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Cyclic refresh.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>tune (</b><i>tune</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the distortion metric the encoder is tuned with. Default is <tt>&quot;psnr&quot;</tt>.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>psnr (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ssim (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>lag-in-frames</b>
<dd> Set the maximum number of frames which the encoder may keep in flight at any one time for lookahead purposes. Defaults to the internal default of the library.
<dt><b>error-resilience</b>
<dd> Enable error resilience features:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd> Improve resilience against losses of whole frames.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Not enabled by default.</dl>

<dt><b>crf</b>
<dd> Set the quality/size tradeoff for constant-quality (no bitrate target) and constrained-quality (with maximum bitrate target) modes. Valid range is 0 to 63, higher numbers indicating lower quality and smaller output size. Only used if set; by default only the bitrate target is used.
<dt><b>static-thresh</b>
<dd> Set a change threshold on blocks below which they will be skipped by the encoder. Defined in arbitrary units as a nonnegative integer, defaulting to zero (no blocks are skipped).
<dt><b>drop-threshold</b>
<dd> Set a threshold for dropping frames when close to rate control bounds. Defined as a percentage of the target buffer - when the rate control buffer falls below this percentage, frames will be dropped until it has refilled above the threshold. Defaults to zero (no frames are dropped).
<dt><b>denoise-noise-level (</b><i>level</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Amount of noise to be removed for grain synthesis. Grain synthesis is disabled if this option is not set or set to 0.
<dt><b>denoise-block-size (</b><i>pixels</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Block size used for denoising for grain synthesis. If not set, <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> codec uses the default value of 32.
<dt><b>undershoot-pct (</b><i>pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set datarate undershoot (min) percentage of the target bitrate. Range is -1 to 100. Default is -1.
<dt><b>overshoot-pct (</b><i>pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set datarate overshoot (max) percentage of the target bitrate. Range is -1 to 1000. Default is -1.
<dt><b>minsection-pct (</b><i>pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Minimum percentage variation of the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> bitrate from the target bitrate. If minsection-pct is not set, the libaomenc wrapper computes it as follows: <tt>&quot;(minrate * 100 / bitrate)&quot;</tt>. Range is -1 to 100. Default is -1 (unset).
<dt><b>maxsection-pct (</b><i>pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Maximum percentage variation of the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> bitrate from the target bitrate. If maxsection-pct is not set, the libaomenc wrapper computes it as follows: <tt>&quot;(maxrate * 100 / bitrate)&quot;</tt>. Range is -1 to 5000. Default is -1 (unset).
<dt><b>frame-parallel (</b><i>boolean</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable frame parallel decodability features. Default is true.
<dt><b>tiles</b>
<dd> Set the number of tiles to encode the input video with, as columns x rows. Larger numbers allow greater parallelism in both encoding and decoding, but may decrease coding efficiency. Defaults to the minimum number of tiles required by the size of the input video (this is 1x1 (that is, a single tile) for sizes up to and including 4K).
<dt><b>tile-columns tile-rows</b>
<dd> Set the number of tiles as log2 of the number of tile rows and columns. Provided for compatibility with libvpx/VP9.
<dt><b>row-mt (Requires libaom &gt;= 1.0.0-759-g90a15f4f2)</b>
<dd> Enable row based multi-threading. Disabled by default.
<dt><b>enable-cdef (</b><i>boolean</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable Constrained Directional Enhancement Filter. The libaom-av1 encoder enables <font SIZE="-1">CDEF</font> by default.
<dt><b>enable-restoration (</b><i>boolean</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable Loop Restoration Filter. Default is true for libaom-av1.
<dt><b>enable-global-motion (</b><i>boolean</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable the use of global motion for block prediction. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-intrabc (</b><i>boolean</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable block copy mode for intra block prediction. This mode is useful for screen content. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-rect-partitions (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable rectangular partitions. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-1to4-partitions (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable 1:4/4:1 partitions. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-ab-partitions (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable <font SIZE="-1">AB</font> shape partitions. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-angle-delta (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable angle delta intra prediction. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-cfl-intra (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable chroma predicted from luma intra prediction. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-filter-intra (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable filter intra predictor. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-intra-edge-filter (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable intra edge filter. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-smooth-intra (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable smooth intra prediction mode. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-paeth-intra (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable paeth predictor in intra prediction. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-palette (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable palette prediction mode. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-flip-idtx (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable extended transform type, including <font SIZE="-1">FLIPADST_DCT, DCT_FLIPADST, FLIPADST_FLIPADST, ADST_FLIPADST, FLIPADST_ADST, IDTX, V_DCT, H_DCT, V_ADST, H_ADST, V_FLIPADST, H_FLIPADST.</font> Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-tx64 (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable 64-pt transform. Default is true.
<dt><b>reduced-tx-type-set (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Use reduced set of transform types. Default is false.
<dt><b>use-intra-dct-only (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">DCT</font> only for <font SIZE="-1">INTRA</font> modes. Default is false.
<dt><b>use-inter-dct-only (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">DCT</font> only for <font SIZE="-1">INTER</font> modes. Default is false.
<dt><b>use-intra-default-tx-only (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Use Default-transform only for <font SIZE="-1">INTRA</font> modes. Default is false.
<dt><b>enable-ref-frame-mvs (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable temporal mv prediction. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-reduced-reference-set (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Use reduced set of single and compound references. Default is false.
<dt><b>enable-obmc (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable obmc. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-dual-filter (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable dual filter. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-diff-wtd-comp (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable difference-weighted compound. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-dist-wtd-comp (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable distance-weighted compound. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-onesided-comp (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable one sided compound. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-interinter-wedge (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable interinter wedge compound. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-interintra-wedge (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable interintra wedge compound. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-masked-comp (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable masked compound. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-interintra-comp (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable interintra compound. Default is true.
<dt><b>enable-smooth-interintra (</b><i>boolean</i><b>) (Requires libaom &gt;= v2.0.0)</b>
<dd> Enable smooth interintra mode. Default is true.
<dt><b>aom-params</b>
<dd> Set libaom options using a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> pairs separated by ``:''. For a list of supported options, see <b>aomenc --help</b> under the section ``<font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> Specific Options''. 

 For example to specify libaom encoding options with <b>-aom-params</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input -c:v libaom-av1 -b:v 500K -aom-params tune=psnr:enable-tpl-model=1 output.mp4
</pre></dl>

<h3>libsvtav1</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">SVT-AV1</font> encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the <font SIZE="-1">SVT-AV1</font> headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libsvtav1&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>profile</b>
<dd> Set the encoding profile.
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd> Set the operating point level.
<dt><b>tier</b>
<dd> Set the operating point tier.
<dt><b>rc</b>
<dd> Set the rate control mode to use. 

 Possible modes:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>cqp</b>
<dd> Constant quantizer: use fixed values of qindex (dependent on the frame type) throughout the stream. This mode is the default.
<dt><b>vbr</b>
<dd> Variable bitrate: use a target bitrate for the whole stream.
<dt><b>cvbr</b>
<dd> Constrained variable bitrate: use a target bitrate for each <font SIZE="-1">GOP.</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>qmax</b>
<dd> Set the maximum quantizer to use when using a bitrate mode.
<dt><b>qmin</b>
<dd> Set the minimum quantizer to use when using a bitrate mode.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd> Set the quantizer used in cqp rate control mode (0-63).
<dt><b>sc_detection</b>
<dd> Enable scene change detection.
<dt><b>la_depth</b>
<dd> Set number of frames to look ahead (0-120).
<dt><b>preset</b>
<dd> Set the quality-speed tradeoff, in the range 0 to 8. Higher values are faster but lower quality. Defaults to 8 (highest speed).
<dt><b>tile_rows</b>
<dd> Set log2 of the number of rows of tiles to use (0-6).
<dt><b>tile_columns</b>
<dd> Set log2 of the number of columns of tiles to use (0-4).</dl>

<h3>libkvazaar</h3>

 Kvazaar H.265/HEVC encoder. 

 Requires the presence of the libkvazaar headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <b>--enable-libkvazaar</b>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> Set target video bitrate in bit/s and enable rate control.
<dt><b>kvazaar-params</b>
<dd> Set kvazaar parameters as a list of <i>name</i>=<i>value</i> pairs separated by commas (,). See kvazaar documentation for a list of options.</dl>

<h3>libopenh264</h3>

 Cisco libopenh264 H.264/MPEG-4 <font SIZE="-1">AVC</font> encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libopenh264 headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libopenh264&quot;</tt>. The library is detected using <b>pkg-config</b>. 

 For more information about the library see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.openh264.org">http://www.openh264.org</a></b>&gt;. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following FFmpeg global options affect the configurations of the libopenh264 encoder.
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> Set the bitrate (as a number of bits per second).
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>maxrate</b>
<dd> Set the max bitrate (as a number of bits per second).
<dt><b>flags +global_header</b>
<dd> Set global header in the bitstream.
<dt><b>slices</b>
<dd> Set the number of slices, used in parallelized encoding. Default value is 0. This is only used when <b>slice_mode</b> is set to <b>fixed</b>.
<dt><b>slice_mode</b>
<dd> Set slice mode. Can assume one of the following possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>fixed</b>
<dd> a fixed number of slices
<dt><b>rowmb</b>
<dd> one slice per row of macroblocks
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> automatic number of slices according to number of threads
<dt><b>dyn</b>
<dd> dynamic slicing</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>auto</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>loopfilter</b>
<dd> Enable loop filter, if set to 1 (automatically enabled). To disable set a value of 0.
<dt><b>profile</b>
<dd> Set profile restrictions. If set to the value of <b>main</b> enable <font SIZE="-1">CABAC</font> (set the <tt>&quot;SEncParamExt.iEntropyCodingModeFlag&quot;</tt> flag to 1).
<dt><b>max_nal_size</b>
<dd> Set maximum <font SIZE="-1">NAL</font> size in bytes.
<dt><b>allow_skip_frames</b>
<dd> Allow skipping frames to hit the target bitrate if set to 1.</dl>

<h3>libtheora</h3>

 libtheora Theora encoder wrapper. 

 Requires the presence of the libtheora headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libtheora&quot;</tt>. 

 For more information about the libtheora project see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.theora.org/">http://www.theora.org/</a></b>&gt;. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following global options are mapped to internal libtheora options which affect the quality and the bitrate of the encoded stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> Set the video bitrate in bit/s for <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> (Constant Bit Rate) mode. In case <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> (Variable Bit Rate) mode is enabled this option is ignored.
<dt><b>flags</b>
<dd> Used to enable constant quality mode (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>) encoding through the <b>qscale</b> flag, and to enable the <tt>&quot;pass1&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;pass2&quot;</tt> modes.
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>global_quality</b>
<dd> Set the global quality as an integer in lambda units. 

 Only relevant when <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode is enabled with <tt>&quot;flags +qscale&quot;</tt>. The value is converted to <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> units by dividing it by <tt>&quot;FF_QP2LAMBDA&quot;</tt>, clipped in the [0 - 10] range, and then multiplied by 6.3 to get a value in the native libtheora range [0-63]. A higher value corresponds to a higher quality.
<dt><b>q</b>
<dd> Enable <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode when set to a non-negative value, and set constant quality value as a double floating point value in <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> units. 

 The value is clipped in the [0-10] range, and then multiplied by 6.3 to get a value in the native libtheora range [0-63]. 

 This option is valid only using the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. For library interface users, use <b>global_quality</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Set maximum constant quality (<font SIZE="-1">VBR</font>) encoding with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -codec:v libtheora -q:v 10 OUTPUT.ogg
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to convert a <font SIZE="-1">CBR 1000</font> kbps Theora video stream: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -codec:v libtheora -b:v 1000k OUTPUT.ogg
</pre></dl>

<h3>libvpx</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">VP8/VP9</font> format supported through libvpx. 

 Requires the presence of the libvpx headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libvpx&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libvpx wrapper. The <b>vpxenc</b>-equivalent options or values are listed in parentheses for easy migration. 

 To reduce the duplication of documentation, only the private options and some others requiring special attention are documented here. For the documentation of the undocumented generic options, see <b>the Codec Options chapter</b>. 

 To get more documentation of the libvpx options, invoke the command <b>ffmpeg -h encoder=libvpx</b>, <b>ffmpeg -h encoder=libvpx-vp9</b> or <b>vpxenc --help</b>. Further information is available in the libvpx <font SIZE="-1">API</font> documentation.
<dl>
<dt><b>b (</b><i>target-bitrate</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set bitrate in bits/s. Note that FFmpeg's <b>b</b> option is expressed in bits/s, while <b>vpxenc</b>'s <b>target-bitrate</b> is in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>g (</b><i>kf-max-dist</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>keyint_min (</b><i>kf-min-dist</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>qmin (</b><i>min-q</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>qmax (</b><i>max-q</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bufsize (</b><i>buf-sz</i><b>,</b> <i>buf-optimal-sz</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set ratecontrol buffer size (in bits). Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s options are specified in milliseconds, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;buf-sz = bufsize * 1000 / bitrate&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;buf-optimal-sz = bufsize * 1000 / bitrate * 5 / 6&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rc_init_occupancy (</b><i>buf-initial-sz</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set number of bits which should be loaded into the rc buffer before decoding starts. Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s option is specified in milliseconds, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;rc_init_occupancy * 1000 / bitrate&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>undershoot-pct</b>
<dd> Set datarate undershoot (min) percentage of the target bitrate.
<dt><b>overshoot-pct</b>
<dd> Set datarate overshoot (max) percentage of the target bitrate.
<dt><b>skip_threshold (</b><i>drop-frame</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>qcomp (</b><i>bias-pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>maxrate (</b><i>maxsection-pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> max bitrate in bits/s. Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s option is specified as a percentage of the target bitrate, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;(maxrate * 100 / bitrate)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>minrate (</b><i>minsection-pct</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> min bitrate in bits/s. Note <b>vpxenc</b>'s option is specified as a percentage of the target bitrate, the libvpx wrapper converts this value as follows: <tt>&quot;(minrate * 100 / bitrate)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>minrate, maxrate, b</b> <i>end-usage=cbr</i>
<dd> <tt>&quot;(minrate == maxrate == bitrate)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>crf (</b><i>end-usage=cq</i><b>,</b> <i>cq-level</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tune (</b><i>tune</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>psnr (</b><i>psnr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ssim (</b><i>ssim</i><b>)</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>quality, deadline (</b><i>deadline</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>best</b>
<dd> Use best quality deadline. Poorly named and quite slow, this option should be avoided as it may give worse quality output than good.
<dt><b>good</b>
<dd> Use good quality deadline. This is a good trade-off between speed and quality when used with the <b>cpu-used</b> option.
<dt><b>realtime</b>
<dd> Use realtime quality deadline.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>speed, cpu-used (</b><i>cpu-used</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set quality/speed ratio modifier. Higher values speed up the encode at the cost of quality.
<dt><b>nr (</b><i>noise-sensitivity</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>static-thresh</b>
<dd> Set a change threshold on blocks below which they will be skipped by the encoder.
<dt><b>slices (</b><i>token-parts</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Note that FFmpeg's <b>slices</b> option gives the total number of partitions, while <b>vpxenc</b>'s <b>token-parts</b> is given as <tt>&quot;log2(partitions)&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>max-intra-rate</b>
<dd> Set maximum I-frame bitrate as a percentage of the target bitrate. A value of 0 means unlimited.
<dt><b>force_key_frames</b>
<dd> <tt>&quot;VPX_EFLAG_FORCE_KF&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>Alternate reference frame related</b>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto-alt-ref</b>
<dd> Enable use of alternate reference frames (2-pass only). Values greater than 1 enable multi-layer alternate reference frames (<font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> only).
<dt><b>arnr-maxframes</b>
<dd> Set altref noise reduction max frame count.
<dt><b>arnr-type</b>
<dd> Set altref noise reduction filter type: backward, forward, centered.
<dt><b>arnr-strength</b>
<dd> Set altref noise reduction filter strength.
<dt><b>rc-lookahead, lag-in-frames (</b><i>lag-in-frames</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set number of frames to look ahead for frametype and ratecontrol.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>error-resilient</b>
<dd> Enable error resiliency features.
<dt><b>sharpness</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Increase sharpness at the expense of lower <font SIZE="-1">PSNR.</font> The valid range is [0, 7].
<dt><b>ts-parameters</b>
<dd> Sets the temporal scalability configuration using a :-separated list of key=value pairs. For example, to specify temporal scalability parameters with <tt>&quot;ffmpeg&quot;</tt>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v libvpx -ts-parameters ts_number_layers=3:\
        ts_target_bitrate=250,500,1000:ts_rate_decimator=4,2,1:\
        ts_periodicity=4:ts_layer_id=0,2,1,2:ts_layering_mode=3 OUTPUT
</pre> 

 Below is a brief explanation of each of the parameters, please refer to <tt>&quot;struct vpx_codec_enc_cfg&quot;</tt> in <tt>&quot;vpx/vpx_encoder.h&quot;</tt> for more details.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>ts_number_layers</b>
<dd> Number of temporal coding layers.
<dt><b>ts_target_bitrate</b>
<dd> Target bitrate for each temporal layer (in kbps). (bitrate should be inclusive of the lower temporal layer).
<dt><b>ts_rate_decimator</b>
<dd> Frame rate decimation factor for each temporal layer.
<dt><b>ts_periodicity</b>
<dd> Length of the sequence defining frame temporal layer membership.
<dt><b>ts_layer_id</b>
<dd> Template defining the membership of frames to temporal layers.
<dt><b>ts_layering_mode</b>
<dd> (optional) Selecting the temporal structure from a set of pre-defined temporal layering modes. Currently supports the following options.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd> No temporal layering flags are provided internally, relies on flags being passed in using <tt>&quot;metadata&quot;</tt> field in <tt>&quot;AVFrame&quot;</tt> with following keys.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>vp8-flags</b>
<dd> Sets the flags passed into the encoder to indicate the referencing scheme for the current frame. Refer to function <tt>&quot;vpx_codec_encode&quot;</tt> in <tt>&quot;vpx/vpx_encoder.h&quot;</tt> for more details.
<dt><b>temporal_id</b>
<dd> Explicitly sets the temporal id of the current frame to encode.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>2</b>
<dd> Two temporal layers. 0-1...
<dt><b>3</b>
<dd> Three temporal layers. 0-2-1-2...; with single reference frame.
<dt><b>4</b>
<dd> Same as option ``3'', except there is a dependency between the two temporal layer 2 frames within the temporal period.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>VP9-specific options</b>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lossless</b>
<dd> Enable lossless mode.
<dt><b>tile-columns</b>
<dd> Set number of tile columns to use. Note this is given as <tt>&quot;log2(tile_columns)&quot;</tt>. For example, 8 tile columns would be requested by setting the <b>tile-columns</b> option to 3.
<dt><b>tile-rows</b>
<dd> Set number of tile rows to use. Note this is given as <tt>&quot;log2(tile_rows)&quot;</tt>. For example, 4 tile rows would be requested by setting the <b>tile-rows</b> option to 2.
<dt><b>frame-parallel</b>
<dd> Enable frame parallel decodability features.
<dt><b>aq-mode</b>
<dd> Set adaptive quantization mode (0: off (default), 1: variance 2: complexity, 3: cyclic refresh, 4: equator360).
<dt><b>colorspace</b> <i>color-space</i>
<dd> Set input color space. The <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> bitstream supports signaling the following colorspaces:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rgb </b>sRGB
<dd>
<dt><b>bt709 </b>bt709
<dd>
<dt><b>unspecified </b>unknown
<dd>
<dt><b>bt470bg </b>bt601
<dd>
<dt><b>smpte170m </b>smpte170
<dd>
<dt><b>smpte240m </b>smpte240
<dd>
<dt><b>bt2020_ncl </b>bt2020
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>row-mt</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Enable row based multi-threading.
<dt><b>tune-content</b>
<dd> Set content type: default (0), screen (1), film (2).
<dt><b>corpus-complexity</b>
<dd> Corpus <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode is a variant of standard <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> where the complexity distribution midpoint is passed in rather than calculated for a specific clip or chunk. 

 The valid range is [0, 10000]. 0 (default) uses standard <font SIZE="-1">VBR.</font>
<dt><b>enable-tpl</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Enable temporal dependency model.
<dt><b>ref-frame-config</b>
<dd> Using per-frame metadata, set members of the structure <tt>&quot;vpx_svc_ref_frame_config_t&quot;</tt> in <tt>&quot;vpx/vp8cx.h&quot;</tt> to fine-control referencing schemes and frame buffer management. Use a :-separated list of key=value pairs. For example, 

 <pre>
        av_dict_set(&amp;av_frame-&gt;metadata, &quot;ref-frame-config&quot;, \
        &quot;rfc_update_buffer_slot=7:rfc_lst_fb_idx=0:rfc_gld_fb_idx=1:rfc_alt_fb_idx=2:rfc_reference_last=0:rfc_reference_golden=0:rfc_reference_alt_ref=0&quot;);
</pre>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rfc_update_buffer_slot</b>
<dd> Indicates the buffer slot number to update
<dt><b>rfc_update_last</b>
<dd> Indicates whether to update the <font SIZE="-1">LAST</font> frame
<dt><b>rfc_update_golden</b>
<dd> Indicates whether to update <font SIZE="-1">GOLDEN</font> frame
<dt><b>rfc_update_alt_ref</b>
<dd> Indicates whether to update <font SIZE="-1">ALT_REF</font> frame
<dt><b>rfc_lst_fb_idx</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">LAST</font> frame buffer index
<dt><b>rfc_gld_fb_idx</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">GOLDEN</font> frame buffer index
<dt><b>rfc_alt_fb_idx</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">ALT_REF</font> frame buffer index
<dt><b>rfc_reference_last</b>
<dd> Indicates whether to reference <font SIZE="-1">LAST</font> frame
<dt><b>rfc_reference_golden</b>
<dd> Indicates whether to reference <font SIZE="-1">GOLDEN</font> frame
<dt><b>rfc_reference_alt_ref</b>
<dd> Indicates whether to reference <font SIZE="-1">ALT_REF</font> frame
<dt><b>rfc_reference_duration</b>
<dd> Indicates frame duration</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 For more information about libvpx see: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.webmproject.org/">http://www.webmproject.org/</a></b>&gt;

<h3>libwebp</h3>

 libwebp WebP Image encoder wrapper 

 libwebp is Google's official encoder for WebP images. It can encode in either lossy or lossless mode. Lossy images are essentially a wrapper around a <font SIZE="-1">VP8</font> frame. Lossless images are a separate codec developed by Google. 

 <i>Pixel Format</i> 

 Currently, libwebp only supports <font SIZE="-1">YUV420</font> for lossy and <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> for lossless due to limitations of the format and libwebp. Alpha is supported for either mode. Because of <font SIZE="-1">API</font> limitations, if <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> is passed in when encoding lossy or <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> is passed in for encoding lossless, the pixel format will automatically be converted using functions from libwebp. This is not ideal and is done only for convenience. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>-lossless</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Enables/Disables use of lossless mode. Default is 0.
<dt><b>-compression_level</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> For lossy, this is a quality/speed tradeoff. Higher values give better quality for a given size at the cost of increased encoding time. For lossless, this is a size/speed tradeoff. Higher values give smaller size at the cost of increased encoding time. More specifically, it controls the number of extra algorithms and compression tools used, and varies the combination of these tools. This maps to the <i>method</i> option in libwebp. The valid range is 0 to 6. Default is 4.
<dt><b>-qscale</b> <i>float</i>
<dd> For lossy encoding, this controls image quality, 0 to 100. For lossless encoding, this controls the effort and time spent at compressing more. The default value is 75. Note that for usage via libavcodec, this option is called <i>global_quality</i> and must be multiplied by <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>FF_QP2LAMBDA</i></font><i></i>.
<dt><b>-preset</b> <i>type</i>
<dd> Configuration preset. This does some automatic settings based on the general type of the image.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Do not use a preset.
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd> Use the encoder default.
<dt><b>picture</b>
<dd> Digital picture, like portrait, inner shot
<dt><b>photo</b>
<dd> Outdoor photograph, with natural lighting
<dt><b>drawing</b>
<dd> Hand or line drawing, with high-contrast details
<dt><b>icon</b>
<dd> Small-sized colorful images
<dt><b>text</b>
<dd> Text-like</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>libx264, libx264rgb</h3>

 x264 H.264/MPEG-4 <font SIZE="-1">AVC</font> encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libx264 headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libx264&quot;</tt>. 

 libx264 supports an impressive number of features, including 8x8 and 4x4 adaptive spatial transform, adaptive B-frame placement, <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC/CABAC</font> entropy coding, interlacing (<font SIZE="-1">MBAFF</font>), lossless mode, psy optimizations for detail retention (adaptive quantization, psy-RD, psy-trellis). 

 Many libx264 encoder options are mapped to FFmpeg global codec options, while unique encoder options are provided through private options. Additionally the <b>x264opts</b> and <b>x264-params</b> private options allows one to pass a list of key=value tuples as accepted by the libx264 <tt>&quot;x264_param_parse&quot;</tt> function. 

 The x264 project website is at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html">http://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html</a></b>&gt;. 

 The libx264rgb encoder is the same as libx264, except it accepts packed <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> pixel formats as input instead of <font SIZE="-1">YUV.</font> 

 <i>Supported Pixel Formats</i> 

 x264 supports 8- to 10-bit color spaces. The exact bit depth is controlled at x264's configure time. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libx264 wrapper. The <b>x264</b>-equivalent options or values are listed in parentheses for easy migration. 

 To reduce the duplication of documentation, only the private options and some others requiring special attention are documented here. For the documentation of the undocumented generic options, see <b>the Codec Options chapter</b>. 

 To get a more accurate and extensive documentation of the libx264 options, invoke the command <b>x264 --fullhelp</b> or consult the libx264 documentation.
<dl>
<dt><b>b (</b><i>bitrate</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set bitrate in bits/s. Note that FFmpeg's <b>b</b> option is expressed in bits/s, while <b>x264</b>'s <b>bitrate</b> is in kilobits/s.
<dt><b>bf (</b><i>bframes</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>g (</b><i>keyint</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>qmin (</b><i>qpmin</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Minimum quantizer scale.
<dt><b>qmax (</b><i>qpmax</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Maximum quantizer scale.
<dt><b>qdiff (</b><i>qpstep</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Maximum difference between quantizer scales.
<dt><b>qblur (</b><i>qblur</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Quantizer curve blur
<dt><b>qcomp (</b><i>qcomp</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Quantizer curve compression factor
<dt><b>refs (</b><i>ref</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Number of reference frames each P-frame can use. The range is from <i>0-16</i>.
<dt><b>sc_threshold (</b><i>scenecut</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Sets the threshold for the scene change detection.
<dt><b>trellis (</b><i>trellis</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Performs Trellis quantization to increase efficiency. Enabled by default.
<dt><b>nr (</b><i>nr</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>me_range (</b><i>merange</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Maximum range of the motion search in pixels.
<dt><b>me_method (</b><i>me</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set motion estimation method. Possible values in the decreasing order of speed:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>dia (</b><i>dia</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>epzs (</b><i>dia</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Diamond search with radius 1 (fastest). <b>epzs</b> is an alias for <b>dia</b>.
<dt><b>hex (</b><i>hex</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Hexagonal search with radius 2.
<dt><b>umh (</b><i>umh</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Uneven multi-hexagon search.
<dt><b>esa (</b><i>esa</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Exhaustive search.
<dt><b>tesa (</b><i>tesa</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Hadamard exhaustive search (slowest).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>forced-idr</b>
<dd> Normally, when forcing a I-frame type, the encoder can select any type of I-frame. This option forces it to choose an IDR-frame.
<dt><b>subq (</b><i>subme</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Sub-pixel motion estimation method.
<dt><b>b_strategy (</b><i>b-adapt</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Adaptive B-frame placement decision algorithm. Use only on first-pass.
<dt><b>keyint_min (</b><i>min-keyint</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Minimum <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>coder</b>
<dd> Set entropy encoder. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>ac</b>
<dd> Enable <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font>
<dt><b>vlc</b>
<dd> Enable <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC</font> and disable <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font> It generates the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-cabac</b> option.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>cmp</b>
<dd> Set full pixel motion estimation comparison algorithm. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>chroma</b>
<dd> Enable chroma in motion estimation.
<dt><b>sad</b>
<dd> Ignore chroma in motion estimation. It generates the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-chroma-me</b> option.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>threads (</b><i>threads</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Number of encoding threads.
<dt><b>thread_type</b>
<dd> Set multithreading technique. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>slice</b>
<dd> Slice-based multithreading. It generates the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--sliced-threads</b> option.
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd> Frame-based multithreading.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>flags</b>
<dd> Set encoding flags. It can be used to disable closed <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> and enable open <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> by setting it to <tt>&quot;-cgop&quot;</tt>. The result is similar to the behavior of <b>x264</b>'s <b>--open-gop</b> option.
<dt><b>rc_init_occupancy (</b><i>vbv-init</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>preset (</b><i>preset</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the encoding preset.
<dt><b>tune (</b><i>tune</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set tuning of the encoding params.
<dt><b>profile (</b><i>profile</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set profile restrictions.
<dt><b>fastfirstpass</b>
<dd> Enable fast settings when encoding first pass, when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect of <b>x264</b>'s <b>--slow-firstpass</b> option.
<dt><b>crf (</b><i>crf</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the quality for constant quality mode.
<dt><b>crf_max (</b><i>crf-max</i><b>)</b>
<dd> In <font SIZE="-1">CRF</font> mode, prevents <font SIZE="-1">VBV</font> from lowering quality beyond this point.
<dt><b>qp (</b><i>qp</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set constant quantization rate control method parameter.
<dt><b>aq-mode (</b><i>aq-mode</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> method. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Disabled.
<dt><b>variance (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Variance <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> (complexity mask).
<dt><b>autovariance (</b><i>2</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Auto-variance <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> (experimental).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>aq-strength (</b><i>aq-strength</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">AQ</font> strength, reduce blocking and blurring in flat and textured areas.
<dt><b>psy</b>
<dd> Use psychovisual optimizations when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-psy</b> option.
<dt><b>psy-rd (</b><i>psy-rd</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set strength of psychovisual optimization, in <i>psy-rd</i>:<i>psy-trellis</i> format.
<dt><b>rc-lookahead (</b><i>rc-lookahead</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set number of frames to look ahead for frametype and ratecontrol.
<dt><b>weightb</b>
<dd> Enable weighted prediction for B-frames when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-weightb</b> option.
<dt><b>weightp (</b><i>weightp</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set weighted prediction method for P-frames. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none (</b><i>0</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Disabled
<dt><b>simple (</b><i>1</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable only weighted refs
<dt><b>smart (</b><i>2</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable both weighted refs and duplicates</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>ssim (</b><i>ssim</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable calculation and printing <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> stats after the encoding.
<dt><b>intra-refresh (</b><i>intra-refresh</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable the use of Periodic Intra Refresh instead of <font SIZE="-1">IDR</font> frames when set to 1.
<dt><b>avcintra-class (</b><i>class</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Configure the encoder to generate AVC-Intra. Valid values are 50,100 and 200
<dt><b>bluray-compat (</b><i>bluray-compat</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Configure the encoder to be compatible with the bluray standard. It is a shorthand for setting ``bluray-compat=1 force-cfr=1''.
<dt><b>b-bias (</b><i>b-bias</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the influence on how often B-frames are used.
<dt><b>b-pyramid (</b><i>b-pyramid</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set method for keeping of some B-frames as references. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Disabled.
<dt><b>strict (</b><i>strict</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Strictly hierarchical pyramid.
<dt><b>normal (</b><i>normal</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Non-strict (not Blu-ray compatible).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>mixed-refs</b>
<dd> Enable the use of one reference per partition, as opposed to one reference per macroblock when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-mixed-refs</b> option.
<dt><b>8x8dct</b>
<dd> Enable adaptive spatial transform (high profile 8x8 transform) when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-8x8dct</b> option.
<dt><b>fast-pskip</b>
<dd> Enable early <font SIZE="-1">SKIP</font> detection on P-frames when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-fast-pskip</b> option.
<dt><b>aud (</b><i>aud</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable use of access unit delimiters when set to 1.
<dt><b>mbtree</b>
<dd> Enable use macroblock tree ratecontrol when set to 1. When set to 0, it has the same effect as <b>x264</b>'s <b>--no-mbtree</b> option.
<dt><b>deblock (</b><i>deblock</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set loop filter parameters, in <i>alpha</i>:<i>beta</i> form.
<dt><b>cplxblur (</b><i>cplxblur</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set fluctuations reduction in <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> (before curve compression).
<dt><b>partitions (</b><i>partitions</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set partitions to consider as a comma-separated list of. Possible values in the list:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>p8x8</b>
<dd> 8x8 P-frame partition.
<dt><b>p4x4</b>
<dd> 4x4 P-frame partition.
<dt><b>b8x8</b>
<dd> 4x4 B-frame partition.
<dt><b>i8x8</b>
<dd> 8x8 I-frame partition.
<dt><b>i4x4</b>
<dd> 4x4 I-frame partition. (Enabling <b>p4x4</b> requires <b>p8x8</b> to be enabled. Enabling <b>i8x8</b> requires adaptive spatial transform (<b>8x8dct</b> option) to be enabled.)
<dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Do not consider any partitions.
<dt><b>all (</b><i>all</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Consider every partition.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>direct-pred (</b><i>direct</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set direct <font SIZE="-1">MV</font> prediction mode. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Disable <font SIZE="-1">MV</font> prediction.
<dt><b>spatial (</b><i>spatial</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable spatial predicting.
<dt><b>temporal (</b><i>temporal</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Enable temporal predicting.
<dt><b>auto (</b><i>auto</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Automatically decided.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>slice-max-size (</b><i>slice-max-size</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the limit of the size of each slice in bytes. If not specified but <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> payload size (<b>ps</b>) is specified, that is used.
<dt><b>stats (</b><i>stats</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the file name for multi-pass stats.
<dt><b>nal-hrd (</b><i>nal-hrd</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set signal <font SIZE="-1">HRD</font> information (requires <b>vbv-bufsize</b> to be set). Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none (</b><i>none</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Disable <font SIZE="-1">HRD</font> information signaling.
<dt><b>vbr (</b><i>vbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Variable bit rate.
<dt><b>cbr (</b><i>cbr</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Constant bit rate (not allowed in <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> container).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>x264opts (N.A.)</b>
<dd> Set any x264 option, see <b>x264 --fullhelp</b> for a list. 

 Argument is a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> couples separated by ``:''. In <i>filter</i> and <i>psy-rd</i> options that use ``:'' as a separator themselves, use ``,'' instead. They accept it as well since long ago but this is kept undocumented for some reason. 

 For example to specify libx264 encoding options with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i foo.mpg -c:v libx264 -x264opts keyint=123:min-keyint=20 -an out.mkv
</pre>
<dt><b>a53cc</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Import closed captions (which must be <font SIZE="-1">ATSC</font> compatible format) into output. Only the mpeg2 and h264 decoders provide these. Default is 1 (on).
<dt><b>x264-params (N.A.)</b>
<dd> Override the x264 configuration using a :-separated list of key=value parameters. 

 This option is functionally the same as the <b>x264opts</b>, but is duplicated for compatibility with the Libav fork. 

 For example to specify libx264 encoding options with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v libx264 -x264-params level=30:bframes=0:weightp=0:\
        cabac=0:ref=1:vbv-maxrate=768:vbv-bufsize=2000:analyse=all:me=umh:\
        no-fast-pskip=1:subq=6:8x8dct=0:trellis=0 OUTPUT
</pre></dl>
 

 Encoding ffpresets for common usages are provided so they can be used with the general presets system (e.g. passing the <b>pre</b> option).

<h3>libx265</h3>

 x265 H.265/HEVC encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libx265 headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <b>--enable-libx265</b>. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> Sets target video bitrate.
<dt><b>bf</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>keyint_min</b>
<dd> Minimum <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size.
<dt><b>refs</b>
<dd> Number of reference frames each P-frame can use. The range is from <i>1-16</i>.
<dt><b>preset</b>
<dd> Set the x265 preset.
<dt><b>tune</b>
<dd> Set the x265 tune parameter.
<dt><b>profile</b>
<dd> Set profile restrictions.
<dt><b>crf</b>
<dd> Set the quality for constant quality mode.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd> Set constant quantization rate control method parameter.
<dt><b>qmin</b>
<dd> Minimum quantizer scale.
<dt><b>qmax</b>
<dd> Maximum quantizer scale.
<dt><b>qdiff</b>
<dd> Maximum difference between quantizer scales.
<dt><b>qblur</b>
<dd> Quantizer curve blur
<dt><b>qcomp</b>
<dd> Quantizer curve compression factor
<dt><b>i_qfactor</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>b_qfactor</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>forced-idr</b>
<dd> Normally, when forcing a I-frame type, the encoder can select any type of I-frame. This option forces it to choose an IDR-frame.
<dt><b>x265-params</b>
<dd> Set x265 options using a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> couples separated by ``:''. See <b>x265 --help</b> for a list of options. 

 For example to specify libx265 encoding options with <b>-x265-params</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input -c:v libx265 -x265-params crf=26:psy-rd=1 output.mp4
</pre></dl>

<h3>libxavs2</h3>

 xavs2 <font SIZE="-1">AVS2-P2/IEEE1857.4</font> encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libxavs2 headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <b>--enable-libxavs2</b>. 

 The following standard libavcodec options are used:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>b</b> / <b>bit_rate</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>g</b> / <b>gop_size</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>bf</b> / <b>max_b_frames</b></dl>
 

 The encoder also has its own specific options: 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>lcu_row_threads</b>
<dd> Set the number of parallel threads for rows from 1 to 8 (default 5).
<dt><b>initial_qp</b>
<dd> Set the xavs2 quantization parameter from 1 to 63 (default 34). This is used to set the initial qp for the first frame.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd> Set the xavs2 quantization parameter from 1 to 63 (default 34). This is used to set the qp value under constant-QP mode.
<dt><b>max_qp</b>
<dd> Set the max qp for rate control from 1 to 63 (default 55).
<dt><b>min_qp</b>
<dd> Set the min qp for rate control from 1 to 63 (default 20).
<dt><b>speed_level</b>
<dd> Set the Speed level from 0 to 9 (default 0). Higher is better but slower.
<dt><b>log_level</b>
<dd> Set the log level from -1 to 3 (default 0). -1: none, 0: error, 1: warning, 2: info, 3: debug.
<dt><b>xavs2-params</b>
<dd> Set xavs2 options using a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> couples separated by ``:''. 

 For example to specify libxavs2 encoding options with <b>-xavs2-params</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input -c:v libxavs2 -xavs2-params RdoqLevel=0 output.avs2
</pre></dl>

<h3>libxvid</h3>

 Xvid <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> Part 2 encoder wrapper. 

 This encoder requires the presence of the libxvidcore headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with <tt>&quot;--enable-libxvid --enable-gpl&quot;</tt>. 

 The native <tt>&quot;mpeg4&quot;</tt> encoder supports the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> Part 2 format, so users can encode to this format without this library. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The following options are supported by the libxvid wrapper. Some of the following options are listed but are not documented, and correspond to shared codec options. See <b>the Codec Options chapter</b> for their documentation. The other shared options which are not listed have no effect for the libxvid encoder.
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>g</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>qmin</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>qmax</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>mpeg_quant</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>threads</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bf</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>b_qfactor</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>b_qoffset</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>flags</b>
<dd> Set specific encoding flags. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>mv4</b>
<dd> Use four motion vector by macroblock.
<dt><b>aic</b>
<dd> Enable high quality <font SIZE="-1">AC</font> prediction.
<dt><b>gray</b>
<dd> Only encode grayscale.
<dt><b>gmc</b>
<dd> Enable the use of global motion compensation (<font SIZE="-1">GMC</font>).
<dt><b>qpel</b>
<dd> Enable quarter-pixel motion compensation.
<dt><b>cgop</b>
<dd> Enable closed <font SIZE="-1">GOP.</font>
<dt><b>global_header</b>
<dd> Place global headers in extradata instead of every keyframe.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>trellis</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>me_method</b>
<dd> Set motion estimation method. Possible values in decreasing order of speed and increasing order of quality:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>zero</b>
<dd> Use no motion estimation (default).
<dt><b>phods</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>x1</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> Enable advanced diamond zonal search for 16x16 blocks and half-pixel refinement for 16x16 blocks. <b>x1</b> and <b>log</b> are aliases for <b>phods</b>.
<dt><b>epzs</b>
<dd> Enable all of the things described above, plus advanced diamond zonal search for 8x8 blocks, half-pixel refinement for 8x8 blocks, and motion estimation on chroma planes.
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd> Enable all of the things described above, plus extended 16x16 and 8x8 blocks search.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>mbd</b>
<dd> Set macroblock decision algorithm. Possible values in the increasing order of quality:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>simple</b>
<dd> Use macroblock comparing function algorithm (default).
<dt><b>bits</b>
<dd> Enable rate distortion-based half pixel and quarter pixel refinement for 16x16 blocks.
<dt><b>rd</b>
<dd> Enable all of the things described above, plus rate distortion-based half pixel and quarter pixel refinement for 8x8 blocks, and rate distortion-based search using square pattern.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>lumi_aq</b>
<dd> Enable lumi masking adaptive quantization when set to 1. Default is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>variance_aq</b>
<dd> Enable variance adaptive quantization when set to 1. Default is 0 (disabled). 

 When combined with <b>lumi_aq</b>, the resulting quality will not be better than any of the two specified individually. In other words, the resulting quality will be the worse one of the two effects.
<dt><b>ssim</b>
<dd> Set structural similarity (<font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font>) displaying method. Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>off</b>
<dd> Disable displaying of <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> information.
<dt><b>avg</b>
<dd> Output average <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> at the end of encoding to stdout. The format of showing the average <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> is: 

 <pre>
        Average SSIM: %f
</pre> 

 For users who are not familiar with C, <tt>%f</tt> means a float number, or a decimal (e.g. 0.939232).
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd> Output both per-frame <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> data during encoding and average <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> at the end of encoding to stdout. The format of per-frame information is: 

 <pre>
               SSIM: avg: %1.3f min: %1.3f max: %1.3f
</pre> 

 For users who are not familiar with C, <tt>%1</tt>.3f means a float number rounded to 3 digits after the dot (e.g. 0.932).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>ssim_acc</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> accuracy. Valid options are integers within the range of 0-4, while 0 gives the most accurate result and 4 computes the fastest.</dl>

<h3>MediaFoundation</h3>

 This provides wrappers to encoders (both audio and video) in the MediaFoundation framework. It can access both <font SIZE="-1">SW</font> and <font SIZE="-1">HW</font> encoders. Video encoders can take input in either of nv12 or yuv420p form (some encoders support both, some support only either - in practice, nv12 is the safer choice, especially among <font SIZE="-1">HW</font> encoders).

<h3>mpeg2</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> video encoder.

</dl>

<dl>

<dd> Select the mpeg2 level to encode:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>high</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>high1440</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>main</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>low</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>

<dt><b>seq_disp_ext</b> <i>integer</i>

<dl>

<dt><b>video_format</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Specifies the video_format written into the sequence display extension indicating the source of the video pictures. The default is <b>unspecified</b>, can be <b>component</b>, <b>pal</b>, <b>ntsc</b>, <b>secam</b> or <b>mac</b>. For maximum compatibility, use <b>component</b>.
<dt><b>a53cc</b> <i>boolean</i>

 <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> image encoder.

<h3>ProRes</h3>

 Apple ProRes encoder. 

 FFmpeg contains 2 ProRes encoders, the prores-aw and prores-ks encoder. The used encoder can be chosen with the <tt>&quot;-vcodec&quot;</tt> option. 

 <i>Private Options for prores-ks</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>profile</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Select the ProRes profile to encode
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>proxy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lt</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>standard</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hq</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>4444</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>4444xq</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>quant_mat</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Select quantization matrix.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>default</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>proxy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lt</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>standard</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hq</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 If set to <i>auto</i>, the matrix matching the profile will be picked. If not set, the matrix providing the highest quality, <i>default</i>, will be picked.</dl>

<dt><b>bits_per_mb</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> How many bits to allot for coding one macroblock. Different profiles use between 200 and 2400 bits per macroblock, the maximum is 8000.
<dt><b>mbs_per_slice</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Number of macroblocks in each slice (1-8); the default value (8) should be good in almost all situations.
<dt><b>vendor</b> <i>string</i>
<dd> Override the 4-byte vendor <font SIZE="-1">ID. A</font> custom vendor <font SIZE="-1">ID</font> like <i>apl0</i> would claim the stream was produced by the Apple encoder.
<dt><b>alpha_bits</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Specify number of bits for alpha component. Possible values are <i>0</i>, <i>8</i> and <i>16</i>. Use <i>0</i> to disable alpha plane coding.</dl>
 

 <i>Speed considerations</i> 

 In the default mode of operation the encoder has to honor frame constraints (i.e. not produce frames with size bigger than requested) while still making output picture as good as possible. A frame containing a lot of small details is harder to compress and the encoder would spend more time searching for appropriate quantizers for each slice. 

 Setting a higher <b>bits_per_mb</b> limit will improve the speed. 

 For the fastest encoding speed set the <b>qscale</b> parameter (4 is the recommended value) and do not set a size constraint.

<h3><font SIZE="-1">QSV</font> encoders</h3>

 The family of Intel QuickSync Video encoders (<font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2, H.264, HEVC, JPEG/MJPEG</font> and <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font>) 

 The ratecontrol method is selected as follows:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> When <b>global_quality</b> is specified, a quality-based mode is used. Specifically this means either
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CQP</i></font><i></i> - constant quantizer scale, when the <b>qscale</b> codec flag is also set (the <b>-qscale</b> ffmpeg option).
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>LA_ICQ</i></font><i></i> - intelligent constant quality with lookahead, when the <b>look_ahead</b> option is also set.
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>ICQ</i></font><i></i> --- intelligent constant quality otherwise.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Otherwise, a bitrate-based mode is used. For all of those, you should specify at least the desired average bitrate with the <b>b</b> option.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>LA</i></font><i></i> - <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> with lookahead, when the <b>look_ahead</b> option is specified.
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>VCM</i></font><i></i> - video conferencing mode, when the <b>vcm</b> option is set.
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CBR</i></font><i></i> - constant bitrate, when <b>maxrate</b> is specified and equal to the average bitrate.
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>VBR</i></font><i></i> - variable bitrate, when <b>maxrate</b> is specified, but is higher than the average bitrate.
<dt>-
<dd> <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AVBR</i></font><i></i> - average <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> mode, when <b>maxrate</b> is not specified. This mode is further configured by the <b>avbr_accuracy</b> and <b>avbr_convergence</b> options.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 Note that depending on your system, a different mode than the one you specified may be selected by the encoder. Set the verbosity level to <i>verbose</i> or higher to see the actual settings used by the <font SIZE="-1">QSV</font> runtime. 

 Additional libavcodec global options are mapped to <font SIZE="-1">MSDK</font> options as follows:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>g/gop_size</b> -&gt; <b>GopPicSize</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>bf/max_b_frames</b>+1 -&gt; <b>GopRefDist</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>rc_init_occupancy/rc_initial_buffer_occupancy</b> -&gt; <b>InitialDelayInKB</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>slices</b> -&gt; <b>NumSlice</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>refs</b> -&gt; <b>NumRefFrame</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>b_strategy/b_frame_strategy</b> -&gt; <b>BRefType</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>cgop/CLOSED_GOP</b> codec flag -&gt; <b>GopOptFlag</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> For the <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CQP</i></font><i></i> mode, the <b>i_qfactor/i_qoffset</b> and <b>b_qfactor/b_qoffset</b> set the difference between <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPP</i></font><i></i> and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPI</i></font><i></i>, and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPP</i></font><i></i> and <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>QPB</i></font><i></i> respectively.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Setting the <b>coder</b> option to the value <i>vlc</i> will make the H.264 encoder use <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC</font> instead of <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font></dl>

<h3>snow</h3>

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>iterative_dia_size</b>
<dd> dia size for the iterative motion estimation</dl>

<h3><font SIZE="-1">VAAPI</font> encoders</h3>

 Wrappers for hardware encoders accessible via <font SIZE="-1">VAAPI.</font> 

 These encoders only accept input in <font SIZE="-1">VAAPI</font> hardware surfaces. If you have input in software frames, use the <b>hwupload</b> filter to upload them to the <font SIZE="-1">GPU.</font> 

 The following standard libavcodec options are used:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>g</b> / <b>gop_size</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>bf</b> / <b>max_b_frames</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>profile</b> 

 If not set, this will be determined automatically from the format of the input frames and the profiles supported by the driver.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>level</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>b</b> / <b>bit_rate</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>maxrate</b> / <b>rc_max_rate</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>bufsize</b> / <b>rc_buffer_size</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>rc_init_occupancy</b> / <b>rc_initial_buffer_occupancy</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>compression_level</b> 

 Speed / quality tradeoff: higher values are faster / worse quality.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>q</b> / <b>global_quality</b> 

 Size / quality tradeoff: higher values are smaller / worse quality.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>qmin</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>qmax</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>i_qfactor</b> / <b>i_quant_factor</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>i_qoffset</b> / <b>i_quant_offset</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>b_qfactor</b> / <b>b_quant_factor</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>b_qoffset</b> / <b>b_quant_offset</b>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <b>slices</b></dl>
 

 All encoders support the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>low_power</b>
<dd> Some drivers/platforms offer a second encoder for some codecs intended to use less power than the default encoder; setting this option will attempt to use that encoder. Note that it may support a reduced feature set, so some other options may not be available in this mode.
<dt><b>idr_interval</b>
<dd> Set the number of normal intra frames between full-refresh (<font SIZE="-1">IDR</font>) frames in open-GOP mode. The intra frames are still IRAPs, but will not include global headers and may have non-decodable leading pictures.
<dt><b>b_depth</b>
<dd> Set the B-frame reference depth. When set to one (the default), all B-frames will refer only to P- or I-frames. When set to greater values multiple layers of B-frames will be present, frames in each layer only referring to frames in higher layers.
<dt><b>rc_mode</b>
<dd> Set the rate control mode to use. A given driver may only support a subset of modes. 

 Possible modes:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> Choose the mode automatically based on driver support and the other options. This is the default.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>CQP</b></font>
<dd> Constant-quality.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>CBR</b></font>
<dd> Constant-bitrate.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VBR</b></font>
<dd> Variable-bitrate.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ICQ</b></font>
<dd> Intelligent constant-quality.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>QVBR</b></font>
<dd> Quality-defined variable-bitrate.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>AVBR</b></font>
<dd> Average variable bitrate.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 Each encoder also has its own specific options:
<dl>
<dt><b>h264_vaapi</b>
<dd> <b>profile</b> sets the value of <i>profile_idc</i> and the <i>constraint_set*_flag</i>s. <b>level</b> sets the value of <i>level_idc</i>.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>coder</b>
<dd> Set entropy encoder (default is <i>cabac</i>). Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>ac</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cabac</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font>
<dt><b>vlc</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cavlc</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">CAVLC.</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>aud</b>
<dd> Include access unit delimiters in the stream (not included by default).
<dt><b>sei</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">SEI</font> message types to include. Some combination of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>identifier</b>
<dd> Include a <i>user_data_unregistered</i> message containing information about the encoder.
<dt><b>timing</b>
<dd> Include picture timing parameters (<i>buffering_period</i> and <i>pic_timing</i> messages).
<dt><b>recovery_point</b>
<dd> Include recovery points where appropriate (<i>recovery_point</i> messages).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>hevc_vaapi</b>
<dd> <b>profile</b> and <b>level</b> set the values of <i>general_profile_idc</i> and <i>general_level_idc</i> respectively.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>aud</b>
<dd> Include access unit delimiters in the stream (not included by default).
<dt><b>tier</b>
<dd> Set <i>general_tier_flag</i>. This may affect the level chosen for the stream if it is not explicitly specified.
<dt><b>sei</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">SEI</font> message types to include. Some combination of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>hdr</b>
<dd> Include <font SIZE="-1">HDR</font> metadata if the input frames have it (<i>mastering_display_colour_volume</i> and <i>content_light_level</i> messages).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>tiles</b>
<dd> Set the number of tiles to encode the input video with, as columns x rows. Larger numbers allow greater parallelism in both encoding and decoding, but may decrease coding efficiency.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>mjpeg_vaapi</b>
<dd> Only baseline <font SIZE="-1">DCT</font> encoding is supported. The encoder always uses the standard quantisation and huffman tables - <b>global_quality</b> scales the standard quantisation table (range 1-100). 

 For <font SIZE="-1">YUV, 4:2:0, 4:2:2</font> and 4:4:4 subsampling modes are supported. <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> is also supported, and will create an <font SIZE="-1">RGB JPEG.</font>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>jfif</b>
<dd> Include <font SIZE="-1">JFIF</font> header in each frame (not included by default).
<dt><b>huffman</b>
<dd> Include standard huffman tables (on by default). Turning this off will save a few hundred bytes in each output frame, but may lose compatibility with some <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> decoders which don't fully handle <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG.</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>mpeg2_vaapi</b>
<dd> <b>profile</b> and <b>level</b> set the value of <i>profile_and_level_indication</i>.
<dt><b>vp8_vaapi</b>
<dd> B-frames are not supported. 

 <b>global_quality</b> sets the <i>q_idx</i> used for non-key frames (range 0-127).
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>loop_filter_level</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>loop_filter_sharpness</b>
<dd> Manually set the loop filter parameters.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>vp9_vaapi</b>
<dd> <b>global_quality</b> sets the <i>q_idx</i> used for P-frames (range 0-255).
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>loop_filter_level</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>loop_filter_sharpness</b>
<dd> Manually set the loop filter parameters.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 B-frames are supported, but the output stream is always in encode order rather than display order. If B-frames are enabled, it may be necessary to use the <b>vp9_raw_reorder</b> bitstream filter to modify the output stream to display frames in the correct order. 

 Only normal frames are produced - the <b>vp9_superframe</b> bitstream filter may be required to produce a stream usable with all decoders.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>vc2</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE VC-2</font> (previously <font SIZE="-1">BBC</font> Dirac Pro). This codec was primarily aimed at professional broadcasting but since it supports yuv420, yuv422 and yuv444 at 8 (limited range or full range), 10 or 12 bits, this makes it suitable for other tasks which require low overhead and low compression (like screen recording). 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> Sets target video bitrate. Usually that's around 1:6 of the uncompressed video bitrate (e.g. for 1920x1080 50fps yuv422p10 that's around 400Mbps). Higher values (close to the uncompressed bitrate) turn on lossless compression mode.
<dt><b>field_order</b>
<dd> Enables field coding when set (e.g. to tt - top field first) for interlaced inputs. Should increase compression with interlaced content as it splits the fields and encodes each separately.
<dt><b>wavelet_depth</b>
<dd> Sets the total amount of wavelet transforms to apply, between 1 and 5 (default). Lower values reduce compression and quality. Less capable decoders may not be able to handle values of <b>wavelet_depth</b> over 3.
<dt><b>wavelet_type</b>
<dd> Sets the transform type. Currently only <i>5_3</i> (LeGall) and <i>9_7</i> (Deslauriers-Dubuc) are implemented, with 9_7 being the one with better compression and thus is the default.
<dt><b>slice_width</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>slice_height</b>
<dd> Sets the slice size for each slice. Larger values result in better compression. For compatibility with other more limited decoders use <b>slice_width</b> of 32 and <b>slice_height</b> of 8.
<dt><b>tolerance</b>
<dd> Sets the undershoot tolerance of the rate control system in percent. This is to prevent an expensive search from being run.
<dt><b>qm</b>
<dd> Sets the quantization matrix preset to use by default or when <b>wavelet_depth</b> is set to 5
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>-
<dd> <i>default</i> Uses the default quantization matrix from the specifications, extended with values for the fifth level. This provides a good balance between keeping detail and omitting artifacts.
<dt>-
<dd> <i>flat</i> Use a completely zeroed out quantization matrix. This increases <font SIZE="-1">PSNR</font> but might reduce perception. Use in bogus benchmarks.
<dt>-
<dd> <i>color</i> Reduces detail but attempts to preserve color at extremely low bitrates.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h2>SUBTITLES ENCODERS</h2>

<h3>dvdsub</h3>

 This codec encodes the bitmap subtitle format that is used in DVDs. Typically they are stored in <font SIZE="-1">VOBSUB</font> file pairs (*.idx + *.sub), and they can also be used in Matroska files. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>palette</b>
<dd> Specify the global palette used by the bitmaps. 

 The format for this option is a string containing 16 24-bits hexadecimal numbers (without 0x prefix) separated by commas, for example <tt>&quot;0d00ee, ee450d, 101010, eaeaea, 0ce60b, ec14ed, ebff0b, 0d617a, 7b7b7b, d1d1d1, 7b2a0e, 0d950c, 0f007b, cf0dec, cfa80c, 7c127b&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>even_rows_fix</b>
<dd> When set to 1, enable a work-around that makes the number of pixel rows even in all subtitles. This fixes a problem with some players that cut off the bottom row if the number is odd. The work-around just adds a fully transparent row if needed. The overhead is low, typically one byte per subtitle on average. 

 By default, this work-around is disabled.</dl>

<h2>BITSTREAM FILTERS</h2>

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported bitstream filters are enabled by default. You can list all available ones using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-bsfs&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the bitstream filters using the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-bsfs&quot;</tt>, and selectively enable any bitstream filter using the option <tt>&quot;--enable-bsf=BSF&quot;</tt>, or you can disable a particular bitstream filter using the option <tt>&quot;--disable-bsf=BSF&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-bsfs&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of all the supported bitstream filters included in your build. 

 The ff* tools have a -bsf option applied per stream, taking a comma-separated list of filters, whose parameters follow the filter name after a '='.
