ffmpeg - i INPUT - c : v copy - bsf : v filter1 [= opt1 = str1:opt2 = str2][, filter2] OUTPUT
 

 Below is a description of the currently available bitstream filters, with their parameters, if any.

<h3>aac_adtstoasc</h3>

 Convert <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2/4 AAC ADTS</font> to an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> Audio Specific Configuration bitstream. 

 This filter creates an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> AudioSpecificConfig from an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2/4 ADTS</font> header and removes the <font SIZE="-1">ADTS</font> header. 

 This filter is required for example when copying an <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> stream from a raw <font SIZE="-1">ADTS AAC</font> or an MPEG-TS container to <font SIZE="-1">MP4A-LATM,</font> to an <font SIZE="-1">FLV</font> file, or to <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> files and related formats such as 3GP or M4A. Please note that it is auto-inserted for <font SIZE="-1">MP4A-LATM</font> and <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> and related formats.

<h3>av1_metadata</h3>

 Modify metadata embedded in an <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>td</b>
<dd> Insert or remove temporal delimiter OBUs in all temporal units of the stream.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>insert</b>
<dd> Insert a <font SIZE="-1">TD</font> at the beginning of every <font SIZE="-1">TU</font> which does not already have one.
<dt><b>remove</b>
<dd> Remove the <font SIZE="-1">TD</font> from the beginning of every <font SIZE="-1">TU</font> which has one.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>color_primaries</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>transfer_characteristics</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>matrix_coefficients</b>
<dd> Set the color description fields in the stream (see <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> section 6.4.2).
<dt><b>color_range</b>
<dd> Set the color range in the stream (see <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> section 6.4.2; note that this cannot be set for streams using <font SIZE="-1">BT.709</font> primaries, sRGB transfer characteristic and identity (<font SIZE="-1">RGB</font>) matrix coefficients).
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>tv</b>
<dd> Limited range.
<dt><b>pc</b>
<dd> Full range.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>chroma_sample_position</b>
<dd> Set the chroma sample location in the stream (see <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> section 6.4.2). This can only be set for 4:2:0 streams.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>vertical</b>
<dd> Left position (matching the default in <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> and H.264).
<dt><b>colocated</b>
<dd> Top-left position.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>tick_rate</b>
<dd> Set the tick rate (<i>num_units_in_display_tick / time_scale</i>) in the timing info in the sequence header.
<dt><b>num_ticks_per_picture</b>
<dd> Set the number of ticks in each picture, to indicate that the stream has a fixed framerate. Ignored if <b>tick_rate</b> is not also set.
<dt><b>delete_padding</b>
<dd> Deletes Padding OBUs.</dl>

<h3>chomp</h3>

 Remove zero padding at the end of a packet.

<h3>dca_core</h3>

 Extract the core from a <font SIZE="-1">DCA/DTS</font> stream, dropping extensions such as DTS-HD.

<h3>dump_extra</h3>

 Add extradata to the beginning of the filtered packets except when said packets already exactly begin with the extradata that is intended to be added.
<dl>
<dt><b>freq</b>
<dd> The additional argument specifies which packets should be filtered. It accepts the values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>k</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>keyframe</b>
<dd> add extradata to all key packets
<dt><b>e</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>all</b>
<dd> add extradata to all packets</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 If not specified it is assumed <b>k</b>. 

 For example the following <b>ffmpeg</b> command forces a global header (thus disabling individual packet headers) in the H.264 packets generated by the <tt>&quot;libx264&quot;</tt> encoder, but corrects them by adding the header stored in extradata to the key packets: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -map 0 -flags:v +global_header -c:v libx264 -bsf:v dump_extra out.ts
</pre>

<h3>eac3_core</h3>

 Extract the core from a E-AC-3 stream, dropping extra channels.

<h3>extract_extradata</h3>

 Extract the in-band extradata. 

 Certain codecs allow the long-term headers (e.g. <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> sequence headers, or H.264/HEVC (<font SIZE="-1">VPS/</font>)SPS/PPS) to be transmitted either ``in-band'' (i.e. as a part of the bitstream containing the coded frames) or ``out of band'' (e.g. on the container level). This latter form is called ``extradata'' in FFmpeg terminology. 

 This bitstream filter detects the in-band headers and makes them available as extradata.
<dl>
<dt><b>remove</b>
<dd> When this option is enabled, the long-term headers are removed from the bitstream after extraction.</dl>

<h3>filter_units</h3>

 Remove units with types in or not in a given set from the stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>pass_types</b>
<dd> List of unit types or ranges of unit types to pass through while removing all others. This is specified as a '|'-separated list of unit type values or ranges of values with '-'.
<dt><b>remove_types</b>
<dd> Identical to <b>pass_types</b>, except the units in the given set removed and all others passed through.</dl>
 

 Extradata is unchanged by this transformation, but note that if the stream contains inline parameter sets then the output may be unusable if they are removed. 

 For example, to remove all non-VCL <font SIZE="-1">NAL</font> units from an H.264 stream: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v copy -bsf:v 'filter_units=pass_types=1-5' OUTPUT
</pre> 

 To remove all AUDs, <font SIZE="-1">SEI</font> and filler from an H.265 stream: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v copy -bsf:v 'filter_units=remove_types=35|38-40' OUTPUT
</pre>

<h3>hapqa_extract</h3>

 Extract Rgb or Alpha part of an <font SIZE="-1">HAPQA</font> file, without recompression, in order to create an <font SIZE="-1">HAPQ</font> or an HAPAlphaOnly file.
<dl>
<dt><b>texture</b>
<dd> Specifies the texture to keep.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>alpha</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 Convert <font SIZE="-1">HAPQA</font> to <font SIZE="-1">HAPQ</font> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i hapqa_inputfile.mov -c copy -bsf:v hapqa_extract=texture=color -tag:v HapY -metadata:s:v:0 encoder=&quot;HAPQ&quot; hapq_file.mov
</pre> 

 Convert <font SIZE="-1">HAPQA</font> to HAPAlphaOnly 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i hapqa_inputfile.mov -c copy -bsf:v hapqa_extract=texture=alpha -tag:v HapA -metadata:s:v:0 encoder=&quot;HAPAlpha Only&quot; hapalphaonly_file.mov
</pre>

<h3>h264_metadata</h3>

 Modify metadata embedded in an H.264 stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>aud</b>
<dd> Insert or remove <font SIZE="-1">AUD NAL</font> units in all access units of the stream.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>insert</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>remove</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>sample_aspect_ratio</b>
<dd> Set the sample aspect ratio of the stream in the <font SIZE="-1">VUI</font> parameters.
<dt><b>overscan_appropriate_flag</b>
<dd> Set whether the stream is suitable for display using overscan or not (see H.264 section E.2.1).
<dt><b>video_format</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>video_full_range_flag</b>
<dd> Set the video format in the stream (see H.264 section E.2.1 and table E-2).
<dt><b>colour_primaries</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>transfer_characteristics</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>matrix_coefficients</b>
<dd> Set the colour description in the stream (see H.264 section E.2.1 and tables E-3, E-4 and E-5).
<dt><b>chroma_sample_loc_type</b>
<dd> Set the chroma sample location in the stream (see H.264 section E.2.1 and figure E-1).
<dt><b>tick_rate</b>
<dd> Set the tick rate (num_units_in_tick / time_scale) in the <font SIZE="-1">VUI</font> parameters. This is the smallest time unit representable in the stream, and in many cases represents the field rate of the stream (double the frame rate).
<dt><b>fixed_frame_rate_flag</b>
<dd> Set whether the stream has fixed framerate - typically this indicates that the framerate is exactly half the tick rate, but the exact meaning is dependent on interlacing and the picture structure (see H.264 section E.2.1 and table E-6).
<dt><b>crop_left</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>crop_right</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>crop_top</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>crop_bottom</b>
<dd> Set the frame cropping offsets in the <font SIZE="-1">SPS.</font> These values will replace the current ones if the stream is already cropped. 

 These fields are set in pixels. Note that some sizes may not be representable if the chroma is subsampled or the stream is interlaced (see H.264 section 7.4.2.1.1).
<dt><b>sei_user_data</b>
<dd> Insert a string as <font SIZE="-1">SEI</font> unregistered user data. The argument must be of the form <i>UUID+string</i>, where the <font SIZE="-1">UUID</font> is as hex digits possibly separated by hyphens, and the string can be anything. 

 For example, <b>086f3693-b7b3-4f2c-9653-21492feee5b8+hello</b> will insert the string ``hello'' associated with the given <font SIZE="-1">UUID.</font>
<dt><b>delete_filler</b>
<dd> Deletes both filler <font SIZE="-1">NAL</font> units and filler <font SIZE="-1">SEI</font> messages.
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd> Set the level in the <font SIZE="-1">SPS.</font> Refer to H.264 section A.3 and tables A-1 to A-5. 

 The argument must be the name of a level (for example, <b>4.2</b>), a level_idc value (for example, <b>42</b>), or the special name <b>auto</b> indicating that the filter should attempt to guess the level from the input stream properties.</dl>

<h3>h264_mp4toannexb</h3>

 Convert an H.264 bitstream from length prefixed mode to start code prefixed mode (as defined in the Annex B of the ITU-T H.264 specification). 

 This is required by some streaming formats, typically the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> transport stream format (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>). 

 For example to remux an <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> file containing an H.264 stream to mpegts format with <b>ffmpeg</b>, you can use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT.mp4 -codec copy -bsf:v h264_mp4toannexb OUTPUT.ts
</pre> 

 Please note that this filter is auto-inserted for MPEG-TS (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>) and raw H.264 (muxer <tt>&quot;h264&quot;</tt>) output formats.

<h3>h264_redundant_pps</h3>

 This applies a specific fixup to some Blu-ray streams which contain redundant PPSs modifying irrelevant parameters of the stream which confuse other transformations which require correct extradata. 

 A new single global <font SIZE="-1">PPS</font> is created, and all of the redundant PPSs within the stream are removed.

<h3>hevc_metadata</h3>

 Modify metadata embedded in an <font SIZE="-1">HEVC</font> stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>aud</b>
<dd> Insert or remove <font SIZE="-1">AUD NAL</font> units in all access units of the stream.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>insert</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>remove</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>sample_aspect_ratio</b>
<dd> Set the sample aspect ratio in the stream in the <font SIZE="-1">VUI</font> parameters.
<dt><b>video_format</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>video_full_range_flag</b>
<dd> Set the video format in the stream (see H.265 section E.3.1 and table E.2).
<dt><b>colour_primaries</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>transfer_characteristics</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>matrix_coefficients</b>
<dd> Set the colour description in the stream (see H.265 section E.3.1 and tables E.3, E.4 and E.5).
<dt><b>chroma_sample_loc_type</b>
<dd> Set the chroma sample location in the stream (see H.265 section E.3.1 and figure E.1).
<dt><b>tick_rate</b>
<dd> Set the tick rate in the <font SIZE="-1">VPS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">VUI</font> parameters (num_units_in_tick / time_scale). Combined with <b>num_ticks_poc_diff_one</b>, this can set a constant framerate in the stream. Note that it is likely to be overridden by container parameters when the stream is in a container.
<dt><b>num_ticks_poc_diff_one</b>
<dd> Set poc_proportional_to_timing_flag in <font SIZE="-1">VPS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">VUI</font> and use this value to set num_ticks_poc_diff_one_minus1 (see H.265 sections 7.4.3.1 and E.3.1). Ignored if <b>tick_rate</b> is not also set.
<dt><b>crop_left</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>crop_right</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>crop_top</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>crop_bottom</b>
<dd> Set the conformance window cropping offsets in the <font SIZE="-1">SPS.</font> These values will replace the current ones if the stream is already cropped. 

 These fields are set in pixels. Note that some sizes may not be representable if the chroma is subsampled (H.265 section 7.4.3.2.1).
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd> Set the level in the <font SIZE="-1">VPS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SPS.</font> See H.265 section A.4 and tables A.6 and A.7. 

 The argument must be the name of a level (for example, <b>5.1</b>), a <i>general_level_idc</i> value (for example, <b>153</b> for level 5.1), or the special name <b>auto</b> indicating that the filter should attempt to guess the level from the input stream properties.</dl>

<h3>hevc_mp4toannexb</h3>

 Convert an <font SIZE="-1">HEVC/H.265</font> bitstream from length prefixed mode to start code prefixed mode (as defined in the Annex B of the ITU-T H.265 specification). 

 This is required by some streaming formats, typically the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> transport stream format (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>). 

 For example to remux an <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> file containing an <font SIZE="-1">HEVC</font> stream to mpegts format with <b>ffmpeg</b>, you can use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT.mp4 -codec copy -bsf:v hevc_mp4toannexb OUTPUT.ts
</pre> 

 Please note that this filter is auto-inserted for MPEG-TS (muxer <tt>&quot;mpegts&quot;</tt>) and raw <font SIZE="-1">HEVC/H.265</font> (muxer <tt>&quot;h265&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;hevc&quot;</tt>) output formats.

<h3>imxdump</h3>

 Modifies the bitstream to fit in <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font> and to be usable by the Final Cut Pro decoder. This filter only applies to the mpeg2video codec, and is likely not needed for Final Cut Pro 7 and newer with the appropriate <b>-tag:v</b>. 

 For example, to remux 30 MB/sec <font SIZE="-1">NTSC IMX</font> to <font SIZE="-1">MOV:</font> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.mxf -c copy -bsf:v imxdump -tag:v mx3n output.mov
</pre>

<h3>mjpeg2jpeg</h3>

 Convert <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG/AVI1</font> packets to full <font SIZE="-1">JPEG/JFIF</font> packets. 

 <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> is a video codec wherein each video frame is essentially a <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> image. The individual frames can be extracted without loss, e.g. by 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i ../some_mjpeg.avi -c:v copy frames_%d.jpg
</pre> 

 Unfortunately, these chunks are incomplete <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> images, because they lack the <font SIZE="-1">DHT</font> segment required for decoding. Quoting from &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.digitalpreservation.gov/formats/fdd/fdd000063.shtml">http://www.digitalpreservation.gov/formats/fdd/fdd000063.shtml</a></b>&gt;: 

 Avery Lee, writing in the rec.video.desktop newsgroup in 2001, commented that ``<font SIZE="-1">MJPEG,</font> or at least the <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> in AVIs having the <font SIZE="-1">MJPG</font> fourcc, is restricted <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> with a fixed --- and *omitted* --- Huffman table. The <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> must be YCbCr colorspace, it must be 4:2:2, and it must use basic Huffman encoding, not arithmetic or progressive. . . . You can indeed extract the <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> frames and decode them with a regular <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> decoder, but you have to prepend the <font SIZE="-1">DHT</font> segment to them, or else the decoder won't have any idea how to decompress the data. The exact table necessary is given in the OpenDML spec.'' 

 This bitstream filter patches the header of frames extracted from an <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> stream (carrying the <font SIZE="-1">AVI1</font> header <font SIZE="-1">ID</font> and lacking a <font SIZE="-1">DHT</font> segment) to produce fully qualified <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> images. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i mjpeg-movie.avi -c:v copy -bsf:v mjpeg2jpeg frame_%d.jpg
        exiftran -i -9 frame*.jpg
        ffmpeg -i frame_%d.jpg -c:v copy rotated.avi
</pre>

<h3>mjpegadump</h3>

 Add an <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG A</font> header to the bitstream, to enable decoding by Quicktime.

<h3>mov2textsub</h3>

 Extract a representable text file from <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font> subtitles, stripping the metadata header from each subtitle packet. 

 See also the <b>text2movsub</b> filter.

<h3>mp3decomp</h3>

 Decompress non-standard compressed <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> audio headers.

<h3>mpeg2_metadata</h3>

 Modify metadata embedded in an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>display_aspect_ratio</b>
<dd> Set the display aspect ratio in the stream. 

 The following fixed values are supported:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>4/3</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>16/9</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>221/100</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Any other value will result in square pixels being signalled instead (see H.262 section 6.3.3 and table 6-3).</dl>

<dt><b>frame_rate</b>
<dd> Set the frame rate in the stream. This is constructed from a table of known values combined with a small multiplier and divisor - if the supplied value is not exactly representable, the nearest representable value will be used instead (see H.262 section 6.3.3 and table 6-4).
<dt><b>video_format</b>
<dd> Set the video format in the stream (see H.262 section 6.3.6 and table 6-6).
<dt><b>colour_primaries</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>transfer_characteristics</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>matrix_coefficients</b>
<dd> Set the colour description in the stream (see H.262 section 6.3.6 and tables 6-7, 6-8 and 6-9).</dl>

<h3>mpeg4_unpack_bframes</h3>

 Unpack DivX-style packed B-frames. 

 DivX-style packed B-frames are not valid <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> and were only a workaround for the broken Video for Windows subsystem. They use more space, can cause minor <font SIZE="-1">AV</font> sync issues, require more <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> power to decode (unless the player has some decoded picture queue to compensate the 2,0,2,0 frame per packet style) and cause trouble if copied into a standard container like mp4 or mpeg-ps/ts, because <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> decoders may not be able to decode them, since they are not valid <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4.</font> 

 For example to fix an <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> file containing an <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> stream with DivX-style packed B-frames using <b>ffmpeg</b>, you can use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT.avi -codec copy -bsf:v mpeg4_unpack_bframes OUTPUT.avi
</pre>

<h3>noise</h3>

 Damages the contents of packets or simply drops them without damaging the container. Can be used for fuzzing or testing error resilience/concealment. 

 Parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>amount</b>
<dd> A numeral string, whose value is related to how often output bytes will be modified. Therefore, values below or equal to 0 are forbidden, and the lower the more frequent bytes will be modified, with 1 meaning every byte is modified.
<dt><b>dropamount</b>
<dd> A numeral string, whose value is related to how often packets will be dropped. Therefore, values below or equal to 0 are forbidden, and the lower the more frequent packets will be dropped, with 1 meaning every packet is dropped.</dl>
 

 The following example applies the modification to every byte but does not drop any packets. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c copy -bsf noise[=1] output.mkv
</pre>

<h3>null</h3>

 This bitstream filter passes the packets through unchanged.

<h3>pcm_rechunk</h3>

 Repacketize <font SIZE="-1">PCM</font> audio to a fixed number of samples per packet or a fixed packet rate per second. This is similar to the <b>asetnsamples audio filter</b> but works on audio packets instead of audio frames.
<dl>
<dt><b>nb_out_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set the number of samples per each output audio packet. The number is intended as the number of samples <i>per each channel</i>. Default value is 1024.
<dt><b>pad, p</b>
<dd> If set to 1, the filter will pad the last audio packet with silence, so that it will contain the same number of samples (or roughly the same number of samples, see <b>frame_rate</b>) as the previous ones. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>frame_rate, r</b>
<dd> This option makes the filter output a fixed number of packets per second instead of a fixed number of samples per packet. If the audio sample rate is not divisible by the frame rate then the number of samples will not be constant but will vary slightly so that each packet will start as close to the frame boundary as possible. Using this option has precedence over <b>nb_out_samples</b>.</dl>
 

 You can generate the well known 1602-1601-1602-1601-1602 pattern of 48kHz audio for <font SIZE="-1">NTSC</font> frame rate using the <b>frame_rate</b> option. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=r=48000:d=1 -c pcm_s16le -bsf pcm_rechunk=r=30000/1001 -f framecrc -
</pre>

<h3>prores_metadata</h3>

 Modify color property metadata embedded in prores stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>color_primaries</b>
<dd> Set the color primaries. Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> Keep the same color primaries property (default).
<dt><b>unknown</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bt470bg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT601 625</font>
<dt><b>smpte170m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT601 525</font>
<dt><b>bt2020</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>smpte431</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">DCI P3</font>
<dt><b>smpte432</b>
<dd> P3 D65</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>transfer_characteristics</b>
<dd> Set the color transfer. Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> Keep the same transfer characteristics property (default).
<dt><b>unknown</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT 601, BT 709, BT 2020</font>
<dt><b>smpte2084</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE ST 2084</font>
<dt><b>arib-std-b67</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">ARIB STD-B67</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>matrix_coefficients</b>
<dd> Set the matrix coefficient. Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> Keep the same colorspace property (default).
<dt><b>unknown</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>smpte170m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT 601</font>
<dt><b>bt2020nc</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 Set Rec709 colorspace for each frame of the file 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c copy -bsf:v prores_metadata=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709 output.mov
</pre> 

 Set Hybrid Log-Gamma parameters for each frame of the file 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c copy -bsf:v prores_metadata=color_primaries=bt2020:color_trc=arib-std-b67:colorspace=bt2020nc output.mov
</pre>

<h3>remove_extra</h3>

 Remove extradata from packets. 

 It accepts the following parameter:
<dl>
<dt><b>freq</b>
<dd> Set which frame types to remove extradata from.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>k</b>
<dd> Remove extradata from non-keyframes only.
<dt><b>keyframe</b>
<dd> Remove extradata from keyframes only.
<dt><b>e, all</b>
<dd> Remove extradata from all frames.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>setts</h3>

 Set <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> in packets. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>ts</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dts</b>
<dd> Set expressions for <font SIZE="-1">PTS, DTS</font> or both.</dl>
 

 The expressions are evaluated through the eval <font SIZE="-1">API</font> and can contain the following constants:
<dl>
<dt><b>N</b>
<dd> The count of the input packet. Starting from 0.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TS</b></font>
<dd> The demux timestamp in input in case of <tt>&quot;ts&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;dts&quot;</tt> option or presentation timestamp in case of <tt>&quot;pts&quot;</tt> option.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>POS</b></font>
<dd> The original position in the file of the packet, or undefined if undefined for the current packet
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>DTS</b></font>
<dd> The demux timestamp in input.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PTS</b></font>
<dd> The presentation timestamp in input.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>STARTDTS</b></font>
<dd> The <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> of the first packet.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>STARTPTS</b></font>
<dd> The <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> of the first packet.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PREV_INDTS</b></font>
<dd> The previous input <font SIZE="-1">DTS.</font>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PREV_INPTS</b></font>
<dd> The previous input <font SIZE="-1">PTS.</font>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PREV_OUTDTS</b></font>
<dd> The previous output <font SIZE="-1">DTS.</font>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PREV_OUTPTS</b></font>
<dd> The previous output <font SIZE="-1">PTS.</font>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TB</b></font>
<dd> The timebase of stream packet belongs.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SR</b></font>
<dd> The sample rate of stream packet belongs.</dl>

<h3>text2movsub</h3>

 Convert text subtitles to <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font> subtitles (as used by the <tt>&quot;mov_text&quot;</tt> codec) with metadata headers. 

 See also the <b>mov2textsub</b> filter.

<h3>trace_headers</h3>

 Log trace output containing all syntax elements in the coded stream headers (everything above the level of individual coded blocks). This can be useful for debugging low-level stream issues. 

 Supports <font SIZE="-1">AV1, H.264, H.265,</font> (M)JPEG, <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> and <font SIZE="-1">VP9,</font> but depending on the build only a subset of these may be available.

<h3>truehd_core</h3>

 Extract the core from a TrueHD stream, dropping <font SIZE="-1">ATMOS</font> data.

<h3>vp9_metadata</h3>

 Modify metadata embedded in a <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>color_space</b>
<dd> Set the color space value in the frame header. Note that any frame set to <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> will be implicitly set to <font SIZE="-1">PC</font> range and that <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> is incompatible with profiles 0 and 2.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>unknown</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bt601</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>smpte170</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>smpte240</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bt2020</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>rgb</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>color_range</b>
<dd> Set the color range value in the frame header. Note that any value imposed by the color space will take precedence over this value.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>tv</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>pc</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>vp9_superframe</h3>

 Merge <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> invisible (alt-ref) frames back into <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> superframes. This fixes merging of split/segmented <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> streams where the alt-ref frame was split from its visible counterpart.

<h3>vp9_superframe_split</h3>

 Split <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> superframes into single frames.

<h3>vp9_raw_reorder</h3>

 Given a <font SIZE="-1">VP9</font> stream with correct timestamps but possibly out of order, insert additional show-existing-frame packets to correct the ordering.

<h2>FORMAT OPTIONS</h2>

 The libavformat library provides some generic global options, which can be set on all the muxers and demuxers. In addition each muxer or demuxer may support so-called private options, which are specific for that component. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, or by setting the value explicitly in the <tt>&quot;AVFormatContext&quot;</tt> options or using the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API</font> for programmatic use. 

 The list of supported options follows:
<dl>
<dt><b>avioflags</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>direct</b>
<dd> Reduce buffering.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>probesize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set probing size in bytes, i.e. the size of the data to analyze to get stream information. A higher value will enable detecting more information in case it is dispersed into the stream, but will increase latency. Must be an integer not lesser than 32. It is 5000000 by default.
<dt><b>max_probe_packets</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the maximum number of buffered packets when probing a codec. Default is 2500 packets.
<dt><b>packetsize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set packet size.
<dt><b>fflags</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd> Set format flags. Some are implemented for a limited number of formats. 

 Possible values for input files:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>discardcorrupt</b>
<dd> Discard corrupted packets.
<dt><b>fastseek</b>
<dd> Enable fast, but inaccurate seeks for some formats.
<dt><b>genpts</b>
<dd> Generate missing <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> if <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> is present.
<dt><b>igndts</b>
<dd> Ignore <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> if <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> is set. Inert when nofillin is set.
<dt><b>ignidx</b>
<dd> Ignore index.
<dt><b>keepside (</b><i>deprecated</i><b>,</b><i>inert</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>nobuffer</b>
<dd> Reduce the latency introduced by buffering during initial input streams analysis.
<dt><b>nofillin</b>
<dd> Do not fill in missing values in packet fields that can be exactly calculated.
<dt><b>noparse</b>
<dd> Disable AVParsers, this needs <tt>&quot;+nofillin&quot;</tt> too.
<dt><b>sortdts</b>
<dd> Try to interleave output packets by <font SIZE="-1">DTS.</font> At present, available only for AVIs with an index.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Possible values for output files:
<dl>
<dt><b>autobsf</b>
<dd> Automatically apply bitstream filters as required by the output format. Enabled by default.
<dt><b>bitexact</b>
<dd> Only write platform-, build- and time-independent data. This ensures that file and data checksums are reproducible and match between platforms. Its primary use is for regression testing.
<dt><b>flush_packets</b>
<dd> Write out packets immediately.
<dt><b>latm (</b><i>deprecated</i><b>,</b><i>inert</i><b>)</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>shortest</b>
<dd> Stop muxing at the end of the shortest stream. It may be needed to increase max_interleave_delta to avoid flushing the longer streams before <font SIZE="-1">EOF.</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>seek2any</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Allow seeking to non-keyframes on demuxer level when supported if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>analyzeduration</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Specify how many microseconds are analyzed to probe the input. A higher value will enable detecting more accurate information, but will increase latency. It defaults to 5,000,000 microseconds = 5 seconds.
<dt><b>cryptokey</b> <i>hexadecimal string</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set decryption key.
<dt><b>indexmem</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set max memory used for timestamp index (per stream).
<dt><b>rtbufsize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set max memory used for buffering real-time frames.
<dt><b>fdebug</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Print specific debug info. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>ts</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>max_delay</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set maximum muxing or demuxing delay in microseconds.
<dt><b>fpsprobesize</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set number of frames used to probe fps.
<dt><b>audio_preload</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set microseconds by which audio packets should be interleaved earlier.
<dt><b>chunk_duration</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set microseconds for each chunk.
<dt><b>chunk_size</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set size in bytes for each chunk.
<dt><b>err_detect, f_err_detect</b> <i>flags</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set error detection flags. <tt>&quot;f_err_detect&quot;</tt> is deprecated and should be used only via the <b>ffmpeg</b> tool. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>crccheck</b>
<dd> Verify embedded CRCs.
<dt><b>bitstream</b>
<dd> Detect bitstream specification deviations.
<dt><b>buffer</b>
<dd> Detect improper bitstream length.
<dt><b>explode</b>
<dd> Abort decoding on minor error detection.
<dt><b>careful</b>
<dd> Consider things that violate the spec and have not been seen in the wild as errors.
<dt><b>compliant</b>
<dd> Consider all spec non compliancies as errors.
<dt><b>aggressive</b>
<dd> Consider things that a sane encoder should not do as an error.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>max_interleave_delta</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set maximum buffering duration for interleaving. The duration is expressed in microseconds, and defaults to 10000000 (10 seconds). 

 To ensure all the streams are interleaved correctly, libavformat will wait until it has at least one packet for each stream before actually writing any packets to the output file. When some streams are ``sparse'' (i.e. there are large gaps between successive packets), this can result in excessive buffering. 

 This field specifies the maximum difference between the timestamps of the first and the last packet in the muxing queue, above which libavformat will output a packet regardless of whether it has queued a packet for all the streams. 

 If set to 0, libavformat will continue buffering packets until it has a packet for each stream, regardless of the maximum timestamp difference between the buffered packets.
<dt><b>use_wallclock_as_timestamps</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Use wallclock as timestamps if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>avoid_negative_ts</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>make_non_negative</b>
<dd> Shift timestamps to make them non-negative. Also note that this affects only leading negative timestamps, and not non-monotonic negative timestamps.
<dt><b>make_zero</b>
<dd> Shift timestamps so that the first timestamp is 0.
<dt><b>auto (default)</b>
<dd> Enables shifting when required by the target format.
<dt><b>disabled</b>
<dd> Disables shifting of timestamp.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 When shifting is enabled, all output timestamps are shifted by the same amount. Audio, video, and subtitles desynching and relative timestamp differences are preserved compared to how they would have been without shifting.</dl>

<dt><b>skip_initial_bytes</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set number of bytes to skip before reading header and frames if set to 1. Default is 0.
<dt><b>correct_ts_overflow</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Correct single timestamp overflows if set to 1. Default is 1.
<dt><b>flush_packets</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Flush the underlying I/O stream after each packet. Default is -1 (auto), which means that the underlying protocol will decide, 1 enables it, and has the effect of reducing the latency, 0 disables it and may increase <font SIZE="-1">IO</font> throughput in some cases.
<dt><b>output_ts_offset</b> <i>offset</i> <b>(</b><i>output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set the output time offset. 

 <i>offset</i> must be a time duration specification, see <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b>. 

 The offset is added by the muxer to the output timestamps. 

 Specifying a positive offset means that the corresponding streams are delayed bt the time duration specified in <i>offset</i>. Default value is <tt>0</tt> (meaning that no offset is applied).
<dt><b>format_whitelist</b> <i>list</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> ``,'' separated list of allowed demuxers. By default all are allowed.
<dt><b>dump_separator</b> <i>string</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Separator used to separate the fields printed on the command line about the Stream parameters. For example, to separate the fields with newlines and indentation: 

 <pre>
        ffprobe -dump_separator &quot;
                                  &quot;  -i ~/videos/matrixbench_mpeg2.mpg
</pre>
<dt><b>max_streams</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Specifies the maximum number of streams. This can be used to reject files that would require too many resources due to a large number of streams.
<dt><b>skip_estimate_duration_from_pts</b> <i>bool</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Skip estimation of input duration when calculated using <font SIZE="-1">PTS.</font> At present, applicable for MPEG-PS and MPEG-TS.
<dt><b>strict, f_strict</b> <i>integer</i> <b>(</b><i>input/output</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Specify how strictly to follow the standards. <tt>&quot;f_strict&quot;</tt> is deprecated and should be used only via the <b>ffmpeg</b> tool. 

 Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>very</b>
<dd> strictly conform to an older more strict version of the spec or reference software
<dt><b>strict</b>
<dd> strictly conform to all the things in the spec no matter what consequences
<dt><b>normal</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>unofficial</b>
<dd> allow unofficial extensions
<dt><b>experimental</b>
<dd> allow non standardized experimental things, experimental (unfinished/work in progress/not well tested) decoders and encoders. Note: experimental decoders can pose a security risk, do not use this for decoding untrusted input.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>Format stream specifiers</h3>

 Format stream specifiers allow selection of one or more streams that match specific properties. 

 The exact semantics of stream specifiers is defined by the <tt>&quot;avformat_match_stream_specifier()&quot;</tt> function declared in the <i>libavformat/avformat.h</i> header and documented in the <b>Stream specifiers section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg/">ffmpeg</a>(1) manual</b>.

<h2>DEMUXERS</h2>

 Demuxers are configured elements in FFmpeg that can read the multimedia streams from a particular type of file. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported demuxers are enabled by default. You can list all available ones using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-demuxers&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the demuxers using the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-demuxers&quot;</tt>, and selectively enable a single demuxer with the option <tt>&quot;--enable-demuxer=</tt>DEMUXER<tt>&quot;</tt>, or disable it with the option <tt>&quot;--disable-demuxer=</tt>DEMUXER<tt>&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-demuxers&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of enabled demuxers. Use <tt>&quot;-formats&quot;</tt> to view a combined list of enabled demuxers and muxers. 

 The description of some of the currently available demuxers follows.

<h3>aa</h3>

 Audible Format 2, 3, and 4 demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux Audible Format 2, 3, and 4 (.aa) files.

<h3>apng</h3>

 Animated Portable Network Graphics demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux <font SIZE="-1">APNG</font> files. All headers, but the <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> signature, up to (but not including) the first fcTL chunk are transmitted as extradata. Frames are then split as being all the chunks between two fcTL ones, or between the last fcTL and <font SIZE="-1">IEND</font> chunks.
<dl>
<dt><b>-ignore_loop</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Ignore the loop variable in the file if set.
<dt><b>-max_fps</b> <i>int</i>
<dd> Maximum framerate in frames per second (0 for no limit).
<dt><b>-default_fps</b> <i>int</i>
<dd> Default framerate in frames per second when none is specified in the file (0 meaning as fast as possible).</dl>

<h3>asf</h3>

 Advanced Systems Format demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux <font SIZE="-1">ASF</font> files and <font SIZE="-1">MMS</font> network streams.
<dl>
<dt><b>-no_resync_search</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Do not try to resynchronize by looking for a certain optional start code.</dl>

<h3>concat</h3>

 Virtual concatenation script demuxer. 

 This demuxer reads a list of files and other directives from a text file and demuxes them one after the other, as if all their packets had been muxed together. 

 The timestamps in the files are adjusted so that the first file starts at 0 and each next file starts where the previous one finishes. Note that it is done globally and may cause gaps if all streams do not have exactly the same length. 

 All files must have the same streams (same codecs, same time base, etc.). 

 The duration of each file is used to adjust the timestamps of the next file: if the duration is incorrect (because it was computed using the bit-rate or because the file is truncated, for example), it can cause artifacts. The <tt>&quot;duration&quot;</tt> directive can be used to override the duration stored in each file. 

 <i>Syntax</i> 

 The script is a text file in extended-ASCII, with one directive per line. Empty lines, leading spaces and lines starting with '#' are ignored. The following directive is recognized:
<dl>
<dt>&quot;file path&quot;
<dd> Path to a file to read; special characters and spaces must be escaped with backslash or single quotes. 

 All subsequent file-related directives apply to that file.
<dt>&quot;ffconcat version 1.0&quot;
<dd> Identify the script type and version. It also sets the <b>safe</b> option to 1 if it was -1. 

 To make FFmpeg recognize the format automatically, this directive must appear exactly as is (no extra space or byte-order-mark) on the very first line of the script.
<dt>&quot;duration dur&quot;
<dd> Duration of the file. This information can be specified from the file; specifying it here may be more efficient or help if the information from the file is not available or accurate. 

 If the duration is set for all files, then it is possible to seek in the whole concatenated video.
<dt>&quot;inpoint timestamp&quot;
<dd> In point of the file. When the demuxer opens the file it instantly seeks to the specified timestamp. Seeking is done so that all streams can be presented successfully at In point. 

 This directive works best with intra frame codecs, because for non-intra frame ones you will usually get extra packets before the actual In point and the decoded content will most likely contain frames before In point too. 

 For each file, packets before the file In point will have timestamps less than the calculated start timestamp of the file (negative in case of the first file), and the duration of the files (if not specified by the <tt>&quot;duration&quot;</tt> directive) will be reduced based on their specified In point. 

 Because of potential packets before the specified In point, packet timestamps may overlap between two concatenated files.
<dt>&quot;outpoint timestamp&quot;
<dd> Out point of the file. When the demuxer reaches the specified decoding timestamp in any of the streams, it handles it as an end of file condition and skips the current and all the remaining packets from all streams. 

 Out point is exclusive, which means that the demuxer will not output packets with a decoding timestamp greater or equal to Out point. 

 This directive works best with intra frame codecs and formats where all streams are tightly interleaved. For non-intra frame codecs you will usually get additional packets with presentation timestamp after Out point therefore the decoded content will most likely contain frames after Out point too. If your streams are not tightly interleaved you may not get all the packets from all streams before Out point and you may only will be able to decode the earliest stream until Out point. 

 The duration of the files (if not specified by the <tt>&quot;duration&quot;</tt> directive) will be reduced based on their specified Out point.
<dt>&quot;file_packet_metadata key=value&quot;
<dd> Metadata of the packets of the file. The specified metadata will be set for each file packet. You can specify this directive multiple times to add multiple metadata entries.
<dt>&quot;stream&quot;
<dd> Introduce a stream in the virtual file. All subsequent stream-related directives apply to the last introduced stream. Some streams properties must be set in order to allow identifying the matching streams in the subfiles. If no streams are defined in the script, the streams from the first file are copied.
<dt>&quot;exact_stream_id id&quot;
<dd> Set the id of the stream. If this directive is given, the string with the corresponding id in the subfiles will be used. This is especially useful for MPEG-PS (<font SIZE="-1">VOB</font>) files, where the order of the streams is not reliable.</dl>
 

 <i>Options</i> 

 This demuxer accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>safe</b>
<dd> If set to 1, reject unsafe file paths. A file path is considered safe if it does not contain a protocol specification and is relative and all components only contain characters from the portable character set (letters, digits, period, underscore and hyphen) and have no period at the beginning of a component. 

 If set to 0, any file name is accepted. 

 The default is 1. 

 -1 is equivalent to 1 if the format was automatically probed and 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>auto_convert</b>
<dd> If set to 1, try to perform automatic conversions on packet data to make the streams concatenable. The default is 1. 

 Currently, the only conversion is adding the h264_mp4toannexb bitstream filter to H.264 streams in <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> format. This is necessary in particular if there are resolution changes.
<dt><b>segment_time_metadata</b>
<dd> If set to 1, every packet will contain the <i>lavf.concat.start_time</i> and the <i>lavf.concat.duration</i> packet metadata values which are the start_time and the duration of the respective file segments in the concatenated output expressed in microseconds. The duration metadata is only set if it is known based on the concat file. The default is 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Use absolute filenames and include some comments: 

 <pre>
        # my first filename
        file /mnt/share/file-1.wav
        # my second filename including whitespace
        file '/mnt/share/file 2.wav'
        # my third filename including whitespace plus single quote
        file '/mnt/share/file 3'\''.wav'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Allow for input format auto-probing, use safe filenames and set the duration of the first file: 

 <pre>
        ffconcat version 1.0
        
        file file-1.wav
        duration 20.0
        
        file subdir/file-2.wav
</pre></dl>

<h3>dash</h3>

 Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> demuxer. 

 This demuxer presents all AVStreams found in the manifest. By setting the discard flags on AVStreams the caller can decide which streams to actually receive. Each stream mirrors the <tt>&quot;id&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;bandwidth&quot;</tt> properties from the <tt>&quot;&lt;Representation&gt;&quot;</tt> as metadata keys named ``id'' and ``variant_bitrate'' respectively.

<h3>flv, live_flv</h3>

 Adobe Flash Video Format demuxer. 

 This demuxer is used to demux <font SIZE="-1">FLV</font> files and <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> network streams. In case of live network streams, if you force format, you may use live_flv option instead of flv to survive timestamp discontinuities. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f flv -i myfile.flv ...
        ffmpeg -f live_flv -i rtmp://&lt;any.server&gt;/anything/key ....
</pre>
<dl>
<dt><b>-flv_metadata</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Allocate the streams according to the onMetaData array content.
<dt><b>-flv_ignore_prevtag</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Ignore the size of previous tag value.
<dt><b>-flv_full_metadata</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Output all context of the onMetadata.</dl>

<h3>gif</h3>

 Animated <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> demuxer. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>min_delay</b>
<dd> Set the minimum valid delay between frames in hundredths of seconds. Range is 0 to 6000. Default value is 2.
<dt><b>max_gif_delay</b>
<dd> Set the maximum valid delay between frames in hundredth of seconds. Range is 0 to 65535. Default value is 65535 (nearly eleven minutes), the maximum value allowed by the specification.
<dt><b>default_delay</b>
<dd> Set the default delay between frames in hundredths of seconds. Range is 0 to 6000. Default value is 10.
<dt><b>ignore_loop</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> files can contain information to loop a certain number of times (or infinitely). If <b>ignore_loop</b> is set to 1, then the loop setting from the input will be ignored and looping will not occur. If set to 0, then looping will occur and will cycle the number of times according to the <font SIZE="-1">GIF.</font> Default value is 1.</dl>
 

 For example, with the overlay filter, place an infinitely looping <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> over another video: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.mp4 -ignore_loop 0 -i input.gif -filter_complex overlay=shortest=1 out.mkv
</pre> 

 Note that in the above example the shortest option for overlay filter is used to end the output video at the length of the shortest input file, which in this case is <i>input.mp4</i> as the <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> in this example loops infinitely.

<h3>hls</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> demuxer 

 Apple <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Live Streaming demuxer. 

 This demuxer presents all AVStreams from all variant streams. The id field is set to the bitrate variant index number. By setting the discard flags on AVStreams (by pressing 'a' or 'v' in ffplay), the caller can decide which variant streams to actually receive. The total bitrate of the variant that the stream belongs to is available in a metadata key named ``variant_bitrate''. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>live_start_index</b>
<dd> segment index to start live streams at (negative values are from the end).
<dt><b>allowed_extensions</b>
<dd> ',' separated list of file extensions that hls is allowed to access.
<dt><b>max_reload</b>
<dd> Maximum number of times a insufficient list is attempted to be reloaded. Default value is 1000.
<dt><b>m3u8_hold_counters</b>
<dd> The maximum number of times to load m3u8 when it refreshes without new segments. Default value is 1000.
<dt><b>http_persistent</b>
<dd> Use persistent <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> connections. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> streams. Enabled by default.
<dt><b>http_multiple</b>
<dd> Use multiple <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> connections for downloading <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> segments. Enabled by default for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP/1.1</font> servers.
<dt><b>http_seekable</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> partial requests for downloading <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> segments. 0 = disable, 1 = enable, -1 = auto, Default is auto.</dl>

<h3>image2</h3>

 Image file demuxer. 

 This demuxer reads from a list of image files specified by a pattern. The syntax and meaning of the pattern is specified by the option <i>pattern_type</i>. 

 The pattern may contain a suffix which is used to automatically determine the format of the images contained in the files. 

 The size, the pixel format, and the format of each image must be the same for all the files in the sequence. 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd> Set the frame rate for the video stream. It defaults to 25.
<dt><b>loop</b>
<dd> If set to 1, loop over the input. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>pattern_type</b>
<dd> Select the pattern type used to interpret the provided filename. 

 <i>pattern_type</i> accepts one of the following values.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Disable pattern matching, therefore the video will only contain the specified image. You should use this option if you do not want to create sequences from multiple images and your filenames may contain special pattern characters.
<dt><b>sequence</b>
<dd> Select a sequence pattern type, used to specify a sequence of files indexed by sequential numbers. 

 A sequence pattern may contain the string ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d``, which specifies the position of the characters representing a sequential number in each filename matched by the pattern. If the form ''%d0<i>N</i>d&quot; is used, the string representing the number in each filename is 0-padded and <i>N</i> is the total number of 0-padded digits representing the number. The literal character '%' can be specified in the pattern with the string ``%%''. 

 If the sequence pattern contains ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d&quot;, the first filename of the file list specified by the pattern must contain a number inclusively contained between <i>start_number</i> and <i>start_number</i>+<i>start_number_range</i>-1, and all the following numbers must be sequential. 

 For example the pattern ``img-%03d.bmp'' will match a sequence of filenames of the form <i>img-001.bmp</i>, <i>img-002.bmp</i>, ..., <i>img-010.bmp</i>, etc.; the pattern ``i%%m%%g-%d.jpg'' will match a sequence of filenames of the form <i>i%m%g-1.jpg</i>, <i>i%m%g-2.jpg</i>, ..., <i>i%m%g-10.jpg</i>, etc. 

 Note that the pattern must not necessarily contain ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d&quot;, for example to convert a single image file <i>img.jpeg</i> you can employ the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i img.jpeg img.png
</pre>
<dt><b>glob</b>
<dd> Select a glob wildcard pattern type. 

 The pattern is interpreted like a <tt>&quot;glob()&quot;</tt> pattern. This is only selectable if libavformat was compiled with globbing support.
<dt><b>glob_sequence</b> <i>(deprecated, will be removed)</i>
<dd> Select a mixed glob wildcard/sequence pattern. 

 If your version of libavformat was compiled with globbing support, and the provided pattern contains at least one glob meta character among <tt>&quot;%*?[]{}&quot;</tt> that is preceded by an unescaped ``%'', the pattern is interpreted like a <tt>&quot;glob()&quot;</tt> pattern, otherwise it is interpreted like a sequence pattern. 

 All glob special characters <tt>&quot;%*?[]{}&quot;</tt> must be prefixed with ``%''. To escape a literal ``%'' you shall use ``%%''. 

 For example the pattern <tt>&quot;foo-%*.jpeg&quot;</tt> will match all the filenames prefixed by ``foo-'' and terminating with ``.jpeg'', and <tt>&quot;foo-%?%?%?.jpeg&quot;</tt> will match all the filenames prefixed with ``foo-'', followed by a sequence of three characters, and terminating with ``.jpeg''. 

 This pattern type is deprecated in favor of <i>glob</i> and <i>sequence</i>.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <i>glob_sequence</i>.</dl>

<dt><b>pixel_format</b>
<dd> Set the pixel format of the images to read. If not specified the pixel format is guessed from the first image file in the sequence.
<dt><b>start_number</b>
<dd> Set the index of the file matched by the image file pattern to start to read from. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>start_number_range</b>
<dd> Set the index interval range to check when looking for the first image file in the sequence, starting from <i>start_number</i>. Default value is 5.
<dt><b>ts_from_file</b>
<dd> If set to 1, will set frame timestamp to modification time of image file. Note that monotonity of timestamps is not provided: images go in the same order as without this option. Default value is 0. If set to 2, will set frame timestamp to the modification time of the image file in nanosecond precision.
<dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd> Set the video size of the images to read. If not specified the video size is guessed from the first image file in the sequence.
<dt><b>export_path_metadata</b>
<dd> If set to 1, will add two extra fields to the metadata found in input, making them also available for other filters (see <i>drawtext</i> filter for examples). Default value is 0. The extra fields are described below:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lavf.image2dec.source_path</b>
<dd> Corresponds to the full path to the input file being read.
<dt><b>lavf.image2dec.source_basename</b>
<dd> Corresponds to the name of the file being read.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Use <b>ffmpeg</b> for creating a video from the images in the file sequence <i>img-001.jpeg</i>, <i>img-002.jpeg</i>, ..., assuming an input frame rate of 10 frames per second: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -framerate 10 -i 'img-%03d.jpeg' out.mkv
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> As above, but start by reading from a file with index 100 in the sequence: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -framerate 10 -start_number 100 -i 'img-%03d.jpeg' out.mkv
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Read images matching the ``*.png'' glob pattern , that is all the files terminating with the ``.png'' suffix: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -framerate 10 -pattern_type glob -i &quot;*.png&quot; out.mkv
</pre></dl>

<h3>libgme</h3>

 The Game Music Emu library is a collection of video game music file emulators. 

 See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://bitbucket.org/mpyne/game-music-emu/overview">https://bitbucket.org/mpyne/game-music-emu/overview</a></b>&gt; for more information. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>track_index</b>
<dd> Set the index of which track to demux. The demuxer can only export one track. Track indexes start at 0. Default is to pick the first track. Number of tracks is exported as <i>tracks</i> metadata entry.
<dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd> Set the sampling rate of the exported track. Range is 1000 to 999999. Default is 44100.
<dt><b>max_size</b> <i>(bytes)</i>
<dd> The demuxer buffers the entire file into memory. Adjust this value to set the maximum buffer size, which in turn, acts as a ceiling for the size of files that can be read. Default is 50 MiB.</dl>

<h3>libmodplug</h3>

 ModPlug based module demuxer 

 See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/Konstanty/libmodplug">https://github.com/Konstanty/libmodplug</a></b>&gt; 

 It will export one 2-channel 16-bit 44.1 kHz audio stream. Optionally, a <tt>&quot;pal8&quot;</tt> 16-color video stream can be exported with or without printed metadata. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>noise_reduction</b>
<dd> Apply a simple low-pass filter. Can be 1 (on) or 0 (off). Default is 0.
<dt><b>reverb_depth</b>
<dd> Set amount of reverb. Range 0-100. Default is 0.
<dt><b>reverb_delay</b>
<dd> Set delay in ms, clamped to 40-250 ms. Default is 0.
<dt><b>bass_amount</b>
<dd> Apply bass expansion a.k.a. XBass or megabass. Range is 0 (quiet) to 100 (loud). Default is 0.
<dt><b>bass_range</b>
<dd> Set cutoff i.e. upper-bound for bass frequencies. Range is 10-100 Hz. Default is 0.
<dt><b>surround_depth</b>
<dd> Apply a Dolby Pro-Logic surround effect. Range is 0 (quiet) to 100 (heavy). Default is 0.
<dt><b>surround_delay</b>
<dd> Set surround delay in ms, clamped to 5-40 ms. Default is 0.
<dt><b>max_size</b>
<dd> The demuxer buffers the entire file into memory. Adjust this value to set the maximum buffer size, which in turn, acts as a ceiling for the size of files that can be read. Range is 0 to 100 MiB. 0 removes buffer size limit (not recommended). Default is 5 MiB.
<dt><b>video_stream_expr</b>
<dd> String which is evaluated using the eval <font SIZE="-1">API</font> to assign colors to the generated video stream. Variables which can be used are <tt>&quot;x&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;y&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;w&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;h&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;t&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;speed&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;tempo&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;order&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;pattern&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;row&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>video_stream</b>
<dd> Generate video stream. Can be 1 (on) or 0 (off). Default is 0.
<dt><b>video_stream_w</b>
<dd> Set video frame width in 'chars' where one char indicates 8 pixels. Range is 20-512. Default is 30.
<dt><b>video_stream_h</b>
<dd> Set video frame height in 'chars' where one char indicates 8 pixels. Range is 20-512. Default is 30.
<dt><b>video_stream_ptxt</b>
<dd> Print metadata on video stream. Includes <tt>&quot;speed&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;tempo&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;order&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;pattern&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;row&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;ts&quot;</tt> (time in ms). Can be 1 (on) or 0 (off). Default is 1.</dl>

<h3>libopenmpt</h3>

 libopenmpt based module demuxer 

 See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://lib.openmpt.org/libopenmpt/">https://lib.openmpt.org/libopenmpt/</a></b>&gt; for more information. 

 Some files have multiple subsongs (tracks) this can be set with the <b>subsong</b> option. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>subsong</b>
<dd> Set the subsong index. This can be either 'all', 'auto', or the index of the subsong. Subsong indexes start at 0. The default is 'auto'. 

 The default value is to let libopenmpt choose.
<dt><b>layout</b>
<dd> Set the channel layout. Valid values are 1, 2, and 4 channel layouts. The default value is <font SIZE="-1">STEREO.</font>
<dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd> Set the sample rate for libopenmpt to output. Range is from 1000 to <font SIZE="-1">INT_MAX.</font> The value default is 48000.</dl>

<h3>mov/mp4/3gp</h3>

 Demuxer for Quicktime File Format &amp; <font SIZE="-1">ISO/IEC</font> Base Media File Format (<font SIZE="-1">ISO/IEC 14496-12</font> or <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-4</font> Part 12, <font SIZE="-1">ISO/IEC 15444-12</font> or <font SIZE="-1">JPEG 2000</font> Part 12). 

 Registered extensions: mov, mp4, m4a, 3gp, 3g2, mj2, psp, m4b, ism, ismv, isma, f4v 

 <i>Options</i> 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>enable_drefs</b>
<dd> Enable loading of external tracks, disabled by default. Enabling this can theoretically leak information in some use cases.
<dt><b>use_absolute_path</b>
<dd> Allows loading of external tracks via absolute paths, disabled by default. Enabling this poses a security risk. It should only be enabled if the source is known to be non-malicious.
<dt><b>seek_streams_individually</b>
<dd> When seeking, identify the closest point in each stream individually and demux packets in that stream from identified point. This can lead to a different sequence of packets compared to demuxing linearly from the beginning. Default is true.
<dt><b>ignore_editlist</b>
<dd> Ignore any edit list atoms. The demuxer, by default, modifies the stream index to reflect the timeline described by the edit list. Default is false.
<dt><b>advanced_editlist</b>
<dd> Modify the stream index to reflect the timeline described by the edit list. <tt>&quot;ignore_editlist&quot;</tt> must be set to false for this option to be effective. If both <tt>&quot;ignore_editlist&quot;</tt> and this option are set to false, then only the start of the stream index is modified to reflect initial dwell time or starting timestamp described by the edit list. Default is true.
<dt><b>ignore_chapters</b>
<dd> Don't parse chapters. This includes GoPro 'HiLight' tags/moments. Note that chapters are only parsed when input is seekable. Default is false.
<dt><b>use_mfra_for</b>
<dd> For seekable fragmented input, set fragment's starting timestamp from media fragment random access box, if present. 

 Following options are available:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> Auto-detect whether to set mfra timestamps as <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> or <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> <i>(default)</i>
<dt><b>dts</b>
<dd> Set mfra timestamps as <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font>
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd> Set mfra timestamps as <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font>
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd> Don't use mfra box to set timestamps</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>export_all</b>
<dd> Export unrecognized boxes within the <i>udta</i> box as metadata entries. The first four characters of the box type are set as the key. Default is false.
<dt><b>export_xmp</b>
<dd> Export entire contents of <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>XMP_</i></font><i></i> box and <i>uuid</i> box as a string with key <tt>&quot;xmp&quot;</tt>. Note that if <tt>&quot;export_all&quot;</tt> is set and this option isn't, the contents of <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>XMP_</i></font><i></i> box are still exported but with key <tt>&quot;XMP_&quot;</tt>. Default is false.
<dt><b>activation_bytes</b>
<dd> 4-byte key required to decrypt Audible <font SIZE="-1">AAX</font> and <font SIZE="-1">AAX+</font> files. See Audible <font SIZE="-1">AAX</font> subsection below.
<dt><b>audible_fixed_key</b>
<dd> Fixed key used for handling Audible <font SIZE="-1">AAX/AAX+</font> files. It has been pre-set so should not be necessary to specify.
<dt><b>decryption_key</b>
<dd> 16-byte key, in hex, to decrypt files encrypted using <font SIZE="-1">ISO</font> Common Encryption (<font SIZE="-1">CENC/AES-128 CTR</font>; <font SIZE="-1">ISO/IEC 23001-7</font>).</dl>
 

 <i>Audible </i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AAX</i></font><i></i> 

 Audible <font SIZE="-1">AAX</font> files are encrypted M4B files, and they can be decrypted by specifying a 4 byte activation secret. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -activation_bytes 1CEB00DA -i test.aax -vn -c:a copy output.mp4
</pre>

<h3>mpegts</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> transport stream demuxer. 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>resync_size</b>
<dd> Set size limit for looking up a new synchronization. Default value is 65536.
<dt><b>skip_unknown_pmt</b>
<dd> Skip PMTs for programs not defined in the <font SIZE="-1">PAT.</font> Default value is 0.
<dt><b>fix_teletext_pts</b>
<dd> Override teletext packet <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> values with the timestamps calculated from the <font SIZE="-1">PCR</font> of the first program which the teletext stream is part of and is not discarded. Default value is 1, set this option to 0 if you want your teletext packet <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> and <font SIZE="-1">DTS</font> values untouched.
<dt><b>ts_packetsize</b>
<dd> Output option carrying the raw packet size in bytes. Show the detected raw packet size, cannot be set by the user.
<dt><b>scan_all_pmts</b>
<dd> Scan and combine all PMTs. The value is an integer with value from -1 to 1 (-1 means automatic setting, 1 means enabled, 0 means disabled). Default value is -1.
<dt><b>merge_pmt_versions</b>
<dd> Re-use existing streams when a <font SIZE="-1">PMT</font>'s version is updated and elementary streams move to different PIDs. Default value is 0.</dl>

<h3>mpjpeg</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG</font> encapsulated in multi-part <font SIZE="-1">MIME</font> demuxer. 

 This demuxer allows reading of <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG,</font> where each frame is represented as a part of multipart/x-mixed-replace stream.
<dl>
<dt><b>strict_mime_boundary</b>
<dd> Default implementation applies a relaxed standard to multi-part <font SIZE="-1">MIME</font> boundary detection, to prevent regression with numerous existing endpoints not generating a proper <font SIZE="-1">MIME MJPEG</font> stream. Turning this option on by setting it to 1 will result in a stricter check of the boundary value.</dl>

<h3>rawvideo</h3>

 Raw video demuxer. 

 This demuxer allows one to read raw video data. Since there is no header specifying the assumed video parameters, the user must specify them in order to be able to decode the data correctly. 

 This demuxer accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>framerate</b>
<dd> Set input video frame rate. Default value is 25.
<dt><b>pixel_format</b>
<dd> Set the input video pixel format. Default value is <tt>&quot;yuv420p&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>video_size</b>
<dd> Set the input video size. This value must be specified explicitly.</dl>
 

 For example to read a rawvideo file <i>input.raw</i> with <b>ffplay</b>, assuming a pixel format of <tt>&quot;rgb24&quot;</tt>, a video size of <tt>&quot;320x240&quot;</tt>, and a frame rate of 10 images per second, use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffplay -f rawvideo -pixel_format rgb24 -video_size 320x240 -framerate 10 input.raw
</pre>

<h3>sbg</h3>

 SBaGen script demuxer. 

 This demuxer reads the script language used by SBaGen &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://uazu.net/sbagen/">http://uazu.net/sbagen/</a></b>&gt; to generate binaural beats sessions. A <font SIZE="-1">SBG</font> script looks like that: 

 
- SE
      a:300 - 2.5 / 3 440 + 4.5 / 0
      b:300 - 2.5 / 0 440 + 4.5 / 3
    off:-NOW == a +
      0:07
       :00 == b +
      0:14
       :00 == a +
      0:21
       :00 == b +
      0:30
       :00 off
 

 A <font SIZE="-1">SBG</font> script can mix absolute and relative timestamps. If the script uses either only absolute timestamps (including the script start time) or only relative ones, then its layout is fixed, and the conversion is straightforward. On the other hand, if the script mixes both kind of timestamps, then the <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>NOW</i></font><i></i> reference for relative timestamps will be taken from the current time of day at the time the script is read, and the script layout will be frozen according to that reference. That means that if the script is directly played, the actual times will match the absolute timestamps up to the sound controller's clock accuracy, but if the user somehow pauses the playback or seeks, all times will be shifted accordingly.

<h3>tedcaptions</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">JSON</font> captions used for &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.ted.com/">http://www.ted.com/</a></b>&gt;. 

 <font SIZE="-1">TED</font> does not provide links to the captions, but they can be guessed from the page. The file <i>tools/bookmarklets.html</i> from the FFmpeg source tree contains a bookmarklet to expose them. 

 This demuxer accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>start_time</b>
<dd> Set the start time of the <font SIZE="-1">TED</font> talk, in milliseconds. The default is 15000 (15s). It is used to sync the captions with the downloadable videos, because they include a 15s intro.</dl>
 

 Example: convert the captions to a format most players understand: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.ted.com/talks/subtitles/id/1/lang/en">http://www.ted.com/talks/subtitles/id/1/lang/en</a> talk1-en.srt
</pre>

<h3>vapoursynth</h3>

 Vapoursynth wrapper. 

 Due to security concerns, Vapoursynth scripts will not be autodetected so the input format has to be forced. For ff* <font SIZE="-1">CLI</font> tools, add <tt>&quot;-f vapoursynth&quot;</tt> before the input <tt>&quot;-i yourscript.vpy&quot;</tt>. 

 This demuxer accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>max_script_size</b>
<dd> The demuxer buffers the entire script into memory. Adjust this value to set the maximum buffer size, which in turn, acts as a ceiling for the size of scripts that can be read. Default is 1 MiB.</dl>

<h2>MUXERS</h2>

 Muxers are configured elements in FFmpeg which allow writing multimedia streams to a particular type of file. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported muxers are enabled by default. You can list all available muxers using the configure option <tt>&quot;--list-muxers&quot;</tt>. 

 You can disable all the muxers with the configure option <tt>&quot;--disable-muxers&quot;</tt> and selectively enable / disable single muxers with the options <tt>&quot;--enable-muxer=</tt>MUXER<tt>&quot;</tt> / <tt>&quot;--disable-muxer=</tt>MUXER<tt>&quot;</tt>. 

 The option <tt>&quot;-muxers&quot;</tt> of the ff* tools will display the list of enabled muxers. Use <tt>&quot;-formats&quot;</tt> to view a combined list of enabled demuxers and muxers. 

 A description of some of the currently available muxers follows.

<h3>aiff</h3>

 Audio Interchange File Format muxer. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>write_id3v2</b>
<dd> Enable ID3v2 tags writing when set to 1. Default is 0 (disabled).
<dt><b>id3v2_version</b>
<dd> Select ID3v2 version to write. Currently only version 3 and 4 (aka. ID3v2.3 and ID3v2.4) are supported. The default is version 4.</dl>

<h3>asf</h3>

 Advanced Systems Format muxer. 

 Note that Windows Media Audio (wma) and Windows Media Video (wmv) use this muxer too. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>packet_size</b>
<dd> Set the muxer packet size. By tuning this setting you may reduce data fragmentation or muxer overhead depending on your source. Default value is 3200, minimum is 100, maximum is 64k.</dl>

<h3>avi</h3>

 Audio Video Interleaved muxer. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>reserve_index_space</b>
<dd> Reserve the specified amount of bytes for the OpenDML master index of each stream within the file header. By default additional master indexes are embedded within the data packets if there is no space left in the first master index and are linked together as a chain of indexes. This index structure can cause problems for some use cases, e.g. third-party software strictly relying on the OpenDML index specification or when file seeking is slow. Reserving enough index space in the file header avoids these problems. 

 The required index space depends on the output file size and should be about 16 bytes per gigabyte. When this option is omitted or set to zero the necessary index space is guessed.
<dt><b>write_channel_mask</b>
<dd> Write the channel layout mask into the audio stream header. 

 This option is enabled by default. Disabling the channel mask can be useful in specific scenarios, e.g. when merging multiple audio streams into one for compatibility with software that only supports a single audio stream in <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> (see <b>the ``amerge'' section in the ffmpeg-filters manual</b>).
<dt><b>flipped_raw_rgb</b>
<dd> If set to true, store positive height for raw <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> bitmaps, which indicates bitmap is stored bottom-up. Note that this option does not flip the bitmap which has to be done manually beforehand, e.g. by using the vflip filter. Default is <i>false</i> and indicates bitmap is stored top down.</dl>

<h3>chromaprint</h3>

 Chromaprint fingerprinter. 

 This muxer feeds audio data to the Chromaprint library, which generates a fingerprint for the provided audio data. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://acoustid.org/chromaprint">https://acoustid.org/chromaprint</a></b>&gt; 

 It takes a single signed native-endian 16-bit raw audio stream of at most 2 channels. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>silence_threshold</b>
<dd> Threshold for detecting silence. Range is from -1 to 32767, where -1 disables silence detection. Silence detection can only be used with version 3 of the algorithm. Silence detection must be disabled for use with the AcoustID service. Default is -1.
<dt><b>algorithm</b>
<dd> Version of algorithm to fingerprint with. Range is 0 to 4. Version 3 enables silence detection. Default is 1.
<dt><b>fp_format</b>
<dd> Format to output the fingerprint as. Accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>raw</b>
<dd> Binary raw fingerprint
<dt><b>compressed</b>
<dd> Binary compressed fingerprint
<dt><b>base64</b>
<dd> Base64 compressed fingerprint <i>(default)</i></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>crc</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> (Cyclic Redundancy Check) testing format. 

 This muxer computes and prints the Adler-32 <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of all the input audio and video frames. By default audio frames are converted to signed 16-bit raw audio and video frames to raw video before computing the <font SIZE="-1">CRC.</font> 

 The output of the muxer consists of a single line of the form: CRC=0x<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CRC</i></font><i></i>, where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CRC</i></font><i></i> is a hexadecimal number 0-padded to 8 digits containing the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> for all the decoded input frames. 

 See also the <b>framecrc</b> muxer. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 For example to compute the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of the input, and store it in the file <i>out.crc</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f crc out.crc
</pre> 

 You can print the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> to stdout with the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f crc -
</pre> 

 You can select the output format of each frame with <b>ffmpeg</b> by specifying the audio and video codec and format. For example to compute the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of the input audio converted to <font SIZE="-1">PCM</font> unsigned 8-bit and the input video converted to <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> video, use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:a pcm_u8 -c:v mpeg2video -f crc -
</pre>

<h3>flv</h3>

 Adobe Flash Video Format muxer. 

 This muxer accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>flvflags</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>aac_seq_header_detect</b>
<dd> Place <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> sequence header based on audio stream data.
<dt><b>no_sequence_end</b>
<dd> Disable sequence end tag.
<dt><b>no_metadata</b>
<dd> Disable metadata tag.
<dt><b>no_duration_filesize</b>
<dd> Disable duration and filesize in metadata when they are equal to zero at the end of stream. (Be used to non-seekable living stream).
<dt><b>add_keyframe_index</b>
<dd> Used to facilitate seeking; particularly for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> pseudo streaming.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>dash</h3>

 Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">DASH</font>) muxer that creates segments and manifest files according to the MPEG-DASH standard <font SIZE="-1">ISO/IEC 23009-1:2014.</font> 

 For more information see:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">ISO DASH</font> Specification: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://standards.iso.org/ittf/PubliclyAvailableStandards/c065274_ISO_IEC_23009-1_2014.zip">http://standards.iso.org/ittf/PubliclyAvailableStandards/c065274_ISO_IEC_23009-1_2014.zip</a></b>&gt;
<dt>&bull;
<dd> WebM <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> Specification: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://sites.google.com/a/webmproject.org/wiki/adaptive-streaming/webm-dash-specification">https://sites.google.com/a/webmproject.org/wiki/adaptive-streaming/webm-dash-specification</a></b>&gt;</dl>
 

 It creates a <font SIZE="-1">MPD</font> manifest file and segment files for each stream. 

 The segment filename might contain pre-defined identifiers used with SegmentTemplate as defined in section 5.3.9.4.4 of the standard. Available identifiers are ``$RepresentationID$'', ``$Number$'', ``$Bandwidth$'' and ``$Time$''. In addition to the standard identifiers, an ffmpeg-specific ``$ext$'' identifier is also supported. When specified ffmpeg will replace <tt>$ext</tt>$ in the file name with muxing format's extensions such as mp4, webm etc., 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -map 0 -map 0 -c:a libfdk_aac -c:v libx264 \
        -b:v:0 800k -b:v:1 300k -s:v:1 320x170 -profile:v:1 baseline \
        -profile:v:0 main -bf 1 -keyint_min 120 -g 120 -sc_threshold 0 \
        -b_strategy 0 -ar:a:1 22050 -use_timeline 1 -use_template 1 \
        -window_size 5 -adaptation_sets &quot;id=0,streams=v id=1,streams=a&quot; \
        -f dash /path/to/out.mpd
</pre>
<dl>
<dt><b>min_seg_duration</b> <i>microseconds</i>
<dd> This is a deprecated option to set the segment length in microseconds, use <i>seg_duration</i> instead.
<dt><b>seg_duration</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Set the segment length in seconds (fractional value can be set). The value is treated as average segment duration when <i>use_template</i> is enabled and <i>use_timeline</i> is disabled and as minimum segment duration for all the other use cases.
<dt><b>frag_duration</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Set the length in seconds of fragments within segments (fractional value can be set).
<dt><b>frag_type</b> <i>type</i>
<dd> Set the type of interval for fragmentation.
<dt><b>window_size</b> <i>size</i>
<dd> Set the maximum number of segments kept in the manifest.
<dt><b>extra_window_size</b> <i>size</i>
<dd> Set the maximum number of segments kept outside of the manifest before removing from disk.
<dt><b>remove_at_exit</b> <i>remove</i>
<dd> Enable (1) or disable (0) removal of all segments when finished.
<dt><b>use_template</b> <i>template</i>
<dd> Enable (1) or disable (0) use of SegmentTemplate instead of SegmentList.
<dt><b>use_timeline</b> <i>timeline</i>
<dd> Enable (1) or disable (0) use of SegmentTimeline in SegmentTemplate.
<dt><b>single_file</b> <i>single_file</i>
<dd> Enable (1) or disable (0) storing all segments in one file, accessed using byte ranges.
<dt><b>single_file_name</b> <i>file_name</i>
