<dd> DASH-templated name to be used for baseURL. Implies <i>single_file</i> set to ``1''. In the template, ``$ext$'' is replaced with the file name extension specific for the segment format.
<dt><b>init_seg_name</b> <i>init_name</i>
<dd> DASH-templated name to used for the initialization segment. Default is ``init-stream$RepresentationID$.$ext$''. ``$ext$'' is replaced with the file name extension specific for the segment format.
<dt><b>media_seg_name</b> <i>segment_name</i>
<dd> DASH-templated name to used for the media segments. Default is ``chunk-stream$RepresentationID$-$Number%05d$.$ext$''. ``$ext$'' is replaced with the file name extension specific for the segment format.
<dt><b>utc_timing_url</b> <i>utc_url</i>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the page that will return the <font SIZE="-1">UTC</font> timestamp in <font SIZE="-1">ISO</font> format. Example: ``<a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://time.akamai.com/?iso''">https://time.akamai.com/?iso''</a>
<dt><b>method</b> <i>method</i>
<dd> Use the given <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method to create output files. Generally set to <font SIZE="-1">PUT</font> or <font SIZE="-1">POST.</font>
<dt><b>http_user_agent</b> <i>user_agent</i>
<dd> Override User-Agent field in <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> header. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.
<dt><b>http_persistent</b> <i>http_persistent</i>
<dd> Use persistent <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> connections. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.
<dt><b>hls_playlist</b> <i>hls_playlist</i>
<dd> Generate <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> playlist files as well. The master playlist is generated with the filename <i>hls_master_name</i>. One media playlist file is generated for each stream with filenames media_0.m3u8, media_1.m3u8, etc.
<dt><b>hls_master_name</b> <i>file_name</i>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> master playlist name. Default is ``master.m3u8''.
<dt><b>streaming</b> <i>streaming</i>
<dd> Enable (1) or disable (0) chunk streaming mode of output. In chunk streaming mode, each frame will be a moof fragment which forms a chunk.
<dt><b>adaptation_sets</b> <i>adaptation_sets</i>
<dd> Assign streams to AdaptationSets. Syntax is ``id=x,streams=a,b,c id=y,streams=d,e'' with x and y being the IDs of the adaptation sets and a,b,c,d and e are the indices of the mapped streams. 

 To map all video (or audio) streams to an AdaptationSet, ``v'' (or ``a'') can be used as stream identifier instead of IDs. 

 When no assignment is defined, this defaults to an AdaptationSet for each stream. 

 Optional syntax is ``id=x,seg_duration=x,frag_duration=x,frag_type=type,descriptor=descriptor_string,streams=a,b,c id=y,seg_duration=y,frag_type=type,streams=d,e'' and so on, descriptor is useful to the scheme defined by <font SIZE="-1">ISO/IEC</font> 23009-1:2014/Amd.2:2015. For example, -adaptation_sets ``id=0,descriptor=&lt;SupplementalProperty schemeIdUri=\''urn:mpeg:dash:srd:2014\`` value=\''0,0,0,1,1,2,2\``/&gt;,streams=v''. Please note that descriptor string should be a self-closing xml tag. seg_duration, frag_duration and frag_type override the global option values for each adaptation set. For example, -adaptation_sets ``id=0,seg_duration=2,frag_duration=1,frag_type=duration,streams=v id=1,seg_duration=2,frag_type=none,streams=a'' type_id marks an adaptation set as containing streams meant to be used for Trick Mode for the referenced adaptation set. For example, -adaptation_sets ``id=0,seg_duration=2,frag_type=none,streams=0 id=1,seg_duration=10,frag_type=none,trick_id=0,streams=1''
<dt><b>timeout</b> <i>timeout</i>
<dd> Set timeout for socket I/O operations. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.
<dt><b>index_correction</b> <i>index_correction</i>
<dd> Enable (1) or Disable (0) segment index correction logic. Applicable only when <i>use_template</i> is enabled and <i>use_timeline</i> is disabled. 

 When enabled, the logic monitors the flow of segment indexes. If a streams's segment index value is not at the expected real time position, then the logic corrects that index value. 

 Typically this logic is needed in live streaming use cases. The network bandwidth fluctuations are common during long run streaming. Each fluctuation can cause the segment indexes fall behind the expected real time position.
<dt><b>format_options</b> <i>options_list</i>
<dd> Set container format (mp4/webm) options using a <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> separated list of key=value parameters. Values containing <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> special characters must be escaped.
<dt><b>global_sidx</b> <i>global_sidx</i>
<dd> Write global <font SIZE="-1">SIDX</font> atom. Applicable only for single file, mp4 output, non-streaming mode.
<dt><b>dash_segment_type</b> <i>dash_segment_type</i>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> If this flag is set, the dash segment files format will be selected based on the stream codec. This is the default mode.
<dt><b>mp4</b>
<dd> If this flag is set, the dash segment files will be in in <font SIZE="-1">ISOBMFF</font> format.
<dt><b>webm</b>
<dd> If this flag is set, the dash segment files will be in in WebM format.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>ignore_io_errors</b> <i>ignore_io_errors</i>
<dd> Ignore <font SIZE="-1">IO</font> errors during open and write. Useful for long-duration runs with network output.
<dt><b>lhls</b> <i>lhls</i>
<dd> Enable Low-latency <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font>(<font SIZE="-1">LHLS</font>). Adds #EXT-X-PREFETCH tag with current segment's <font SIZE="-1">URI.</font> Apple doesn't have an official spec for <font SIZE="-1">LHLS.</font> Meanwhile hls.js player folks are trying to standardize a open <font SIZE="-1">LHLS</font> spec. The draft spec is available in <a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/video-dev/hlsjs-rfcs/blob/lhls-spec/proposals/0001-lhls.md">https://github.com/video-dev/hlsjs-rfcs/blob/lhls-spec/proposals/0001-lhls.md</a> This option will also try to comply with the above open spec, till Apple's spec officially supports it. Applicable only when <i>streaming</i> and <i>hls_playlist</i> options are enabled. This is an experimental feature.
<dt><b>ldash</b> <i>ldash</i>
<dd> Enable Low-latency Dash by constraining the presence and values of some elements.
<dt><b>master_m3u8_publish_rate</b> <i>master_m3u8_publish_rate</i>
<dd> Publish master playlist repeatedly every after specified number of segment intervals.
<dt><b>write_prft</b> <i>write_prft</i>
<dd> Write Producer Reference Time elements on supported streams. This also enables writing prft boxes in the underlying muxer. Applicable only when the <i>utc_url</i> option is enabled. It's set to auto by default, in which case the muxer will attempt to enable it only in modes that require it.
<dt><b>mpd_profile</b> <i>mpd_profile</i>
<dd> Set one or more manifest profiles.
<dt><b>http_opts</b> <i>http_opts</i>
<dd> A :-separated list of key=value options to pass to the underlying <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> protocol. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.
<dt><b>target_latency</b> <i>target_latency</i>
<dd> Set an intended target latency in seconds (fractional value can be set) for serving. Applicable only when <i>streaming</i> and <i>write_prft</i> options are enabled. This is an informative fields clients can use to measure the latency of the service.
<dt><b>min_playback_rate</b> <i>min_playback_rate</i>
<dd> Set the minimum playback rate indicated as appropriate for the purposes of automatically adjusting playback latency and buffer occupancy during normal playback by clients.
<dt><b>max_playback_rate</b> <i>max_playback_rate</i>
<dd> Set the maximum playback rate indicated as appropriate for the purposes of automatically adjusting playback latency and buffer occupancy during normal playback by clients.
<dt><b>update_period</b> <i>update_period</i>
<dd> <pre>
 Set the mpd update period ,for dynamic content.
 The unit is second.
</pre></dl>

<h3>framecrc</h3>

 Per-packet <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> (Cyclic Redundancy Check) testing format. 

 This muxer computes and prints the Adler-32 <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> for each audio and video packet. By default audio frames are converted to signed 16-bit raw audio and video frames to raw video before computing the <font SIZE="-1">CRC.</font> 

 The output of the muxer consists of a line for each audio and video packet of the form: 

 <pre>
        &lt;stream_index&gt;, &lt;packet_dts&gt;, &lt;packet_pts&gt;, &lt;packet_duration&gt;, &lt;packet_size&gt;, 0x&lt;CRC&gt;
</pre> 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CRC</i></font><i></i> is a hexadecimal number 0-padded to 8 digits containing the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of the packet. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 For example to compute the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of the audio and video frames in <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>INPUT</i></font><i></i>, converted to raw audio and video packets, and store it in the file <i>out.crc</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f framecrc out.crc
</pre> 

 To print the information to stdout, use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f framecrc -
</pre> 

 With <b>ffmpeg</b>, you can select the output format to which the audio and video frames are encoded before computing the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> for each packet by specifying the audio and video codec. For example, to compute the <font SIZE="-1">CRC</font> of each decoded input audio frame converted to <font SIZE="-1">PCM</font> unsigned 8-bit and of each decoded input video frame converted to <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> video, use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:a pcm_u8 -c:v mpeg2video -f framecrc -
</pre> 

 See also the <b>crc</b> muxer.

<h3>framehash</h3>

 Per-packet hash testing format. 

 This muxer computes and prints a cryptographic hash for each audio and video packet. This can be used for packet-by-packet equality checks without having to individually do a binary comparison on each. 

 By default audio frames are converted to signed 16-bit raw audio and video frames to raw video before computing the hash, but the output of explicit conversions to other codecs can also be used. It uses the <font SIZE="-1">SHA-256</font> cryptographic hash function by default, but supports several other algorithms. 

 The output of the muxer consists of a line for each audio and video packet of the form: 

 <pre>
        &lt;stream_index&gt;, &lt;packet_dts&gt;, &lt;packet_pts&gt;, &lt;packet_duration&gt;, &lt;packet_size&gt;, &lt;hash&gt;
</pre> 

 <i>hash</i> is a hexadecimal number representing the computed hash for the packet.
<dl>
<dt><b>hash</b> <i>algorithm</i>
<dd> Use the cryptographic hash function specified by the string <i>algorithm</i>. Supported values include <tt>&quot;MD5&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;murmur3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD128&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD160&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD256&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD320&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA160&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA224&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA256&quot;</tt> (default), <tt>&quot;SHA512/224&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA512/256&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA384&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA512&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;CRC32&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;adler32&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 To compute the <font SIZE="-1">SHA-256</font> hash of the audio and video frames in <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>INPUT</i></font><i></i>, converted to raw audio and video packets, and store it in the file <i>out.sha256</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f framehash out.sha256
</pre> 

 To print the information to stdout, using the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash function, use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f framehash -hash md5 -
</pre> 

 See also the <b>hash</b> muxer.

<h3>framemd5</h3>

 Per-packet <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> testing format. 

 This is a variant of the <b>framehash</b> muxer. Unlike that muxer, it defaults to using the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash function. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 To compute the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash of the audio and video frames in <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>INPUT</i></font><i></i>, converted to raw audio and video packets, and store it in the file <i>out.md5</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f framemd5 out.md5
</pre> 

 To print the information to stdout, use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f framemd5 -
</pre> 

 See also the <b>framehash</b> and <b>md5</b> muxers.

<h3>gif</h3>

 Animated <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> muxer. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>loop</b>
<dd> Set the number of times to loop the output. Use <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt> for no loop, <tt>0</tt> for looping indefinitely (default).
<dt><b>final_delay</b>
<dd> Force the delay (expressed in centiseconds) after the last frame. Each frame ends with a delay until the next frame. The default is <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt>, which is a special value to tell the muxer to re-use the previous delay. In case of a loop, you might want to customize this value to mark a pause for instance.</dl>
 

 For example, to encode a gif looping 10 times, with a 5 seconds delay between the loops: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -loop 10 -final_delay 500 out.gif
</pre> 

 Note 1: if you wish to extract the frames into separate <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> files, you need to force the <b>image2</b> muxer: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v gif -f image2 &quot;out%d.gif&quot;
</pre> 

 Note 2: the <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> format has a very large time base: the delay between two frames can therefore not be smaller than one centi second.

<h3>hash</h3>

 Hash testing format. 

 This muxer computes and prints a cryptographic hash of all the input audio and video frames. This can be used for equality checks without having to do a complete binary comparison. 

 By default audio frames are converted to signed 16-bit raw audio and video frames to raw video before computing the hash, but the output of explicit conversions to other codecs can also be used. Timestamps are ignored. It uses the <font SIZE="-1">SHA-256</font> cryptographic hash function by default, but supports several other algorithms. 

 The output of the muxer consists of a single line of the form: <i>algo</i>=<i>hash</i>, where <i>algo</i> is a short string representing the hash function used, and <i>hash</i> is a hexadecimal number representing the computed hash.
<dl>
<dt><b>hash</b> <i>algorithm</i>
<dd> Use the cryptographic hash function specified by the string <i>algorithm</i>. Supported values include <tt>&quot;MD5&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;murmur3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD128&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD160&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD256&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD320&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA160&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA224&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA256&quot;</tt> (default), <tt>&quot;SHA512/224&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA512/256&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA384&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA512&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;CRC32&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;adler32&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 To compute the <font SIZE="-1">SHA-256</font> hash of the input converted to raw audio and video, and store it in the file <i>out.sha256</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f hash out.sha256
</pre> 

 To print an <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash to stdout use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f hash -hash md5 -
</pre> 

 See also the <b>framehash</b> muxer.

<h3>hls</h3>

 Apple <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Live Streaming muxer that segments MPEG-TS according to the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Live Streaming (<font SIZE="-1">HLS</font>) specification. 

 It creates a playlist file, and one or more segment files. The output filename specifies the playlist filename. 

 By default, the muxer creates a file for each segment produced. These files have the same name as the playlist, followed by a sequential number and a .ts extension. 

 Make sure to require a closed <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> when encoding and to set the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size to fit your segment time constraint. 

 For example, to convert an input file with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -c:v h264 -flags +cgop -g 30 -hls_time 1 out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will produce the playlist, <i>out.m3u8</i>, and segment files: <i>out0.ts</i>, <i>out1.ts</i>, <i>out2.ts</i>, etc. 

 See also the <b>segment</b> muxer, which provides a more generic and flexible implementation of a segmenter, and can be used to perform <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> segmentation. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 This muxer supports the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>hls_init_time</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Set the initial target segment length. Default value is <i>0</i>. 

 <i>duration</i> must be a time duration specification, see <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b>. 

 Segment will be cut on the next key frame after this time has passed on the first m3u8 list. After the initial playlist is filled <b>ffmpeg</b> will cut segments at duration equal to <tt>&quot;hls_time&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>hls_time</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Set the target segment length. Default value is 2. 

 <i>duration</i> must be a time duration specification, see <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b>. Segment will be cut on the next key frame after this time has passed.
<dt><b>hls_list_size</b> <i>size</i>
<dd> Set the maximum number of playlist entries. If set to 0 the list file will contain all the segments. Default value is 5.
<dt><b>hls_delete_threshold</b> <i>size</i>
<dd> Set the number of unreferenced segments to keep on disk before <tt>&quot;hls_flags delete_segments&quot;</tt> deletes them. Increase this to allow continue clients to download segments which were recently referenced in the playlist. Default value is 1, meaning segments older than <tt>&quot;hls_list_size+1&quot;</tt> will be deleted.
<dt><b>hls_ts_options</b> <i>options_list</i>
<dd> Set output format options using a :-separated list of key=value parameters. Values containing <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> special characters must be escaped.
<dt><b>hls_wrap</b> <i>wrap</i>
<dd> This is a deprecated option, you can use <tt>&quot;hls_list_size&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;hls_flags delete_segments&quot;</tt> instead it 

 This option is useful to avoid to fill the disk with many segment files, and limits the maximum number of segment files written to disk to <i>wrap</i>.
<dt><b>hls_start_number_source</b>
<dd> Start the playlist sequence number (<tt>&quot;#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE&quot;</tt>) according to the specified source. Unless <tt>&quot;hls_flags single_file&quot;</tt> is set, it also specifies source of starting sequence numbers of segment and subtitle filenames. In any case, if <tt>&quot;hls_flags append_list&quot;</tt> is set and read playlist sequence number is greater than the specified start sequence number, then that value will be used as start value. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>generic (default)</b>
<dd> Set the starting sequence numbers according to <i>start_number</i> option value.
<dt><b>epoch</b>
<dd> The start number will be the seconds since epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00)
<dt><b>epoch_us</b>
<dd> The start number will be the microseconds since epoch (1970-01-01 00:00:00)
<dt><b>datetime</b>
<dd> The start number will be based on the current date/time as YYYYmmddHHMMSS. e.g. 20161231235759.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>start_number</b> <i>number</i>
<dd> Start the playlist sequence number (<tt>&quot;#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE&quot;</tt>) from the specified <i>number</i> when <i>hls_start_number_source</i> value is <i>generic</i>. (This is the default case.) Unless <tt>&quot;hls_flags single_file&quot;</tt> is set, it also specifies starting sequence numbers of segment and subtitle filenames. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>hls_allow_cache</b> <i>allowcache</i>
<dd> Explicitly set whether the client <font SIZE="-1">MAY</font> (1) or <font SIZE="-1">MUST NOT</font> (0) cache media segments.
<dt><b>hls_base_url</b> <i>baseurl</i>
<dd> Append <i>baseurl</i> to every entry in the playlist. Useful to generate playlists with absolute paths. 

 Note that the playlist sequence number must be unique for each segment and it is not to be confused with the segment filename sequence number which can be cyclic, for example if the <b>wrap</b> option is specified.
<dt><b>hls_segment_filename</b> <i>filename</i>
<dd> Set the segment filename. Unless <tt>&quot;hls_flags single_file&quot;</tt> is set, <i>filename</i> is used as a string format with the segment number: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.nut -hls_segment_filename 'file%03d.ts' out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will produce the playlist, <i>out.m3u8</i>, and segment files: <i>file000.ts</i>, <i>file001.ts</i>, <i>file002.ts</i>, etc. 

 <i>filename</i> may contain full path or relative path specification, but only the file name part without any path info will be contained in the m3u8 segment list. Should a relative path be specified, the path of the created segment files will be relative to the current working directory. When strftime_mkdir is set, the whole expanded value of <i>filename</i> will be written into the m3u8 segment list. 

 When <tt>&quot;var_stream_map&quot;</tt> is set with two or more variant streams, the <i>filename</i> pattern must contain the string ``%v'', this string specifies the position of variant stream index in the generated segment file names. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.ts -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 256k -b:a:0 64k -b:a:1 32k \
          -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:a -f hls -var_stream_map &quot;v:0,a:0 v:1,a:1&quot; \
          -hls_segment_filename 'file_%v_%03d.ts' out_%v.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will produce the playlists segment file sets: <i>file_0_000.ts</i>, <i>file_0_001.ts</i>, <i>file_0_002.ts</i>, etc. and <i>file_1_000.ts</i>, <i>file_1_001.ts</i>, <i>file_1_002.ts</i>, etc. 

 The string ``%v'' may be present in the filename or in the last directory name containing the file, but only in one of them. (Additionally, <tt>%v</tt> may appear multiple times in the last sub-directory or filename.) If the string <tt>%v</tt> is present in the directory name, then sub-directories are created after expanding the directory name pattern. This enables creation of segments corresponding to different variant streams in subdirectories. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.ts -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 256k -b:a:0 64k -b:a:1 32k \
          -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:a -f hls -var_stream_map &quot;v:0,a:0 v:1,a:1&quot; \
          -hls_segment_filename 'vs%v/file_%03d.ts' vs%v/out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will produce the playlists segment file sets: <i>vs0/file_000.ts</i>, <i>vs0/file_001.ts</i>, <i>vs0/file_002.ts</i>, etc. and <i>vs1/file_000.ts</i>, <i>vs1/file_001.ts</i>, <i>vs1/file_002.ts</i>, etc.
<dt><b>use_localtime</b>
<dd> Same as strftime option, will be deprecated.
<dt><b>strftime</b>
<dd> Use <b>strftime()</b> on <i>filename</i> to expand the segment filename with localtime. The segment number is also available in this mode, but to use it, you need to specify second_level_segment_index hls_flag and %%d will be the specifier. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.nut -strftime 1 -hls_segment_filename 'file-%Y%m%d-%s.ts' out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will produce the playlist, <i>out.m3u8</i>, and segment files: <i>file-20160215-1455569023.ts</i>, <i>file-20160215-1455569024.ts</i>, etc. Note: On some systems/environments, the <tt>%s</tt> specifier is not available. See 
&nbsp;<wbr>&nbsp;<tt>&quot;strftime()&quot;</tt>&nbsp;documentation. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.nut -strftime 1 -hls_flags second_level_segment_index -hls_segment_filename 'file-%Y%m%d-%%04d.ts' out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will produce the playlist, <i>out.m3u8</i>, and segment files: <i>file-20160215-0001.ts</i>, <i>file-20160215-0002.ts</i>, etc.
<dt><b>use_localtime_mkdir</b>
<dd> Same as strftime_mkdir option, will be deprecated .
<dt><b>strftime_mkdir</b>
<dd> Used together with -strftime_mkdir, it will create all subdirectories which is expanded in <i>filename</i>. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.nut -strftime 1 -strftime_mkdir 1 -hls_segment_filename '%Y%m%d/file-%Y%m%d-%s.ts' out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will create a directory 201560215 (if it does not exist), and then produce the playlist, <i>out.m3u8</i>, and segment files: <i>20160215/file-20160215-1455569023.ts</i>, <i>20160215/file-20160215-1455569024.ts</i>, etc. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.nut -strftime 1 -strftime_mkdir 1 -hls_segment_filename '%Y/%m/%d/file-%Y%m%d-%s.ts' out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example will create a directory hierarchy 2016/02/15 (if any of them do not exist), and then produce the playlist, <i>out.m3u8</i>, and segment files: <i>2016/02/15/file-20160215-1455569023.ts</i>, <i>2016/02/15/file-20160215-1455569024.ts</i>, etc.
<dt><b>hls_key_info_file</b> <i>key_info_file</i>
<dd> Use the information in <i>key_info_file</i> for segment encryption. The first line of <i>key_info_file</i> specifies the key <font SIZE="-1">URI</font> written to the playlist. The key <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> is used to access the encryption key during playback. The second line specifies the path to the key file used to obtain the key during the encryption process. The key file is read as a single packed array of 16 octets in binary format. The optional third line specifies the initialization vector (<font SIZE="-1">IV</font>) as a hexadecimal string to be used instead of the segment sequence number (default) for encryption. Changes to <i>key_info_file</i> will result in segment encryption with the new key/IV and an entry in the playlist for the new key <font SIZE="-1">URI/IV</font> if <tt>&quot;hls_flags periodic_rekey&quot;</tt> is enabled. 

 Key info file format: 

 <pre>
        &lt;key URI&gt;
        &lt;key file path&gt;
        &lt;IV&gt; (optional)
</pre> 

 Example key URIs: 

 <pre>
        <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://server/file.key">http://server/file.key</a>
        /path/to/file.key
        file.key
</pre> 

 Example key file paths: 

 <pre>
        file.key
        /path/to/file.key
</pre> 

 Example <font SIZE="-1">IV:</font> 

 <pre>
        0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
</pre> 

 Key info file example: 

 <pre>
        <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://server/file.key">http://server/file.key</a>
        /path/to/file.key
        0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
</pre> 

 Example shell script: 

 <pre>
        #!/bin/sh
        BASE_URL=${1:-'.'}
        openssl rand 16 &gt; file.key
        echo $BASE_URL/file.key &gt; file.keyinfo
        echo file.key &gt;&gt; file.keyinfo
        echo $(openssl rand -hex 16) &gt;&gt; file.keyinfo
        ffmpeg -f lavfi -re -i testsrc -c:v h264 -hls_flags delete_segments \
          -hls_key_info_file file.keyinfo out.m3u8
</pre>
<dt><b>-hls_enc</b> <i>enc</i>
<dd> Enable (1) or disable (0) the <font SIZE="-1">AES128</font> encryption. When enabled every segment generated is encrypted and the encryption key is saved as <i>playlist name</i>.key.
<dt><b>-hls_enc_key</b> <i>key</i>
<dd> 16-octet key to encrypt the segments, by default it is randomly generated.
<dt><b>-hls_enc_key_url</b> <i>keyurl</i>
<dd> If set, <i>keyurl</i> is prepended instead of <i>baseurl</i> to the key filename in the playlist.
<dt><b>-hls_enc_iv</b> <i>iv</i>
<dd> 16-octet initialization vector for every segment instead of the autogenerated ones.
<dt><b>hls_segment_type</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>mpegts</b>
<dd> Output segment files in <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> Transport Stream format. This is compatible with all <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> versions.
<dt><b>fmp4</b>
<dd> Output segment files in fragmented <font SIZE="-1">MP4</font> format, similar to MPEG-DASH. fmp4 files may be used in <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> version 7 and above.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>hls_fmp4_init_filename</b> <i>filename</i>
<dd> Set filename to the fragment files header file, default filename is <i>init.mp4</i>. 

 Use <tt>&quot;-strftime 1&quot;</tt> on <i>filename</i> to expand the segment filename with localtime. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.nut  -hls_segment_type fmp4 -strftime 1 -hls_fmp4_init_filename &quot;%s_init.mp4&quot; out.m3u8
</pre> 

 This will produce init like this <i>1602678741_init.mp4</i>
<dt><b>hls_fmp4_init_resend</b>
<dd> Resend init file after m3u8 file refresh every time, default is <i>0</i>. 

 When <tt>&quot;var_stream_map&quot;</tt> is set with two or more variant streams, the <i>filename</i> pattern must contain the string ``%v'', this string specifies the position of variant stream index in the generated init file names. The string ``%v'' may be present in the filename or in the last directory name containing the file. If the string is present in the directory name, then sub-directories are created after expanding the directory name pattern. This enables creation of init files corresponding to different variant streams in subdirectories.
<dt><b>hls_flags</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd> Possible values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>single_file</b>
<dd> If this flag is set, the muxer will store all segments in a single MPEG-TS file, and will use byte ranges in the playlist. <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> playlists generated with this way will have the version number 4. For example: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.nut -hls_flags single_file out.m3u8
</pre> 

 Will produce the playlist, <i>out.m3u8</i>, and a single segment file, <i>out.ts</i>.
<dt><b>delete_segments</b>
<dd> Segment files removed from the playlist are deleted after a period of time equal to the duration of the segment plus the duration of the playlist.
<dt><b>append_list</b>
<dd> Append new segments into the end of old segment list, and remove the <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-ENDLIST&quot;</tt> from the old segment list.
<dt><b>round_durations</b>
<dd> Round the duration info in the playlist file segment info to integer values, instead of using floating point.
<dt><b>discont_start</b>
<dd> Add the <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY&quot;</tt> tag to the playlist, before the first segment's information.
<dt><b>omit_endlist</b>
<dd> Do not append the <tt>&quot;EXT-X-ENDLIST&quot;</tt> tag at the end of the playlist.
<dt><b>periodic_rekey</b>
<dd> The file specified by <tt>&quot;hls_key_info_file&quot;</tt> will be checked periodically and detect updates to the encryption info. Be sure to replace this file atomically, including the file containing the <font SIZE="-1">AES</font> encryption key.
<dt><b>independent_segments</b>
<dd> Add the <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS&quot;</tt> to playlists that has video segments and when all the segments of that playlist are guaranteed to start with a Key frame.
<dt><b>iframes_only</b>
<dd> Add the <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-I-FRAMES-ONLY&quot;</tt> to playlists that has video segments and can play only I-frames in the <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-BYTERANGE&quot;</tt> mode.
<dt><b>split_by_time</b>
<dd> Allow segments to start on frames other than keyframes. This improves behavior on some players when the time between keyframes is inconsistent, but may make things worse on others, and can cause some oddities during seeking. This flag should be used with the <tt>&quot;hls_time&quot;</tt> option.
<dt><b>program_date_time</b>
<dd> Generate <tt>&quot;EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME&quot;</tt> tags.
<dt><b>second_level_segment_index</b>
<dd> Makes it possible to use segment indexes as %%d in hls_segment_filename expression besides date/time values when strftime is on. To get fixed width numbers with trailing zeroes, %%0xd format is available where x is the required width.
<dt><b>second_level_segment_size</b>
<dd> Makes it possible to use segment sizes (counted in bytes) as %%s in hls_segment_filename expression besides date/time values when strftime is on. To get fixed width numbers with trailing zeroes, %%0xs format is available where x is the required width.
<dt><b>second_level_segment_duration</b>
<dd> Makes it possible to use segment duration (calculated in microseconds) as %%t in hls_segment_filename expression besides date/time values when strftime is on. To get fixed width numbers with trailing zeroes, %%0xt format is available where x is the required width. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i sample.mpeg \
           -f hls -hls_time 3 -hls_list_size 5 \
           -hls_flags second_level_segment_index+second_level_segment_size+second_level_segment_duration \
           -strftime 1 -strftime_mkdir 1 -hls_segment_filename &quot;segment_%Y%m%d%H%M%S_%%04d_%%08s_%%013t.ts&quot; stream.m3u8
</pre> 

 This will produce segments like this: <i>segment_20170102194334_0003_00122200_0000003000000.ts</i>, <i>segment_20170102194334_0004_00120072_0000003000000.ts</i> etc.
<dt><b>temp_file</b>
<dd> Write segment data to filename.tmp and rename to filename only once the segment is complete. A webserver serving up segments can be configured to reject requests to *.tmp to prevent access to in-progress segments before they have been added to the m3u8 playlist. This flag also affects how m3u8 playlist files are created. If this flag is set, all playlist files will written into temporary file and renamed after they are complete, similarly as segments are handled. But playlists with <tt>&quot;file&quot;</tt> protocol and with type (<tt>&quot;hls_playlist_type&quot;</tt>) other than <tt>&quot;vod&quot;</tt> are always written into temporary file regardless of this flag. Master playlist files (<tt>&quot;master_pl_name&quot;</tt>), if any, with <tt>&quot;file&quot;</tt> protocol, are always written into temporary file regardless of this flag if <tt>&quot;master_pl_publish_rate&quot;</tt> value is other than zero.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>hls_playlist_type event</b>
<dd> Emit <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:EVENT&quot;</tt> in the m3u8 header. Forces <b>hls_list_size</b> to 0; the playlist can only be appended to.
<dt><b>hls_playlist_type vod</b>
<dd> Emit <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD&quot;</tt> in the m3u8 header. Forces <b>hls_list_size</b> to 0; the playlist must not change.
<dt><b>method</b>
<dd> Use the given <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method to create the hls files. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -f hls -method PUT <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example will upload all the mpegts segment files to the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server using the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP PUT</font> method, and update the m3u8 files every <tt>&quot;refresh&quot;</tt> times using the same method. Note that the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server must support the given method for uploading files.
<dt><b>http_user_agent</b>
<dd> Override User-Agent field in <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> header. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.
<dt><b>var_stream_map</b>
<dd> Map string which specifies how to group the audio, video and subtitle streams into different variant streams. The variant stream groups are separated by space. Expected string format is like this ``a:0,v:0 a:1,v:1 ....''. Here a:, v:, s: are the keys to specify audio, video and subtitle streams respectively. Allowed values are 0 to 9 (limited just based on practical usage). 

 When there are two or more variant streams, the output filename pattern must contain the string ``%v'', this string specifies the position of variant stream index in the output media playlist filenames. The string ``%v'' may be present in the filename or in the last directory name containing the file. If the string is present in the directory name, then sub-directories are created after expanding the directory name pattern. This enables creation of variant streams in subdirectories. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 256k -b:a:0 64k -b:a:1 32k \
          -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:a -f hls -var_stream_map &quot;v:0,a:0 v:1,a:1&quot; \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates two hls variant streams. The first variant stream will contain video stream of bitrate 1000k and audio stream of bitrate 64k and the second variant stream will contain video stream of bitrate 256k and audio stream of bitrate 32k. Here, two media playlist with file names out_0.m3u8 and out_1.m3u8 will be created. If you want something meaningful text instead of indexes in result names, you may specify names for each or some of the variants as in the following example. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 256k -b:a:0 64k -b:a:1 32k \
          -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:a -f hls -var_stream_map &quot;v:0,a:0,name:my_hd v:1,a:1,name:my_sd&quot; \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates two hls variant streams as in the previous one. But here, the two media playlist with file names out_my_hd.m3u8 and out_my_sd.m3u8 will be created. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 256k -b:a:0 64k \
          -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -f hls -var_stream_map &quot;v:0 a:0 v:1&quot; \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates three hls variant streams. The first variant stream will be a video only stream with video bitrate 1000k, the second variant stream will be an audio only stream with bitrate 64k and the third variant stream will be a video only stream with bitrate 256k. Here, three media playlist with file names out_0.m3u8, out_1.m3u8 and out_2.m3u8 will be created. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 256k -b:a:0 64k -b:a:1 32k \
          -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:a -f hls -var_stream_map &quot;v:0,a:0 v:1,a:1&quot; \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/vs_%v/out.m3u8">http://example.com/live/vs_%v/out.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates the variant streams in subdirectories. Here, the first media playlist is created at <i><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/vs_0/out.m3u8">http://example.com/live/vs_0/out.m3u8</a></i> and the second one at <i><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/vs_1/out.m3u8">http://example.com/live/vs_1/out.m3u8</a></i>. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:a:0 32k -b:a:1 64k -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 3000k  \
          -map 0:a -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:v -f hls \
          -var_stream_map &quot;a:0,agroup:aud_low a:1,agroup:aud_high v:0,agroup:aud_low v:1,agroup:aud_high&quot; \
          -master_pl_name master.m3u8 \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates two audio only and two video only variant streams. In addition to the #EXT-X-STREAM-INF tag for each variant stream in the master playlist, #EXT-X-MEDIA tag is also added for the two audio only variant streams and they are mapped to the two video only variant streams with audio group names 'aud_low' and 'aud_high'. 

 By default, a single hls variant containing all the encoded streams is created. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:a:0 32k -b:a:1 64k -b:v:0 1000k \
          -map 0:a -map 0:a -map 0:v -f hls \
          -var_stream_map &quot;a:0,agroup:aud_low,default:yes a:1,agroup:aud_low v:0,agroup:aud_low&quot; \
          -master_pl_name master.m3u8 \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates two audio only and one video only variant streams. In addition to the #EXT-X-STREAM-INF tag for each variant stream in the master playlist, #EXT-X-MEDIA tag is also added for the two audio only variant streams and they are mapped to the one video only variant streams with audio group name 'aud_low', and the audio group have default stat is <font SIZE="-1">NO</font> or <font SIZE="-1">YES.</font> 

 By default, a single hls variant containing all the encoded streams is created. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:a:0 32k -b:a:1 64k -b:v:0 1000k \
          -map 0:a -map 0:a -map 0:v -f hls \
          -var_stream_map &quot;a:0,agroup:aud_low,default:yes,language:ENG a:1,agroup:aud_low,language:CHN v:0,agroup:aud_low&quot; \
          -master_pl_name master.m3u8 \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates two audio only and one video only variant streams. In addition to the #EXT-X-STREAM-INF tag for each variant stream in the master playlist, #EXT-X-MEDIA tag is also added for the two audio only variant streams and they are mapped to the one video only variant streams with audio group name 'aud_low', and the audio group have default stat is <font SIZE="-1">NO</font> or <font SIZE="-1">YES,</font> and one audio have and language is named <font SIZE="-1">ENG,</font> the other audio language is named <font SIZE="-1">CHN.</font> 

 By default, a single hls variant containing all the encoded streams is created. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -y -i input_with_subtitle.mkv \
         -b:v:0 5250k -c:v h264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -profile:v main -level 4.1 \
         -b:a:0 256k \
         -c:s webvtt -c:a mp2 -ar 48000 -ac 2 -map 0:v -map 0:a:0 -map 0:s:0 \
         -f hls -var_stream_map &quot;v:0,a:0,s:0,sgroup:subtitle&quot; \
         -master_pl_name master.m3u8 -t 300 -hls_time 10 -hls_init_time 4 -hls_list_size \
         10 -master_pl_publish_rate 10  -hls_flags \
         delete_segments+discont_start+split_by_time ./tmp/video.m3u8
</pre> 

 This example adds <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-MEDIA&quot;</tt> tag with <tt>&quot;TYPE=SUBTITLES&quot;</tt> in the master playlist with webvtt subtitle group name 'subtitle'. Please make sure the input file has one text subtitle stream at least.
<dt><b>cc_stream_map</b>
<dd> Map string which specifies different closed captions groups and their attributes. The closed captions stream groups are separated by space. Expected string format is like this ``ccgroup:&lt;group name&gt;,instreamid:&lt;<font SIZE="-1">INSTREAM-ID</font>&gt;,language:&lt;language code&gt; ....''. 'ccgroup' and 'instreamid' are mandatory attributes. 'language' is an optional attribute. The closed captions groups configured using this option are mapped to different variant streams by providing the same 'ccgroup' name in the <tt>&quot;var_stream_map&quot;</tt> string. If <tt>&quot;var_stream_map&quot;</tt> is not set, then the first available ccgroup in <tt>&quot;cc_stream_map&quot;</tt> is mapped to the output variant stream. The examples for these two use cases are given below. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:v 1000k -b:a 64k -a53cc 1 -f hls \
          -cc_stream_map &quot;ccgroup:cc,instreamid:CC1,language:en&quot; \
          -master_pl_name master.m3u8 \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example adds <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-MEDIA&quot;</tt> tag with <tt>&quot;TYPE=CLOSED-CAPTIONS&quot;</tt> in the master playlist with group name 'cc', language 'en' (english) and INSTREAM-ID '<font SIZE="-1">CC1</font>'. Also, it adds <tt>&quot;CLOSED-CAPTIONS&quot;</tt> attribute with group name 'cc' for the output variant stream. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -b:v:0 1000k -b:v:1 256k -b:a:0 64k -b:a:1 32k \
          -a53cc:0 1 -a53cc:1 1\
          -map 0:v -map 0:a -map 0:v -map 0:a -f hls \
          -cc_stream_map &quot;ccgroup:cc,instreamid:CC1,language:en ccgroup:cc,instreamid:CC2,language:sp&quot; \
          -var_stream_map &quot;v:0,a:0,ccgroup:cc v:1,a:1,ccgroup:cc&quot; \
          -master_pl_name master.m3u8 \
          <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out_%v.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example adds two <tt>&quot;#EXT-X-MEDIA&quot;</tt> tags with <tt>&quot;TYPE=CLOSED-CAPTIONS&quot;</tt> in the master playlist for the INSTREAM-IDs '<font SIZE="-1">CC1</font>' and '<font SIZE="-1">CC2</font>'. Also, it adds <tt>&quot;CLOSED-CAPTIONS&quot;</tt> attribute with group name 'cc' for the two output variant streams.
<dt><b>master_pl_name</b>
<dd> Create <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> master playlist with the given name. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -f hls -master_pl_name master.m3u8 <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> master playlist with name master.m3u8 and it is published at <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/">http://example.com/live/</a>
<dt><b>master_pl_publish_rate</b>
<dd> Publish master play list repeatedly every after specified number of segment intervals. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.ts -f hls -master_pl_name master.m3u8 \
        -hls_time 2 -master_pl_publish_rate 30 <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/live/out.m3u8">http://example.com/live/out.m3u8</a>
</pre> 

 This example creates <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> master playlist with name master.m3u8 and keep publishing it repeatedly every after 30 segments i.e. every after 60s.
<dt><b>http_persistent</b>
<dd> Use persistent <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> connections. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd> Set timeout for socket I/O operations. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.
<dt><b>-ignore_io_errors</b>
<dd> Ignore <font SIZE="-1">IO</font> errors during open, write and delete. Useful for long-duration runs with network output.
<dt><b>headers</b>
<dd> Set custom <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> headers, can override built in default headers. Applicable only for <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> output.</dl>

<h3>ico</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">ICO</font> file muxer. 

 Microsoft's icon file format (<font SIZE="-1">ICO</font>) has some strict limitations that should be noted:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Size cannot exceed 256 pixels in any dimension
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Only <font SIZE="-1">BMP</font> and <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> images can be stored
<dt>&bull;
<dd> If a <font SIZE="-1">BMP</font> image is used, it must be one of the following pixel formats: 

 <pre>
        BMP Bit Depth      FFmpeg Pixel Format
        1bit               pal8
        4bit               pal8
        8bit               pal8
        16bit              rgb555le
        24bit              bgr24
        32bit              bgra
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> If a <font SIZE="-1">BMP</font> image is used, it must use the <font SIZE="-1">BITMAPINFOHEADER DIB</font> header
<dt>&bull;
<dd> If a <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> image is used, it must use the rgba pixel format</dl>

<h3>image2</h3>

 Image file muxer. 

 The image file muxer writes video frames to image files. 

 The output filenames are specified by a pattern, which can be used to produce sequentially numbered series of files. The pattern may contain the string ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d``, this string specifies the position of the characters representing a numbering in the filenames. If the form ''%0<i>N</i>d&quot; is used, the string representing the number in each filename is 0-padded to <i>N</i> digits. The literal character '%' can be specified in the pattern with the string ``%%''. 

 If the pattern contains ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d&quot;, the first filename of the file list specified will contain the number 1, all the following numbers will be sequential. 

 The pattern may contain a suffix which is used to automatically determine the format of the image files to write. 

 For example the pattern ``img-%03d.bmp'' will specify a sequence of filenames of the form <i>img-001.bmp</i>, <i>img-002.bmp</i>, ..., <i>img-010.bmp</i>, etc. The pattern ``img%%-%d.jpg'' will specify a sequence of filenames of the form <i>img%-1.jpg</i>, <i>img%-2.jpg</i>, ..., <i>img%-10.jpg</i>, etc. 

 The image muxer supports the .Y.U.V image file format. This format is special in that that each image frame consists of three files, for each of the <font SIZE="-1">YUV420P</font> components. To read or write this image file format, specify the name of the '.Y' file. The muxer will automatically open the '.U' and '.V' files as required. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>frame_pts</b>
<dd> If set to 1, expand the filename with pts from pkt-&gt;pts. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>start_number</b>
<dd> Start the sequence from the specified number. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>update</b>
<dd> If set to 1, the filename will always be interpreted as just a filename, not a pattern, and the corresponding file will be continuously overwritten with new images. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>strftime</b>
<dd> If set to 1, expand the filename with date and time information from <tt>&quot;strftime()&quot;</tt>. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>protocol_opts</b> <i>options_list</i>
<dd> Set protocol options as a :-separated list of key=value parameters. Values containing the <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> special character must be escaped.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 The following example shows how to use <b>ffmpeg</b> for creating a sequence of files <i>img-001.jpeg</i>, <i>img-002.jpeg</i>, ..., taking one image every second from the input video: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.avi -vsync cfr -r 1 -f image2 'img-%03d.jpeg'
</pre> 

 Note that with <b>ffmpeg</b>, if the format is not specified with the <tt>&quot;-f&quot;</tt> option and the output filename specifies an image file format, the image2 muxer is automatically selected, so the previous command can be written as: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.avi -vsync cfr -r 1 'img-%03d.jpeg'
</pre> 

 Note also that the pattern must not necessarily contain ``%d'' or &quot;%0<i>N</i>d&quot;, for example to create a single image file <i>img.jpeg</i> from the start of the input video you can employ the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.avi -f image2 -frames:v 1 img.jpeg
</pre> 

 The <b>strftime</b> option allows you to expand the filename with date and time information. Check the documentation of the <tt>&quot;strftime()&quot;</tt> function for the syntax. 

 For example to generate image files from the <tt>&quot;strftime()&quot;</tt> ``%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S'' pattern, the following <b>ffmpeg</b> command can be used: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f v4l2 -r 1 -i /dev/video0 -f image2 -strftime 1 &quot;%Y-%m-%d_%H-%M-%S.jpg&quot;
</pre> 

 You can set the file name with current frame's <font SIZE="-1">PTS:</font> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f v4l2 -r 1 -i /dev/video0 -copyts -f image2 -frame_pts true %d.jpg&quot;
</pre> 

 A more complex example is to publish contents of your desktop directly to a WebDAV server every second: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f x11grab -framerate 1 -i :0.0 -q:v 6 -update 1 -protocol_opts method=PUT <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com/desktop.jpg">http://example.com/desktop.jpg</a>
</pre>

<h3>matroska</h3>

 Matroska container muxer. 

 This muxer implements the matroska and webm container specs. 

 <i>Metadata</i> 

 The recognized metadata settings in this muxer are:
<dl>
<dt><b>title</b>
<dd> Set title name provided to a single track. This gets mapped to the FileDescription element for a stream written as attachment.
<dt><b>language</b>
<dd> Specify the language of the track in the Matroska languages form. 

 The language can be either the 3 letters bibliographic <font SIZE="-1">ISO-639-2</font> (<font SIZE="-1">ISO 639-2/B</font>) form (like ``fre'' for French), or a language code mixed with a country code for specialities in languages (like ``fre-ca'' for Canadian French).
<dt><b>stereo_mode</b>
<dd> Set stereo 3D video layout of two views in a single video track. 

 The following values are recognized:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>mono</b>
<dd> video is not stereo
<dt><b>left_right</b>
<dd> Both views are arranged side by side, Left-eye view is on the left
<dt><b>bottom_top</b>
<dd> Both views are arranged in top-bottom orientation, Left-eye view is at bottom
<dt><b>top_bottom</b>
<dd> Both views are arranged in top-bottom orientation, Left-eye view is on top
<dt><b>checkerboard_rl</b>
<dd> Each view is arranged in a checkerboard interleaved pattern, Left-eye view being first
<dt><b>checkerboard_lr</b>
<dd> Each view is arranged in a checkerboard interleaved pattern, Right-eye view being first
<dt><b>row_interleaved_rl</b>
<dd> Each view is constituted by a row based interleaving, Right-eye view is first row
<dt><b>row_interleaved_lr</b>
<dd> Each view is constituted by a row based interleaving, Left-eye view is first row
<dt><b>col_interleaved_rl</b>
<dd> Both views are arranged in a column based interleaving manner, Right-eye view is first column
<dt><b>col_interleaved_lr</b>
<dd> Both views are arranged in a column based interleaving manner, Left-eye view is first column
<dt><b>anaglyph_cyan_red</b>
<dd> All frames are in anaglyph format viewable through red-cyan filters
<dt><b>right_left</b>
<dd> Both views are arranged side by side, Right-eye view is on the left
<dt><b>anaglyph_green_magenta</b>
<dd> All frames are in anaglyph format viewable through green-magenta filters
<dt><b>block_lr</b>
<dd> Both eyes laced in one Block, Left-eye view is first
<dt><b>block_rl</b>
<dd> Both eyes laced in one Block, Right-eye view is first</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 For example a 3D WebM clip can be created using the following command line: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i sample_left_right_clip.mpg -an -c:v libvpx -metadata stereo_mode=left_right -y stereo_clip.webm
</pre> 

 <i>Options</i> 

 This muxer supports the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>reserve_index_space</b>
<dd> By default, this muxer writes the index for seeking (called cues in Matroska terms) at the end of the file, because it cannot know in advance how much space to leave for the index at the beginning of the file. However for some use cases --- e.g. streaming where seeking is possible but slow --- it is useful to put the index at the beginning of the file. 

 If this option is set to a non-zero value, the muxer will reserve a given amount of space in the file header and then try to write the cues there when the muxing finishes. If the reserved space does not suffice, no Cues will be written, the file will be finalized and writing the trailer will return an error. A safe size for most use cases should be about 50kB per hour of video. 

 Note that cues are only written if the output is seekable and this option will have no effect if it is not.
<dt><b>default_mode</b>
<dd> This option controls how the FlagDefault of the output tracks will be set. It influences which tracks players should play by default. The default mode is <b>infer</b>.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>infer</b>
<dd> In this mode, for each type of track (audio, video or subtitle), if there is a track with disposition default of this type, then the first such track (i.e. the one with the lowest index) will be marked as default; if no such track exists, the first track of this type will be marked as default instead (if existing). This ensures that the default flag is set in a sensible way even if the input originated from containers that lack the concept of default tracks.
<dt><b>infer_no_subs</b>
<dd> This mode is the same as infer except that if no subtitle track with disposition default exists, no subtitle track will be marked as default.
<dt><b>passthrough</b>
<dd> In this mode the FlagDefault is set if and only if the <font SIZE="-1">AV_DISPOSITION_DEFAULT</font> flag is set in the disposition of the corresponding stream.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>flipped_raw_rgb</b>
<dd> If set to true, store positive height for raw <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> bitmaps, which indicates bitmap is stored bottom-up. Note that this option does not flip the bitmap which has to be done manually beforehand, e.g. by using the vflip filter. Default is <i>false</i> and indicates bitmap is stored top down.</dl>

<h3>md5</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> testing format. 

 This is a variant of the <b>hash</b> muxer. Unlike that muxer, it defaults to using the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash function. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 To compute the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash of the input converted to raw audio and video, and store it in the file <i>out.md5</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f md5 out.md5
</pre> 

 You can print the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> to stdout with the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f md5 -
</pre> 

 See also the <b>hash</b> and <b>framemd5</b> muxers.

<h3>mov, mp4, ismv</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4/ISMV</font> (Smooth Streaming) muxer. 

 The mov/mp4/ismv muxer supports fragmentation. Normally, a <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> file has all the metadata about all packets stored in one location (written at the end of the file, it can be moved to the start for better playback by adding <i>faststart</i> to the <i>movflags</i>, or using the <b>qt-faststart</b> tool). A fragmented file consists of a number of fragments, where packets and metadata about these packets are stored together. Writing a fragmented file has the advantage that the file is decodable even if the writing is interrupted (while a normal <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> is undecodable if it is not properly finished), and it requires less memory when writing very long files (since writing normal <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> files stores info about every single packet in memory until the file is closed). The downside is that it is less compatible with other applications. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 Fragmentation is enabled by setting one of the AVOptions that define how to cut the file into fragments:
<dl>
<dt><b>-moov_size</b> <i>bytes</i>
<dd> Reserves space for the moov atom at the beginning of the file instead of placing the moov atom at the end. If the space reserved is insufficient, muxing will fail.
<dt><b>-movflags frag_keyframe</b>
<dd> Start a new fragment at each video keyframe.
<dt><b>-frag_duration</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Create fragments that are <i>duration</i> microseconds long.
<dt><b>-frag_size</b> <i>size</i>
<dd> Create fragments that contain up to <i>size</i> bytes of payload data.
<dt><b>-movflags frag_custom</b>
<dd> Allow the caller to manually choose when to cut fragments, by calling <tt>&quot;av_write_frame(ctx, NULL)&quot;</tt> to write a fragment with the packets written so far. (This is only useful with other applications integrating libavformat, not from <b>ffmpeg</b>.)
<dt><b>-min_frag_duration</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Don't create fragments that are shorter than <i>duration</i> microseconds long.</dl>
 

 If more than one condition is specified, fragments are cut when one of the specified conditions is fulfilled. The exception to this is <tt>&quot;-min_frag_duration&quot;</tt>, which has to be fulfilled for any of the other conditions to apply. 

 Additionally, the way the output file is written can be adjusted through a few other options:
<dl>
<dt><b>-movflags empty_moov</b>
<dd> Write an initial moov atom directly at the start of the file, without describing any samples in it. Generally, an mdat/moov pair is written at the start of the file, as a normal <font SIZE="-1">MOV/MP4</font> file, containing only a short portion of the file. With this option set, there is no initial mdat atom, and the moov atom only describes the tracks but has a zero duration. 

 This option is implicitly set when writing ismv (Smooth Streaming) files.
<dt><b>-movflags separate_moof</b>
<dd> Write a separate moof (movie fragment) atom for each track. Normally, packets for all tracks are written in a moof atom (which is slightly more efficient), but with this option set, the muxer writes one moof/mdat pair for each track, making it easier to separate tracks. 

 This option is implicitly set when writing ismv (Smooth Streaming) files.
<dt><b>-movflags skip_sidx</b>
<dd> Skip writing of sidx atom. When bitrate overhead due to sidx atom is high, this option could be used for cases where sidx atom is not mandatory. When global_sidx flag is enabled, this option will be ignored.
<dt><b>-movflags faststart</b>
<dd> Run a second pass moving the index (moov atom) to the beginning of the file. This operation can take a while, and will not work in various situations such as fragmented output, thus it is not enabled by default.
<dt><b>-movflags rtphint</b>
<dd> Add <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> hinting tracks to the output file.
<dt><b>-movflags disable_chpl</b>
<dd> Disable Nero chapter markers (chpl atom). Normally, both Nero chapters and a QuickTime chapter track are written to the file. With this option set, only the QuickTime chapter track will be written. Nero chapters can cause failures when the file is reprocessed with certain tagging programs, like mp3Tag 2.61a and iTunes 11.3, most likely other versions are affected as well.
<dt><b>-movflags omit_tfhd_offset</b>
<dd> Do not write any absolute base_data_offset in tfhd atoms. This avoids tying fragments to absolute byte positions in the file/streams.
<dt><b>-movflags default_base_moof</b>
<dd> Similarly to the omit_tfhd_offset, this flag avoids writing the absolute base_data_offset field in tfhd atoms, but does so by using the new default-base-is-moof flag instead. This flag is new from 14496-12:2012. This may make the fragments easier to parse in certain circumstances (avoiding basing track fragment location calculations on the implicit end of the previous track fragment).
<dt><b>-write_tmcd</b>
<dd> Specify <tt>&quot;on&quot;</tt> to force writing a timecode track, <tt>&quot;off&quot;</tt> to disable it and <tt>&quot;auto&quot;</tt> to write a timecode track only for mov and mp4 output (default).
<dt><b>-movflags negative_cts_offsets</b>
<dd> Enables utilization of version 1 of the <font SIZE="-1">CTTS</font> box, in which the <font SIZE="-1">CTS</font> offsets can be negative. This enables the initial sample to have <font SIZE="-1">DTS/CTS</font> of zero, and reduces the need for edit lists for some cases such as video tracks with B-frames. Additionally, eases conformance with the DASH-IF interoperability guidelines. 

 This option is implicitly set when writing ismv (Smooth Streaming) files.
<dt><b>-write_prft</b>
<dd> Write producer time reference box (<font SIZE="-1">PRFT</font>) with a specified time source for the <font SIZE="-1">NTP</font> field in the <font SIZE="-1">PRFT</font> box. Set value as <b>wallclock</b> to specify timesource as wallclock time and <b>pts</b> to specify timesource as input packets' <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> values. 

 Setting value to <b>pts</b> is applicable only for a live encoding use case, where <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> values are set as as wallclock time at the source. For example, an encoding use case with decklink capture source where <b>video_pts</b> and <b>audio_pts</b> are set to <b>abs_wallclock</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Example</i> 

 Smooth Streaming content can be pushed in real time to a publishing point on <font SIZE="-1">IIS</font> with this muxer. Example: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re &lt;&lt;normal input/transcoding options&gt;&gt; -movflags isml+frag_keyframe -f ismv <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://server/publishingpoint.isml/Streams(Encoder1)">http://server/publishingpoint.isml/Streams(Encoder1)</a>
</pre>

<h3>mp3</h3>

 The <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> muxer writes a raw <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> stream with the following optional features:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> An ID3v2 metadata header at the beginning (enabled by default). Versions 2.3 and 2.4 are supported, the <tt>&quot;id3v2_version&quot;</tt> private option controls which one is used (3 or 4). Setting <tt>&quot;id3v2_version&quot;</tt> to 0 disables the ID3v2 header completely. 

 The muxer supports writing attached pictures (<font SIZE="-1">APIC</font> frames) to the ID3v2 header. The pictures are supplied to the muxer in form of a video stream with a single packet. There can be any number of those streams, each will correspond to a single <font SIZE="-1">APIC</font> frame. The stream metadata tags <i>title</i> and <i>comment</i> map to <font SIZE="-1">APIC</font> <i>description</i> and <i>picture type</i> respectively. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://id3.org/id3v2.4.0-frames">http://id3.org/id3v2.4.0-frames</a></b>&gt; for allowed picture types. 

 Note that the <font SIZE="-1">APIC</font> frames must be written at the beginning, so the muxer will buffer the audio frames until it gets all the pictures. It is therefore advised to provide the pictures as soon as possible to avoid excessive buffering.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A Xing/LAME frame right after the ID3v2 header (if present). It is enabled by default, but will be written only if the output is seekable. The <tt>&quot;write_xing&quot;</tt> private option can be used to disable it. The frame contains various information that may be useful to the decoder, like the audio duration or encoder delay.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A legacy ID3v1 tag at the end of the file (disabled by default). It may be enabled with the <tt>&quot;write_id3v1&quot;</tt> private option, but as its capabilities are very limited, its usage is not recommended.</dl>
 

 Examples: 

 Write an mp3 with an ID3v2.3 header and an ID3v1 footer: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -id3v2_version 3 -write_id3v1 1 out.mp3
</pre> 

 To attach a picture to an mp3 file select both the audio and the picture stream with <tt>&quot;map&quot;</tt>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.mp3 -i cover.png -c copy -map 0 -map 1
        -metadata:s:v title=&quot;Album cover&quot; -metadata:s:v comment=&quot;Cover (Front)&quot; out.mp3
</pre> 

 Write a ``clean'' <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> without any extra features: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.wav -write_xing 0 -id3v2_version 0 out.mp3
</pre>

<h3>mpegts</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> transport stream muxer. 

 This muxer implements <font SIZE="-1">ISO 13818-1</font> and part of <font SIZE="-1">ETSI EN 300 468.</font> 

 The recognized metadata settings in mpegts muxer are <tt>&quot;service_provider&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;service_name&quot;</tt>. If they are not set the default for <tt>&quot;service_provider&quot;</tt> is <b>FFmpeg</b> and the default for <tt>&quot;service_name&quot;</tt> is <b>Service01</b>. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The muxer options are:
<dl>
<dt><b>mpegts_transport_stream_id</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set the <b>transport_stream_id</b>. This identifies a transponder in <font SIZE="-1">DVB.</font> Default is <tt>0x0001</tt>.
<dt><b>mpegts_original_network_id</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set the <b>original_network_id</b>. This is unique identifier of a network in <font SIZE="-1">DVB.</font> Its main use is in the unique identification of a service through the path <b>Original_Network_ID, Transport_Stream_ID</b>. Default is <tt>0x0001</tt>.
<dt><b>mpegts_service_id</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set the <b>service_id</b>, also known as program in <font SIZE="-1">DVB.</font> Default is <tt>0x0001</tt>.
<dt><b>mpegts_service_type</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set the program <b>service_type</b>. Default is <tt>&quot;digital_tv&quot;</tt>. Accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>hex_value</b>
<dd> Any hexadecimal value between <tt>0x01</tt> and <tt>0xff</tt> as defined in <font SIZE="-1">ETSI 300 468.</font>
<dt><b>digital_tv</b>
<dd> Digital <font SIZE="-1">TV</font> service.
<dt><b>digital_radio</b>
<dd> Digital Radio service.
<dt><b>teletext</b>
<dd> Teletext service.
<dt><b>advanced_codec_digital_radio</b>
<dd> Advanced Codec Digital Radio service.
<dt><b>mpeg2_digital_hdtv</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">MPEG2</font> Digital <font SIZE="-1">HDTV</font> service.
<dt><b>advanced_codec_digital_sdtv</b>
<dd> Advanced Codec Digital <font SIZE="-1">SDTV</font> service.
<dt><b>advanced_codec_digital_hdtv</b>
<dd> Advanced Codec Digital <font SIZE="-1">HDTV</font> service.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>mpegts_pmt_start_pid</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set the first <font SIZE="-1">PID</font> for PMTs. Default is <tt>0x1000</tt>, minimum is <tt>0x0020</tt>, maximum is <tt>0x1ffa</tt>. This option has no effect in m2ts mode where the <font SIZE="-1">PMT PID</font> is fixed <tt>0x0100</tt>.
<dt><b>mpegts_start_pid</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set the first <font SIZE="-1">PID</font> for elementary streams. Default is <tt>0x0100</tt>, minimum is <tt>0x0020</tt>, maximum is <tt>0x1ffa</tt>. This option has no effect in m2ts mode where the elementary stream PIDs are fixed.
<dt><b>mpegts_m2ts_mode</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Enable m2ts mode if set to <tt>1</tt>. Default value is <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt> which disables m2ts mode.
<dt><b>muxrate</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set a constant muxrate. Default is <font SIZE="-1">VBR.</font>
<dt><b>pes_payload_size</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set minimum <font SIZE="-1">PES</font> packet payload in bytes. Default is <tt>2930</tt>.
<dt><b>mpegts_flags</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd> Set mpegts flags. Accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>resend_headers</b>
<dd> Reemit <font SIZE="-1">PAT/PMT</font> before writing the next packet.
<dt><b>latm</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">LATM</font> packetization for <font SIZE="-1">AAC.</font>
<dt><b>pat_pmt_at_frames</b>
<dd> Reemit <font SIZE="-1">PAT</font> and <font SIZE="-1">PMT</font> at each video frame.
<dt><b>system_b</b>
<dd> Conform to System B (<font SIZE="-1">DVB</font>) instead of System A (<font SIZE="-1">ATSC</font>).
<dt><b>initial_discontinuity</b>
<dd> Mark the initial packet of each stream as discontinuity.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>mpegts_copyts</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Preserve original timestamps, if value is set to <tt>1</tt>. Default value is <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt>, which results in shifting timestamps so that they start from 0.
<dt><b>omit_video_pes_length</b> <i>boolean</i>
<dd> Omit the <font SIZE="-1">PES</font> packet length for video packets. Default is <tt>1</tt> (true).
<dt><b>pcr_period</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Override the default <font SIZE="-1">PCR</font> retransmission time in milliseconds. Default is <tt>&quot;-1&quot;</tt> which means that the <font SIZE="-1">PCR</font> interval will be determined automatically: 20 ms is used for <font SIZE="-1">CBR</font> streams, the highest multiple of the frame duration which is less than 100 ms is used for <font SIZE="-1">VBR</font> streams.
<dt><b>pat_period</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Maximum time in seconds between <font SIZE="-1">PAT/PMT</font> tables. Default is <tt>0.1</tt>.
<dt><b>sdt_period</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Maximum time in seconds between <font SIZE="-1">SDT</font> tables. Default is <tt>0.5</tt>.
<dt><b>tables_version</b> <i>integer</i>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">PAT, PMT</font> and <font SIZE="-1">SDT</font> version (default <tt>0</tt>, valid values are from 0 to 31, inclusively). This option allows updating stream structure so that standard consumer may detect the change. To do so, reopen output <tt>&quot;AVFormatContext&quot;</tt> (in case of <font SIZE="-1">API</font> usage) or restart <b>ffmpeg</b> instance, cyclically changing <b>tables_version</b> value: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i source1.ts -codec copy -f mpegts -tables_version 0 <a HREF="udp://1.1.1.1:1111">udp://1.1.1.1:1111</a>
        ffmpeg -i source2.ts -codec copy -f mpegts -tables_version 1 <a HREF="udp://1.1.1.1:1111">udp://1.1.1.1:1111</a>
        ...
        ffmpeg -i source3.ts -codec copy -f mpegts -tables_version 31 <a HREF="udp://1.1.1.1:1111">udp://1.1.1.1:1111</a>
        ffmpeg -i source1.ts -codec copy -f mpegts -tables_version 0 <a HREF="udp://1.1.1.1:1111">udp://1.1.1.1:1111</a>
        ffmpeg -i source2.ts -codec copy -f mpegts -tables_version 1 <a HREF="udp://1.1.1.1:1111">udp://1.1.1.1:1111</a>
        ...
</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Example</i> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i file.mpg -c copy \
             -mpegts_original_network_id 0x1122 \
             -mpegts_transport_stream_id 0x3344 \
             -mpegts_service_id 0x5566 \
             -mpegts_pmt_start_pid 0x1500 \
             -mpegts_start_pid 0x150 \
             -metadata service_provider=&quot;Some provider&quot; \
             -metadata service_name=&quot;Some Channel&quot; \
             out.ts
</pre>

<h3>mxf, mxf_d10, mxf_opatom</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MXF</font> muxer. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The muxer options are:
<dl>
<dt><b>store_user_comments</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Set if user comments should be stored if available or never. <font SIZE="-1">IRT D-10</font> does not allow user comments. The default is thus to write them for mxf and mxf_opatom but not for mxf_d10</dl>

<h3>null</h3>

 Null muxer. 

 This muxer does not generate any output file, it is mainly useful for testing or benchmarking purposes. 

 For example to benchmark decoding with <b>ffmpeg</b> you can use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -benchmark -i INPUT -f null out.null
</pre> 

 Note that the above command does not read or write the <i>out.null</i> file, but specifying the output file is required by the <b>ffmpeg</b> syntax. 

 Alternatively you can write the command as: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -benchmark -i INPUT -f null -
</pre>

<h3>nut</h3>

<dl>
<dt><b>-syncpoints</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd> Change the syncpoint usage in nut:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><i>default</i> <b>use the normal low-overhead seeking aids.</b>
<dd>
<dt><i>none</i> <b>do not use the syncpoints at all, reducing the overhead but making the stream non-seekable;</b>
<dd> <pre>
    Use of this option is not recommended, as the resulting files are very damage
    sensitive and seeking is not possible. Also in general the overhead from
    syncpoints is negligible. Note, -C&lt;write_index&gt; 0 can be used to disable
    all growing data tables, allowing to mux endless streams with limited memory
    and without these disadvantages.
</pre>
<dt><i>timestamped</i> <b>extend the syncpoint with a wallclock field.</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 The <i>none</i> and <i>timestamped</i> flags are experimental.</dl>

<dt><b>-write_index</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Write index at the end, the default is to write an index.</dl>
 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f_strict experimental -syncpoints none - | processor
</pre>

<h3>ogg</h3>

 Ogg container muxer.
<dl>
<dt><b>-page_duration</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Preferred page duration, in microseconds. The muxer will attempt to create pages that are approximately <i>duration</i> microseconds long. This allows the user to compromise between seek granularity and container overhead. The default is 1 second. A value of 0 will fill all segments, making pages as large as possible. A value of 1 will effectively use 1 packet-per-page in most situations, giving a small seek granularity at the cost of additional container overhead.
<dt><b>-serial_offset</b> <i>value</i>
<dd> Serial value from which to set the streams serial number. Setting it to different and sufficiently large values ensures that the produced ogg files can be safely chained.</dl>

<h3>segment, stream_segment, ssegment</h3>

 Basic stream segmenter. 

 This muxer outputs streams to a number of separate files of nearly fixed duration. Output filename pattern can be set in a fashion similar to <b>image2</b>, or by using a <tt>&quot;strftime&quot;</tt> template if the <b>strftime</b> option is enabled. 

 <tt>&quot;stream_segment&quot;</tt> is a variant of the muxer used to write to streaming output formats, i.e. which do not require global headers, and is recommended for outputting e.g. to <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> transport stream segments. <tt>&quot;ssegment&quot;</tt> is a shorter alias for <tt>&quot;stream_segment&quot;</tt>. 

 Every segment starts with a keyframe of the selected reference stream, which is set through the <b>reference_stream</b> option. 

 Note that if you want accurate splitting for a video file, you need to make the input key frames correspond to the exact splitting times expected by the segmenter, or the segment muxer will start the new segment with the key frame found next after the specified start time. 

 The segment muxer works best with a single constant frame rate video. 

 Optionally it can generate a list of the created segments, by setting the option <i>segment_list</i>. The list type is specified by the <i>segment_list_type</i> option. The entry filenames in the segment list are set by default to the basename of the corresponding segment files. 

 See also the <b>hls</b> muxer, which provides a more specific implementation for <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> segmentation. 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The segment muxer supports the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>increment_tc</b> <i>1|0</i>
<dd> if set to <tt>1</tt>, increment timecode between each segment If this is selected, the input need to have a timecode in the first video stream. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>reference_stream</b> <i>specifier</i>
<dd> Set the reference stream, as specified by the string <i>specifier</i>. If <i>specifier</i> is set to <tt>&quot;auto&quot;</tt>, the reference is chosen automatically. Otherwise it must be a stream specifier (see the ``Stream specifiers'' chapter in the ffmpeg manual) which specifies the reference stream. The default value is <tt>&quot;auto&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>segment_format</b> <i>format</i>
<dd> Override the inner container format, by default it is guessed by the filename extension.
<dt><b>segment_format_options</b> <i>options_list</i>
<dd> Set output format options using a :-separated list of key=value parameters. Values containing the <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> special character must be escaped.
<dt><b>segment_list</b> <i>name</i>
<dd> Generate also a listfile named <i>name</i>. If not specified no listfile is generated.
<dt><b>segment_list_flags</b> <i>flags</i>
<dd> Set flags affecting the segment list generation. 

 It currently supports the following flags:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>cache</b>
<dd> Allow caching (only affects M3U8 list files).
<dt><b>live</b>
<dd> Allow live-friendly file generation.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>segment_list_size</b> <i>size</i>
<dd> Update the list file so that it contains at most <i>size</i> segments. If 0 the list file will contain all the segments. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>segment_list_entry_prefix</b> <i>prefix</i>
<dd> Prepend <i>prefix</i> to each entry. Useful to generate absolute paths. By default no prefix is applied.
<dt><b>segment_list_type</b> <i>type</i>
<dd> Select the listing format. 

 The following values are recognized:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>flat</b>
<dd> Generate a flat list for the created segments, one segment per line.
<dt><b>csv, ext</b>
<dd> Generate a list for the created segments, one segment per line, each line matching the format (comma-separated values): 

 <pre>
        &lt;segment_filename&gt;,&lt;segment_start_time&gt;,&lt;segment_end_time&gt;
</pre> 

 <i>segment_filename</i> is the name of the output file generated by the muxer according to the provided pattern. <font SIZE="-1">CSV</font> escaping (according to <font SIZE="-1">RFC4180</font>) is applied if required. 

 <i>segment_start_time</i> and <i>segment_end_time</i> specify the segment start and end time expressed in seconds. 

 A list file with the suffix <tt>&quot;.csv&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;.ext&quot;</tt> will auto-select this format. 

 <b>ext</b> is deprecated in favor or <b>csv</b>.
<dt><b>ffconcat</b>
<dd> Generate an ffconcat file for the created segments. The resulting file can be read using the FFmpeg <b>concat</b> demuxer. 

 A list file with the suffix <tt>&quot;.ffcat&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;.ffconcat&quot;</tt> will auto-select this format.
<dt><b>m3u8</b>
<dd> Generate an extended M3U8 file, version 3, compliant with &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://tools.ietf.org/id/draft-pantos-http-live-streaming">http://tools.ietf.org/id/draft-pantos-http-live-streaming</a></b>&gt;. 

 A list file with the suffix <tt>&quot;.m3u8&quot;</tt> will auto-select this format.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
