 If not specified the type is guessed from the list file name suffix.</dl>

<dt><b>segment_time</b> <i>time</i>
<dd> Set segment duration to <i>time</i>, the value must be a duration specification. Default value is ``2''. See also the <b>segment_times</b> option. 

 Note that splitting may not be accurate, unless you force the reference stream key-frames at the given time. See the introductory notice and the examples below.
<dt><b>segment_atclocktime</b> <i>1|0</i>
<dd> If set to ``1'' split at regular clock time intervals starting from 00:00 o'clock. The <i>time</i> value specified in <b>segment_time</b> is used for setting the length of the splitting interval. 

 For example with <b>segment_time</b> set to ``900'' this makes it possible to create files at 12:00 o'clock, 12:15, 12:30, etc. 

 Default value is ``0''.
<dt><b>segment_clocktime_offset</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Delay the segment splitting times with the specified duration when using <b>segment_atclocktime</b>. 

 For example with <b>segment_time</b> set to ``900'' and <b>segment_clocktime_offset</b> set to ``300'' this makes it possible to create files at 12:05, 12:20, 12:35, etc. 

 Default value is ``0''.
<dt><b>segment_clocktime_wrap_duration</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Force the segmenter to only start a new segment if a packet reaches the muxer within the specified duration after the segmenting clock time. This way you can make the segmenter more resilient to backward local time jumps, such as leap seconds or transition to standard time from daylight savings time. 

 Default is the maximum possible duration which means starting a new segment regardless of the elapsed time since the last clock time.
<dt><b>segment_time_delta</b> <i>delta</i>
<dd> Specify the accuracy time when selecting the start time for a segment, expressed as a duration specification. Default value is ``0''. 

 When delta is specified a key-frame will start a new segment if its <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> satisfies the relation: 

 <pre>
        PTS &gt;= start_time - time_delta
</pre> 

 This option is useful when splitting video content, which is always split at <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> boundaries, in case a key frame is found just before the specified split time. 

 In particular may be used in combination with the <i>ffmpeg</i> option <i>force_key_frames</i>. The key frame times specified by <i>force_key_frames</i> may not be set accurately because of rounding issues, with the consequence that a key frame time may result set just before the specified time. For constant frame rate videos a value of 1/(2*<i>frame_rate</i>) should address the worst case mismatch between the specified time and the time set by <i>force_key_frames</i>.
<dt><b>segment_times</b> <i>times</i>
<dd> Specify a list of split points. <i>times</i> contains a list of comma separated duration specifications, in increasing order. See also the <b>segment_time</b> option.
<dt><b>segment_frames</b> <i>frames</i>
<dd> Specify a list of split video frame numbers. <i>frames</i> contains a list of comma separated integer numbers, in increasing order. 

 This option specifies to start a new segment whenever a reference stream key frame is found and the sequential number (starting from 0) of the frame is greater or equal to the next value in the list.
<dt><b>segment_wrap</b> <i>limit</i>
<dd> Wrap around segment index once it reaches <i>limit</i>.
<dt><b>segment_start_number</b> <i>number</i>
<dd> Set the sequence number of the first segment. Defaults to <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>strftime</b> <i>1|0</i>
<dd> Use the <tt>&quot;strftime&quot;</tt> function to define the name of the new segments to write. If this is selected, the output segment name must contain a <tt>&quot;strftime&quot;</tt> function template. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>break_non_keyframes</b> <i>1|0</i>
<dd> If enabled, allow segments to start on frames other than keyframes. This improves behavior on some players when the time between keyframes is inconsistent, but may make things worse on others, and can cause some oddities during seeking. Defaults to <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>reset_timestamps</b> <i>1|0</i>
<dd> Reset timestamps at the beginning of each segment, so that each segment will start with near-zero timestamps. It is meant to ease the playback of the generated segments. May not work with some combinations of muxers/codecs. It is set to <tt>0</tt> by default.
<dt><b>initial_offset</b> <i>offset</i>
<dd> Specify timestamp offset to apply to the output packet timestamps. The argument must be a time duration specification, and defaults to 0.
<dt><b>write_empty_segments</b> <i>1|0</i>
<dd> If enabled, write an empty segment if there are no packets during the period a segment would usually span. Otherwise, the segment will be filled with the next packet written. Defaults to <tt>0</tt>.</dl>
 

 Make sure to require a closed <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> when encoding and to set the <font SIZE="-1">GOP</font> size to fit your segment time constraint. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Remux the content of file <i>in.mkv</i> to a list of segments <i>out-000.nut</i>, <i>out-001.nut</i>, etc., and write the list of generated segments to <i>out.list</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -codec hevc -flags +cgop -g 60 -map 0 -f segment -segment_list out.list out%03d.nut
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Segment input and set output format options for the output segments: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -f segment -segment_time 10 -segment_format_options movflags=+faststart out%03d.mp4
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Segment the input file according to the split points specified by the <i>segment_times</i> option: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -codec copy -map 0 -f segment -segment_list out.csv -segment_times 1,2,3,5,8,13,21 out%03d.nut
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Use the <b>ffmpeg</b> <b>force_key_frames</b> option to force key frames in the input at the specified location, together with the segment option <b>segment_time_delta</b> to account for possible roundings operated when setting key frame times. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -force_key_frames 1,2,3,5,8,13,21 -codec:v mpeg4 -codec:a pcm_s16le -map 0 \
        -f segment -segment_list out.csv -segment_times 1,2,3,5,8,13,21 -segment_time_delta 0.05 out%03d.nut
</pre> 

 In order to force key frames on the input file, transcoding is required.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Segment the input file by splitting the input file according to the frame numbers sequence specified with the <b>segment_frames</b> option: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -codec copy -map 0 -f segment -segment_list out.csv -segment_frames 100,200,300,500,800 out%03d.nut
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Convert the <i>in.mkv</i> to <font SIZE="-1">TS</font> segments using the <tt>&quot;libx264&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;aac&quot;</tt> encoders: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.mkv -map 0 -codec:v libx264 -codec:a aac -f ssegment -segment_list out.list out%03d.ts
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Segment the input file, and create an M3U8 live playlist (can be used as live <font SIZE="-1">HLS</font> source): 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i in.mkv -codec copy -map 0 -f segment -segment_list playlist.m3u8 \
        -segment_list_flags +live -segment_time 10 out%03d.mkv
</pre></dl>

<h3>smoothstreaming</h3>

 Smooth Streaming muxer generates a set of files (Manifest, chunks) suitable for serving with conventional web server.
<dl>
<dt><b>window_size</b>
<dd> Specify the number of fragments kept in the manifest. Default 0 (keep all).
<dt><b>extra_window_size</b>
<dd> Specify the number of fragments kept outside of the manifest before removing from disk. Default 5.
<dt><b>lookahead_count</b>
<dd> Specify the number of lookahead fragments. Default 2.
<dt><b>min_frag_duration</b>
<dd> Specify the minimum fragment duration (in microseconds). Default 5000000.
<dt><b>remove_at_exit</b>
<dd> Specify whether to remove all fragments when finished. Default 0 (do not remove).</dl>

<h3>streamhash</h3>

 Per stream hash testing format. 

 This muxer computes and prints a cryptographic hash of all the input frames, on a per-stream basis. This can be used for equality checks without having to do a complete binary comparison. 

 By default audio frames are converted to signed 16-bit raw audio and video frames to raw video before computing the hash, but the output of explicit conversions to other codecs can also be used. Timestamps are ignored. It uses the <font SIZE="-1">SHA-256</font> cryptographic hash function by default, but supports several other algorithms. 

 The output of the muxer consists of one line per stream of the form: <i>streamindex</i>,<i>streamtype</i>,<i>algo</i>=<i>hash</i>, where <i>streamindex</i> is the index of the mapped stream, <i>streamtype</i> is a single character indicating the type of stream, <i>algo</i> is a short string representing the hash function used, and <i>hash</i> is a hexadecimal number representing the computed hash.
<dl>
<dt><b>hash</b> <i>algorithm</i>
<dd> Use the cryptographic hash function specified by the string <i>algorithm</i>. Supported values include <tt>&quot;MD5&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;murmur3&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD128&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD160&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD256&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;RIPEMD320&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA160&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA224&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA256&quot;</tt> (default), <tt>&quot;SHA512/224&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA512/256&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA384&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;SHA512&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;CRC32&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;adler32&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 To compute the <font SIZE="-1">SHA-256</font> hash of the input converted to raw audio and video, and store it in the file <i>out.sha256</i>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f streamhash out.sha256
</pre> 

 To print an <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash to stdout use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f streamhash -hash md5 -
</pre> 

 See also the <b>hash</b> and <b>framehash</b> muxers.

<h3>fifo</h3>

 The fifo pseudo-muxer allows the separation of encoding and muxing by using first-in-first-out queue and running the actual muxer in a separate thread. This is especially useful in combination with the <b>tee</b> muxer and can be used to send data to several destinations with different reliability/writing speed/latency. 

 <font SIZE="-1">API</font> users should be aware that callback functions (interrupt_callback, io_open and io_close) used within its AVFormatContext must be thread-safe. 

 The behavior of the fifo muxer if the queue fills up or if the output fails is selectable,
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> output can be transparently restarted with configurable delay between retries based on real time or time of the processed stream.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> encoding can be blocked during temporary failure, or continue transparently dropping packets in case fifo queue fills up.
<dt><b>fifo_format</b>
<dd> Specify the format name. Useful if it cannot be guessed from the output name suffix.
<dt><b>queue_size</b>
<dd> Specify size of the queue (number of packets). Default value is 60.
<dt><b>format_opts</b>
<dd> Specify format options for the underlying muxer. Muxer options can be specified as a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> pairs separated by ':'.
<dt><b>drop_pkts_on_overflow</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> If set to 1 (true), in case the fifo queue fills up, packets will be dropped rather than blocking the encoder. This makes it possible to continue streaming without delaying the input, at the cost of omitting part of the stream. By default this option is set to 0 (false), so in such cases the encoder will be blocked until the muxer processes some of the packets and none of them is lost.
<dt><b>attempt_recovery</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> If failure occurs, attempt to recover the output. This is especially useful when used with network output, since it makes it possible to restart streaming transparently. By default this option is set to 0 (false).
<dt><b>max_recovery_attempts</b>
<dd> Sets maximum number of successive unsuccessful recovery attempts after which the output fails permanently. By default this option is set to 0 (unlimited).
<dt><b>recovery_wait_time</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Waiting time before the next recovery attempt after previous unsuccessful recovery attempt. Default value is 5 seconds.
<dt><b>recovery_wait_streamtime</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> If set to 0 (false), the real time is used when waiting for the recovery attempt (i.e. the recovery will be attempted after at least recovery_wait_time seconds). If set to 1 (true), the time of the processed stream is taken into account instead (i.e. the recovery will be attempted after at least <i>recovery_wait_time</i> seconds of the stream is omitted). By default, this option is set to 0 (false).
<dt><b>recover_any_error</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> If set to 1 (true), recovery will be attempted regardless of type of the error causing the failure. By default this option is set to 0 (false) and in case of certain (usually permanent) errors the recovery is not attempted even when <i>attempt_recovery</i> is set to 1.
<dt><b>restart_with_keyframe</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> Specify whether to wait for the keyframe after recovering from queue overflow or failure. This option is set to 0 (false) by default.
<dt><b>timeshift</b> <i>duration</i>
<dd> Buffer the specified amount of packets and delay writing the output. Note that <i>queue_size</i> must be big enough to store the packets for timeshift. At the end of the input the fifo buffer is flushed at realtime speed.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Stream something to rtmp server, continue processing the stream at real-time rate even in case of temporary failure (network outage) and attempt to recover streaming every second indefinitely. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i ... -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -f fifo -fifo_format flv -map 0:v -map 0:a
          -drop_pkts_on_overflow 1 -attempt_recovery 1 -recovery_wait_time 1 <a HREF="rtmp://example.com/live/stream_name">rtmp://example.com/live/stream_name</a>
</pre></dl>

<h3>tee</h3>

 The tee muxer can be used to write the same data to several outputs, such as files or streams. It can be used, for example, to stream a video over a network and save it to disk at the same time. 

 It is different from specifying several outputs to the <b>ffmpeg</b> command-line tool. With the tee muxer, the audio and video data will be encoded only once. With conventional multiple outputs, multiple encoding operations in parallel are initiated, which can be a very expensive process. The tee muxer is not useful when using the libavformat <font SIZE="-1">API</font> directly because it is then possible to feed the same packets to several muxers directly. 

 Since the tee muxer does not represent any particular output format, ffmpeg cannot auto-select output streams. So all streams intended for output must be specified using <tt>&quot;-map&quot;</tt>. See the examples below. 

 Some encoders may need different options depending on the output format; the auto-detection of this can not work with the tee muxer, so they need to be explicitly specified. The main example is the <b>global_header</b> flag. 

 The slave outputs are specified in the file name given to the muxer, separated by '|'. If any of the slave name contains the '|' separator, leading or trailing spaces or any special character, those must be escaped (see <b>the ``Quoting and escaping'' section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b>). 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>use_fifo</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> If set to 1, slave outputs will be processed in separate threads using the <b>fifo</b> muxer. This allows to compensate for different speed/latency/reliability of outputs and setup transparent recovery. By default this feature is turned off.
<dt><b>fifo_options</b>
<dd> Options to pass to fifo pseudo-muxer instances. See <b>fifo</b>.</dl>
 

 Muxer options can be specified for each slave by prepending them as a list of <i>key</i>=<i>value</i> pairs separated by ':', between square brackets. If the options values contain a special character or the ':' separator, they must be escaped; note that this is a second level escaping. 

 The following special options are also recognized:
<dl>
<dt><b>f</b>
<dd> Specify the format name. Required if it cannot be guessed from the output <font SIZE="-1">URL.</font>
<dt><b>bsfs[/</b><i>spec</i><b>]</b>
<dd> Specify a list of bitstream filters to apply to the specified output. 

 It is possible to specify to which streams a given bitstream filter applies, by appending a stream specifier to the option separated by <tt>&quot;/&quot;</tt>. <i>spec</i> must be a stream specifier (see <b>Format stream specifiers</b>). 

 If the stream specifier is not specified, the bitstream filters will be applied to all streams in the output. This will cause that output operation to fail if the output contains streams to which the bitstream filter cannot be applied e.g. <tt>&quot;h264_mp4toannexb&quot;</tt> being applied to an output containing an audio stream. 

 Options for a bitstream filter must be specified in the form of <tt>&quot;opt=value&quot;</tt>. 

 Several bitstream filters can be specified, separated by ``,''.
<dt><b>use_fifo</b> <i>bool</i>
<dd> This allows to override tee muxer use_fifo option for individual slave muxer.
<dt><b>fifo_options</b>
<dd> This allows to override tee muxer fifo_options for individual slave muxer. See <b>fifo</b>.
<dt><b>select</b>
<dd> Select the streams that should be mapped to the slave output, specified by a stream specifier. If not specified, this defaults to all the mapped streams. This will cause that output operation to fail if the output format does not accept all mapped streams. 

 You may use multiple stream specifiers separated by commas (<tt>&quot;,&quot;</tt>) e.g.: <tt>&quot;a:0,v&quot;</tt>
<dt><b>onfail</b>
<dd> Specify behaviour on output failure. This can be set to either <tt>&quot;abort&quot;</tt> (which is default) or <tt>&quot;ignore&quot;</tt>. <tt>&quot;abort&quot;</tt> will cause whole process to fail in case of failure on this slave output. <tt>&quot;ignore&quot;</tt> will ignore failure on this output, so other outputs will continue without being affected.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Encode something and both archive it in a WebM file and stream it as MPEG-TS over <font SIZE="-1">UDP:</font> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i ... -c:v libx264 -c:a mp2 -f tee -map 0:v -map 0:a
          &quot;archive-20121107.mkv|[f=mpegts]<a HREF="udp://10.0.1.255:1234/">udp://10.0.1.255:1234/</a>&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> As above, but continue streaming even if output to local file fails (for example local drive fills up): 

 
ffmpeg - i... - c : v libx264 - c : a mp2 - f tee - map 0 : v - map 0 : a "[onfail=ignore]archive-20121107.mkv|[f=mpegts]udp://10.0.1.255:1234/"

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Use <b>ffmpeg</b> to encode the input, and send the output to three different destinations. The <tt>&quot;dump_extra&quot;</tt> bitstream filter is used to add extradata information to all the output video keyframes packets, as requested by the MPEG-TS format. The select option is applied to <i>out.aac</i> in order to make it contain only audio packets. 

 
ffmpeg - i... - map 0 - flags + global_header - c : v libx264 - c : a aac - f tee "[bsfs/v=dump_extra=freq=keyframe]out.ts|[movflags=+faststart]out.mp4|[select=a]out.aac"

<dt>&bull;
<dd> As above, but select only stream <tt>&quot;a:1&quot;</tt> for the audio output. Note that a second level escaping must be performed, as ``:'' is a special character used to separate options. 

 
ffmpeg - i... - map 0 - flags + global_header - c : v libx264 - c : a aac - f tee "[bsfs/v=dump_extra=freq=keyframe]out.ts|[movflags=+faststart]out.mp4|[select=\'a:1\']out.aac"
</dl>

<h3>webm_dash_manifest</h3>

 WebM <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> Manifest muxer. 

 This muxer implements the WebM <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> Manifest specification to generate the <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> manifest <font SIZE="-1">XML.</font> It also supports manifest generation for <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> live streams. 

 For more information see:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> WebM <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> Specification: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://sites.google.com/a/webmproject.org/wiki/adaptive-streaming/webm-dash-specification">https://sites.google.com/a/webmproject.org/wiki/adaptive-streaming/webm-dash-specification</a></b>&gt;
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">ISO DASH</font> Specification: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://standards.iso.org/ittf/PubliclyAvailableStandards/c065274_ISO_IEC_23009-1_2014.zip">http://standards.iso.org/ittf/PubliclyAvailableStandards/c065274_ISO_IEC_23009-1_2014.zip</a></b>&gt;</dl>
 

 <i>Options</i> 

 This muxer supports the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>adaptation_sets</b>
<dd> This option has the following syntax: ``id=x,streams=a,b,c id=y,streams=d,e'' where x and y are the unique identifiers of the adaptation sets and a,b,c,d and e are the indices of the corresponding audio and video streams. Any number of adaptation sets can be added using this option.
<dt><b>live</b>
<dd> Set this to 1 to create a live stream <font SIZE="-1">DASH</font> Manifest. Default: 0.
<dt><b>chunk_start_index</b>
<dd> Start index of the first chunk. This will go in the <b>startNumber</b> attribute of the <b>SegmentTemplate</b> element in the manifest. Default: 0.
<dt><b>chunk_duration_ms</b>
<dd> Duration of each chunk in milliseconds. This will go in the <b>duration</b> attribute of the <b>SegmentTemplate</b> element in the manifest. Default: 1000.
<dt><b>utc_timing_url</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the page that will return the <font SIZE="-1">UTC</font> timestamp in <font SIZE="-1">ISO</font> format. This will go in the <b>value</b> attribute of the <b>UTCTiming</b> element in the manifest. Default: None.
<dt><b>time_shift_buffer_depth</b>
<dd> Smallest time (in seconds) shifting buffer for which any Representation is guaranteed to be available. This will go in the <b>timeShiftBufferDepth</b> attribute of the <font SIZE="-1"><b>MPD</b></font> element. Default: 60.
<dt><b>minimum_update_period</b>
<dd> Minimum update period (in seconds) of the manifest. This will go in the <b>minimumUpdatePeriod</b> attribute of the <font SIZE="-1"><b>MPD</b></font> element. Default: 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Example</i> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f webm_dash_manifest -i video1.webm \
               -f webm_dash_manifest -i video2.webm \
               -f webm_dash_manifest -i audio1.webm \
               -f webm_dash_manifest -i audio2.webm \
               -map 0 -map 1 -map 2 -map 3 \
               -c copy \
               -f webm_dash_manifest \
               -adaptation_sets &quot;id=0,streams=0,1 id=1,streams=2,3&quot; \
               manifest.xml
</pre>

<h3>webm_chunk</h3>

 WebM Live Chunk Muxer. 

 This muxer writes out WebM headers and chunks as separate files which can be consumed by clients that support WebM Live streams via <font SIZE="-1">DASH.</font> 

 <i>Options</i> 

 This muxer supports the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>chunk_start_index</b>
<dd> Index of the first chunk (defaults to 0).
<dt><b>header</b>
<dd> Filename of the header where the initialization data will be written.
<dt><b>audio_chunk_duration</b>
<dd> Duration of each audio chunk in milliseconds (defaults to 5000).</dl>
 

 <i>Example</i> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f v4l2 -i /dev/video0 \
               -f alsa -i hw:0 \
               -map 0:0 \
               -c:v libvpx-vp9 \
               -s 640x360 -keyint_min 30 -g 30 \
               -f webm_chunk \
               -header webm_live_video_360.hdr \
               -chunk_start_index 1 \
               webm_live_video_360_%d.chk \
               -map 1:0 \
               -c:a libvorbis \
               -b:a 128k \
               -f webm_chunk \
               -header webm_live_audio_128.hdr \
               -chunk_start_index 1 \
               -audio_chunk_duration 1000 \
               webm_live_audio_128_%d.chk
</pre>

<h2>METADATA</h2>

 FFmpeg is able to dump metadata from media files into a simple UTF-8-encoded INI-like text file and then load it back using the metadata muxer/demuxer. 

 The file format is as follows:
<dl>
<dt>1.
<dd> A file consists of a header and a number of metadata tags divided into sections, each on its own line.
<dt>2.
<dd> The header is a <b>;FFMETADATA</b> string, followed by a version number (now 1).
<dt>3.
<dd> Metadata tags are of the form <b>key=value</b>
<dt>4.
<dd> Immediately after header follows global metadata
<dt>5.
<dd> After global metadata there may be sections with per-stream/per-chapter metadata.
<dt>6.
<dd> A section starts with the section name in uppercase (i.e. <font SIZE="-1">STREAM</font> or <font SIZE="-1">CHAPTER</font>) in brackets (<b>[</b>, <b>]</b>) and ends with next section or end of file.
<dt>7.
<dd> At the beginning of a chapter section there may be an optional timebase to be used for start/end values. It must be in form <b>TIMEBASE=</b><i>num</i><b>/</b><i>den</i>, where <i>num</i> and <i>den</i> are integers. If the timebase is missing then start/end times are assumed to be in nanoseconds. 

 Next a chapter section must contain chapter start and end times in form <b>START=</b><i>num</i>, <b>END=</b><i>num</i>, where <i>num</i> is a positive integer.
<dt>8.
<dd> Empty lines and lines starting with <b>;</b> or <b>#</b> are ignored.
<dt>9.
<dd> Metadata keys or values containing special characters (<b>=</b>, <b>;</b>, <b>#</b>, <b>\</b> and a newline) must be escaped with a backslash <b>\</b>.
<dt>10.
<dd> Note that whitespace in metadata (e.g. <b>foo = bar</b>) is considered to be a part of the tag (in the example above key is <b>foo</b> , value is 
&nbsp;<b>bar</b>).</dl>
 

 A ffmetadata file might look like this: 

 
;
FFMETADATA1
title = bike\\shed;
this is a comment
    artist = FFmpeg troll team

        [CHAPTER] TIMEBASE = 1 / 1000 START = 0
#chapter ends at 0 : 01 : 00
    END = 60000 title = chapter \#1
        [STREAM] title = multi
            line
 

 By using the ffmetadata muxer and demuxer it is possible to extract metadata from an input file to an ffmetadata file, and then transcode the file into an output file with the edited ffmetadata file. 

 Extracting an ffmetadata file with <i>ffmpeg</i> goes as follows: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f ffmetadata FFMETADATAFILE
</pre> 

 Reinserting edited metadata information from the <font SIZE="-1">FFMETADATAFILE</font> file can be done as: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -i FFMETADATAFILE -map_metadata 1 -codec copy OUTPUT
</pre>

<h2>PROTOCOL OPTIONS</h2>

 The libavformat library provides some generic global options, which can be set on all the protocols. In addition each protocol may support so-called private options, which are specific for that component. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, or by setting the value explicitly in the <tt>&quot;AVFormatContext&quot;</tt> options or using the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API</font> for programmatic use. 

 The list of supported options follows:
<dl>
<dt><b>protocol_whitelist</b> <i>list</i> <b>(</b><i>input</i><b>)</b>
<dd> Set a ``,''-separated list of allowed protocols. ``<font SIZE="-1">ALL''</font> matches all protocols. Protocols prefixed by ``-'' are disabled. All protocols are allowed by default but protocols used by an another protocol (nested protocols) are restricted to a per protocol subset.</dl>

<h2>PROTOCOLS</h2>

 Protocols are configured elements in FFmpeg that enable access to resources that require specific protocols. 

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, all the supported protocols are enabled by default. You can list all available ones using the configure option ``--list-protocols''. 

 You can disable all the protocols using the configure option ``--disable-protocols'', and selectively enable a protocol using the option &quot;--enable-protocol=<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>PROTOCOL</i></font><i></i>``, or you can disable a particular protocol using the option ''--disable-protocol=<i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>PROTOCOL</i></font><i></i>&quot;. 

 The option ``-protocols'' of the ff* tools will display the list of supported protocols. 

 All protocols accept the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>rw_timeout</b>
<dd> Maximum time to wait for (network) read/write operations to complete, in microseconds.</dl>
 

 A description of the currently available protocols follows.

<h3>amqp</h3>

 Advanced Message Queueing Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">AMQP</font>) version 0-9-1 is a broker based publish-subscribe communication protocol. 

 FFmpeg must be compiled with --enable-librabbitmq to support <font SIZE="-1">AMQP. A</font> separate <font SIZE="-1">AMQP</font> broker must also be run. An example open-source <font SIZE="-1">AMQP</font> broker is RabbitMQ. 

 After starting the broker, an FFmpeg client may stream data to the broker using the command: 

 
ffmpeg - re - i input - f mpegts amqp: //[[user]:[password]@]hostname[:port][/vhost]
 

 Where hostname and port (default is 5672) is the address of the broker. The client may also set a user/password for authentication. The default for both fields is ``guest''. Name of virtual host on broker can be set with vhost. The default value is ``/''. 

 Muliple subscribers may stream from the broker using the command: 

 
ffplay amqp: //[[user]:[password]@]hostname[:port][/vhost]
 

 In RabbitMQ all data published to the broker flows through a specific exchange, and each subscribing client has an assigned queue/buffer. When a packet arrives at an exchange, it may be copied to a client's queue depending on the exchange and routing_key fields. 

 The following options are supported:
<dl>
<dt><b>exchange</b>
<dd> Sets the exchange to use on the broker. RabbitMQ has several predefined exchanges: ``amq.direct'' is the default exchange, where the publisher and subscriber must have a matching routing_key; ``amq.fanout'' is the same as a broadcast operation (i.e. the data is forwarded to all queues on the fanout exchange independent of the routing_key); and ``amq.topic'' is similar to ``amq.direct'', but allows for more complex pattern matching (refer to the RabbitMQ documentation).
<dt><b>routing_key</b>
<dd> Sets the routing key. The default value is ``amqp''. The routing key is used on the ``amq.direct'' and ``amq.topic'' exchanges to decide whether packets are written to the queue of a subscriber.
<dt><b>pkt_size</b>
<dd> Maximum size of each packet sent/received to the broker. Default is 131072. Minimum is 4096 and max is any large value (representable by an int). When receiving packets, this sets an internal buffer size in FFmpeg. It should be equal to or greater than the size of the published packets to the broker. Otherwise the received message may be truncated causing decoding errors.
<dt><b>connection_timeout</b>
<dd> The timeout in seconds during the initial connection to the broker. The default value is rw_timeout, or 5 seconds if rw_timeout is not set.
<dt><b>delivery_mode</b> <i>mode</i>
<dd> Sets the delivery mode of each message sent to broker. The following values are accepted:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>persistent</b>
<dd> Delivery mode set to ``persistent'' (2). This is the default value. Messages may be written to the broker's disk depending on its setup.
<dt><b>non-persistent</b>
<dd> Delivery mode set to ``non-persistent'' (1). Messages will stay in broker's memory unless the broker is under memory pressure.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>async</h3>

 Asynchronous data filling wrapper for input stream. 

 Fill data in a background thread, to decouple I/O operation from demux thread. 

 <pre>
        async:&lt;URL&gt;
        async:<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://host/resource">http://host/resource</a>
        async:cache:<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://host/resource">http://host/resource</a>
</pre>

<h3>bluray</h3>

 Read BluRay playlist. 

 The accepted options are:
<dl>
<dt><b>angle</b>
<dd> BluRay angle
<dt><b>chapter</b>
<dd> Start chapter (1...N)
<dt><b>playlist</b>
<dd> Playlist to read (<font SIZE="-1">BDMV/PLAYLIST/</font>?????.mpls)</dl>
 

 Examples: 

 Read longest playlist from BluRay mounted to /mnt/bluray: 

 <pre>
        bluray:/mnt/bluray
</pre> 

 Read angle 2 of playlist 4 from BluRay mounted to /mnt/bluray, start from chapter 2: 

 <pre>
        -playlist 4 -angle 2 -chapter 2 bluray:/mnt/bluray
</pre>

<h3>cache</h3>

 Caching wrapper for input stream. 

 Cache the input stream to temporary file. It brings seeking capability to live streams. 

 The accepted options are:
<dl>
<dt><b>read_ahead_limit</b>
<dd> Amount in bytes that may be read ahead when seeking isn't supported. Range is -1 to <font SIZE="-1">INT_MAX.</font> -1 for unlimited. Default is 65536.</dl>
 

 <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> Syntax is 

 <pre>
        cache:&lt;URL&gt;
</pre>

<h3>concat</h3>

 Physical concatenation protocol. 

 Read and seek from many resources in sequence as if they were a unique resource. 

 A <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> accepted by this protocol has the syntax: 

 <pre>
        concat:&lt;URL1&gt;|&lt;URL2&gt;|...|&lt;URLN&gt;
</pre> 

 where <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>URL1</i></font><i></i>, <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>URL2</i></font><i></i>, ..., <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>URLN</i></font><i></i> are the urls of the resource to be concatenated, each one possibly specifying a distinct protocol. 

 For example to read a sequence of files <i>split1.mpeg</i>, <i>split2.mpeg</i>, <i>split3.mpeg</i> with <b>ffplay</b> use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffplay concat:split1.mpeg\|split2.mpeg\|split3.mpeg
</pre> 

 Note that you may need to escape the character ``|'' which is special for many shells.

<h3>crypto</h3>

 AES-encrypted stream reading protocol. 

 The accepted options are:
<dl>
<dt><b>key</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">AES</font> decryption key binary block from given hexadecimal representation.
<dt><b>iv</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">AES</font> decryption initialization vector binary block from given hexadecimal representation.</dl>
 

 Accepted <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> formats: 

 <pre>
        crypto:&lt;URL&gt;
        crypto+&lt;URL&gt;
</pre>

<h3>data</h3>

 Data in-line in the <font SIZE="-1">URI.</font> See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_URI_scheme">http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_URI_scheme</a></b>&gt;. 

 For example, to convert a <font SIZE="-1">GIF</font> file given inline with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i &quot;data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODdhCAAIAMIEAAAAAAAA//8AAP//AP///////////////ywAAAAACAAIAAADF0gEDLojDgdGiJdJqUX02iB4E8Q9jUMkADs=&quot; smiley.png
</pre>

<h3>file</h3>

 File access protocol. 

 Read from or write to a file. 

 A file <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> can have the form: 

 <pre>
        file:&lt;filename&gt;
</pre> 

 where <i>filename</i> is the path of the file to read. 

 An <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> that does not have a protocol prefix will be assumed to be a file <font SIZE="-1">URL.</font> Depending on the build, an <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> that looks like a Windows path with the drive letter at the beginning will also be assumed to be a file <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> (usually not the case in builds for unix-like systems). 

 For example to read from a file <i>input.mpeg</i> with <b>ffmpeg</b> use the command: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i file:input.mpeg output.mpeg
</pre> 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>truncate</b>
<dd> Truncate existing files on write, if set to 1. A value of 0 prevents truncating. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>blocksize</b>
<dd> Set I/O operation maximum block size, in bytes. Default value is <tt>&quot;INT_MAX&quot;</tt>, which results in not limiting the requested block size. Setting this value reasonably low improves user termination request reaction time, which is valuable for files on slow medium.
<dt><b>follow</b>
<dd> If set to 1, the protocol will retry reading at the end of the file, allowing reading files that still are being written. In order for this to terminate, you either need to use the rw_timeout option, or use the interrupt callback (for <font SIZE="-1">API</font> users).
<dt><b>seekable</b>
<dd> Controls if seekability is advertised on the file. 0 means non-seekable, -1 means auto (seekable for normal files, non-seekable for named pipes). 

 Many demuxers handle seekable and non-seekable resources differently, overriding this might speed up opening certain files at the cost of losing some features (e.g. accurate seeking).</dl>

<h3>ftp</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> (File Transfer Protocol). 

 Read from or write to remote resources using <font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> protocol. 

 Following syntax is required. 

 
ftp: //[user[:password]@]server[:port]/path/to/remote/resource.mpeg
 

 This protocol accepts the following options.
<dl>
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd> Set timeout in microseconds of socket I/O operations used by the underlying low level operation. By default it is set to -1, which means that the timeout is not specified.
<dt><b>ftp-user</b>
<dd> Set a user to be used for authenticating to the <font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> server. This is overridden by the user in the <font SIZE="-1">FTP URL.</font>
<dt><b>ftp-password</b>
<dd> Set a password to be used for authenticating to the <font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> server. This is overridden by the password in the <font SIZE="-1">FTP URL,</font> or by <b>ftp-anonymous-password</b> if no user is set.
<dt><b>ftp-anonymous-password</b>
<dd> Password used when login as anonymous user. Typically an e-mail address should be used.
<dt><b>ftp-write-seekable</b>
<dd> Control seekability of connection during encoding. If set to 1 the resource is supposed to be seekable, if set to 0 it is assumed not to be seekable. Default value is 0.</dl>
 

 <font SIZE="-1">NOTE:</font> Protocol can be used as output, but it is recommended to not do it, unless special care is taken (tests, customized server configuration etc.). Different <font SIZE="-1">FTP</font> servers behave in different way during seek operation. ff* tools may produce incomplete content due to server limitations.

<h3>gopher</h3>

 Gopher protocol.

<h3>gophers</h3>

 Gophers protocol. 

 The Gopher protocol with <font SIZE="-1">TLS</font> encapsulation.

<h3>hls</h3>

 Read Apple <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Live Streaming compliant segmented stream as a uniform one. The M3U8 playlists describing the segments can be remote <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> resources or local files, accessed using the standard file protocol. The nested protocol is declared by specifying &quot;+<i>proto</i>&quot; after the hls <font SIZE="-1">URI</font> scheme name, where <i>proto</i> is either ``file'' or ``http''. 

 <pre>
        hls+<a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://host/path/to/remote/resource.m3u8">http://host/path/to/remote/resource.m3u8</a>
        hls+file://path/to/local/resource.m3u8
</pre> 

 Using this protocol is discouraged - the hls demuxer should work just as well (if not, please report the issues) and is more complete. To use the hls demuxer instead, simply use the direct URLs to the m3u8 files.

<h3>http</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol). 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>seekable</b>
<dd> Control seekability of connection. If set to 1 the resource is supposed to be seekable, if set to 0 it is assumed not to be seekable, if set to -1 it will try to autodetect if it is seekable. Default value is -1.
<dt><b>chunked_post</b>
<dd> If set to 1 use chunked Transfer-Encoding for posts, default is 1.
<dt><b>content_type</b>
<dd> Set a specific content type for the <font SIZE="-1">POST</font> messages or for listen mode.
<dt><b>http_proxy</b>
<dd> set <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> proxy to tunnel through e.g. <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://example.com:1234">http://example.com:1234</a>
<dt><b>headers</b>
<dd> Set custom <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> headers, can override built in default headers. The value must be a string encoding the headers.
<dt><b>multiple_requests</b>
<dd> Use persistent connections if set to 1, default is 0.
<dt><b>post_data</b>
<dd> Set custom <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> post data.
<dt><b>referer</b>
<dd> Set the Referer header. Include 'Referer: <font SIZE="-1">URL</font>' header in <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> request.
<dt><b>user_agent</b>
<dd> Override the User-Agent header. If not specified the protocol will use a string describing the libavformat build. (``Lavf/&lt;version&gt;'')
<dt><b>user-agent</b>
<dd> This is a deprecated option, you can use user_agent instead it.
<dt><b>reconnect_at_eof</b>
<dd> If set then eof is treated like an error and causes reconnection, this is useful for live / endless streams.
<dt><b>reconnect_streamed</b>
<dd> If set then even streamed/non seekable streams will be reconnected on errors.
<dt><b>reconnect_on_network_error</b>
<dd> Reconnect automatically in case of <font SIZE="-1">TCP/TLS</font> errors during connect.
<dt><b>reconnect_on_http_error</b>
<dd> A comma separated list of <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> status codes to reconnect on. The list can include specific status codes (e.g. '503') or the strings '4xx' / '5xx'.
<dt><b>reconnect_delay_max</b>
<dd> Sets the maximum delay in seconds after which to give up reconnecting
<dt><b>mime_type</b>
<dd> Export the <font SIZE="-1">MIME</font> type.
<dt><b>http_version</b>
<dd> Exports the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> response version number. Usually ``1.0'' or ``1.1''.
<dt><b>icy</b>
<dd> If set to 1 request <font SIZE="-1">ICY</font> (SHOUTcast) metadata from the server. If the server supports this, the metadata has to be retrieved by the application by reading the <b>icy_metadata_headers</b> and <b>icy_metadata_packet</b> options. The default is 1.
<dt><b>icy_metadata_headers</b>
<dd> If the server supports <font SIZE="-1">ICY</font> metadata, this contains the ICY-specific <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> reply headers, separated by newline characters.
<dt><b>icy_metadata_packet</b>
<dd> If the server supports <font SIZE="-1">ICY</font> metadata, and <b>icy</b> was set to 1, this contains the last non-empty metadata packet sent by the server. It should be polled in regular intervals by applications interested in mid-stream metadata updates.
<dt><b>cookies</b>
<dd> Set the cookies to be sent in future requests. The format of each cookie is the same as the value of a Set-Cookie <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> response field. Multiple cookies can be delimited by a newline character.
<dt><b>offset</b>
<dd> Set initial byte offset.
<dt><b>end_offset</b>
<dd> Try to limit the request to bytes preceding this offset.
<dt><b>method</b>
<dd> When used as a client option it sets the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method for the request. 

 When used as a server option it sets the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method that is going to be expected from the client(s). If the expected and the received <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method do not match the client will be given a Bad Request response. When unset the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> method is not checked for now. This will be replaced by autodetection in the future.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd> If set to 1 enables experimental <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server. This can be used to send data when used as an output option, or read data from a client with <font SIZE="-1">HTTP POST</font> when used as an input option. If set to 2 enables experimental multi-client <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> server. This is not yet implemented in ffmpeg.c and thus must not be used as a command line option. 

 <pre>
        # Server side (sending):
        ffmpeg -i somefile.ogg -c copy -listen 1 -f ogg http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
        
        # Client side (receiving):
        ffmpeg -i http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt; -c copy somefile.ogg
        
        # Client can also be done with wget:
        wget http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt; -O somefile.ogg
        
        # Server side (receiving):
        ffmpeg -listen 1 -i http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt; -c copy somefile.ogg
        
        # Client side (sending):
        ffmpeg -i somefile.ogg -chunked_post 0 -c copy -f ogg http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
        
        # Client can also be done with wget:
        wget --post-file=somefile.ogg http://&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
</pre>
<dt><b>send_expect_100</b>
<dd> Send an Expect: 100-continue header for <font SIZE="-1">POST.</font> If set to 1 it will send, if set to 0 it won't, if set to -1 it will try to send if it is applicable. Default value is -1.
<dt><b>auth_type</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> authentication type. No option for Digest, since this method requires getting nonce parameters from the server first and can't be used straight away like Basic.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Choose the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> authentication type automatically. This is the default.
<dt><b>basic</b>
<dd> Choose the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> basic authentication. 

 Basic authentication sends a Base64-encoded string that contains a user name and password for the client. Base64 is not a form of encryption and should be considered the same as sending the user name and password in clear text (Base64 is a reversible encoding). If a resource needs to be protected, strongly consider using an authentication scheme other than basic authentication. <font SIZE="-1">HTTPS/TLS</font> should be used with basic authentication. Without these additional security enhancements, basic authentication should not be used to protect sensitive or valuable information.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>HTTP</i></font><i> Cookies</i> 

 Some <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests will be denied unless cookie values are passed in with the request. The <b>cookies</b> option allows these cookies to be specified. At the very least, each cookie must specify a value along with a path and domain. <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests that match both the domain and path will automatically include the cookie value in the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> Cookie header field. Multiple cookies can be delimited by a newline. 

 The required syntax to play a stream specifying a cookie is: 

 <pre>
        ffplay -cookies &quot;nlqptid=nltid=tsn; path=/; domain=somedomain.com;&quot; <a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://somedomain.com/somestream.m3u8">http://somedomain.com/somestream.m3u8</a>
</pre>

<h3>Icecast</h3>

 Icecast protocol (stream to Icecast servers) 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>ice_genre</b>
<dd> Set the stream genre.
<dt><b>ice_name</b>
<dd> Set the stream name.
<dt><b>ice_description</b>
<dd> Set the stream description.
<dt><b>ice_url</b>
<dd> Set the stream website <font SIZE="-1">URL.</font>
<dt><b>ice_public</b>
<dd> Set if the stream should be public. The default is 0 (not public).
<dt><b>user_agent</b>
<dd> Override the User-Agent header. If not specified a string of the form ``Lavf/&lt;version&gt;'' will be used.
<dt><b>password</b>
<dd> Set the Icecast mountpoint password.
<dt><b>content_type</b>
<dd> Set the stream content type. This must be set if it is different from audio/mpeg.
<dt><b>legacy_icecast</b>
<dd> This enables support for Icecast versions &lt; 2.4.0, that do not support the <font SIZE="-1">HTTP PUT</font> method but the <font SIZE="-1">SOURCE</font> method.
<dt><b>tls</b>
<dd> Establish a <font SIZE="-1">TLS</font> (<font SIZE="-1">HTTPS</font>) connection to Icecast.</dl>
 

 
icecast: //[&lt;username&gt;[:&lt;password&gt;]@]&lt;server&gt;:&lt;port&gt;/&lt;mountpoint&gt;


<h3>mmst</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MMS</font> (Microsoft Media Server) protocol over <font SIZE="-1">TCP.</font>

<h3>mmsh</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MMS</font> (Microsoft Media Server) protocol over <font SIZE="-1">HTTP.</font> 

 The required syntax is: 

 
mmsh: //&lt;server&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][/&lt;app&gt;][/&lt;playpath&gt;]


<h3>md5</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> output protocol. 

 Computes the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> hash of the data to be written, and on close writes this to the designated output or stdout if none is specified. It can be used to test muxers without writing an actual file. 

 Some examples follow. 

 <pre>
        # Write the MD5 hash of the encoded AVI file to the file output.avi.md5.
        ffmpeg -i input.flv -f avi -y md5:output.avi.md5
        
        # Write the MD5 hash of the encoded AVI file to stdout.
        ffmpeg -i input.flv -f avi -y md5:
</pre> 

 Note that some formats (typically <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font>) require the output protocol to be seekable, so they will fail with the <font SIZE="-1">MD5</font> output protocol.

<h3>pipe</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">UNIX</font> pipe access protocol. 

 Read and write from <font SIZE="-1">UNIX</font> pipes. 

 The accepted syntax is: 

 <pre>
        pipe:[&lt;number&gt;]
</pre> 

 <i>number</i> is the number corresponding to the file descriptor of the pipe (e.g. 0 for stdin, 1 for stdout, 2 for stderr). If <i>number</i> is not specified, by default the stdout file descriptor will be used for writing, stdin for reading. 

 For example to read from stdin with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        cat test.wav | ffmpeg -i pipe:0
        # ...this is the same as...
        cat test.wav | ffmpeg -i pipe:
</pre> 

 For writing to stdout with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i test.wav -f avi pipe:1 | cat &gt; test.avi
        # ...this is the same as...
        ffmpeg -i test.wav -f avi pipe: | cat &gt; test.avi
</pre> 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>blocksize</b>
<dd> Set I/O operation maximum block size, in bytes. Default value is <tt>&quot;INT_MAX&quot;</tt>, which results in not limiting the requested block size. Setting this value reasonably low improves user termination request reaction time, which is valuable if data transmission is slow.</dl>
 

 Note that some formats (typically <font SIZE="-1">MOV</font>), require the output protocol to be seekable, so they will fail with the pipe output protocol.

<h3>prompeg</h3>

 Pro-MPEG Code of Practice #3 Release 2 <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> protocol. 

 The Pro-MPEG CoP#3 <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> is a 2D parity-check forward error correction mechanism for <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-2</font> Transport Streams sent over <font SIZE="-1">RTP.</font> 

 This protocol must be used in conjunction with the <tt>&quot;rtp_mpegts&quot;</tt> muxer and the <tt>&quot;rtp&quot;</tt> protocol. 

 The required syntax is: 

 <pre>
        -f rtp_mpegts -fec prompeg=&lt;option&gt;=&lt;val&gt;... rtp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
</pre> 

 The destination <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> ports are <tt>&quot;port + 2&quot;</tt> for the column <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> stream and <tt>&quot;port + 4&quot;</tt> for the row <font SIZE="-1">FEC</font> stream. 

 This protocol accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>l=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> The number of columns (4-20, LxD &lt;= 100)
<dt><b>d=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> The number of rows (4-20, LxD &lt;= 100)</dl>
 

 Example usage: 

 <pre>
        -f rtp_mpegts -fec prompeg=l=8:d=4 rtp://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
</pre>

<h3>rist</h3>

 Reliable Internet Streaming Transport protocol 

 The accepted options are:
<dl>
<dt><b>rist_profile</b>
<dd> Supported values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>simple</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>main</b>
<dd> This one is default.
<dt><b>advanced</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>buffer_size</b>
<dd> Set internal <font SIZE="-1">RIST</font> buffer size in milliseconds for retransmission of data. Default value is 0 which means the librist default (1 sec). Maximum value is 30 seconds.
<dt><b>pkt_size</b>
<dd> Set maximum packet size for sending data. 1316 by default.
<dt><b>log_level</b>
<dd> Set loglevel for <font SIZE="-1">RIST</font> logging messages. You only need to set this if you explicitly want to enable debug level messages or packet loss simulation, otherwise the regular loglevel is respected.
<dt><b>secret</b>
<dd> Set override of encryption secret, by default is unset.
<dt><b>encryption</b>
<dd> Set encryption type, by default is disabled. Acceptable values are 128 and 256.</dl>

<h3>rtmp</h3>

 Real-Time Messaging Protocol. 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content across a <font SIZE="-1">TCP/IP</font> network. 

 The required syntax is: 

 
rtmp: //[&lt;username&gt;:&lt;password&gt;@]&lt;server&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][/&lt;app&gt;][/&lt;instance&gt;][/&lt;playpath&gt;]
 

 The accepted parameters are:
<dl>
<dt><b>username</b>
<dd> An optional username (mostly for publishing).
<dt><b>password</b>
<dd> An optional password (mostly for publishing).
<dt><b>server</b>
<dd> The address of the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server.
<dt><b>port</b>
<dd> The number of the <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> port to use (by default is 1935).
<dt><b>app</b>
<dd> It is the name of the application to access. It usually corresponds to the path where the application is installed on the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server (e.g. <i>/ondemand/</i>, <i>/flash/live/</i>, etc.). You can override the value parsed from the <font SIZE="-1">URI</font> through the <tt>&quot;rtmp_app&quot;</tt> option, too.
<dt><b>playpath</b>
<dd> It is the path or name of the resource to play with reference to the application specified in <i>app</i>, may be prefixed by ``mp4:''. You can override the value parsed from the <font SIZE="-1">URI</font> through the <tt>&quot;rtmp_playpath&quot;</tt> option, too.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd> Act as a server, listening for an incoming connection.
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd> Maximum time to wait for the incoming connection. Implies listen.</dl>
 

 Additionally, the following parameters can be set via command line options (or in code via <tt>&quot;AVOption&quot;</tt>s):
<dl>
<dt><b>rtmp_app</b>
<dd> Name of application to connect on the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server. This option overrides the parameter specified in the <font SIZE="-1">URI.</font>
<dt><b>rtmp_buffer</b>
<dd> Set the client buffer time in milliseconds. The default is 3000.
<dt><b>rtmp_conn</b>
<dd> Extra arbitrary <font SIZE="-1">AMF</font> connection parameters, parsed from a string, e.g. like <tt>&quot;B:1 S:authMe O:1 NN:code:1.23 NS:flag:ok O:0&quot;</tt>. Each value is prefixed by a single character denoting the type, B for Boolean, N for number, S for string, O for object, or Z for null, followed by a colon. For Booleans the data must be either 0 or 1 for <font SIZE="-1">FALSE</font> or <font SIZE="-1">TRUE,</font> respectively. Likewise for Objects the data must be 0 or 1 to end or begin an object, respectively. Data items in subobjects may be named, by prefixing the type with 'N' and specifying the name before the value (i.e. <tt>&quot;NB:myFlag:1&quot;</tt>). This option may be used multiple times to construct arbitrary <font SIZE="-1">AMF</font> sequences.
<dt><b>rtmp_flashver</b>
<dd> Version of the Flash plugin used to run the <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> player. The default is <font SIZE="-1">LNX 9,0,124,2.</font> (When publishing, the default is <font SIZE="-1">FMLE/3.0</font> (compatible; &lt;libavformat version&gt;).)
<dt><b>rtmp_flush_interval</b>
<dd> Number of packets flushed in the same request (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPT</font> only). The default is 10.
<dt><b>rtmp_live</b>
<dd> Specify that the media is a live stream. No resuming or seeking in live streams is possible. The default value is <tt>&quot;any&quot;</tt>, which means the subscriber first tries to play the live stream specified in the playpath. If a live stream of that name is not found, it plays the recorded stream. The other possible values are <tt>&quot;live&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;recorded&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rtmp_pageurl</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the web page in which the media was embedded. By default no value will be sent.
<dt><b>rtmp_playpath</b>
<dd> Stream identifier to play or to publish. This option overrides the parameter specified in the <font SIZE="-1">URI.</font>
<dt><b>rtmp_subscribe</b>
<dd> Name of live stream to subscribe to. By default no value will be sent. It is only sent if the option is specified or if rtmp_live is set to live.
<dt><b>rtmp_swfhash</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SHA256</font> hash of the decompressed <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> file (32 bytes).
<dt><b>rtmp_swfsize</b>
<dd> Size of the decompressed <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> file, required for SWFVerification.
<dt><b>rtmp_swfurl</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the <font SIZE="-1">SWF</font> player for the media. By default no value will be sent.
<dt><b>rtmp_swfverify</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> to player swf file, compute hash/size automatically.
<dt><b>rtmp_tcurl</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> of the target stream. Defaults to <a HREF="proto://host[:port]/app.">proto://host[:port]/app.</a></dl>
 

 For example to read with <b>ffplay</b> a multimedia resource named ``sample'' from the application ``vod'' from an <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server ``myserver'': 

 <pre>
        ffplay <a HREF="rtmp://myserver/vod/sample">rtmp://myserver/vod/sample</a>
</pre> 

 To publish to a password protected server, passing the playpath and app names separately: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f flv -rtmp_playpath some/long/path -rtmp_app long/app/name <a HREF="rtmp://username:password@myserver/">rtmp://username:password@myserver/</a>
</pre>

<h3>rtmpe</h3>

 Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol. 

 The Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPE</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within standard cryptographic primitives, consisting of Diffie-Hellman key exchange and <font SIZE="-1">HMACSHA256,</font> generating a pair of <font SIZE="-1">RC4</font> keys.

<h3>rtmps</h3>

 Real-Time Messaging Protocol over a secure <font SIZE="-1">SSL</font> connection. 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPS</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content across an encrypted connection.

<h3>rtmpt</h3>

 Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP.</font> 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPT</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests to traverse firewalls.

<h3>rtmpte</h3>

 Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP.</font> 

 The Encrypted Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPTE</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> requests to traverse firewalls.

<h3>rtmpts</h3>

 Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTPS.</font> 

 The Real-Time Messaging Protocol tunneled through <font SIZE="-1">HTTPS</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPTS</font>) is used for streaming multimedia content within <font SIZE="-1">HTTPS</font> requests to traverse firewalls.

<h3>libsmbclient</h3>

 libsmbclient permits one to manipulate <font SIZE="-1">CIFS/SMB</font> network resources. 

 Following syntax is required. 

 
smb: //[[domain:]user[:password@]]server[/share[/path[/file]]]
 

 This protocol accepts the following options.
<dl>
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd> Set timeout in milliseconds of socket I/O operations used by the underlying low level operation. By default it is set to -1, which means that the timeout is not specified.
<dt><b>truncate</b>
<dd> Truncate existing files on write, if set to 1. A value of 0 prevents truncating. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>workgroup</b>
<dd> Set the workgroup used for making connections. By default workgroup is not specified.</dl>
 

 For more information see: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.samba.org/">http://www.samba.org/</a></b>&gt;.

<h3>libssh</h3>

 Secure File Transfer Protocol via libssh 

 Read from or write to remote resources using <font SIZE="-1">SFTP</font> protocol. 

 Following syntax is required. 

 
sftp: //[user[:password]@]server[:port]/path/to/remote/resource.mpeg
 

 This protocol accepts the following options.
<dl>
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd> Set timeout of socket I/O operations used by the underlying low level operation. By default it is set to -1, which means that the timeout is not specified.
<dt><b>truncate</b>
<dd> Truncate existing files on write, if set to 1. A value of 0 prevents truncating. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>private_key</b>
<dd> Specify the path of the file containing private key to use during authorization. By default libssh searches for keys in the <i>~/.ssh/</i> directory.</dl>
 

 Example: Play a file stored on remote server. 

 <pre>
        ffplay <a HREF="sftp://user:password@server_address:22/home/user/resource.mpeg">sftp://user:password@server_address:22/home/user/resource.mpeg</a>
</pre>

<h3>librtmp rtmp, rtmpe, rtmps, rtmpt, rtmpte</h3>

 Real-Time Messaging Protocol and its variants supported through librtmp. 

 Requires the presence of the librtmp headers and library during configuration. You need to explicitly configure the build with ``--enable-librtmp''. If enabled this will replace the native <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> protocol. 

 This protocol provides most client functions and a few server functions needed to support <font SIZE="-1">RTMP, RTMP</font> tunneled in <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPT</font>), encrypted <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPE</font>), <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> over <font SIZE="-1">SSL/TLS</font> (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPS</font>) and tunneled variants of these encrypted types (<font SIZE="-1">RTMPTE, RTMPTS</font>). 

 The required syntax is: 

 
        &lt;rtmp_proto&gt;://&lt;server&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][/&lt;app&gt;][/&lt;playpath&gt;] &lt;options&gt;
 

 where <i>rtmp_proto</i> is one of the strings ``rtmp'', ``rtmpt'', ``rtmpe'', ``rtmps'', ``rtmpte'', ``rtmpts'' corresponding to each <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> variant, and <i>server</i>, <i>port</i>, <i>app</i> and <i>playpath</i> have the same meaning as specified for the <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> native protocol. <i>options</i> contains a list of space-separated options of the form <i>key</i>=<i>val</i>. 

 See the librtmp manual page (man 3 librtmp) for more information. 

 For example, to stream a file in real-time to an <font SIZE="-1">RTMP</font> server using <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i myfile -f flv <a HREF="rtmp://myserver/live/mystream">rtmp://myserver/live/mystream</a>
</pre> 

 To play the same stream using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffplay &quot;<a HREF="rtmp://myserver/live/mystream">rtmp://myserver/live/mystream</a> live=1&quot;
</pre>

<h3>rtp</h3>

 Real-time Transport Protocol. 

 The required syntax for an <font SIZE="-1">RTP URL</font> is: rtp://<i>hostname</i>[:<i>port</i>][?<i>option</i>=<i>val</i>...] 

 <i>port</i> specifies the <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port to use. 

 The following <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> options are supported:
<dl>
<dt><b>ttl=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">TTL</font> (Time-To-Live) value (for multicast only).
<dt><b>rtcpport=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> Set the remote <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>localrtpport=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> Set the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>localrtcpport=</b><i>n</i><b>'</b>
<dd> Set the local <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>pkt_size=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> Set max packet size (in bytes) to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>buffer_size=</b><i>size</i>
<dd> Set the maximum <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> socket buffer size in bytes.
<dt><b>connect=0|1</b>
<dd> Do a <tt>&quot;connect()&quot;</tt> on the <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> socket (if set to 1) or not (if set to 0).
<dt><b>sources=</b><i>ip</i><b>[,</b><i>ip</i><b>]</b>
<dd> List allowed source <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> addresses.
<dt><b>block=</b><i>ip</i><b>[,</b><i>ip</i><b>]</b>
<dd> List disallowed (blocked) source <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> addresses.
<dt><b>write_to_source=0|1</b>
<dd> Send packets to the source address of the latest received packet (if set to 1) or to a default remote address (if set to 0).
<dt><b>localport=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> Set the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port to <i>n</i>.
<dt><b>timeout=</b><i>n</i>
<dd> Set timeout (in microseconds) of socket I/O operations to <i>n</i>. 

 This is a deprecated option. Instead, <b>localrtpport</b> should be used.</dl>
 

 Important notes:
<dl>
<dt>1.
<dd> If <b>rtcpport</b> is not set the <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port will be set to the <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port value plus 1.
<dt>2.
<dd> If <b>localrtpport</b> (the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port) is not set any available port will be used for the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> and <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> ports.
<dt>3.
<dd> If <b>localrtcpport</b> (the local <font SIZE="-1">RTCP</font> port) is not set it will be set to the local <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> port value plus 1.</dl>

<h3>rtsp</h3>

 Real-Time Streaming Protocol. 

 <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> is not technically a protocol handler in libavformat, it is a demuxer and muxer. The demuxer supports both normal <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> (with data transferred over <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font>; this is used by e.g. Apple and Microsoft) and Real-RTSP (with data transferred over <font SIZE="-1">RDT</font>). 

 The muxer can be used to send a stream using <font SIZE="-1">RTSP ANNOUNCE</font> to a server supporting it (currently Darwin Streaming Server and Mischa Spiegelmock's &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/revmischa/rtsp-server">https://github.com/revmischa/rtsp-server</a></b>&gt;). 

 The required syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> url is: 

 <pre>
        rtsp://&lt;hostname&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;]/&lt;path&gt;
</pre> 

 Options can be set on the <b>ffmpeg</b>/<b>ffplay</b> command line, or set in code via <tt>&quot;AVOption&quot;</tt>s or in <tt>&quot;avformat_open_input&quot;</tt>. 

 The following options are supported.
<dl>
<dt><b>initial_pause</b>
<dd> Do not start playing the stream immediately if set to 1. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>rtsp_transport</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> transport protocols. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>udp</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> as lower transport protocol.
<dt><b>tcp</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> (interleaving within the <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> control channel) as lower transport protocol.
<dt><b>udp_multicast</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> multicast as lower transport protocol.
<dt><b>http</b>
<dd> Use <font SIZE="-1">HTTP</font> tunneling as lower transport protocol, which is useful for passing proxies.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Multiple lower transport protocols may be specified, in that case they are tried one at a time (if the setup of one fails, the next one is tried). For the muxer, only the <b>tcp</b> and <b>udp</b> options are supported.</dl>

<dt><b>rtsp_flags</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> flags. 

 The following values are accepted:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>filter_src</b>
<dd> Accept packets only from negotiated peer address and port.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd> Act as a server, listening for an incoming connection.
<dt><b>prefer_tcp</b>
<dd> Try <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> for <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> transport first, if <font SIZE="-1">TCP</font> is available as <font SIZE="-1">RTSP RTP</font> transport.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>none</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>allowed_media_types</b>
<dd> Set media types to accept from the server. 

 The following flags are accepted:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>video</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>audio</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>data</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 By default it accepts all media types.</dl>

<dt><b>min_port</b>
<dd> Set minimum local <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> port. Default value is 5000.
<dt><b>max_port</b>
<dd> Set maximum local <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> port. Default value is 65000.
<dt><b>timeout</b>
<dd> Set maximum timeout (in seconds) to wait for incoming connections. 

 A value of -1 means infinite (default). This option implies the <b>rtsp_flags</b> set to <b>listen</b>.
<dt><b>reorder_queue_size</b>
<dd> Set number of packets to buffer for handling of reordered packets.
<dt><b>stimeout</b>
<dd> Set socket <font SIZE="-1">TCP I/O</font> timeout in microseconds.
<dt><b>user-agent</b>
<dd> Override User-Agent header. If not specified, it defaults to the libavformat identifier string.</dl>
 

 When receiving data over <font SIZE="-1">UDP,</font> the demuxer tries to reorder received packets (since they may arrive out of order, or packets may get lost totally). This can be disabled by setting the maximum demuxing delay to zero (via the <tt>&quot;max_delay&quot;</tt> field of AVFormatContext). 

 When watching multi-bitrate Real-RTSP streams with <b>ffplay</b>, the streams to display can be chosen with <tt>&quot;-vst&quot;</tt> <i>n</i> and <tt>&quot;-ast&quot;</tt> <i>n</i> for video and audio respectively, and can be switched on the fly by pressing <tt>&quot;v&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;a&quot;</tt>. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 The following examples all make use of the <b>ffplay</b> and <b>ffmpeg</b> tools.
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Watch a stream over <font SIZE="-1">UDP,</font> with a max reordering delay of 0.5 seconds: 

 <pre>
        ffplay -max_delay 500000 -rtsp_transport udp <a HREF="rtsp://server/video.mp4">rtsp://server/video.mp4</a>
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Watch a stream tunneled over <font SIZE="-1">HTTP:</font> 

 <pre>
        ffplay -rtsp_transport http <a HREF="rtsp://server/video.mp4">rtsp://server/video.mp4</a>
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Send a stream in realtime to a <font SIZE="-1">RTSP</font> server, for others to watch: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f rtsp -muxdelay 0.1 <a HREF="rtsp://server/live.sdp">rtsp://server/live.sdp</a>
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Receive a stream in realtime: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -rtsp_flags listen -i <a HREF="rtsp://ownaddress/live.sdp">rtsp://ownaddress/live.sdp</a> &lt;output&gt;
</pre></dl>

<h3>sap</h3>

 Session Announcement Protocol (<font SIZE="-1">RFC 2974</font>). This is not technically a protocol handler in libavformat, it is a muxer and demuxer. It is used for signalling of <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> streams, by announcing the <font SIZE="-1">SDP</font> for the streams regularly on a separate port. 

 <i>Muxer</i> 

 The syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> url given to the muxer is: 

 
sap: //&lt;destination&gt;[:&lt;port&gt;][?&lt;options&gt;]
 

 The <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> packets are sent to <i>destination</i> on port <i>port</i>, or to port 5004 if no port is specified. <i>options</i> is a <tt>&quot;&amp;&quot;</tt>-separated list. The following options are supported:
<dl>
<dt><b>announce_addr=</b><i>address</i>
<dd> Specify the destination <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> address for sending the announcements to. If omitted, the announcements are sent to the commonly used <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> announcement multicast address 224.2.127.254 (sap.mcast.net), or ff0e::2:7ffe if <i>destination</i> is an IPv6 address.
<dt><b>announce_port=</b><i>port</i>
<dd> Specify the port to send the announcements on, defaults to 9875 if not specified.
<dt><b>ttl=</b><i>ttl</i>
<dd> Specify the time to live value for the announcements and <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> packets, defaults to 255.
<dt><b>same_port=</b><i>0|1</i>
<dd> If set to 1, send all <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> streams on the same port pair. If zero (the default), all streams are sent on unique ports, with each stream on a port 2 numbers higher than the previous. VLC/Live555 requires this to be set to 1, to be able to receive the stream. The <font SIZE="-1">RTP</font> stack in libavformat for receiving requires all streams to be sent on unique ports.</dl>
 

 Example command lines follow. 

 To broadcast a stream on the local subnet, for watching in <font SIZE="-1">VLC:</font> 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f sap <a HREF="sap://224.0.0.255?same_port=1">sap://224.0.0.255?same_port=1</a>
</pre> 

 Similarly, for watching in <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f sap <a HREF="sap://224.0.0.255">sap://224.0.0.255</a>
</pre> 

 And for watching in <b>ffplay</b>, over IPv6: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i &lt;input&gt; -f sap <a HREF="sap://[ff0e::1:2:3:4]">sap://[ff0e::1:2:3:4]</a>
</pre> 

 <i>Demuxer</i> 

 The syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> url given to the demuxer is: 

 
sap: //[&lt;address&gt;][:&lt;port&gt;]
 

 <i>address</i> is the multicast address to listen for announcements on, if omitted, the default 224.2.127.254 (sap.mcast.net) is used. <i>port</i> is the port that is listened on, 9875 if omitted. 

 The demuxers listens for announcements on the given address and port. Once an announcement is received, it tries to receive that particular stream. 

 Example command lines follow. 

 To play back the first stream announced on the normal <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> multicast address: 

 <pre>
        ffplay sap://
</pre> 

 To play back the first stream announced on one the default IPv6 <font SIZE="-1">SAP</font> multicast address: 

 <pre>
        ffplay <a HREF="sap://[ff0e::2:7ffe]">sap://[ff0e::2:7ffe]</a>
</pre>

<h3>sctp</h3>

 Stream Control Transmission Protocol. 

 The accepted <font SIZE="-1">URL</font> syntax is: 

 <pre>
        sctp://&lt;host&gt;:&lt;port&gt;[?&lt;options&gt;]
</pre> 

 The protocol accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd> If set to any value, listen for an incoming connection. Outgoing connection is done by default.
<dt><b>max_streams</b>
<dd> Set the maximum number of streams. By default no limit is set.</dl>

<h3>srt</h3>

 Haivision Secure Reliable Transport Protocol via libsrt. 

 The supported syntax for a <font SIZE="-1">SRT URL</font> is: 

 <pre>
        srt://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;[?&lt;options&gt;]
</pre> 

 <i>options</i> contains a list of &amp;-separated options of the form <i>key</i>=<i>val</i>. 

 or 

 <pre>
        &lt;options&gt; srt://&lt;hostname&gt;:&lt;port&gt;
</pre> 

 <i>options</i> contains a list of '-<i>key</i> <i>val</i>' options. 

 This protocol accepts the following options.
<dl>
<dt><b>connect_timeout=</b><i>milliseconds</i>
<dd> Connection timeout; <font SIZE="-1">SRT</font> cannot connect for <font SIZE="-1">RTT</font> &gt; 1500 msec (2 handshake exchanges) with the default connect timeout of 3 seconds. This option applies to the caller and rendezvous connection modes. The connect timeout is 10 times the value set for the rendezvous mode (which can be used as a workaround for this connection problem with earlier versions).
<dt><b>ffs=</b><i>bytes</i>
<dd> Flight Flag Size (Window Size), in bytes. <font SIZE="-1">FFS</font> is actually an internal parameter and you should set it to not less than <b>recv_buffer_size</b> and <b>mss</b>. The default value is relatively large, therefore unless you set a very large receiver buffer, you do not need to change this option. Default value is 25600.
<dt><b>inputbw=</b><i>bytes/seconds</i>
<dd> Sender nominal input rate, in bytes per seconds. Used along with <b>oheadbw</b>, when <b>maxbw</b> is set to relative (0), to calculate maximum sending rate when recovery packets are sent along with the main media stream: <b>inputbw</b> * (100 + <b>oheadbw</b>) / 100 if <b>inputbw</b> is not set while <b>maxbw</b> is set to relative (0), the actual input rate is evaluated inside the library. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>iptos=</b><i>tos</i>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> Type of Service. Applies to sender only. Default value is 0xB8.
<dt><b>ipttl=</b><i>ttl</i>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> Time To Live. Applies to sender only. Default value is 64.
<dt><b>latency=</b><i>microseconds</i>
<dd> Timestamp-based Packet Delivery Delay. Used to absorb bursts of missed packet retransmissions. This flag sets both <b>rcvlatency</b> and <b>peerlatency</b> to the same value. Note that prior to version 1.3.0 this is the only flag to set the latency, however this is effectively equivalent to setting <b>peerlatency</b>, when side is sender and <b>rcvlatency</b> when side is receiver, and the bidirectional stream sending is not supported.
<dt><b>listen_timeout=</b><i>microseconds</i>
<dd> Set socket listen timeout.
<dt><b>maxbw=</b><i>bytes/seconds</i>
<dd> Maximum sending bandwidth, in bytes per seconds. -1 infinite (<font SIZE="-1">CSRTCC</font> limit is 30mbps) 0 relative to input rate (see <b>inputbw</b>) &gt;0 absolute limit value Default value is 0 (relative)
<dt><b>mode=</b><i>caller|listener|rendezvous</i>
<dd> Connection mode. <b>caller</b> opens client connection. <b>listener</b> starts server to listen for incoming connections. <b>rendezvous</b> use Rendez-Vous connection mode. Default value is caller.
<dt><b>mss=</b><i>bytes</i>
<dd> Maximum Segment Size, in bytes. Used for buffer allocation and rate calculation using a packet counter assuming fully filled packets. The smallest <font SIZE="-1">MSS</font> between the peers is used. This is 1500 by default in the overall internet. This is the maximum size of the <font SIZE="-1">UDP</font> packet and can be only decreased, unless you have some unusual dedicated network settings. Default value is 1500.
<dt><b>nakreport=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd> If set to 1, Receiver will send `UMSG_LOSSREPORT` messages periodically until a lost packet is retransmitted or intentionally dropped. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>oheadbw=</b><i>percents</i>
<dd> Recovery bandwidth overhead above input rate, in percents. See <b>inputbw</b>. Default value is 25%.
<dt><b>passphrase=</b><i>string</i>
<dd> HaiCrypt Encryption/Decryption Passphrase string, length from 10 to 79 characters. The passphrase is the shared secret between the sender and the receiver. It is used to generate the Key Encrypting Key using <font SIZE="-1">PBKDF2</font> (Password-Based Key Derivation Function). It is used only if <b>pbkeylen</b> is non-zero. It is used on the receiver only if the received data is encrypted. The configured passphrase cannot be recovered (write-only).
<dt><b>enforced_encryption=</b><i>1|0</i>
<dd> If true, both connection parties must have the same password set (including empty, that is, with no encryption). If the password doesn't match or only one side is unencrypted, the connection is rejected. Default is true.
<dt><b>kmrefreshrate=</b><i>packets</i>
<dd> The number of packets to be transmitted after which the encryption key is switched to a new key. Default is -1. -1 means auto (0x1000000 in srt library). The range for this option is integers in the 0 - <tt>&quot;INT_MAX&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>kmpreannounce=</b><i>packets</i>
<dd> The interval between when a new encryption key is sent and when switchover occurs. This value also applies to the subsequent interval between when switchover occurs and when the old encryption key is decommissioned. Default is -1. -1 means auto (0x1000 in srt library). The range for this option is integers in the 0 - <tt>&quot;INT_MAX&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>payload_size=</b><i>bytes</i>
<dd> Sets the maximum declared size of a packet transferred during the single call to the sending function in Live mode. Use 0 if this value isn't used (which is default in file mode). Default is -1 (automatic), which typically means MPEG-TS; if you are going to use <font SIZE="-1">SRT</font> to send any different kind of payload, such as, for example, wrapping a live stream in very small frames, then you can use a bigger maximum frame size, though not greater than 1456 bytes.
<dt><b>pkt_size=</b><i>bytes</i>
<dd> Alias for <b>payload_size</b>.
<dt><b>peerlatency=</b><i>microseconds</i>
