On Windows, you need to run the <font SIZE="-1">IDL</font> files through <b>widl</b>. 

 DeckLink is very picky about the formats it supports. Pixel format is always uyvy422, framerate, field order and video size must be determined for your device with <b>-list_formats 1</b>. Audio sample rate is always 48 kHz. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>list_devices</b>
<dd> If set to <b>true</b>, print a list of devices and exit. Defaults to <b>false</b>. This option is deprecated, please use the <tt>&quot;-sinks&quot;</tt> option of ffmpeg to list the available output devices.
<dt><b>list_formats</b>
<dd> If set to <b>true</b>, print a list of supported formats and exit. Defaults to <b>false</b>.
<dt><b>preroll</b>
<dd> Amount of time to preroll video in seconds. Defaults to <b>0.5</b>.
<dt><b>duplex_mode</b>
<dd> Sets the decklink device duplex mode. Must be <b>unset</b>, <b>half</b> or <b>full</b>. Defaults to <b>unset</b>.
<dt><b>timing_offset</b>
<dd> Sets the genlock timing pixel offset on the used output. Defaults to <b>unset</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> List output devices: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -sinks decklink
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> List supported formats: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i test.avi -f decklink -list_formats 1 'DeckLink Mini Monitor'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Play video clip: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i test.avi -f decklink -pix_fmt uyvy422 'DeckLink Mini Monitor'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Play video clip with non-standard framerate or video size: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i test.avi -f decklink -pix_fmt uyvy422 -s 720x486 -r 24000/1001 'DeckLink Mini Monitor'
</pre></dl>

<h3>fbdev</h3>

 Linux framebuffer output device. 

 The Linux framebuffer is a graphic hardware-independent abstraction layer to show graphics on a computer monitor, typically on the console. It is accessed through a file device node, usually <i>/dev/fb0</i>. 

 For more detailed information read the file <i>Documentation/fb/framebuffer.txt</i> included in the Linux source tree. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>xoffset</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>yoffset</b>
<dd> Set x/y coordinate of top left corner. Default is 0.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 Play a file on framebuffer device <i>/dev/fb0</i>. Required pixel format depends on current framebuffer settings. 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -re -i INPUT -c:v rawvideo -pix_fmt bgra -f fbdev /dev/fb0
</pre> 

 See also &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://linux-fbdev.sourceforge.net/">http://linux-fbdev.sourceforge.net/</a></b>&gt;, and <b><a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-fbset/">fbset</a></b>(1).

<h3>opengl</h3>

 OpenGL output device. 

 To enable this output device you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-opengl&quot;</tt>. 

 This output device allows one to render to OpenGL context. Context may be provided by application or default <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window is created. 

 When device renders to external context, application must implement handlers for following messages: <tt>&quot;AV_DEV_TO_APP_CREATE_WINDOW_BUFFER&quot;</tt> - create OpenGL context on current thread. <tt>&quot;AV_DEV_TO_APP_PREPARE_WINDOW_BUFFER&quot;</tt> - make OpenGL context current. <tt>&quot;AV_DEV_TO_APP_DISPLAY_WINDOW_BUFFER&quot;</tt> - swap buffers. <tt>&quot;AV_DEV_TO_APP_DESTROY_WINDOW_BUFFER&quot;</tt> - destroy OpenGL context. Application is also required to inform a device about current resolution by sending <tt>&quot;AV_APP_TO_DEV_WINDOW_SIZE&quot;</tt> message. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>background</b>
<dd> Set background color. Black is a default.
<dt><b>no_window</b>
<dd> Disables default <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window when set to non-zero value. Application must provide OpenGL context and both <tt>&quot;window_size_cb&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;window_swap_buffers_cb&quot;</tt> callbacks when set.
<dt><b>window_title</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window title, if not specified default to the filename specified for the output device. Ignored when <b>no_window</b> is set.
<dt><b>window_size</b>
<dd> Set preferred window size, can be a string of the form widthxheight or a video size abbreviation. If not specified it defaults to the size of the input video, downscaled according to the aspect ratio. Mostly usable when <b>no_window</b> is not set.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 Play a file on <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window using OpenGL rendering: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg  -i INPUT -f opengl &quot;window title&quot;
</pre>

<h3>oss</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">OSS</font> (Open Sound System) output device.

<h3>pulse</h3>

 PulseAudio output device. 

 To enable this output device you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libpulse&quot;</tt>. 

 More information about PulseAudio can be found on &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.pulseaudio.org">http://www.pulseaudio.org</a></b>&gt; 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>server</b>
<dd> Connect to a specific PulseAudio server, specified by an <font SIZE="-1">IP</font> address. Default server is used when not provided.
<dt><b>name</b>
<dd> Specify the application name PulseAudio will use when showing active clients, by default it is the <tt>&quot;LIBAVFORMAT_IDENT&quot;</tt> string.
<dt><b>stream_name</b>
<dd> Specify the stream name PulseAudio will use when showing active streams, by default it is set to the specified output name.
<dt><b>device</b>
<dd> Specify the device to use. Default device is used when not provided. List of output devices can be obtained with command <b>pactl list sinks</b>.
<dt><b>buffer_size</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>buffer_duration</b>
<dd> Control the size and duration of the PulseAudio buffer. A small buffer gives more control, but requires more frequent updates. 

 <b>buffer_size</b> specifies size in bytes while <b>buffer_duration</b> specifies duration in milliseconds. 

 When both options are provided then the highest value is used (duration is recalculated to bytes using stream parameters). If they are set to 0 (which is default), the device will use the default PulseAudio duration value. By default PulseAudio set buffer duration to around 2 seconds.
<dt><b>prebuf</b>
<dd> Specify pre-buffering size in bytes. The server does not start with playback before at least <b>prebuf</b> bytes are available in the buffer. By default this option is initialized to the same value as <b>buffer_size</b> or <b>buffer_duration</b> (whichever is bigger).
<dt><b>minreq</b>
<dd> Specify minimum request size in bytes. The server does not request less than <b>minreq</b> bytes from the client, instead waits until the buffer is free enough to request more bytes at once. It is recommended to not set this option, which will initialize this to a value that is deemed sensible by the server.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 Play a file on default device on default server: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg  -i INPUT -f pulse &quot;stream name&quot;
</pre>

<h3>sdl</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> (Simple DirectMedia Layer) output device. 

 ``sdl2'' can be used as alias for ``sdl''. 

 This output device allows one to show a video stream in an <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window. Only one <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window is allowed per application, so you can have only one instance of this output device in an application. 

 To enable this output device you need libsdl installed on your system when configuring your build. 

 For more information about <font SIZE="-1">SDL,</font> check: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.libsdl.org/">http://www.libsdl.org/</a></b>&gt; 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>window_title</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window title, if not specified default to the filename specified for the output device.
<dt><b>icon_title</b>
<dd> Set the name of the iconified <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window, if not specified it is set to the same value of <i>window_title</i>.
<dt><b>window_size</b>
<dd> Set the <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window size, can be a string of the form <i>width</i>x<i>height</i> or a video size abbreviation. If not specified it defaults to the size of the input video, downscaled according to the aspect ratio.
<dt><b>window_x</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>window_y</b>
<dd> Set the position of the window on the screen.
<dt><b>window_fullscreen</b>
<dd> Set fullscreen mode when non-zero value is provided. Default value is zero.
<dt><b>window_enable_quit</b>
<dd> Enable quit action (using window button or keyboard key) when non-zero value is provided. Default value is 1 (enable quit action)</dl>
 

 <i>Interactive commands</i> 

 The window created by the device can be controlled through the following interactive commands.
<dl>
<dt><b>q, </b><font SIZE="-1"><b>ESC</b></font>
<dd> Quit the device immediately.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 The following command shows the <b>ffmpeg</b> output is an <font SIZE="-1">SDL</font> window, forcing its size to the qcif format: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -c:v rawvideo -pix_fmt yuv420p -window_size qcif -f sdl &quot;SDL output&quot;
</pre>

<h3>sndio</h3>

 sndio audio output device.

<h3>v4l2</h3>

 Video4Linux2 output device.

<h3>xv</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">XV</font> (XVideo) output device. 

 This output device allows one to show a video stream in a X Window System window. 

 <i>Options</i>
<dl>
<dt><b>display_name</b>
<dd> Specify the hardware display name, which determines the display and communications domain to be used. 

 The display name or <font SIZE="-1">DISPLAY</font> environment variable can be a string in the format <i>hostname</i>[:<i>number</i>[.<i>screen_number</i>]]. 

 <i>hostname</i> specifies the name of the host machine on which the display is physically attached. <i>number</i> specifies the number of the display server on that host machine. <i>screen_number</i> specifies the screen to be used on that server. 

 If unspecified, it defaults to the value of the <font SIZE="-1">DISPLAY</font> environment variable. 

 For example, <tt>&quot;dual-headed:0.1&quot;</tt> would specify screen 1 of display 0 on the machine named ``dual-headed''. 

 Check the X11 specification for more detailed information about the display name format.
<dt><b>window_id</b>
<dd> When set to non-zero value then device doesn't create new window, but uses existing one with provided <i>window_id</i>. By default this options is set to zero and device creates its own window.
<dt><b>window_size</b>
<dd> Set the created window size, can be a string of the form <i>width</i>x<i>height</i> or a video size abbreviation. If not specified it defaults to the size of the input video. Ignored when <i>window_id</i> is set.
<dt><b>window_x</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>window_y</b>
<dd> Set the X and Y window offsets for the created window. They are both set to 0 by default. The values may be ignored by the window manager. Ignored when <i>window_id</i> is set.
<dt><b>window_title</b>
<dd> Set the window title, if not specified default to the filename specified for the output device. Ignored when <i>window_id</i> is set.</dl>
 

 For more information about XVideo see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.x.org/">http://www.x.org/</a></b>&gt;. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Decode, display and encode video input with <b>ffmpeg</b> at the same time: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT OUTPUT -f xv display
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Decode and display the input video to multiple X11 windows: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -f xv normal -vf negate -f xv negated
</pre></dl>

<h2>RESAMPLER OPTIONS</h2>

 The audio resampler supports the following named options. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, <i>option</i>=<i>value</i> for the aresample filter, by setting the value explicitly in the <tt>&quot;SwrContext&quot;</tt> options or using the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API</font> for programmatic use.
<dl>
<dt><b>ich, in_channel_count</b>
<dd> Set the number of input channels. Default value is 0. Setting this value is not mandatory if the corresponding channel layout <b>in_channel_layout</b> is set.
<dt><b>och, out_channel_count</b>
<dd> Set the number of output channels. Default value is 0. Setting this value is not mandatory if the corresponding channel layout <b>out_channel_layout</b> is set.
<dt><b>uch, used_channel_count</b>
<dd> Set the number of used input channels. Default value is 0. This option is only used for special remapping.
<dt><b>isr, in_sample_rate</b>
<dd> Set the input sample rate. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>osr, out_sample_rate</b>
<dd> Set the output sample rate. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>isf, in_sample_fmt</b>
<dd> Specify the input sample format. It is set by default to <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>osf, out_sample_fmt</b>
<dd> Specify the output sample format. It is set by default to <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>tsf, internal_sample_fmt</b>
<dd> Set the internal sample format. Default value is <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>. This will automatically be chosen when it is not explicitly set.
<dt><b>icl, in_channel_layout</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ocl, out_channel_layout</b>
<dd> Set the input/output channel layout. 

 See <b>the Channel Layout section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the required syntax.
<dt><b>clev, center_mix_level</b>
<dd> Set the center mix level. It is a value expressed in deciBel, and must be in the interval [-32,32].
<dt><b>slev, surround_mix_level</b>
<dd> Set the surround mix level. It is a value expressed in deciBel, and must be in the interval [-32,32].
<dt><b>lfe_mix_level</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> mix into non <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> level. It is used when there is a <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> input but no <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> output. It is a value expressed in deciBel, and must be in the interval [-32,32].
<dt><b>rmvol, rematrix_volume</b>
<dd> Set rematrix volume. Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>rematrix_maxval</b>
<dd> Set maximum output value for rematrixing. This can be used to prevent clipping vs. preventing volume reduction. A value of 1.0 prevents clipping.
<dt><b>flags, swr_flags</b>
<dd> Set flags used by the converter. Default value is 0. 

 It supports the following individual flags:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>res</b>
<dd> force resampling, this flag forces resampling to be used even when the input and output sample rates match.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>dither_scale</b>
<dd> Set the dither scale. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>dither_method</b>
<dd> Set dither method. Default value is 0. 

 Supported values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rectangular</b>
<dd> select rectangular dither
<dt><b>triangular</b>
<dd> select triangular dither
<dt><b>triangular_hp</b>
<dd> select triangular dither with high pass
<dt><b>lipshitz</b>
<dd> select Lipshitz noise shaping dither.
<dt><b>shibata</b>
<dd> select Shibata noise shaping dither.
<dt><b>low_shibata</b>
<dd> select low Shibata noise shaping dither.
<dt><b>high_shibata</b>
<dd> select high Shibata noise shaping dither.
<dt><b>f_weighted</b>
<dd> select f-weighted noise shaping dither
<dt><b>modified_e_weighted</b>
<dd> select modified-e-weighted noise shaping dither
<dt><b>improved_e_weighted</b>
<dd> select improved-e-weighted noise shaping dither</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>resampler</b>
<dd> Set resampling engine. Default value is swr. 

 Supported values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>swr</b>
<dd> select the native <font SIZE="-1">SW</font> Resampler; filter options precision and cheby are not applicable in this case.
<dt><b>soxr</b>
<dd> select the SoX Resampler (where available); compensation, and filter options filter_size, phase_shift, exact_rational, filter_type &amp; kaiser_beta, are not applicable in this case.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>filter_size</b>
<dd> For swr only, set resampling filter size, default value is 32.
<dt><b>phase_shift</b>
<dd> For swr only, set resampling phase shift, default value is 10, and must be in the interval [0,30].
<dt><b>linear_interp</b>
<dd> Use linear interpolation when enabled (the default). Disable it if you want to preserve speed instead of quality when exact_rational fails.
<dt><b>exact_rational</b>
<dd> For swr only, when enabled, try to use exact phase_count based on input and output sample rate. However, if it is larger than <tt>&quot;1 &lt;&lt; phase_shift&quot;</tt>, the phase_count will be <tt>&quot;1 &lt;&lt; phase_shift&quot;</tt> as fallback. Default is enabled.
<dt><b>cutoff</b>
<dd> Set cutoff frequency (swr: 6dB point; soxr: 0dB point) ratio; must be a float value between 0 and 1. Default value is 0.97 with swr, and 0.91 with soxr (which, with a sample-rate of 44100, preserves the entire audio band to 20kHz).
<dt><b>precision</b>
<dd> For soxr only, the precision in bits to which the resampled signal will be calculated. The default value of 20 (which, with suitable dithering, is appropriate for a destination bit-depth of 16) gives SoX's 'High Quality'; a value of 28 gives SoX's 'Very High Quality'.
<dt><b>cheby</b>
<dd> For soxr only, selects passband rolloff none (Chebyshev) &amp; higher-precision approximation for 'irrational' ratios. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>async</b>
<dd> For swr only, simple 1 parameter audio sync to timestamps using stretching, squeezing, filling and trimming. Setting this to 1 will enable filling and trimming, larger values represent the maximum amount in samples that the data may be stretched or squeezed for each second. Default value is 0, thus no compensation is applied to make the samples match the audio timestamps.
<dt><b>first_pts</b>
<dd> For swr only, assume the first pts should be this value. The time unit is 1 / sample rate. This allows for padding/trimming at the start of stream. By default, no assumption is made about the first frame's expected pts, so no padding or trimming is done. For example, this could be set to 0 to pad the beginning with silence if an audio stream starts after the video stream or to trim any samples with a negative pts due to encoder delay.
<dt><b>min_comp</b>
<dd> For swr only, set the minimum difference between timestamps and audio data (in seconds) to trigger stretching/squeezing/filling or trimming of the data to make it match the timestamps. The default is that stretching/squeezing/filling and trimming is disabled (<b>min_comp</b> = <tt>&quot;FLT_MAX&quot;</tt>).
<dt><b>min_hard_comp</b>
<dd> For swr only, set the minimum difference between timestamps and audio data (in seconds) to trigger adding/dropping samples to make it match the timestamps. This option effectively is a threshold to select between hard (trim/fill) and soft (squeeze/stretch) compensation. Note that all compensation is by default disabled through <b>min_comp</b>. The default is 0.1.
<dt><b>comp_duration</b>
<dd> For swr only, set duration (in seconds) over which data is stretched/squeezed to make it match the timestamps. Must be a non-negative double float value, default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>max_soft_comp</b>
<dd> For swr only, set maximum factor by which data is stretched/squeezed to make it match the timestamps. Must be a non-negative double float value, default value is 0.
<dt><b>matrix_encoding</b>
<dd> Select matrixed stereo encoding. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> select none
<dt><b>dolby</b>
<dd> select Dolby
<dt><b>dplii</b>
<dd> select Dolby Pro Logic <font SIZE="-1">II</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>filter_type</b>
<dd> For swr only, select resampling filter type. This only affects resampling operations. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>cubic</b>
<dd> select cubic
<dt><b>blackman_nuttall</b>
<dd> select Blackman Nuttall windowed sinc
<dt><b>kaiser</b>
<dd> select Kaiser windowed sinc</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>kaiser_beta</b>
<dd> For swr only, set Kaiser window beta value. Must be a double float value in the interval [2,16], default value is 9.
<dt><b>output_sample_bits</b>
<dd> For swr only, set number of used output sample bits for dithering. Must be an integer in the interval [0,64], default value is 0, which means it's not used.</dl>

<h2>SCALER OPTIONS</h2>

 The video scaler supports the following named options. 

 Options may be set by specifying -<i>option</i> <i>value</i> in the FFmpeg tools, with a few API-only exceptions noted below. For programmatic use, they can be set explicitly in the <tt>&quot;SwsContext&quot;</tt> options or through the <i>libavutil/opt.h</i> <font SIZE="-1">API.</font>
<dl>
<dt><b>sws_flags</b>
<dd> Set the scaler flags. This is also used to set the scaling algorithm. Only a single algorithm should be selected. Default value is <b>bicubic</b>. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>fast_bilinear</b>
<dd> Select fast bilinear scaling algorithm.
<dt><b>bilinear</b>
<dd> Select bilinear scaling algorithm.
<dt><b>bicubic</b>
<dd> Select bicubic scaling algorithm.
<dt><b>experimental</b>
<dd> Select experimental scaling algorithm.
<dt><b>neighbor</b>
<dd> Select nearest neighbor rescaling algorithm.
<dt><b>area</b>
<dd> Select averaging area rescaling algorithm.
<dt><b>bicublin</b>
<dd> Select bicubic scaling algorithm for the luma component, bilinear for chroma components.
<dt><b>gauss</b>
<dd> Select Gaussian rescaling algorithm.
<dt><b>sinc</b>
<dd> Select sinc rescaling algorithm.
<dt><b>lanczos</b>
<dd> Select Lanczos rescaling algorithm. The default width (alpha) is 3 and can be changed by setting <tt>&quot;param0&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>spline</b>
<dd> Select natural bicubic spline rescaling algorithm.
<dt><b>print_info</b>
<dd> Enable printing/debug logging.
<dt><b>accurate_rnd</b>
<dd> Enable accurate rounding.
<dt><b>full_chroma_int</b>
<dd> Enable full chroma interpolation.
<dt><b>full_chroma_inp</b>
<dd> Select full chroma input.
<dt><b>bitexact</b>
<dd> Enable bitexact output.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>srcw</b> <i>(</i><font SIZE="-1"><i>API</i></font><i> only)</i>
<dd> Set source width.
<dt><b>srch</b> <i>(</i><font SIZE="-1"><i>API</i></font><i> only)</i>
<dd> Set source height.
<dt><b>dstw</b> <i>(</i><font SIZE="-1"><i>API</i></font><i> only)</i>
<dd> Set destination width.
<dt><b>dsth</b> <i>(</i><font SIZE="-1"><i>API</i></font><i> only)</i>
<dd> Set destination height.
<dt><b>src_format</b> <i>(</i><font SIZE="-1"><i>API</i></font><i> only)</i>
<dd> Set source pixel format (must be expressed as an integer).
<dt><b>dst_format</b> <i>(</i><font SIZE="-1"><i>API</i></font><i> only)</i>
<dd> Set destination pixel format (must be expressed as an integer).
<dt><b>src_range</b> <i>(boolean)</i>
<dd> If value is set to <tt>1</tt>, indicates source is full range. Default value is <tt>0</tt>, which indicates source is limited range.
<dt><b>dst_range</b> <i>(boolean)</i>
<dd> If value is set to <tt>1</tt>, enable full range for destination. Default value is <tt>0</tt>, which enables limited range.
<dt><b>param0, param1</b>
<dd> Set scaling algorithm parameters. The specified values are specific of some scaling algorithms and ignored by others. The specified values are floating point number values.
<dt><b>sws_dither</b>
<dd> Set the dithering algorithm. Accepts one of the following values. Default value is <b>auto</b>.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> automatic choice
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> no dithering
<dt><b>bayer</b>
<dd> bayer dither
<dt><b>ed</b>
<dd> error diffusion dither
<dt><b>a_dither</b>
<dd> arithmetic dither, based using addition
<dt><b>x_dither</b>
<dd> arithmetic dither, based using xor (more random/less apparent patterning that a_dither).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>alphablend</b>
<dd> Set the alpha blending to use when the input has alpha but the output does not. Default value is <b>none</b>.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>uniform_color</b>
<dd> Blend onto a uniform background color
<dt><b>checkerboard</b>
<dd> Blend onto a checkerboard
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> No blending</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h2>FILTERING INTRODUCTION</h2>

 Filtering in FFmpeg is enabled through the libavfilter library. 

 In libavfilter, a filter can have multiple inputs and multiple outputs. To illustrate the sorts of things that are possible, we consider the following filtergraph. 

 
[main] input-- &gt; split-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- ---&gt;overlay-- &gt; output | ^ | [tmp][flip] |
    +-- ---&gt;crop-- &gt; vflip-- -- -- -+
 

 This filtergraph splits the input stream in two streams, then sends one stream through the crop filter and the vflip filter, before merging it back with the other stream by overlaying it on top. You can use the following command to achieve this: 

 
ffmpeg - i INPUT - vf "split [main][tmp]; [tmp] crop=iw:ih/2:0:0, vflip [flip]; [main][flip] overlay=0:H/2" OUTPUT
 

 The result will be that the top half of the video is mirrored onto the bottom half of the output video. 

 Filters in the same linear chain are separated by commas, and distinct linear chains of filters are separated by semicolons. In our example, <i>crop,vflip</i> are in one linear chain, <i>split</i> and <i>overlay</i> are separately in another. The points where the linear chains join are labelled by names enclosed in square brackets. In the example, the split filter generates two outputs that are associated to the labels <i>[main]</i> and <i>[tmp]</i>. 

 The stream sent to the second output of <i>split</i>, labelled as <i>[tmp]</i>, is processed through the <i>crop</i> filter, which crops away the lower half part of the video, and then vertically flipped. The <i>overlay</i> filter takes in input the first unchanged output of the split filter (which was labelled as <i>[main]</i>), and overlay on its lower half the output generated by the <i>crop,vflip</i> filterchain. 

 Some filters take in input a list of parameters: they are specified after the filter name and an equal sign, and are separated from each other by a colon. 

 There exist so-called <i>source filters</i> that do not have an audio/video input, and <i>sink filters</i> that will not have audio/video output.

<h2>GRAPH</h2>

 The <i>graph2dot</i> program included in the FFmpeg <i>tools</i> directory can be used to parse a filtergraph description and issue a corresponding textual representation in the dot language. 

 Invoke the command: 

 <pre>
        graph2dot -h
</pre> 

 to see how to use <i>graph2dot</i>. 

 You can then pass the dot description to the <i>dot</i> program (from the graphviz suite of programs) and obtain a graphical representation of the filtergraph. 

 For example the sequence of commands: 

 <pre>
        echo &lt;GRAPH_DESCRIPTION&gt; | \
        tools/graph2dot -o graph.tmp &amp;&amp; \
        dot -Tpng graph.tmp -o graph.png &amp;&amp; \
        display graph.png
</pre> 

 can be used to create and display an image representing the graph described by the <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>GRAPH_DESCRIPTION</i></font><i></i> string. Note that this string must be a complete self-contained graph, with its inputs and outputs explicitly defined. For example if your command line is of the form: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i infile -vf scale=640:360 outfile
</pre> 

 your <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>GRAPH_DESCRIPTION</i></font><i></i> string will need to be of the form: 

 <pre>
        nullsrc,scale=640:360,nullsink
</pre> 

 you may also need to set the <i>nullsrc</i> parameters and add a <i>format</i> filter in order to simulate a specific input file.

<h2>FILTERGRAPH DESCRIPTION</h2>

 A filtergraph is a directed graph of connected filters. It can contain cycles, and there can be multiple links between a pair of filters. Each link has one input pad on one side connecting it to one filter from which it takes its input, and one output pad on the other side connecting it to one filter accepting its output. 

 Each filter in a filtergraph is an instance of a filter class registered in the application, which defines the features and the number of input and output pads of the filter. 

 A filter with no input pads is called a ``source'', and a filter with no output pads is called a ``sink''.

<h3>Filtergraph syntax</h3>

 A filtergraph has a textual representation, which is recognized by the <b>-filter</b>/<b>-vf</b>/<b>-af</b> and <b>-filter_complex</b> options in <b>ffmpeg</b> and <b>-vf</b>/<b>-af</b> in <b>ffplay</b>, and by the <tt>&quot;avfilter_graph_parse_ptr()&quot;</tt> function defined in <i>libavfilter/avfilter.h</i>. 

 A filterchain consists of a sequence of connected filters, each one connected to the previous one in the sequence. A filterchain is represented by a list of ``,''-separated filter descriptions. 

 A filtergraph consists of a sequence of filterchains. A sequence of filterchains is represented by a list of ``;''-separated filterchain descriptions. 

 A filter is represented by a string of the form: [<i>in_link_1</i>]...[<i>in_link_N</i>]<i>filter_name</i>@<i>id</i>=<i>arguments</i>[<i>out_link_1</i>]...[<i>out_link_M</i>] 

 <i>filter_name</i> is the name of the filter class of which the described filter is an instance of, and has to be the name of one of the filter classes registered in the program optionally followed by &quot;@<i>id</i>``. The name of the filter class is optionally followed by a string ''=<i>arguments</i>&quot;. 

 <i>arguments</i> is a string which contains the parameters used to initialize the filter instance. It may have one of two forms:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A ':'-separated list of <i>key=value</i> pairs.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A ':'-separated list of <i>value</i>. In this case, the keys are assumed to be the option names in the order they are declared. E.g. the <tt>&quot;fade&quot;</tt> filter declares three options in this order --- <b>type</b>, <b>start_frame</b> and <b>nb_frames</b>. Then the parameter list <i>in:0:30</i> means that the value <i>in</i> is assigned to the option <b>type</b>, <i>0</i> to <b>start_frame</b> and <i>30</i> to <b>nb_frames</b>.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A ':'-separated list of mixed direct <i>value</i> and long <i>key=value</i> pairs. The direct <i>value</i> must precede the <i>key=value</i> pairs, and follow the same constraints order of the previous point. The following <i>key=value</i> pairs can be set in any preferred order.</dl>
 

 If the option value itself is a list of items (e.g. the <tt>&quot;format&quot;</tt> filter takes a list of pixel formats), the items in the list are usually separated by <b>|</b>. 

 The list of arguments can be quoted using the character <b>'</b> as initial and ending mark, and the character <b>\</b> for escaping the characters within the quoted text; otherwise the argument string is considered terminated when the next special character (belonging to the set <b>[]=;,</b>) is encountered. 

 The name and arguments of the filter are optionally preceded and followed by a list of link labels. A link label allows one to name a link and associate it to a filter output or input pad. The preceding labels <i>in_link_1</i> ... <i>in_link_N</i>, are associated to the filter input pads, the following labels <i>out_link_1</i> ... <i>out_link_M</i>, are associated to the output pads. 

 When two link labels with the same name are found in the filtergraph, a link between the corresponding input and output pad is created. 

 If an output pad is not labelled, it is linked by default to the first unlabelled input pad of the next filter in the filterchain. For example in the filterchain 

 
nullsrc, split[L1], [L2] overlay, nullsink
 

 the split filter instance has two output pads, and the overlay filter instance two input pads. The first output pad of split is labelled ``L1'', the first input pad of overlay is labelled ``L2'', and the second output pad of split is linked to the second input pad of overlay, which are both unlabelled. 

 In a filter description, if the input label of the first filter is not specified, ``in'' is assumed; if the output label of the last filter is not specified, ``out'' is assumed. 

 In a complete filterchain all the unlabelled filter input and output pads must be connected. A filtergraph is considered valid if all the filter input and output pads of all the filterchains are connected. 

 Libavfilter will automatically insert <b>scale</b> filters where format conversion is required. It is possible to specify swscale flags for those automatically inserted scalers by prepending <tt>&quot;sws_flags=</tt>flags<tt>;&quot;</tt> to the filtergraph description. 

 Here is a <font SIZE="-1">BNF</font> description of the filtergraph syntax: 

 
        &lt;NAME&gt;             ::= sequence of alphanumeric characters and '_'
        &lt;FILTER_NAME&gt;      ::= &lt;NAME&gt;["@"&lt;NAME&gt;]
        &lt;LINKLABEL&gt;        ::= "[" &lt;NAME&gt; "]"
        &lt;LINKLABELS&gt;       ::= &lt;LINKLABEL&gt; [&lt;LINKLABELS&gt;]
        &lt;FILTER_ARGUMENTS&gt; ::= sequence of chars (possibly quoted)
        &lt;FILTER&gt;           ::= [&lt;LINKLABELS&gt;] &lt;FILTER_NAME&gt; ["=" &lt;FILTER_ARGUMENTS&gt;] [&lt;LINKLABELS&gt;]
        &lt;FILTERCHAIN&gt;      ::= &lt;FILTER&gt; [,&lt;FILTERCHAIN&gt;]
        &lt;FILTERGRAPH&gt;      ::= [sws_flags=&lt;flags&gt;;] &lt;FILTERCHAIN&gt; [;&lt;FILTERGRAPH&gt;]


<h3>Notes on filtergraph escaping</h3>

 Filtergraph description composition entails several levels of escaping. See <b>the ``Quoting and escaping'' section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for more information about the employed escaping procedure. 

 A first level escaping affects the content of each filter option value, which may contain the special character <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> used to separate values, or one of the escaping characters <tt>&quot;\'&quot;</tt>. 

 A second level escaping affects the whole filter description, which may contain the escaping characters <tt>&quot;\'&quot;</tt> or the special characters <tt>&quot;[],;&quot;</tt> used by the filtergraph description. 

 Finally, when you specify a filtergraph on a shell commandline, you need to perform a third level escaping for the shell special characters contained within it. 

 For example, consider the following string to be embedded in the <b>drawtext</b> filter description <b>text</b> value: 

 <pre>
        this is a 'string': may contain one, or more, special characters
</pre> 

 This string contains the <tt>&quot;'&quot;</tt> special escaping character, and the <tt>&quot;:&quot;</tt> special character, so it needs to be escaped in this way: 

 <pre>
        text=this is a \'string\'\: may contain one, or more, special characters
</pre> 

 A second level of escaping is required when embedding the filter description in a filtergraph description, in order to escape all the filtergraph special characters. Thus the example above becomes: 

 <pre>
        drawtext=text=this is a \\\'string\\\'\\: may contain one\, or more\, special characters
</pre> 

 (note that in addition to the <tt>&quot;\'&quot;</tt> escaping special characters, also <tt>&quot;,&quot;</tt> needs to be escaped). 

 Finally an additional level of escaping is needed when writing the filtergraph description in a shell command, which depends on the escaping rules of the adopted shell. For example, assuming that <tt>&quot;\&quot;</tt> is special and needs to be escaped with another <tt>&quot;\&quot;</tt>, the previous string will finally result in: 

 <pre>
        -vf &quot;drawtext=text=this is a \\\\\\'string\\\\\\'\\\\: may contain one\\, or more\\, special characters&quot;
</pre>

<h2>TIMELINE EDITING</h2>

 Some filters support a generic <b>enable</b> option. For the filters supporting timeline editing, this option can be set to an expression which is evaluated before sending a frame to the filter. If the evaluation is non-zero, the filter will be enabled, otherwise the frame will be sent unchanged to the next filter in the filtergraph. 

 The expression accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd> timestamp expressed in seconds, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input timestamp is unknown
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> sequential number of the input frame, starting from 0
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd> the position in the file of the input frame, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if unknown
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> width and height of the input frame if video</dl>
 

 Additionally, these filters support an <b>enable</b> command that can be used to re-define the expression. 

 Like any other filtering option, the <b>enable</b> option follows the same rules. 

 For example, to enable a blur filter (<b>smartblur</b>) from 10 seconds to 3 minutes, and a <b>curves</b> filter starting at 3 seconds: 

 <pre>
        smartblur = enable='between(t,10,3*60)',
        curves    = enable='gte(t,3)' : preset=cross_process
</pre> 

 See <tt>&quot;ffmpeg -filters&quot;</tt> to view which filters have timeline support.

<h2>CHANGING OPTIONS AT RUNTIME WITH A COMMAND</h2>

 Some options can be changed during the operation of the filter using a command. These options are marked 'T' on the output of <b>ffmpeg</b> <b>-h filter=&lt;name of filter&gt;</b>. The name of the command is the name of the option and the argument is the new value.

<h2>OPTIONS FOR FILTERS WITH SEVERAL INPUTS</h2>

 Some filters with several inputs support a common set of options. These options can only be set by name, not with the short notation.
<dl>
<dt><b>eof_action</b>
<dd> The action to take when <font SIZE="-1">EOF</font> is encountered on the secondary input; it accepts one of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>repeat</b>
<dd> Repeat the last frame (the default).
<dt><b>endall</b>
<dd> End both streams.
<dt><b>pass</b>
<dd> Pass the main input through.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>shortest</b>
<dd> If set to 1, force the output to terminate when the shortest input terminates. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>repeatlast</b>
<dd> If set to 1, force the filter to extend the last frame of secondary streams until the end of the primary stream. A value of 0 disables this behavior. Default value is 1.</dl>

<h2>AUDIO FILTERS</h2>

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, you can disable any of the existing filters using <tt>&quot;--disable-filters&quot;</tt>. The configure output will show the audio filters included in your build. 

 Below is a description of the currently available audio filters.

<h3>acompressor</h3>

 A compressor is mainly used to reduce the dynamic range of a signal. Especially modern music is mostly compressed at a high ratio to improve the overall loudness. It's done to get the highest attention of a listener, ``fatten'' the sound and bring more ``power'' to the track. If a signal is compressed too much it may sound dull or ``dead'' afterwards or it may start to ``pump'' (which could be a powerful effect but can also destroy a track completely). The right compression is the key to reach a professional sound and is the high art of mixing and mastering. Because of its complex settings it may take a long time to get the right feeling for this kind of effect. 

 Compression is done by detecting the volume above a chosen level <tt>&quot;threshold&quot;</tt> and dividing it by the factor set with <tt>&quot;ratio&quot;</tt>. So if you set the threshold to -12dB and your signal reaches -6dB a ratio of 2:1 will result in a signal at -9dB. Because an exact manipulation of the signal would cause distortion of the waveform the reduction can be levelled over the time. This is done by setting ``Attack'' and ``Release''. <tt>&quot;attack&quot;</tt> determines how long the signal has to rise above the threshold before any reduction will occur and <tt>&quot;release&quot;</tt> sets the time the signal has to fall below the threshold to reduce the reduction again. Shorter signals than the chosen attack time will be left untouched. The overall reduction of the signal can be made up afterwards with the <tt>&quot;makeup&quot;</tt> setting. So compressing the peaks of a signal about 6dB and raising the makeup to this level results in a signal twice as loud than the source. To gain a softer entry in the compression the <tt>&quot;knee&quot;</tt> flattens the hard edge at the threshold in the range of the chosen decibels. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>level_in</b>
<dd> Set input gain. Default is 1. Range is between 0.015625 and 64.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set mode of compressor operation. Can be <tt>&quot;upward&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;downward&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;downward&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd> If a signal of stream rises above this level it will affect the gain reduction. By default it is 0.125. Range is between 0.00097563 and 1.
<dt><b>ratio</b>
<dd> Set a ratio by which the signal is reduced. 1:2 means that if the level rose 4dB above the threshold, it will be only 2dB above after the reduction. Default is 2. Range is between 1 and 20.
<dt><b>attack</b>
<dd> Amount of milliseconds the signal has to rise above the threshold before gain reduction starts. Default is 20. Range is between 0.01 and 2000.
<dt><b>release</b>
<dd> Amount of milliseconds the signal has to fall below the threshold before reduction is decreased again. Default is 250. Range is between 0.01 and 9000.
<dt><b>makeup</b>
<dd> Set the amount by how much signal will be amplified after processing. Default is 1. Range is from 1 to 64.
<dt><b>knee</b>
<dd> Curve the sharp knee around the threshold to enter gain reduction more softly. Default is 2.82843. Range is between 1 and 8.
<dt><b>link</b>
<dd> Choose if the <tt>&quot;average&quot;</tt> level between all channels of input stream or the louder(<tt>&quot;maximum&quot;</tt>) channel of input stream affects the reduction. Default is <tt>&quot;average&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>detection</b>
<dd> Should the exact signal be taken in case of <tt>&quot;peak&quot;</tt> or an <font SIZE="-1">RMS</font> one in case of <tt>&quot;rms&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;rms&quot;</tt> which is mostly smoother.
<dt><b>mix</b>
<dd> How much to use compressed signal in output. Default is 1. Range is between 0 and 1.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>acontrast</h3>

 Simple audio dynamic range compression/expansion filter. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>contrast</b>
<dd> Set contrast. Default is 33. Allowed range is between 0 and 100.</dl>

<h3>acopy</h3>

 Copy the input audio source unchanged to the output. This is mainly useful for testing purposes.

<h3>acrossfade</h3>

 Apply cross fade from one input audio stream to another input audio stream. The cross fade is applied for specified duration near the end of first stream. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>nb_samples, ns</b>
<dd> Specify the number of samples for which the cross fade effect has to last. At the end of the cross fade effect the first input audio will be completely silent. Default is 44100.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd> Specify the duration of the cross fade effect. See <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. By default the duration is determined by <i>nb_samples</i>. If set this option is used instead of <i>nb_samples</i>.
<dt><b>overlap, o</b>
<dd> Should first stream end overlap with second stream start. Default is enabled.
<dt><b>curve1</b>
<dd> Set curve for cross fade transition for first stream.
<dt><b>curve2</b>
<dd> Set curve for cross fade transition for second stream. 

 For description of available curve types see <b>afade</b> filter description.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Cross fade from one input to another: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i first.flac -i second.flac -filter_complex acrossfade=d=10:c1=exp:c2=exp output.flac
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Cross fade from one input to another but without overlapping: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i first.flac -i second.flac -filter_complex acrossfade=d=10:o=0:c1=exp:c2=exp output.flac
</pre></dl>

<h3>acrossover</h3>

 Split audio stream into several bands. 

 This filter splits audio stream into two or more frequency ranges. Summing all streams back will give flat output. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>split</b>
<dd> Set split frequencies. Those must be positive and increasing.
<dt><b>order</b>
<dd> Set filter order for each band split. This controls filter roll-off or steepness of filter transfer function. Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>2nd</b>
<dd> 12 dB per octave.
<dt><b>4th</b>
<dd> 24 dB per octave.
<dt><b>6th</b>
<dd> 36 dB per octave.
<dt><b>8th</b>
<dd> 48 dB per octave.
<dt><b>10th</b>
<dd> 60 dB per octave.
<dt><b>12th</b>
<dd> 72 dB per octave.
<dt><b>14th</b>
<dd> 84 dB per octave.
<dt><b>16th</b>
<dd> 96 dB per octave.
<dt><b>18th</b>
<dd> 108 dB per octave.
<dt><b>20th</b>
<dd> 120 dB per octave.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <i>4th</i>.</dl>

<dt><b>level</b>
<dd> Set input gain level. Allowed range is from 0 to 1. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>gains</b>
<dd> Set output gain for each band. Default value is 1 for all bands.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Split input audio stream into two bands (low and high) with split frequency of 1500 Hz, each band will be in separate stream: 

 
ffmpeg - i in.flac - filter_complex 'acrossover=split=1500[LOW][HIGH]' - map '[LOW]' low.wav - map '[HIGH]' high.wav

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but with higher filter order: 

 
ffmpeg - i in.flac - filter_complex 'acrossover=split=1500:order=8th[LOW][HIGH]' - map '[LOW]' low.wav - map '[HIGH]' high.wav

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but also with additional middle band (frequencies between 1500 and 8000): 

 
ffmpeg - i in.flac - filter_complex 'acrossover=split=1500 8000:order=8th[LOW][MID][HIGH]' - map '[LOW]' low.wav - map '[MID]' mid.wav - map '[HIGH]' high.wav
</dl>

<h3>acrusher</h3>

 Reduce audio bit resolution. 

 This filter is bit crusher with enhanced functionality. A bit crusher is used to audibly reduce number of bits an audio signal is sampled with. This doesn't change the bit depth at all, it just produces the effect. Material reduced in bit depth sounds more harsh and ``digital''. This filter is able to even round to continuous values instead of discrete bit depths. Additionally it has a D/C offset which results in different crushing of the lower and the upper half of the signal. An Anti-Aliasing setting is able to produce ``softer'' crushing sounds. 

 Another feature of this filter is the logarithmic mode. This setting switches from linear distances between bits to logarithmic ones. The result is a much more ``natural'' sounding crusher which doesn't gate low signals for example. The human ear has a logarithmic perception, so this kind of crushing is much more pleasant. Logarithmic crushing is also able to get anti-aliased. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>level_in</b>
<dd> Set level in.
<dt><b>level_out</b>
<dd> Set level out.
<dt><b>bits</b>
<dd> Set bit reduction.
<dt><b>mix</b>
<dd> Set mixing amount.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Can be linear: <tt>&quot;lin&quot;</tt> or logarithmic: <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>dc</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">DC.</font>
<dt><b>aa</b>
<dd> Set anti-aliasing.
<dt><b>samples</b>
<dd> Set sample reduction.
<dt><b>lfo</b>
<dd> Enable <font SIZE="-1">LFO.</font> By default disabled.
<dt><b>lforange</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFO</font> range.
<dt><b>lforate</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFO</font> rate.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>acue</h3>

 Delay audio filtering until a given wallclock timestamp. See the <b>cue</b> filter.

<h3>adeclick</h3>

 Remove impulsive noise from input audio. 

 Samples detected as impulsive noise are replaced by interpolated samples using autoregressive modelling.
<dl>
<dt><b>window, w</b>
<dd> Set window size, in milliseconds. Allowed range is from <tt>10</tt> to <tt>100</tt>. Default value is <tt>55</tt> milliseconds. This sets size of window which will be processed at once.
<dt><b>overlap, o</b>
<dd> Set window overlap, in percentage of window size. Allowed range is from <tt>50</tt> to <tt>95</tt>. Default value is <tt>75</tt> percent. Setting this to a very high value increases impulsive noise removal but makes whole process much slower.
<dt><b>arorder, a</b>
<dd> Set autoregression order, in percentage of window size. Allowed range is from <tt>0</tt> to <tt>25</tt>. Default value is <tt>2</tt> percent. This option also controls quality of interpolated samples using neighbour good samples.
<dt><b>threshold, t</b>
<dd> Set threshold value. Allowed range is from <tt>1</tt> to <tt>100</tt>. Default value is <tt>2</tt>. This controls the strength of impulsive noise which is going to be removed. The lower value, the more samples will be detected as impulsive noise.
<dt><b>burst, b</b>
<dd> Set burst fusion, in percentage of window size. Allowed range is <tt>0</tt> to <tt>10</tt>. Default value is <tt>2</tt>. If any two samples detected as noise are spaced less than this value then any sample between those two samples will be also detected as noise.
<dt><b>method, m</b>
<dd> Set overlap method. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>add, a</b>
<dd> Select overlap-add method. Even not interpolated samples are slightly changed with this method.
<dt><b>save, s</b>
<dd> Select overlap-save method. Not interpolated samples remain unchanged.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;a&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>adeclip</h3>

 Remove clipped samples from input audio. 

 Samples detected as clipped are replaced by interpolated samples using autoregressive modelling.
<dl>
<dt><b>window, w</b>
<dd> Set window size, in milliseconds. Allowed range is from <tt>10</tt> to <tt>100</tt>. Default value is <tt>55</tt> milliseconds. This sets size of window which will be processed at once.
<dt><b>overlap, o</b>
<dd> Set window overlap, in percentage of window size. Allowed range is from <tt>50</tt> to <tt>95</tt>. Default value is <tt>75</tt> percent.
<dt><b>arorder, a</b>
<dd> Set autoregression order, in percentage of window size. Allowed range is from <tt>0</tt> to <tt>25</tt>. Default value is <tt>8</tt> percent. This option also controls quality of interpolated samples using neighbour good samples.
<dt><b>threshold, t</b>
<dd> Set threshold value. Allowed range is from <tt>1</tt> to <tt>100</tt>. Default value is <tt>10</tt>. Higher values make clip detection less aggressive.
<dt><b>hsize, n</b>
<dd> Set size of histogram used to detect clips. Allowed range is from <tt>100</tt> to <tt>9999</tt>. Default value is <tt>1000</tt>. Higher values make clip detection less aggressive.
<dt><b>method, m</b>
<dd> Set overlap method. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>add, a</b>
<dd> Select overlap-add method. Even not interpolated samples are slightly changed with this method.
<dt><b>save, s</b>
<dd> Select overlap-save method. Not interpolated samples remain unchanged.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;a&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>adelay</h3>

 Delay one or more audio channels. 

 Samples in delayed channel are filled with silence. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>delays</b>
<dd> Set list of delays in milliseconds for each channel separated by '|'. Unused delays will be silently ignored. If number of given delays is smaller than number of channels all remaining channels will not be delayed. If you want to delay exact number of samples, append 'S' to number. If you want instead to delay in seconds, append 's' to number.
<dt><b>all</b>
<dd> Use last set delay for all remaining channels. By default is disabled. This option if enabled changes how option <tt>&quot;delays&quot;</tt> is interpreted.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Delay first channel by 1.5 seconds, the third channel by 0.5 seconds and leave the second channel (and any other channels that may be present) unchanged. 

 <pre>
        adelay=1500|0|500
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Delay second channel by 500 samples, the third channel by 700 samples and leave the first channel (and any other channels that may be present) unchanged. 

 <pre>
        adelay=0|500S|700S
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Delay all channels by same number of samples: 

 <pre>
        adelay=delays=64S:all=1
</pre></dl>

<h3>adenorm</h3>

 Remedy denormals in audio by adding extremely low-level noise. 

 This filter shall be placed before any filter that can produce denormals. 

 A description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd> Set level of added noise in dB. Default is <tt>&quot;-351&quot;</tt>. Allowed range is from -451 to -90.
<dt><b>type</b>
<dd> Set type of added noise.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>dc</b>
<dd> Add <font SIZE="-1">DC</font> signal.
<dt><b>ac</b>
<dd> Add <font SIZE="-1">AC</font> signal.
<dt><b>square</b>
<dd> Add square signal.
<dt><b>pulse</b>
<dd> Add pulse signal.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;dc&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>aderivative, aintegral</h3>

 Compute derivative/integral of audio stream. 

 Applying both filters one after another produces original audio.

<h3>aecho</h3>

 Apply echoing to the input audio. 

 Echoes are reflected sound and can occur naturally amongst mountains (and sometimes large buildings) when talking or shouting; digital echo effects emulate this behaviour and are often used to help fill out the sound of a single instrument or vocal. The time difference between the original signal and the reflection is the <tt>&quot;delay&quot;</tt>, and the loudness of the reflected signal is the <tt>&quot;decay&quot;</tt>. Multiple echoes can have different delays and decays. 

 A description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>in_gain</b>
<dd> Set input gain of reflected signal. Default is <tt>0.6</tt>.
<dt><b>out_gain</b>
<dd> Set output gain of reflected signal. Default is <tt>0.3</tt>.
<dt><b>delays</b>
<dd> Set list of time intervals in milliseconds between original signal and reflections separated by '|'. Allowed range for each <tt>&quot;delay&quot;</tt> is <tt>&quot;(0 - 90000.0]&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>1000</tt>.
<dt><b>decays</b>
<dd> Set list of loudness of reflected signals separated by '|'. Allowed range for each <tt>&quot;decay&quot;</tt> is <tt>&quot;(0 - 1.0]&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>0.5</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Make it sound as if there are twice as many instruments as are actually playing: 

 <pre>
        aecho=0.8:0.88:60:0.4
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> If delay is very short, then it sounds like a (metallic) robot playing music: 

 <pre>
        aecho=0.8:0.88:6:0.4
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A longer delay will sound like an open air concert in the mountains: 

 <pre>
        aecho=0.8:0.9:1000:0.3
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above but with one more mountain: 

 <pre>
        aecho=0.8:0.9:1000|1800:0.3|0.25
</pre></dl>

<h3>aemphasis</h3>

 Audio emphasis filter creates or restores material directly taken from LPs or emphased CDs with different filter curves. E.g. to store music on vinyl the signal has to be altered by a filter first to even out the disadvantages of this recording medium. Once the material is played back the inverse filter has to be applied to restore the distortion of the frequency response. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>level_in</b>
<dd> Set input gain.
<dt><b>level_out</b>
<dd> Set output gain.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set filter mode. For restoring material use <tt>&quot;reproduction&quot;</tt> mode, otherwise use <tt>&quot;production&quot;</tt> mode. Default is <tt>&quot;reproduction&quot;</tt> mode.
<dt><b>type</b>
<dd> Set filter type. Selects medium. Can be one of the following:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>col</b>
<dd> select Columbia.
<dt><b>emi</b>
<dd> select <font SIZE="-1">EMI.</font>
<dt><b>bsi</b>
<dd> select <font SIZE="-1">BSI</font> (78RPM).
<dt><b>riaa</b>
<dd> select <font SIZE="-1">RIAA.</font>
<dt><b>cd</b>
<dd> select Compact Disc (<font SIZE="-1">CD</font>).
<dt><b>50fm</b>
<dd> select 50Xs (<font SIZE="-1">FM</font>).
<dt><b>75fm</b>
<dd> select 75Xs (<font SIZE="-1">FM</font>).
<dt><b>50kf</b>
<dd> select 50Xs (FM-KF).
<dt><b>75kf</b>
<dd> select 75Xs (FM-KF).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>aeval</h3>

 Modify an audio signal according to the specified expressions. 

 This filter accepts one or more expressions (one for each channel), which are evaluated and used to modify a corresponding audio signal. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>exprs</b>
<dd> Set the '|'-separated expressions list for each separate channel. If the number of input channels is greater than the number of expressions, the last specified expression is used for the remaining output channels.
<dt><b>channel_layout, c</b>
<dd> Set output channel layout. If not specified, the channel layout is specified by the number of expressions. If set to <b>same</b>, it will use by default the same input channel layout.</dl>
 

 Each expression in <i>exprs</i> can contain the following constants and functions:
<dl>
<dt><b>ch</b>
<dd> channel number of the current expression
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> number of the evaluated sample, starting from 0
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> sample rate
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd> time of the evaluated sample expressed in seconds
<dt><b>nb_in_channels</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>nb_out_channels</b>
<dd> input and output number of channels
<dt><b>val(</b><font SIZE="-1"><b>CH</b></font><b>)</b>
<dd> the value of input channel with number <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>CH</i></font><i></i></dl>
 

 Note: this filter is slow. For faster processing you should use a dedicated filter. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Half volume: 

 <pre>
        aeval=val(ch)/2:c=same
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Invert phase of the second channel: 

 <pre>
        aeval=val(0)|<a HREF="//www.systutorials.com/docs/linux/man/1--val/">-val</a>(1)
</pre></dl>

<h3>aexciter</h3>

 An exciter is used to produce high sound that is not present in the original signal. This is done by creating harmonic distortions of the signal which are restricted in range and added to the original signal. An Exciter raises the upper end of an audio signal without simply raising the higher frequencies like an equalizer would do to create a more ``crisp'' or ``brilliant'' sound. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>level_in</b>
<dd> Set input level prior processing of signal. Allowed range is from 0 to 64. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>level_out</b>
<dd> Set output level after processing of signal. Allowed range is from 0 to 64. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>amount</b>
<dd> Set the amount of harmonics added to original signal. Allowed range is from 0 to 64. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>drive</b>
<dd> Set the amount of newly created harmonics. Allowed range is from 0.1 to 10. Default value is 8.5.
<dt><b>blend</b>
<dd> Set the octave of newly created harmonics. Allowed range is from -10 to 10. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>freq</b>
<dd> Set the lower frequency limit of producing harmonics in Hz. Allowed range is from 2000 to 12000 Hz. Default is 7500 Hz.
<dt><b>ceil</b>
<dd> Set the upper frequency limit of producing harmonics. Allowed range is from 9999 to 20000 Hz. If value is lower than 10000 Hz no limit is applied.
<dt><b>listen</b>
<dd> Mute the original signal and output only added harmonics. By default is disabled.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>afade</h3>

 Apply fade-in/out effect to input audio. 

 A description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>type, t</b>
<dd> Specify the effect type, can be either <tt>&quot;in&quot;</tt> for fade-in, or <tt>&quot;out&quot;</tt> for a fade-out effect. Default is <tt>&quot;in&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>start_sample, ss</b>
<dd> Specify the number of the start sample for starting to apply the fade effect. Default is 0.
<dt><b>nb_samples, ns</b>
<dd> Specify the number of samples for which the fade effect has to last. At the end of the fade-in effect the output audio will have the same volume as the input audio, at the end of the fade-out transition the output audio will be silence. Default is 44100.
<dt><b>start_time, st</b>
<dd> Specify the start time of the fade effect. Default is 0. The value must be specified as a time duration; see <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. If set this option is used instead of <i>start_sample</i>.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd> Specify the duration of the fade effect. See <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. At the end of the fade-in effect the output audio will have the same volume as the input audio, at the end of the fade-out transition the output audio will be silence. By default the duration is determined by <i>nb_samples</i>. If set this option is used instead of <i>nb_samples</i>.
<dt><b>curve</b>
<dd> Set curve for fade transition. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>tri</b>
<dd> select triangular, linear slope (default)
<dt><b>qsin</b>
<dd> select quarter of sine wave
<dt><b>hsin</b>
<dd> select half of sine wave
<dt><b>esin</b>
<dd> select exponential sine wave
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> select logarithmic
<dt><b>ipar</b>
<dd> select inverted parabola
<dt><b>qua</b>
<dd> select quadratic
<dt><b>cub</b>
<dd> select cubic
<dt><b>squ</b>
<dd> select square root
<dt><b>cbr</b>
<dd> select cubic root
<dt><b>par</b>
<dd> select parabola
<dt><b>exp</b>
<dd> select exponential
<dt><b>iqsin</b>
<dd> select inverted quarter of sine wave
<dt><b>ihsin</b>
<dd> select inverted half of sine wave
<dt><b>dese</b>
<dd> select double-exponential seat
<dt><b>desi</b>
<dd> select double-exponential sigmoid
<dt><b>losi</b>
<dd> select logistic sigmoid
<dt><b>sinc</b>
<dd> select sine cardinal function
<dt><b>isinc</b>
<dd> select inverted sine cardinal function
<dt><b>nofade</b>
<dd> no fade applied</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Fade in first 15 seconds of audio: 

 <pre>
        afade=t=in:ss=0:d=15
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Fade out last 25 seconds of a 900 seconds audio: 

 <pre>
        afade=t=out:st=875:d=25
</pre></dl>

<h3>afftdn</h3>

 Denoise audio samples with <font SIZE="-1">FFT.</font> 

 A description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>nr</b>
<dd> Set the noise reduction in dB, allowed range is 0.01 to 97. Default value is 12 dB.
<dt><b>nf</b>
<dd> Set the noise floor in dB, allowed range is -80 to -20. Default value is -50 dB.
<dt><b>nt</b>
<dd> Set the noise type. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd> Select white noise.
<dt><b>v</b>
<dd> Select vinyl noise.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> Select shellac noise.
<dt><b>c</b>
<dd> Select custom noise, defined in <tt>&quot;bn&quot;</tt> option. 

 Default value is white noise.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>bn</b>
<dd> Set custom band noise for every one of 15 bands. Bands are separated by ' ' or '|'.
<dt><b>rf</b>
<dd> Set the residual floor in dB, allowed range is -80 to -20. Default value is -38 dB.
<dt><b>tn</b>
<dd> Enable noise tracking. By default is disabled. With this enabled, noise floor is automatically adjusted.
<dt><b>tr</b>
<dd> Enable residual tracking. By default is disabled.
<dt><b>om</b>
<dd> Set the output mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>i</b>
<dd> Pass input unchanged.
<dt><b>o</b>
<dd> Pass noise filtered out.
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> Pass only noise. 

 Default value is <i>o</i>.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl>
<dt><b>sample_noise, sn</b>
<dd> Start or stop measuring noise profile. Syntax for the command is : ``start'' or ``stop'' string. After measuring noise profile is stopped it will be automatically applied in filtering.
<dt><b>noise_reduction, nr</b>
<dd> Change noise reduction. Argument is single float number. Syntax for the command is : &quot;<i>noise_reduction</i>&quot;
<dt><b>noise_floor, nf</b>
<dd> Change noise floor. Argument is single float number. Syntax for the command is : &quot;<i>noise_floor</i>&quot;
<dt><b>output_mode, om</b>
<dd> Change output mode operation. Syntax for the command is : ``i'', ``o'' or ``n'' string.</dl>

<h3>afftfilt</h3>

 Apply arbitrary expressions to samples in frequency domain.
<dl>
<dt><b>real</b>
<dd> Set frequency domain real expression for each separate channel separated by '|'. Default is ``re''. If the number of input channels is greater than the number of expressions, the last specified expression is used for the remaining output channels.
<dt><b>imag</b>
<dd> Set frequency domain imaginary expression for each separate channel separated by '|'. Default is ``im''. 

 Each expression in <i>real</i> and <i>imag</i> can contain the following constants and functions:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>sr</b>
<dd> sample rate
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> current frequency bin number
<dt><b>nb</b>
<dd> number of available bins
<dt><b>ch</b>
<dd> channel number of the current expression
<dt><b>chs</b>
<dd> number of channels
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd> current frame pts
<dt><b>re</b>
<dd> current real part of frequency bin of current channel
<dt><b>im</b>
<dd> current imaginary part of frequency bin of current channel
<dt><b>real(b, ch)</b>
<dd> Return the value of real part of frequency bin at location (<i>bin</i>,<i>channel</i>)
<dt><b>imag(b, ch)</b>
<dd> Return the value of imaginary part of frequency bin at location (<i>bin</i>,<i>channel</i>)</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>win_size</b>
<dd> Set window size. Allowed range is from 16 to 131072. Default is <tt>4096</tt>
<dt><b>win_func</b>
<dd> Set window function. Default is <tt>&quot;hann&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd> Set window overlap. If set to 1, the recommended overlap for selected window function will be picked. Default is <tt>0.75</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Leave almost only low frequencies in audio: 

 <pre>
        afftfilt=&quot;'real=re * (1-clip((b/nb)*b,0,1))':imag='im * (1-clip((b/nb)*b,0,1))'&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply robotize effect: 

 <pre>
        afftfilt=&quot;real='hypot(re,im)*sin(0)':imag='hypot(re,im)*cos(0)':win_size=512:overlap=0.75&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply whisper effect: 

 <pre>
        afftfilt=&quot;real='hypot(re,im)*cos((random(0)*2-1)*2*3.14)':imag='hypot(re,im)*sin((<a HREF="//www.systutorials.com/docs/linux/man/1-random/">random</a>(1)*2-1)*2*3.14)':win_size=128:overlap=0.8&quot;
</pre></dl>

<h3>afir</h3>

 Apply an arbitrary Finite Impulse Response filter. 

 This filter is designed for applying long <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> filters, up to 60 seconds long. 

 It can be used as component for digital crossover filters, room equalization, cross talk cancellation, wavefield synthesis, auralization, ambiophonics, ambisonics and spatialization. 

 This filter uses the streams higher than first one as <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> coefficients. If the non-first stream holds a single channel, it will be used for all input channels in the first stream, otherwise the number of channels in the non-first stream must be same as the number of channels in the first stream. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>dry</b>
<dd> Set dry gain. This sets input gain.
<dt><b>wet</b>
<dd> Set wet gain. This sets final output gain.
<dt><b>length</b>
<dd> Set Impulse Response filter length. Default is 1, which means whole <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> is processed.
<dt><b>gtype</b>
<dd> Enable applying gain measured from power of <font SIZE="-1">IR.</font> 

 Set which approach to use for auto gain measurement.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Do not apply any gain.
<dt><b>peak</b>
<dd> select peak gain, very conservative approach. This is default value.
<dt><b>dc</b>
<dd> select <font SIZE="-1">DC</font> gain, limited application.
<dt><b>gn</b>
<dd> select gain to noise approach, this is most popular one.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>irgain</b>
<dd> Set gain to be applied to <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> coefficients before filtering. Allowed range is 0 to 1. This gain is applied after any gain applied with <i>gtype</i> option.
<dt><b>irfmt</b>
<dd> Set format of <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> stream. Can be <tt>&quot;mono&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;input&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;input&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>maxir</b>
<dd> Set max allowed Impulse Response filter duration in seconds. Default is 30 seconds. Allowed range is 0.1 to 60 seconds.
<dt><b>response</b>
<dd> Show <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> frequency response, magnitude(magenta), phase(green) and group delay(yellow) in additional video stream. By default it is disabled.
<dt><b>channel</b>
<dd> Set for which <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> channel to display frequency response. By default is first channel displayed. This option is used only when <i>response</i> is enabled.
<dt><b>size</b>
<dd> Set video stream size. This option is used only when <i>response</i> is enabled.
<dt><b>rate</b>
<dd> Set video stream frame rate. This option is used only when <i>response</i> is enabled.
<dt><b>minp</b>
<dd> Set minimal partition size used for convolution. Default is <i>8192</i>. Allowed range is from <i>1</i> to <i>32768</i>. Lower values decreases latency at cost of higher <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> usage.
<dt><b>maxp</b>
<dd> Set maximal partition size used for convolution. Default is <i>8192</i>. Allowed range is from <i>8</i> to <i>32768</i>. Lower values may increase <font SIZE="-1">CPU</font> usage.
<dt><b>nbirs</b>
<dd> Set number of input impulse responses streams which will be switchable at runtime. Allowed range is from <i>1</i> to <i>32</i>. Default is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>ir</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> stream which will be used for convolution, starting from <i>0</i>, should always be lower than supplied value by <tt>&quot;nbirs&quot;</tt> option. Default is <i>0</i>. This option can be changed at runtime via <b>commands</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply reverb to stream using mono <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> file as second input, complete command using ffmpeg: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.wav -i middle_tunnel_1way_mono.wav -lavfi afir output.wav
</pre></dl>

<h3>aformat</h3>

 Set output format constraints for the input audio. The framework will negotiate the most appropriate format to minimize conversions. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>sample_fmts, f</b>
<dd> A '|'-separated list of requested sample formats.
<dt><b>sample_rates, r</b>
<dd> A '|'-separated list of requested sample rates.
<dt><b>channel_layouts, cl</b>
<dd> A '|'-separated list of requested channel layouts. 

 See <b>the Channel Layout section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the required syntax.</dl>
 

 If a parameter is omitted, all values are allowed. 

 Force the output to either unsigned 8-bit or signed 16-bit stereo 

 <pre>
        aformat=sample_fmts=u8|s16:channel_layouts=stereo
</pre>

<h3>afreqshift</h3>

 Apply frequency shift to input audio samples. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>shift</b>
<dd> Specify frequency shift. Allowed range is -INT_MAX to <font SIZE="-1">INT_MAX.</font> Default value is 0.0.
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd> Set output gain applied to final output. Allowed range is from 0.0 to 1.0. Default value is 1.0.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>agate</h3>

 A gate is mainly used to reduce lower parts of a signal. This kind of signal processing reduces disturbing noise between useful signals. 

 Gating is done by detecting the volume below a chosen level <i>threshold</i> and dividing it by the factor set with <i>ratio</i>. The bottom of the noise floor is set via <i>range</i>. Because an exact manipulation of the signal would cause distortion of the waveform the reduction can be levelled over time. This is done by setting <i>attack</i> and <i>release</i>. 

 <i>attack</i> determines how long the signal has to fall below the threshold before any reduction will occur and <i>release</i> sets the time the signal has to rise above the threshold to reduce the reduction again. Shorter signals than the chosen attack time will be left untouched.
<dl>
<dt><b>level_in</b>
<dd> Set input level before filtering. Default is 1. Allowed range is from 0.015625 to 64.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set the mode of operation. Can be <tt>&quot;upward&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;downward&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;downward&quot;</tt>. If set to <tt>&quot;upward&quot;</tt> mode, higher parts of signal will be amplified, expanding dynamic range in upward direction. Otherwise, in case of <tt>&quot;downward&quot;</tt> lower parts of signal will be reduced.
<dt><b>range</b>
<dd> Set the level of gain reduction when the signal is below the threshold. Default is 0.06125. Allowed range is from 0 to 1. Setting this to 0 disables reduction and then filter behaves like expander.
<dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd> If a signal rises above this level the gain reduction is released. Default is 0.125. Allowed range is from 0 to 1.
<dt><b>ratio</b>
<dd> Set a ratio by which the signal is reduced. Default is 2. Allowed range is from 1 to 9000.
<dt><b>attack</b>
<dd> Amount of milliseconds the signal has to rise above the threshold before gain reduction stops. Default is 20 milliseconds. Allowed range is from 0.01 to 9000.
<dt><b>release</b>
<dd> Amount of milliseconds the signal has to fall below the threshold before the reduction is increased again. Default is 250 milliseconds. Allowed range is from 0.01 to 9000.
<dt><b>makeup</b>
<dd> Set amount of amplification of signal after processing. Default is 1. Allowed range is from 1 to 64.
<dt><b>knee</b>
<dd> Curve the sharp knee around the threshold to enter gain reduction more softly. Default is 2.828427125. Allowed range is from 1 to 8.
<dt><b>detection</b>
<dd> Choose if exact signal should be taken for detection or an <font SIZE="-1">RMS</font> like one. Default is <tt>&quot;rms&quot;</tt>. Can be <tt>&quot;peak&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;rms&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>link</b>
<dd> Choose if the average level between all channels or the louder channel affects the reduction. Default is <tt>&quot;average&quot;</tt>. Can be <tt>&quot;average&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;maximum&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>aiir</h3>

 Apply an arbitrary Infinite Impulse Response filter. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>zeros, z</b>
<dd> Set B/numerator/zeros/reflection coefficients.
<dt><b>poles, p</b>
<dd> Set A/denominator/poles/ladder coefficients.
<dt><b>gains, k</b>
<dd> Set channels gains.
<dt><b>dry_gain</b>
<dd> Set input gain.
<dt><b>wet_gain</b>
<dd> Set output gain.
<dt><b>format, f</b>
<dd> Set coefficients format.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>ll</b>
<dd> lattice-ladder function
<dt><b>sf</b>
<dd> analog transfer function
<dt><b>tf</b>
<dd> digital transfer function
<dt><b>zp</b>
<dd> Z-plane zeros/poles, cartesian (default)
<dt><b>pr</b>
<dd> Z-plane zeros/poles, polar radians
<dt><b>pd</b>
<dd> Z-plane zeros/poles, polar degrees
<dt><b>sp</b>
<dd> S-plane zeros/poles</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>process, r</b>
<dd> Set type of processing.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>d</b>
<dd> direct processing
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> serial processing
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd> parallel processing</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>precision, e</b>
<dd> Set filtering precision.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>dbl</b>
<dd> double-precision floating-point (default)
<dt><b>flt</b>
<dd> single-precision floating-point
<dt><b>i32</b>
<dd> 32-bit integers
<dt><b>i16</b>
<dd> 16-bit integers</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>normalize, n</b>
<dd> Normalize filter coefficients, by default is enabled. Enabling it will normalize magnitude response at <font SIZE="-1">DC</font> to 0dB.
<dt><b>mix</b>
<dd> How much to use filtered signal in output. Default is 1. Range is between 0 and 1.
<dt><b>response</b>
<dd> Show <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> frequency response, magnitude(magenta), phase(green) and group delay(yellow) in additional video stream. By default it is disabled.
<dt><b>channel</b>
<dd> Set for which <font SIZE="-1">IR</font> channel to display frequency response. By default is first channel displayed. This option is used only when <i>response</i> is enabled.
<dt><b>size</b>
<dd> Set video stream size. This option is used only when <i>response</i> is enabled.</dl>
 

 Coefficients in <tt>&quot;tf&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;sf&quot;</tt> format are separated by spaces and are in ascending order. 

 Coefficients in <tt>&quot;zp&quot;</tt> format are separated by spaces and order of coefficients doesn't matter. Coefficients in <tt>&quot;zp&quot;</tt> format are complex numbers with <i>i</i> imaginary unit. 

 Different coefficients and gains can be provided for every channel, in such case use '|' to separate coefficients or gains. Last provided coefficients will be used for all remaining channels. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply 2 pole elliptic notch at around 5000Hz for 48000 Hz sample rate: 

 <pre>
        aiir=k=1:z=7.957584807809675810E-1 -2.575128568908332300 3.674839853930788710 -2.57512875289799137 7.957586296317130880E-1:p=1 -2.86950072432325953 3.63022088054647218 -2.28075678147272232 6.361362326477423500E-1:f=tf:r=d
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above but in <tt>&quot;zp&quot;</tt> format: 

 <pre>
        aiir=k=0.79575848078096756:z=0.80918701+0.58773007i 0.80918701-0.58773007i 0.80884700+0.58784055i 0.80884700-0.58784055i:p=0.63892345+0.59951235i 0.63892345-0.59951235i 0.79582691+0.44198673i 0.79582691-0.44198673i:f=zp:r=s
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply 3-rd order analog normalized Butterworth low-pass filter, using analog transfer function format: 

 <pre>
        aiir=z=1.3057 0 0 0:p=1.3057 2.3892 2.1860 1:f=sf:r=d
</pre></dl>

<h3>alimiter</h3>

 The limiter prevents an input signal from rising over a desired threshold. This limiter uses lookahead technology to prevent your signal from distorting. It means that there is a small delay after the signal is processed. Keep in mind that the delay it produces is the attack time you set. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>level_in</b>
<dd> Set input gain. Default is 1.
<dt><b>level_out</b>
<dd> Set output gain. Default is 1.
<dt><b>limit</b>
<dd> Don't let signals above this level pass the limiter. Default is 1.
<dt><b>attack</b>
<dd> The limiter will reach its attenuation level in this amount of time in milliseconds. Default is 5 milliseconds.
<dt><b>release</b>
<dd> Come back from limiting to attenuation 1.0 in this amount of milliseconds. Default is 50 milliseconds.
<dt><b>asc</b>
<dd> When gain reduction is always needed <font SIZE="-1">ASC</font> takes care of releasing to an average reduction level rather than reaching a reduction of 0 in the release time.
<dt><b>asc_level</b>
<dd> Select how much the release time is affected by <font SIZE="-1">ASC, 0</font> means nearly no changes in release time while 1 produces higher release times.
<dt><b>level</b>
<dd> Auto level output signal. Default is enabled. This normalizes audio back to 0dB if enabled.</dl>
