<dd> Mute the left channel. Disabled by default.
<dt><b>muter</b>
<dd> Mute the right channel. Disabled by default.
<dt><b>phasel</b>
<dd> Change the phase of the left channel. Disabled by default.
<dt><b>phaser</b>
<dd> Change the phase of the right channel. Disabled by default.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set stereo mode. Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lr&gt;lr</b>
<dd> Left/Right to Left/Right, this is default.
<dt><b>lr&gt;ms</b>
<dd> Left/Right to Mid/Side.
<dt><b>ms&gt;lr</b>
<dd> Mid/Side to Left/Right.
<dt><b>lr&gt;ll</b>
<dd> Left/Right to Left/Left.
<dt><b>lr&gt;rr</b>
<dd> Left/Right to Right/Right.
<dt><b>lr&gt;l+r</b>
<dd> Left/Right to Left + Right.
<dt><b>lr&gt;rl</b>
<dd> Left/Right to Right/Left.
<dt><b>ms&gt;ll</b>
<dd> Mid/Side to Left/Left.
<dt><b>ms&gt;rr</b>
<dd> Mid/Side to Right/Right.
<dt><b>ms&gt;rl</b>
<dd> Mid/Side to Right/Left.
<dt><b>lr&gt;l-r</b>
<dd> Left/Right to Left - Right.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>slev</b>
<dd> Set level of side signal. Default is 1. Allowed range is from 0.015625 to 64.
<dt><b>sbal</b>
<dd> Set balance of side signal. Default is 0. Allowed range is from -1 to 1.
<dt><b>mlev</b>
<dd> Set level of the middle signal. Default is 1. Allowed range is from 0.015625 to 64.
<dt><b>mpan</b>
<dd> Set middle signal pan. Default is 0. Allowed range is from -1 to 1.
<dt><b>base</b>
<dd> Set stereo base between mono and inversed channels. Default is 0. Allowed range is from -1 to 1.
<dt><b>delay</b>
<dd> Set delay in milliseconds how much to delay left from right channel and vice versa. Default is 0. Allowed range is from -20 to 20.
<dt><b>sclevel</b>
<dd> Set S/C level. Default is 1. Allowed range is from 1 to 100.
<dt><b>phase</b>
<dd> Set the stereo phase in degrees. Default is 0. Allowed range is from 0 to 360.
<dt><b>bmode_in, bmode_out</b>
<dd> Set balance mode for balance_in/balance_out option. 

 Can be one of the following:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>balance</b>
<dd> Classic balance mode. Attenuate one channel at time. Gain is raised up to 1.
<dt><b>amplitude</b>
<dd> Similar as classic mode above but gain is raised up to 2.
<dt><b>power</b>
<dd> Equal power distribution, from -6dB to +6dB range.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply karaoke like effect: 

 <pre>
        stereotools=mlev=0.015625
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Convert M/S signal to L/R: 

 <pre>
        &quot;stereotools=mode=ms&gt;lr&quot;
</pre></dl>

<h3>stereowiden</h3>

 This filter enhance the stereo effect by suppressing signal common to both channels and by delaying the signal of left into right and vice versa, thereby widening the stereo effect. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>delay</b>
<dd> Time in milliseconds of the delay of left signal into right and vice versa. Default is 20 milliseconds.
<dt><b>feedback</b>
<dd> Amount of gain in delayed signal into right and vice versa. Gives a delay effect of left signal in right output and vice versa which gives widening effect. Default is 0.3.
<dt><b>crossfeed</b>
<dd> Cross feed of left into right with inverted phase. This helps in suppressing the mono. If the value is 1 it will cancel all the signal common to both channels. Default is 0.3.
<dt><b>drymix</b>
<dd> Set level of input signal of original channel. Default is 0.8.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options except <tt>&quot;delay&quot;</tt> as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>superequalizer</h3>

 Apply 18 band equalizer. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>1b</b>
<dd> Set 65Hz band gain.
<dt><b>2b</b>
<dd> Set 92Hz band gain.
<dt><b>3b</b>
<dd> Set 131Hz band gain.
<dt><b>4b</b>
<dd> Set 185Hz band gain.
<dt><b>5b</b>
<dd> Set 262Hz band gain.
<dt><b>6b</b>
<dd> Set 370Hz band gain.
<dt><b>7b</b>
<dd> Set 523Hz band gain.
<dt><b>8b</b>
<dd> Set 740Hz band gain.
<dt><b>9b</b>
<dd> Set 1047Hz band gain.
<dt><b>10b</b>
<dd> Set 1480Hz band gain.
<dt><b>11b</b>
<dd> Set 2093Hz band gain.
<dt><b>12b</b>
<dd> Set 2960Hz band gain.
<dt><b>13b</b>
<dd> Set 4186Hz band gain.
<dt><b>14b</b>
<dd> Set 5920Hz band gain.
<dt><b>15b</b>
<dd> Set 8372Hz band gain.
<dt><b>16b</b>
<dd> Set 11840Hz band gain.
<dt><b>17b</b>
<dd> Set 16744Hz band gain.
<dt><b>18b</b>
<dd> Set 20000Hz band gain.</dl>

<h3>surround</h3>

 Apply audio surround upmix filter. 

 This filter allows to produce multichannel output from audio stream. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>chl_out</b>
<dd> Set output channel layout. By default, this is <i>5.1</i>. 

 See <b>the Channel Layout section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the required syntax.
<dt><b>chl_in</b>
<dd> Set input channel layout. By default, this is <i>stereo</i>. 

 See <b>the Channel Layout section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the required syntax.
<dt><b>level_in</b>
<dd> Set input volume level. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>level_out</b>
<dd> Set output volume level. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>lfe</b>
<dd> Enable <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> channel output if output channel layout has it. By default, this is enabled.
<dt><b>lfe_low</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> low cut off frequency. By default, this is <i>128</i> Hz.
<dt><b>lfe_high</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> high cut off frequency. By default, this is <i>256</i> Hz.
<dt><b>lfe_mode</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> mode, can be <i>add</i> or <i>sub</i>. Default is <i>add</i>. In <i>add</i> mode, <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> channel is created from input audio and added to output. In <i>sub</i> mode, <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> channel is created from input audio and added to output but also all non-LFE output channels are subtracted with output <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> channel.
<dt><b>angle</b>
<dd> Set angle of stereo surround transform, Allowed range is from <i>0</i> to <i>360</i>. Default is <i>90</i>.
<dt><b>fc_in</b>
<dd> Set front center input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>fc_out</b>
<dd> Set front center output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>fl_in</b>
<dd> Set front left input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>fl_out</b>
<dd> Set front left output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>fr_in</b>
<dd> Set front right input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>fr_out</b>
<dd> Set front right output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>sl_in</b>
<dd> Set side left input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>sl_out</b>
<dd> Set side left output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>sr_in</b>
<dd> Set side right input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>sr_out</b>
<dd> Set side right output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>bl_in</b>
<dd> Set back left input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>bl_out</b>
<dd> Set back left output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>br_in</b>
<dd> Set back right input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>br_out</b>
<dd> Set back right output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>bc_in</b>
<dd> Set back center input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>bc_out</b>
<dd> Set back center output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>lfe_in</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> input volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>lfe_out</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">LFE</font> output volume. By default, this is <i>1</i>.
<dt><b>allx</b>
<dd> Set spread usage of stereo image across X axis for all channels.
<dt><b>ally</b>
<dd> Set spread usage of stereo image across Y axis for all channels.
<dt><b>fcx, flx, frx, blx, brx, slx, srx, bcx</b>
<dd> Set spread usage of stereo image across X axis for each channel.
<dt><b>fcy, fly, fry, bly, bry, sly, sry, bcy</b>
<dd> Set spread usage of stereo image across Y axis for each channel.
<dt><b>win_size</b>
<dd> Set window size. Allowed range is from <i>1024</i> to <i>65536</i>. Default size is <i>4096</i>.
<dt><b>win_func</b>
<dd> Set window function. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rect</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bartlett</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hann, hanning</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hamming</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>blackman</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>welch</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>flattop</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bharris</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bnuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bhann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>sine</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>nuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lanczos</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gauss</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tukey</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dolph</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cauchy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>parzen</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>poisson</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bohman</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;hann&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd> Set window overlap. If set to 1, the recommended overlap for selected window function will be picked. Default is <tt>0.5</tt>.</dl>

<h3>treble, highshelf</h3>

 Boost or cut treble (upper) frequencies of the audio using a two-pole shelving filter with a response similar to that of a standard hi-fi's tone-controls. This is also known as shelving equalisation (<font SIZE="-1">EQ</font>). 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>gain, g</b>
<dd> Give the gain at whichever is the lower of ~22 kHz and the Nyquist frequency. Its useful range is about -20 (for a large cut) to +20 (for a large boost). Beware of clipping when using a positive gain.
<dt><b>frequency, f</b>
<dd> Set the filter's central frequency and so can be used to extend or reduce the frequency range to be boosted or cut. The default value is <tt>3000</tt> Hz.
<dt><b>width_type, t</b>
<dd> Set method to specify band-width of filter.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> Hz
<dt><b>q</b>
<dd> Q-Factor
<dt><b>o</b>
<dd> octave
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> slope
<dt><b>k</b>
<dd> kHz</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd> Determine how steep is the filter's shelf transition.
<dt><b>poles, p</b>
<dd> Set number of poles. Default is 2.
<dt><b>mix, m</b>
<dd> How much to use filtered signal in output. Default is 1. Range is between 0 and 1.
<dt><b>channels, c</b>
<dd> Specify which channels to filter, by default all available are filtered.
<dt><b>normalize, n</b>
<dd> Normalize biquad coefficients, by default is disabled. Enabling it will normalize magnitude response at <font SIZE="-1">DC</font> to 0dB.
<dt><b>transform, a</b>
<dd> Set transform type of <font SIZE="-1">IIR</font> filter.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>di</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dii</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tdii</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>latt</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>precision, r</b>
<dd> Set precison of filtering.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> Pick automatic sample format depending on surround filters.
<dt><b>s16</b>
<dd> Always use signed 16-bit.
<dt><b>s32</b>
<dd> Always use signed 32-bit.
<dt><b>f32</b>
<dd> Always use float 32-bit.
<dt><b>f64</b>
<dd> Always use float 64-bit.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl>
<dt><b>frequency, f</b>
<dd> Change treble frequency. Syntax for the command is : &quot;<i>frequency</i>&quot;
<dt><b>width_type, t</b>
<dd> Change treble width_type. Syntax for the command is : &quot;<i>width_type</i>&quot;
<dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd> Change treble width. Syntax for the command is : &quot;<i>width</i>&quot;
<dt><b>gain, g</b>
<dd> Change treble gain. Syntax for the command is : &quot;<i>gain</i>&quot;
<dt><b>mix, m</b>
<dd> Change treble mix. Syntax for the command is : &quot;<i>mix</i>&quot;</dl>

<h3>tremolo</h3>

 Sinusoidal amplitude modulation. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>f</b>
<dd> Modulation frequency in Hertz. Modulation frequencies in the subharmonic range (20 Hz or lower) will result in a tremolo effect. This filter may also be used as a ring modulator by specifying a modulation frequency higher than 20 Hz. Range is 0.1 - 20000.0. Default value is 5.0 Hz.
<dt><b>d</b>
<dd> Depth of modulation as a percentage. Range is 0.0 - 1.0. Default value is 0.5.</dl>

<h3>vibrato</h3>

 Sinusoidal phase modulation. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>f</b>
<dd> Modulation frequency in Hertz. Range is 0.1 - 20000.0. Default value is 5.0 Hz.
<dt><b>d</b>
<dd> Depth of modulation as a percentage. Range is 0.0 - 1.0. Default value is 0.5.</dl>

<h3>volume</h3>

 Adjust the input audio volume. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>volume</b>
<dd> Set audio volume expression. 

 Output values are clipped to the maximum value. 

 The output audio volume is given by the relation: 

 <pre>
        &lt;output_volume&gt; = &lt;volume&gt; * &lt;input_volume&gt;
</pre> 

 The default value for <i>volume</i> is ``1.0''.
<dt><b>precision</b>
<dd> This parameter represents the mathematical precision. 

 It determines which input sample formats will be allowed, which affects the precision of the volume scaling.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>fixed</b>
<dd> 8-bit fixed-point; this limits input sample format to U8, S16, and S32.
<dt><b>float</b>
<dd> 32-bit floating-point; this limits input sample format to <font SIZE="-1">FLT.</font> (default)
<dt><b>double</b>
<dd> 64-bit floating-point; this limits input sample format to <font SIZE="-1">DBL.</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>replaygain</b>
<dd> Choose the behaviour on encountering ReplayGain side data in input frames.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>drop</b>
<dd> Remove ReplayGain side data, ignoring its contents (the default).
<dt><b>ignore</b>
<dd> Ignore ReplayGain side data, but leave it in the frame.
<dt><b>track</b>
<dd> Prefer the track gain, if present.
<dt><b>album</b>
<dd> Prefer the album gain, if present.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>replaygain_preamp</b>
<dd> Pre-amplification gain in dB to apply to the selected replaygain gain. 

 Default value for <i>replaygain_preamp</i> is 0.0.
<dt><b>replaygain_noclip</b>
<dd> Prevent clipping by limiting the gain applied. 

 Default value for <i>replaygain_noclip</i> is 1.
<dt><b>eval</b>
<dd> Set when the volume expression is evaluated. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>once</b>
<dd> only evaluate expression once during the filter initialization, or when the <b>volume</b> command is sent
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd> evaluate expression for each incoming frame</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>once</b>.</dl>
</dl>
 

 The volume expression can contain the following parameters.
<dl>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> frame number (starting at zero)
<dt><b>nb_channels</b>
<dd> number of channels
<dt><b>nb_consumed_samples</b>
<dd> number of samples consumed by the filter
<dt><b>nb_samples</b>
<dd> number of samples in the current frame
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd> original frame position in the file
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd> frame <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font>
<dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd> sample rate
<dt><b>startpts</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> at start of stream
<dt><b>startt</b>
<dd> time at start of stream
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd> frame time
<dt><b>tb</b>
<dd> timestamp timebase
<dt><b>volume</b>
<dd> last set volume value</dl>
 

 Note that when <b>eval</b> is set to <b>once</b> only the <i>sample_rate</i> and <i>tb</i> variables are available, all other variables will evaluate to <font SIZE="-1">NAN.</font> 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl>
<dt><b>volume</b>
<dd> Modify the volume expression. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Halve the input audio volume: 

 <pre>
        volume=volume=0.5
        volume=volume=1/2
        volume=volume=-6.0206dB
</pre> 

 In all the above example the named key for <b>volume</b> can be omitted, for example like in: 

 <pre>
        volume=0.5
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Increase input audio power by 6 decibels using fixed-point precision: 

 <pre>
        volume=volume=6dB:precision=fixed
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Fade volume after time 10 with an annihilation period of 5 seconds: 

 <pre>
        volume='if(lt(t,10),1,max(1-(t-10)/5,0))':eval=frame
</pre></dl>

<h3>volumedetect</h3>

 Detect the volume of the input video. 

 The filter has no parameters. The input is not modified. Statistics about the volume will be printed in the log when the input stream end is reached. 

 In particular it will show the mean volume (root mean square), maximum volume (on a per-sample basis), and the beginning of a histogram of the registered volume values (from the maximum value to a cumulated 1/1000 of the samples). 

 All volumes are in decibels relative to the maximum <font SIZE="-1">PCM</font> value. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 Here is an excerpt of the output: 

 
[Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] mean_volume : -27 dB
                                                   [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] max_volume : -4 dB
                                                                                                     [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] histogram_4db : 6
                                                                                                         [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] histogram_5db : 62
                                                                                                             [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] histogram_6db : 286
                                                                                                                 [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] histogram_7db : 1042
                                                                                                                     [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] histogram_8db : 2551
                                                                                                                         [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] histogram_9db : 4609
                                                                                                                             [Parsed_volumedetect_0 0xa23120] histogram_10db : 8409
 

 It means that:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> The mean square energy is approximately -27 dB, or 10^-2.7.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> The largest sample is at -4 dB, or more precisely between -4 dB and -5 dB.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> There are 6 samples at -4 dB, 62 at -5 dB, 286 at -6 dB, etc.</dl>
 

 In other words, raising the volume by +4 dB does not cause any clipping, raising it by +5 dB causes clipping for 6 samples, etc.

<h2>AUDIO SOURCES</h2>

 Below is a description of the currently available audio sources.

<h3>abuffer</h3>

 Buffer audio frames, and make them available to the filter chain. 

 This source is mainly intended for a programmatic use, in particular through the interface defined in <i>libavfilter/buffersrc.h</i>. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>time_base</b>
<dd> The timebase which will be used for timestamps of submitted frames. It must be either a floating-point number or in <i>numerator</i>/<i>denominator</i> form.
<dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd> The sample rate of the incoming audio buffers.
<dt><b>sample_fmt</b>
<dd> The sample format of the incoming audio buffers. Either a sample format name or its corresponding integer representation from the enum AVSampleFormat in <i>libavutil/samplefmt.h</i>
<dt><b>channel_layout</b>
<dd> The channel layout of the incoming audio buffers. Either a channel layout name from channel_layout_map in <i>libavutil/channel_layout.c</i> or its corresponding integer representation from the AV_CH_LAYOUT_* macros in <i>libavutil/channel_layout.h</i>
<dt><b>channels</b>
<dd> The number of channels of the incoming audio buffers. If both <i>channels</i> and <i>channel_layout</i> are specified, then they must be consistent.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 <pre>
        abuffer=sample_rate=44100:sample_fmt=s16p:channel_layout=stereo
</pre> 

 will instruct the source to accept planar 16bit signed stereo at 44100Hz. Since the sample format with name ``s16p'' corresponds to the number 6 and the ``stereo'' channel layout corresponds to the value 0x3, this is equivalent to: 

 <pre>
        abuffer=sample_rate=44100:sample_fmt=6:channel_layout=0x3
</pre>

<h3>aevalsrc</h3>

 Generate an audio signal specified by an expression. 

 This source accepts in input one or more expressions (one for each channel), which are evaluated and used to generate a corresponding audio signal. 

 This source accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>exprs</b>
<dd> Set the '|'-separated expressions list for each separate channel. In case the <b>channel_layout</b> option is not specified, the selected channel layout depends on the number of provided expressions. Otherwise the last specified expression is applied to the remaining output channels.
<dt><b>channel_layout, c</b>
<dd> Set the channel layout. The number of channels in the specified layout must be equal to the number of specified expressions.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd> Set the minimum duration of the sourced audio. See <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. Note that the resulting duration may be greater than the specified duration, as the generated audio is always cut at the end of a complete frame. 

 If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the audio is supposed to be generated forever.
<dt><b>nb_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set the number of samples per channel per each output frame, default to 1024.
<dt><b>sample_rate, s</b>
<dd> Specify the sample rate, default to 44100.</dl>
 

 Each expression in <i>exprs</i> can contain the following constants:
<dl>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> number of the evaluated sample, starting from 0
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd> time of the evaluated sample expressed in seconds, starting from 0
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> sample rate</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate silence: 

 <pre>
        aevalsrc=0
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate a sin signal with frequency of 440 Hz, set sample rate to 8000 Hz: 

 <pre>
        aevalsrc=&quot;sin(440*2*PI*t):s=8000&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate a two channels signal, specify the channel layout (Front Center + Back Center) explicitly: 

 <pre>
        aevalsrc=&quot;sin(420*2*PI*t)|cos(430*2*PI*t):c=FC|BC&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate white noise: 

 <pre>
        aevalsrc=&quot;-2+random(0)&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate an amplitude modulated signal: 

 <pre>
        aevalsrc=&quot;sin(10*2*PI*t)*sin(880*2*PI*t)&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate 2.5 Hz binaural beats on a 360 Hz carrier: 

 <pre>
        aevalsrc=&quot;0.1*sin(2*PI*(360-2.5/2)*t) | 0.1*sin(2*PI*(360+2.5/2)*t)&quot;
</pre></dl>

<h3>afirsrc</h3>

 Generate a <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> coefficients using frequency sampling method. 

 The resulting stream can be used with <b>afir</b> filter for filtering the audio signal. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>taps, t</b>
<dd> Set number of filter coefficents in output audio stream. Default value is 1025.
<dt><b>frequency, f</b>
<dd> Set frequency points from where magnitude and phase are set. This must be in non decreasing order, and first element must be 0, while last element must be 1. Elements are separated by white spaces.
<dt><b>magnitude, m</b>
<dd> Set magnitude value for every frequency point set by <b>frequency</b>. Number of values must be same as number of frequency points. Values are separated by white spaces.
<dt><b>phase, p</b>
<dd> Set phase value for every frequency point set by <b>frequency</b>. Number of values must be same as number of frequency points. Values are separated by white spaces.
<dt><b>sample_rate, r</b>
<dd> Set sample rate, default is 44100.
<dt><b>nb_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set number of samples per each frame. Default is 1024.
<dt><b>win_func, w</b>
<dd> Set window function. Default is blackman.</dl>

<h3>anullsrc</h3>

 The null audio source, return unprocessed audio frames. It is mainly useful as a template and to be employed in analysis / debugging tools, or as the source for filters which ignore the input data (for example the sox synth filter). 

 This source accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>channel_layout, cl</b>
<dd> Specifies the channel layout, and can be either an integer or a string representing a channel layout. The default value of <i>channel_layout</i> is ``stereo''. 

 Check the channel_layout_map definition in <i>libavutil/channel_layout.c</i> for the mapping between strings and channel layout values.
<dt><b>sample_rate, r</b>
<dd> Specifies the sample rate, and defaults to 44100.
<dt><b>nb_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set the number of samples per requested frames.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd> Set the duration of the sourced audio. See <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. 

 If not specified, or the expressed duration is negative, the audio is supposed to be generated forever.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Set the sample rate to 48000 Hz and the channel layout to <font SIZE="-1">AV_CH_LAYOUT_MONO.</font> 

 <pre>
        anullsrc=r=48000:cl=4
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Do the same operation with a more obvious syntax: 

 <pre>
        anullsrc=r=48000:cl=mono
</pre></dl>
 

 All the parameters need to be explicitly defined.

<h3>flite</h3>

 Synthesize a voice utterance using the libflite library. 

 To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libflite&quot;</tt>. 

 Note that versions of the flite library prior to 2.0 are not thread-safe. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>list_voices</b>
<dd> If set to 1, list the names of the available voices and exit immediately. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>nb_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set the maximum number of samples per frame. Default value is 512.
<dt><b>textfile</b>
<dd> Set the filename containing the text to speak.
<dt><b>text</b>
<dd> Set the text to speak.
<dt><b>voice, v</b>
<dd> Set the voice to use for the speech synthesis. Default value is <tt>&quot;kal&quot;</tt>. See also the <i>list_voices</i> option.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Read from file <i>speech.txt</i>, and synthesize the text using the standard flite voice: 

 <pre>
        flite=textfile=speech.txt
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Read the specified text selecting the <tt>&quot;slt&quot;</tt> voice: 

 <pre>
        flite=text='So fare thee well, poor devil of a Sub-Sub, whose commentator I am':voice=slt
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Input text to ffmpeg: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -f lavfi -i flite=text='So fare thee well, poor devil of a Sub-Sub, whose commentator I am':voice=slt
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Make <i>ffplay</i> speak the specified text, using <tt>&quot;flite&quot;</tt> and the <tt>&quot;lavfi&quot;</tt> device: 

 <pre>
        ffplay -f lavfi flite=text='No more be grieved for which that thou hast done.'
</pre></dl>
 

 For more information about libflite, check: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.festvox.org/flite/">http://www.festvox.org/flite/</a></b>&gt;

<h3>anoisesrc</h3>

 Generate a noise audio signal. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>sample_rate, r</b>
<dd> Specify the sample rate. Default value is 48000 Hz.
<dt><b>amplitude, a</b>
<dd> Specify the amplitude (0.0 - 1.0) of the generated audio stream. Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd> Specify the duration of the generated audio stream. Not specifying this option results in noise with an infinite length.
<dt><b>color, colour, c</b>
<dd> Specify the color of noise. Available noise colors are white, pink, brown, blue, violet and velvet. Default color is white.
<dt><b>seed, s</b>
<dd> Specify a value used to seed the <font SIZE="-1">PRNG.</font>
<dt><b>nb_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set the number of samples per each output frame, default is 1024.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate 60 seconds of pink noise, with a 44.1 kHz sampling rate and an amplitude of 0.5: 

 <pre>
        anoisesrc=d=60:c=pink:r=44100:a=0.5
</pre></dl>

<h3>hilbert</h3>

 Generate odd-tap Hilbert transform <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> coefficients. 

 The resulting stream can be used with <b>afir</b> filter for phase-shifting the signal by 90 degrees. 

 This is used in many matrix coding schemes and for analytic signal generation. The process is often written as a multiplication by i (or j), the imaginary unit. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>sample_rate, s</b>
<dd> Set sample rate, default is 44100.
<dt><b>taps, t</b>
<dd> Set length of <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> filter, default is 22051.
<dt><b>nb_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set number of samples per each frame.
<dt><b>win_func, w</b>
<dd> Set window function to be used when generating <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> coefficients.</dl>

<h3>sinc</h3>

 Generate a sinc kaiser-windowed low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, or band-reject <font SIZE="-1">FIR</font> coefficients. 

 The resulting stream can be used with <b>afir</b> filter for filtering the audio signal. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>sample_rate, r</b>
<dd> Set sample rate, default is 44100.
<dt><b>nb_samples, n</b>
<dd> Set number of samples per each frame. Default is 1024.
<dt><b>hp</b>
<dd> Set high-pass frequency. Default is 0.
<dt><b>lp</b>
<dd> Set low-pass frequency. Default is 0. If high-pass frequency is lower than low-pass frequency and low-pass frequency is higher than 0 then filter will create band-pass filter coefficients, otherwise band-reject filter coefficients.
<dt><b>phase</b>
<dd> Set filter phase response. Default is 50. Allowed range is from 0 to 100.
<dt><b>beta</b>
<dd> Set Kaiser window beta.
<dt><b>att</b>
<dd> Set stop-band attenuation. Default is 120dB, allowed range is from 40 to 180 dB.
<dt><b>round</b>
<dd> Enable rounding, by default is disabled.
<dt><b>hptaps</b>
<dd> Set number of taps for high-pass filter.
<dt><b>lptaps</b>
<dd> Set number of taps for low-pass filter.</dl>

<h3>sine</h3>

 Generate an audio signal made of a sine wave with amplitude 1/8. 

 The audio signal is bit-exact. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>frequency, f</b>
<dd> Set the carrier frequency. Default is 440 Hz.
<dt><b>beep_factor, b</b>
<dd> Enable a periodic beep every second with frequency <i>beep_factor</i> times the carrier frequency. Default is 0, meaning the beep is disabled.
<dt><b>sample_rate, r</b>
<dd> Specify the sample rate, default is 44100.
<dt><b>duration, d</b>
<dd> Specify the duration of the generated audio stream.
<dt><b>samples_per_frame</b>
<dd> Set the number of samples per output frame. 

 The expression can contain the following constants:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> The (sequential) number of the output audio frame, starting from 0.
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd> The <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> (Presentation TimeStamp) of the output audio frame, expressed in <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>TB</i></font><i></i> units.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd> The <font SIZE="-1">PTS</font> of the output audio frame, expressed in seconds.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TB</b></font>
<dd> The timebase of the output audio frames.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>1024</tt>.</dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate a simple 440 Hz sine wave: 

 <pre>
        sine
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate a 220 Hz sine wave with a 880 Hz beep each second, for 5 seconds: 

 <pre>
        sine=220:4:d=5
        sine=f=220:b=4:d=5
        sine=frequency=220:beep_factor=4:duration=5
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Generate a 1 kHz sine wave following <tt>&quot;1602,1601,1602,1601,1602&quot;</tt> <font SIZE="-1">NTSC</font> pattern: 

 <pre>
        sine=1000:samples_per_frame='st(0,mod(n,5)); 1602-not(not(eq(ld(0),1)+eq(ld(0),3)))'
</pre></dl>

<h2>AUDIO SINKS</h2>

 Below is a description of the currently available audio sinks.

<h3>abuffersink</h3>

 Buffer audio frames, and make them available to the end of filter chain. 

 This sink is mainly intended for programmatic use, in particular through the interface defined in <i>libavfilter/buffersink.h</i> or the options system. 

 It accepts a pointer to an AVABufferSinkContext structure, which defines the incoming buffers' formats, to be passed as the opaque parameter to <tt>&quot;avfilter_init_filter&quot;</tt> for initialization.

<h3>anullsink</h3>

 Null audio sink; do absolutely nothing with the input audio. It is mainly useful as a template and for use in analysis / debugging tools.

<h2>VIDEO FILTERS</h2>

 When you configure your FFmpeg build, you can disable any of the existing filters using <tt>&quot;--disable-filters&quot;</tt>. The configure output will show the video filters included in your build. 

 Below is a description of the currently available video filters.

<h3>addroi</h3>

 Mark a region of interest in a video frame. 

 The frame data is passed through unchanged, but metadata is attached to the frame indicating regions of interest which can affect the behaviour of later encoding. Multiple regions can be marked by applying the filter multiple times.
<dl>
<dt><b>x</b>
<dd> Region distance in pixels from the left edge of the frame.
<dt><b>y</b>
<dd> Region distance in pixels from the top edge of the frame.
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd> Region width in pixels.
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> Region height in pixels. 

 The parameters <i>x</i>, <i>y</i>, <i>w</i> and <i>h</i> are expressions, and may contain the following variables:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>iw</b>
<dd> Width of the input frame.
<dt><b>ih</b>
<dd> Height of the input frame.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>qoffset</b>
<dd> Quantisation offset to apply within the region. 

 This must be a real value in the range -1 to +1. A value of zero indicates no quality change. A negative value asks for better quality (less quantisation), while a positive value asks for worse quality (greater quantisation). 

 The range is calibrated so that the extreme values indicate the largest possible offset - if the rest of the frame is encoded with the worst possible quality, an offset of -1 indicates that this region should be encoded with the best possible quality anyway. Intermediate values are then interpolated in some codec-dependent way. 

 For example, in 10-bit H.264 the quantisation parameter varies between -12 and 51. A typical qoffset value of -1/10 therefore indicates that this region should be encoded with a <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> around one-tenth of the full range better than the rest of the frame. So, if most of the frame were to be encoded with a <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> of around 30, this region would get a <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> of around 24 (an offset of approximately -1/10 * (51 - -12) = -6.3). An extreme value of -1 would indicate that this region should be encoded with the best possible quality regardless of the treatment of the rest of the frame - that is, should be encoded at a <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> of -12.
<dt><b>clear</b>
<dd> If set to true, remove any existing regions of interest marked on the frame before adding the new one.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Mark the centre quarter of the frame as interesting. 

 <pre>
        addroi=iw/4:ih/4:iw/2:ih/2:-1/10
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Mark the 100-pixel-wide region on the left edge of the frame as very uninteresting (to be encoded at much lower quality than the rest of the frame). 

 <pre>
        addroi=0:0:100:ih:+1/5
</pre></dl>

<h3>alphaextract</h3>

 Extract the alpha component from the input as a grayscale video. This is especially useful with the <i>alphamerge</i> filter.

<h3>alphamerge</h3>

 Add or replace the alpha component of the primary input with the grayscale value of a second input. This is intended for use with <i>alphaextract</i> to allow the transmission or storage of frame sequences that have alpha in a format that doesn't support an alpha channel. 

 For example, to reconstruct full frames from a normal YUV-encoded video and a separate video created with <i>alphaextract</i>, you might use: 

 
movie = in_alpha.mkv[alpha];
[in][alpha] alphamerge[out]


<h3>amplify</h3>

 Amplify differences between current pixel and pixels of adjacent frames in same pixel location. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>radius</b>
<dd> Set frame radius. Default is 2. Allowed range is from 1 to 63. For example radius of 3 will instruct filter to calculate average of 7 frames.
<dt><b>factor</b>
<dd> Set factor to amplify difference. Default is 2. Allowed range is from 0 to 65535.
<dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd> Set threshold for difference amplification. Any difference greater or equal to this value will not alter source pixel. Default is 10. Allowed range is from 0 to 65535.
<dt><b>tolerance</b>
<dd> Set tolerance for difference amplification. Any difference lower to this value will not alter source pixel. Default is 0. Allowed range is from 0 to 65535.
<dt><b>low</b>
<dd> Set lower limit for changing source pixel. Default is 65535. Allowed range is from 0 to 65535. This option controls maximum possible value that will decrease source pixel value.
<dt><b>high</b>
<dd> Set high limit for changing source pixel. Default is 65535. Allowed range is from 0 to 65535. This option controls maximum possible value that will increase source pixel value.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set which planes to filter. Default is all. Allowed range is from 0 to 15.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following <b>commands</b> that corresponds to option of same name:
<dl>
<dt><b>factor</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>threshold</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tolerance</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>low</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>high</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd></dl>

<h3>ass</h3>

 Same as the <b>subtitles</b> filter, except that it doesn't require libavcodec and libavformat to work. On the other hand, it is limited to <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> (Advanced Substation Alpha) subtitles files. 

 This filter accepts the following option in addition to the common options from the <b>subtitles</b> filter:
<dl>
<dt><b>shaping</b>
<dd> Set the shaping engine 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>auto</b>
<dd> The default libass shaping engine, which is the best available.
<dt><b>simple</b>
<dd> Fast, font-agnostic shaper that can do only substitutions
<dt><b>complex</b>
<dd> Slower shaper using OpenType for substitutions and positioning</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 The default is <tt>&quot;auto&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>atadenoise</h3>

 Apply an Adaptive Temporal Averaging Denoiser to the video input. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>0a</b>
<dd> Set threshold A for 1st plane. Default is 0.02. Valid range is 0 to 0.3.
<dt><b>0b</b>
<dd> Set threshold B for 1st plane. Default is 0.04. Valid range is 0 to 5.
<dt><b>1a</b>
<dd> Set threshold A for 2nd plane. Default is 0.02. Valid range is 0 to 0.3.
<dt><b>1b</b>
<dd> Set threshold B for 2nd plane. Default is 0.04. Valid range is 0 to 5.
<dt><b>2a</b>
<dd> Set threshold A for 3rd plane. Default is 0.02. Valid range is 0 to 0.3.
<dt><b>2b</b>
<dd> Set threshold B for 3rd plane. Default is 0.04. Valid range is 0 to 5. 

 Threshold A is designed to react on abrupt changes in the input signal and threshold B is designed to react on continuous changes in the input signal.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> Set number of frames filter will use for averaging. Default is 9. Must be odd number in range [5, 129].
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd> Set what planes of frame filter will use for averaging. Default is all.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd> Set what variant of algorithm filter will use for averaging. Default is <tt>&quot;p&quot;</tt> parallel. Alternatively can be set to <tt>&quot;s&quot;</tt> serial. 

 Parallel can be faster then serial, while other way around is never true. Parallel will abort early on first change being greater then thresholds, while serial will continue processing other side of frames if they are equal or below thresholds.
<dt><b>0s</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>1s</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>2s</b>
<dd> Set sigma for 1st plane, 2nd plane or 3rd plane. Default is 32767. Valid range is from 0 to 32767. This options controls weight for each pixel in radius defined by size. Default value means every pixel have same weight. Setting this option to 0 effectively disables filtering.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options except option <tt>&quot;s&quot;</tt>. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option.

<h3>avgblur</h3>

 Apply average blur filter. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>sizeX</b>
<dd> Set horizontal radius size.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set which planes to filter. By default all planes are filtered.
<dt><b>sizeY</b>
<dd> Set vertical radius size, if zero it will be same as <tt>&quot;sizeX&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>0</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same commands as options. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.

<h3>bbox</h3>

 Compute the bounding box for the non-black pixels in the input frame luminance plane. 

 This filter computes the bounding box containing all the pixels with a luminance value greater than the minimum allowed value. The parameters describing the bounding box are printed on the filter log. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>min_val</b>
<dd> Set the minimal luminance value. Default is <tt>16</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>bilateral</h3>

 Apply bilateral filter, spatial smoothing while preserving edges. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>sigmaS</b>
<dd> Set sigma of gaussian function to calculate spatial weight. Allowed range is 0 to 512. Default is 0.1.
<dt><b>sigmaR</b>
<dd> Set sigma of gaussian function to calculate range weight. Allowed range is 0 to 1. Default is 0.1.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set planes to filter. Default is first only.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>bitplanenoise</h3>

 Show and measure bit plane noise. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>bitplane</b>
<dd> Set which plane to analyze. Default is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>filter</b>
<dd> Filter out noisy pixels from <tt>&quot;bitplane&quot;</tt> set above. Default is disabled.</dl>

<h3>blackdetect</h3>

 Detect video intervals that are (almost) completely black. Can be useful to detect chapter transitions, commercials, or invalid recordings. 

 The filter outputs its detection analysis to both the log as well as frame metadata. If a black segment of at least the specified minimum duration is found, a line with the start and end timestamps as well as duration is printed to the log with level <tt>&quot;info&quot;</tt>. In addition, a log line with level <tt>&quot;debug&quot;</tt> is printed per frame showing the black amount detected for that frame. 

 The filter also attaches metadata to the first frame of a black segment with key <tt>&quot;lavfi.black_start&quot;</tt> and to the first frame after the black segment ends with key <tt>&quot;lavfi.black_end&quot;</tt>. The value is the frame's timestamp. This metadata is added regardless of the minimum duration specified. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>black_min_duration, d</b>
<dd> Set the minimum detected black duration expressed in seconds. It must be a non-negative floating point number. 

 Default value is 2.0.
<dt><b>picture_black_ratio_th, pic_th</b>
<dd> Set the threshold for considering a picture ``black''. Express the minimum value for the ratio: 

 <pre>
        &lt;nb_black_pixels&gt; / &lt;nb_pixels&gt;
</pre> 

 for which a picture is considered black. Default value is 0.98.
<dt><b>pixel_black_th, pix_th</b>
<dd> Set the threshold for considering a pixel ``black''. 

 The threshold expresses the maximum pixel luminance value for which a pixel is considered ``black''. The provided value is scaled according to the following equation: 

 <pre>
        &lt;absolute_threshold&gt; = &lt;luminance_minimum_value&gt; + &lt;pixel_black_th&gt; * &lt;luminance_range_size&gt;
</pre> 

 <i>luminance_range_size</i> and <i>luminance_minimum_value</i> depend on the input video format, the range is [0-255] for <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> full-range formats and [16-235] for <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> non full-range formats. 

 Default value is 0.10.</dl>
 

 The following example sets the maximum pixel threshold to the minimum value, and detects only black intervals of 2 or more seconds: 

 <pre>
        blackdetect=d=2:pix_th=0.00
</pre>

<h3>blackframe</h3>

 Detect frames that are (almost) completely black. Can be useful to detect chapter transitions or commercials. Output lines consist of the frame number of the detected frame, the percentage of blackness, the position in the file if known or -1 and the timestamp in seconds. 

 In order to display the output lines, you need to set the loglevel at least to the <font SIZE="-1">AV_LOG_INFO</font> value. 

 This filter exports frame metadata <tt>&quot;lavfi.blackframe.pblack&quot;</tt>. The value represents the percentage of pixels in the picture that are below the threshold value. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>amount</b>
<dd> The percentage of the pixels that have to be below the threshold; it defaults to <tt>98</tt>.
<dt><b>threshold, thresh</b>
<dd> The threshold below which a pixel value is considered black; it defaults to <tt>32</tt>.</dl>

<h3>blend</h3>

 Blend two video frames into each other. 

 The <tt>&quot;blend&quot;</tt> filter takes two input streams and outputs one stream, the first input is the ``top'' layer and second input is ``bottom'' layer. By default, the output terminates when the longest input terminates. 

 The <tt>&quot;tblend&quot;</tt> (time blend) filter takes two consecutive frames from one single stream, and outputs the result obtained by blending the new frame on top of the old frame. 

 A description of the accepted options follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>c0_mode</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c1_mode</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c2_mode</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c3_mode</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>all_mode</b>
<dd> Set blend mode for specific pixel component or all pixel components in case of <i>all_mode</i>. Default value is <tt>&quot;normal&quot;</tt>. 

 Available values for component modes are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>addition</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>grainmerge</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>and</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>average</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>burn</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>darken</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>difference</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>grainextract</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>divide</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dodge</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>freeze</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>exclusion</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>extremity</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>glow</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hardlight</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hardmix</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>heat</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lighten</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>linearlight</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>multiply</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>multiply128</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>negation</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>normal</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>or</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>overlay</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>phoenix</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>pinlight</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>reflect</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>screen</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>softlight</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>subtract</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>vividlight</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>xor</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>c0_opacity</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c1_opacity</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c2_opacity</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c3_opacity</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>all_opacity</b>
<dd> Set blend opacity for specific pixel component or all pixel components in case of <i>all_opacity</i>. Only used in combination with pixel component blend modes.
<dt><b>c0_expr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c1_expr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c2_expr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c3_expr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>all_expr</b>
<dd> Set blend expression for specific pixel component or all pixel components in case of <i>all_expr</i>. Note that related mode options will be ignored if those are set. 

 The expressions can use the following variables:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>N</b>
<dd> The sequential number of the filtered frame, starting from <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>X</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>Y</b>
<dd> the coordinates of the current sample
<dt><b>W</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>H</b>
<dd> the width and height of currently filtered plane
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SW</b></font>
<dd>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SH</b></font>
<dd> Width and height scale for the plane being filtered. It is the ratio between the dimensions of the current plane to the luma plane, e.g. for a <tt>&quot;yuv420p&quot;</tt> frame, the values are <tt>&quot;1,1&quot;</tt> for the luma plane and <tt>&quot;0.5,0.5&quot;</tt> for the chroma planes.
<dt><b>T</b>
<dd> Time of the current frame, expressed in seconds.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>TOP, A</b></font>
<dd> Value of pixel component at current location for first video frame (top layer).
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>BOTTOM, B</b></font>
<dd> Value of pixel component at current location for second video frame (bottom layer).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 The <tt>&quot;blend&quot;</tt> filter also supports the <b>framesync</b> options. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply transition from bottom layer to top layer in first 10 seconds: 

 <pre>
        blend=all_expr='A*(if(gte(T,10),1,T/10))+B*(1-(if(gte(T,10),1,T/10)))'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply linear horizontal transition from top layer to bottom layer: 

 <pre>
        blend=all_expr='A*(X/W)+B*(1-X/W)'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply 1x1 checkerboard effect: 

 <pre>
        blend=all_expr='if(eq(mod(X,2),mod(Y,2)),A,B)'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply uncover left effect: 

 <pre>
        blend=all_expr='if(gte(N*SW+X,W),A,B)'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply uncover down effect: 

 <pre>
        blend=all_expr='if(gte(Y-N*SH,0),A,B)'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply uncover up-left effect: 

 <pre>
        blend=all_expr='if(gte(T*SH*40+Y,H)*gte((T*40*SW+X)*W/H,W),A,B)'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Split diagonally video and shows top and bottom layer on each side: 

 <pre>
        blend=all_expr='if(gt(X,Y*(W/H)),A,B)'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Display differences between the current and the previous frame: 

 <pre>
        tblend=all_mode=grainextract
</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options.

<h3>bm3d</h3>

 Denoise frames using Block-Matching 3D algorithm. 

 The filter accepts the following options.
<dl>
<dt><b>sigma</b>
<dd> Set denoising strength. Default value is 1. Allowed range is from 0 to 999.9. The denoising algorithm is very sensitive to sigma, so adjust it according to the source.
<dt><b>block</b>
<dd> Set local patch size. This sets dimensions in 2D.
<dt><b>bstep</b>
<dd> Set sliding step for processing blocks. Default value is 4. Allowed range is from 1 to 64. Smaller values allows processing more reference blocks and is slower.
<dt><b>group</b>
<dd> Set maximal number of similar blocks for 3rd dimension. Default value is 1. When set to 1, no block matching is done. Larger values allows more blocks in single group. Allowed range is from 1 to 256.
<dt><b>range</b>
<dd> Set radius for search block matching. Default is 9. Allowed range is from 1 to <font SIZE="-1">INT32_MAX.</font>
<dt><b>mstep</b>
<dd> Set step between two search locations for block matching. Default is 1. Allowed range is from 1 to 64. Smaller is slower.
<dt><b>thmse</b>
<dd> Set threshold of mean square error for block matching. Valid range is 0 to <font SIZE="-1">INT32_MAX.</font>
<dt><b>hdthr</b>
<dd> Set thresholding parameter for hard thresholding in 3D transformed domain. Larger values results in stronger hard-thresholding filtering in frequency domain.
<dt><b>estim</b>
<dd> Set filtering estimation mode. Can be <tt>&quot;basic&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;final&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;basic&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>ref</b>
<dd> If enabled, filter will use 2nd stream for block matching. Default is disabled for <tt>&quot;basic&quot;</tt> value of <i>estim</i> option, and always enabled if value of <i>estim</i> is <tt>&quot;final&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set planes to filter. Default is all available except alpha.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Basic filtering with bm3d: 

 <pre>
        bm3d=sigma=3:block=4:bstep=2:group=1:estim=basic
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but filtering only luma: 

 <pre>
        bm3d=sigma=3:block=4:bstep=2:group=1:estim=basic:planes=1
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but with both estimation modes: 

 
split[a][b], [a] bm3d = sigma = 3 : block = 4 : bstep = 2 : group = 1 : estim = basic[a], [b][a] bm3d = sigma = 3 : block = 4 : bstep = 2 : group = 16 : estim = final : ref = 1

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but prefilter with <b>nlmeans</b> filter instead: 

 
split[a][b], [a] nlmeans = s = 3 : r = 7 : p = 3 [a], [b][a] bm3d = sigma = 3 : block = 4 : bstep = 2 : group = 16 : estim = final : ref = 1
</dl>

<h3>boxblur</h3>

 Apply a boxblur algorithm to the input video. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>luma_radius, lr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>luma_power, lp</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>chroma_radius, cr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>chroma_power, cp</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>alpha_radius, ar</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>alpha_power, ap</b>
<dd></dl>
 

 A description of the accepted options follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>luma_radius, lr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>chroma_radius, cr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>alpha_radius, ar</b>
<dd> Set an expression for the box radius in pixels used for blurring the corresponding input plane. 

 The radius value must be a non-negative number, and must not be greater than the value of the expression <tt>&quot;min(w,h)/2&quot;</tt> for the luma and alpha planes, and of <tt>&quot;min(cw,ch)/2&quot;</tt> for the chroma planes. 

 Default value for <b>luma_radius</b> is ``2''. If not specified, <b>chroma_radius</b> and <b>alpha_radius</b> default to the corresponding value set for <b>luma_radius</b>. 

 The expressions can contain the following constants:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> The input width and height in pixels.
<dt><b>cw</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ch</b>
<dd> The input chroma image width and height in pixels.
<dt><b>hsub</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>vsub</b>
<dd> The horizontal and vertical chroma subsample values. For example, for the pixel format ``yuv422p'', <i>hsub</i> is 2 and <i>vsub</i> is 1.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>luma_power, lp</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>chroma_power, cp</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>alpha_power, ap</b>
<dd> Specify how many times the boxblur filter is applied to the corresponding plane. 

 Default value for <b>luma_power</b> is 2. If not specified, <b>chroma_power</b> and <b>alpha_power</b> default to the corresponding value set for <b>luma_power</b>. 

 A value of 0 will disable the effect.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply a boxblur filter with the luma, chroma, and alpha radii set to 2: 

 <pre>
        boxblur=luma_radius=2:luma_power=1
        boxblur=2:1
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Set the luma radius to 2, and alpha and chroma radius to 0: 

 <pre>
        boxblur=2:1:cr=0:ar=0
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Set the luma and chroma radii to a fraction of the video dimension: 

 <pre>
        boxblur=luma_radius=min(h\,w)/10:luma_power=1:chroma_radius=min(cw\,ch)/10:chroma_power=1
</pre></dl>

<h3>bwdif</h3>

 Deinterlace the input video (``bwdif'' stands for ``Bob Weaver Deinterlacing Filter''). 

 Motion adaptive deinterlacing based on yadif with the use of w3fdif and cubic interpolation algorithms. It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> The interlacing mode to adopt. It accepts one of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0, send_frame</b>
<dd> Output one frame for each frame.
<dt><b>1, send_field</b>
<dd> Output one frame for each field.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 The default value is <tt>&quot;send_field&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>parity</b>
<dd> The picture field parity assumed for the input interlaced video. It accepts one of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0, tff</b>
<dd> Assume the top field is first.
<dt><b>1, bff</b>
<dd> Assume the bottom field is first.
<dt><b>-1, auto</b>
<dd> Enable automatic detection of field parity.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 The default value is <tt>&quot;auto&quot;</tt>. If the interlacing is unknown or the decoder does not export this information, top field first will be assumed.</dl>

<dt><b>deint</b>
<dd> Specify which frames to deinterlace. Accepts one of the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0, all</b>
<dd> Deinterlace all frames.
<dt><b>1, interlaced</b>
<dd> Only deinterlace frames marked as interlaced.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 The default value is <tt>&quot;all&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>cas</h3>

 Apply Contrast Adaptive Sharpen filter to video stream. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>strength</b>
<dd> Set the sharpening strength. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set planes to filter. Default value is to filter all planes except alpha plane.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options.

<h3>chromahold</h3>

 Remove all color information for all colors except for certain one. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> The color which will not be replaced with neutral chroma.
<dt><b>similarity</b>
<dd> Similarity percentage with the above color. 0.01 matches only the exact key color, while 1.0 matches everything.
<dt><b>blend</b>
<dd> Blend percentage. 0.0 makes pixels either fully gray, or not gray at all. Higher values result in more preserved color.
<dt><b>yuv</b>
<dd> Signals that the color passed is already in <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> instead of <font SIZE="-1">RGB.</font> 

 Literal colors like ``green'' or ``red'' don't make sense with this enabled anymore. This can be used to pass exact <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> values as hexadecimal numbers.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.

<h3>chromakey</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> colorspace color/chroma keying. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> The color which will be replaced with transparency.
<dt><b>similarity</b>
<dd> Similarity percentage with the key color. 

 0.01 matches only the exact key color, while 1.0 matches everything.
<dt><b>blend</b>
<dd> Blend percentage. 

 0.0 makes pixels either fully transparent, or not transparent at all. 

 Higher values result in semi-transparent pixels, with a higher transparency the more similar the pixels color is to the key color.
<dt><b>yuv</b>
<dd> Signals that the color passed is already in <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> instead of <font SIZE="-1">RGB.</font> 

 Literal colors like ``green'' or ``red'' don't make sense with this enabled anymore. This can be used to pass exact <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> values as hexadecimal numbers.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Make every green pixel in the input image transparent: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.png -vf chromakey=green out.png
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Overlay a greenscreen-video on top of a static black background. 

 
ffmpeg - f lavfi - i color = c = black : s = 1280x720 - i video.mp4 - shortest - filter_complex "[1:v]chromakey=0x70de77:0.1:0.2[ckout];[0:v][ckout]overlay[out]" - map "[out]" output.mkv
</dl>

<h3>chromanr</h3>

 Reduce chrominance noise. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>thres</b>
<dd> Set threshold for averaging chrominance values. Sum of absolute difference of Y, U and V pixel components of current pixel and neighbour pixels lower than this threshold will be used in averaging. Luma component is left unchanged and is copied to output. Default value is 30. Allowed range is from 1 to 200.
<dt><b>sizew</b>
<dd> Set horizontal radius of rectangle used for averaging. Allowed range is from 1 to 100. Default value is 5.
<dt><b>sizeh</b>
<dd> Set vertical radius of rectangle used for averaging. Allowed range is from 1 to 100. Default value is 5.
<dt><b>stepw</b>
<dd> Set horizontal step when averaging. Default value is 1. Allowed range is from 1 to 50. Mostly useful to speed-up filtering.
<dt><b>steph</b>
<dd> Set vertical step when averaging. Default value is 1. Allowed range is from 1 to 50. Mostly useful to speed-up filtering.
<dt><b>threy</b>
<dd> Set Y threshold for averaging chrominance values. Set finer control for max allowed difference between Y components of current pixel and neigbour pixels. Default value is 200. Allowed range is from 1 to 200.
<dt><b>threu</b>
<dd> Set U threshold for averaging chrominance values. Set finer control for max allowed difference between U components of current pixel and neigbour pixels. Default value is 200. Allowed range is from 1 to 200.
<dt><b>threv</b>
<dd> Set V threshold for averaging chrominance values. Set finer control for max allowed difference between V components of current pixel and neigbour pixels. Default value is 200. Allowed range is from 1 to 200.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option.

<h3>chromashift</h3>

 Shift chroma pixels horizontally and/or vertically. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>cbh</b>
<dd> Set amount to shift chroma-blue horizontally.
<dt><b>cbv</b>
<dd> Set amount to shift chroma-blue vertically.
<dt><b>crh</b>
<dd> Set amount to shift chroma-red horizontally.
<dt><b>crv</b>
<dd> Set amount to shift chroma-red vertically.
<dt><b>edge</b>
<dd> Set edge mode, can be <i>smear</i>, default, or <i>warp</i>.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>ciescope</h3>

 Display <font SIZE="-1">CIE</font> color diagram with pixels overlaid onto it. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>system</b>
<dd> Set color system.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>ntsc, 470m</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ebu, 470bg</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>smpte</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>240m</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>apple</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>widergb</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cie1931</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>rec709, hdtv</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>uhdtv, rec2020</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dcip3</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>cie</b>
<dd> Set <font SIZE="-1">CIE</font> system.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>xyy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ucs</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>luv</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>gamuts</b>
<dd> Set what gamuts to draw. 

 See <tt>&quot;system&quot;</tt> option for available values.
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd> Set ciescope size, by default set to 512.
<dt><b>intensity, i</b>
<dd> Set intensity used to map input pixel values to <font SIZE="-1">CIE</font> diagram.
<dt><b>contrast</b>
<dd> Set contrast used to draw tongue colors that are out of active color system gamut.
<dt><b>corrgamma</b>
<dd> Correct gamma displayed on scope, by default enabled.
<dt><b>showwhite</b>
<dd> Show white point on <font SIZE="-1">CIE</font> diagram, by default disabled.
<dt><b>gamma</b>
<dd> Set input gamma. Used only with <font SIZE="-1">XYZ</font> input color space.</dl>

<h3>codecview</h3>

 Visualize information exported by some codecs. 

 Some codecs can export information through frames using side-data or other means. For example, some <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> based codecs export motion vectors through the <i>export_mvs</i> flag in the codec <b>flags2</b> option. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>mv</b>
<dd> Set motion vectors to visualize. 

 Available flags for <i>mv</i> are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>pf</b>
<dd> forward predicted MVs of P-frames
<dt><b>bf</b>
<dd> forward predicted MVs of B-frames
<dt><b>bb</b>
<dd> backward predicted MVs of B-frames</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd> Display quantization parameters using the chroma planes.
<dt><b>mv_type, mvt</b>
<dd> Set motion vectors type to visualize. Includes MVs from all frames unless specified by <i>frame_type</i> option. 

 Available flags for <i>mv_type</i> are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>fp</b>
<dd> forward predicted MVs
<dt><b>bp</b>
<dd> backward predicted MVs</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>frame_type, ft</b>
<dd> Set frame type to visualize motion vectors of. 

 Available flags for <i>frame_type</i> are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>if</b>
<dd> intra-coded frames (I-frames)
<dt><b>pf</b>
<dd> predicted frames (P-frames)
<dt><b>bf</b>
<dd> bi-directionally predicted frames (B-frames)</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Visualize forward predicted MVs of all frames using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffplay -flags2 +export_mvs input.mp4 -vf codecview=mv_type=fp
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Visualize multi-directionals MVs of P and B-Frames using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffplay -flags2 +export_mvs input.mp4 -vf codecview=mv=pf+bf+bb
</pre></dl>

<h3>colorbalance</h3>

 Modify intensity of primary colors (red, green and blue) of input frames. 

 The filter allows an input frame to be adjusted in the shadows, midtones or highlights regions for the red-cyan, green-magenta or blue-yellow balance. 

 A positive adjustment value shifts the balance towards the primary color, a negative value towards the complementary color. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>rs</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gs</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bs</b>
<dd> Adjust red, green and blue shadows (darkest pixels).
<dt><b>rm</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gm</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bm</b>
<dd> Adjust red, green and blue midtones (medium pixels).
<dt><b>rh</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gh</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bh</b>
<dd> Adjust red, green and blue highlights (brightest pixels). 

 Allowed ranges for options are <tt>&quot;[-1.0, 1.0]&quot;</tt>. Defaults are <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>pl</b>
<dd> Preserve lightness when changing color balance. Default is disabled.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Add red color cast to shadows: 

 <pre>
        colorbalance=rs=.3
</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>colorcontrast</h3>

 Adjust color contrast between <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> components. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>rc</b>
<dd> Set the red-cyan contrast. Defaults is 0.0. Allowed range is from -1.0 to 1.0.
<dt><b>gm</b>
<dd> Set the green-magenta contrast. Defaults is 0.0. Allowed range is from -1.0 to 1.0.
<dt><b>by</b>
<dd> Set the blue-yellow contrast. Defaults is 0.0. Allowed range is from -1.0 to 1.0.
<dt><b>rcw</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gmw</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>byw</b>
<dd> Set the weight of each <tt>&quot;rc&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;gm&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;by&quot;</tt> option value. Default value is 0.0. Allowed range is from 0.0 to 1.0. If all weights are 0.0 filtering is disabled.
<dt><b>pl</b>
<dd> Set the amount of preserving lightness. Default value is 0.0. Allowed range is from 0.0 to 1.0.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>colorcorrect</h3>

 Adjust color white balance selectively for blacks and whites. This filter operates in <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> colorspace. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>rl</b>
<dd> Set the red shadow spot. Allowed range is from -1.0 to 1.0. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>bl</b>
<dd> Set the blue shadow spot. Allowed range is from -1.0 to 1.0. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>rh</b>
<dd> Set the red highlight spot. Allowed range is from -1.0 to 1.0. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>bh</b>
<dd> Set the red highlight spot. Allowed range is from -1.0 to 1.0. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>saturation</b>
<dd> Set the amount of saturation. Allowed range is from -3.0 to 3.0. Default value is 1.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>colorchannelmixer</h3>

 Adjust video input frames by re-mixing color channels. 

 This filter modifies a color channel by adding the values associated to the other channels of the same pixels. For example if the value to modify is red, the output value will be: 

 <pre>
        &lt;red&gt;=&lt;red&gt;*&lt;rr&gt; + &lt;blue&gt;*&lt;rb&gt; + &lt;green&gt;*&lt;rg&gt; + &lt;alpha&gt;*&lt;ra&gt;
</pre> 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>rr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>rg</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>rb</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ra</b>
<dd> Adjust contribution of input red, green, blue and alpha channels for output red channel. Default is <tt>1</tt> for <i>rr</i>, and <tt>0</tt> for <i>rg</i>, <i>rb</i> and <i>ra</i>.
<dt><b>gr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gg</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gb</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ga</b>
<dd> Adjust contribution of input red, green, blue and alpha channels for output green channel. Default is <tt>1</tt> for <i>gg</i>, and <tt>0</tt> for <i>gr</i>, <i>gb</i> and <i>ga</i>.
<dt><b>br</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bg</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bb</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ba</b>
<dd> Adjust contribution of input red, green, blue and alpha channels for output blue channel. Default is <tt>1</tt> for <i>bb</i>, and <tt>0</tt> for <i>br</i>, <i>bg</i> and <i>ba</i>.
<dt><b>ar</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ag</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>ab</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>aa</b>
<dd> Adjust contribution of input red, green, blue and alpha channels for output alpha channel. Default is <tt>1</tt> for <i>aa</i>, and <tt>0</tt> for <i>ar</i>, <i>ag</i> and <i>ab</i>. 

 Allowed ranges for options are <tt>&quot;[-2.0, 2.0]&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>pl</b>
<dd> Preserve lightness when changing colors. Allowed range is from <tt>&quot;[0.0, 1.0]&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>0.0</tt>, thus disabled.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Convert source to grayscale: 

 <pre>
        colorchannelmixer=.3:.4:.3:0:.3:.4:.3:0:.3:.4:.3
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Simulate sepia tones: 

 <pre>
        colorchannelmixer=.393:.769:.189:0:.349:.686:.168:0:.272:.534:.131
</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>colorize</h3>

 Overlay a solid color on the video stream. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>hue</b>
<dd> Set the color hue. Allowed range is from 0 to 360. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>saturation</b>
<dd> Set the color saturation. Allowed range is from 0 to 1. Default value is 0.5.
<dt><b>lightness</b>
<dd> Set the color lightness. Allowed range is from 0 to 1. Default value is 0.5.
<dt><b>mix</b>
<dd> Set the mix of source lightness. By default is set to 1.0. Allowed range is from 0.0 to 1.0.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>colorkey</h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> colorspace color keying. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> The color which will be replaced with transparency.
<dt><b>similarity</b>
<dd> Similarity percentage with the key color. 

 0.01 matches only the exact key color, while 1.0 matches everything.
<dt><b>blend</b>
<dd> Blend percentage. 

 0.0 makes pixels either fully transparent, or not transparent at all. 

 Higher values result in semi-transparent pixels, with a higher transparency the more similar the pixels color is to the key color.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Make every green pixel in the input image transparent: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.png -vf colorkey=green out.png
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Overlay a greenscreen-video on top of a static background image. 

 
ffmpeg - i background.png - i video.mp4 - filter_complex "[1:v]colorkey=0x3BBD1E:0.3:0.2[ckout];[0:v][ckout]overlay[out]" - map "[out]" output.flv
</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.

<h3>colorhold</h3>

 Remove all color information for all <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> colors except for certain one. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> The color which will not be replaced with neutral gray.
<dt><b>similarity</b>
<dd> Similarity percentage with the above color. 0.01 matches only the exact key color, while 1.0 matches everything.
<dt><b>blend</b>
<dd> Blend percentage. 0.0 makes pixels fully gray. Higher values result in more preserved color.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports same <b>commands</b> as options. The command accepts the same syntax of the corresponding option. 

 If the specified expression is not valid, it is kept at its current value.

<h3>colorlevels</h3>

 Adjust video input frames using levels. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>rimin</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gimin</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bimin</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>aimin</b>
<dd> Adjust red, green, blue and alpha input black point. Allowed ranges for options are <tt>&quot;[-1.0, 1.0]&quot;</tt>. Defaults are <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>rimax</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gimax</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bimax</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>aimax</b>
<dd> Adjust red, green, blue and alpha input white point. Allowed ranges for options are <tt>&quot;[-1.0, 1.0]&quot;</tt>. Defaults are <tt>1</tt>. 

 Input levels are used to lighten highlights (bright tones), darken shadows (dark tones), change the balance of bright and dark tones.
<dt><b>romin</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gomin</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bomin</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>aomin</b>
<dd> Adjust red, green, blue and alpha output black point. Allowed ranges for options are <tt>&quot;[0, 1.0]&quot;</tt>. Defaults are <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>romax</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gomax</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bomax</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>aomax</b>
<dd> Adjust red, green, blue and alpha output white point. Allowed ranges for options are <tt>&quot;[0, 1.0]&quot;</tt>. Defaults are <tt>1</tt>. 

 Output levels allows manual selection of a constrained output level range.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Make video output darker: 

 <pre>
        colorlevels=rimin=0.058:gimin=0.058:bimin=0.058
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Increase contrast: 

 <pre>
        colorlevels=rimin=0.039:gimin=0.039:bimin=0.039:rimax=0.96:gimax=0.96:bimax=0.96
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Make video output lighter: 

 <pre>
        colorlevels=rimax=0.902:gimax=0.902:bimax=0.902
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Increase brightness: 

 <pre>
        colorlevels=romin=0.5:gomin=0.5:bomin=0.5
</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>colormatrix</h3>

 Convert color matrix. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>src</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dst</b>
<dd> Specify the source and destination color matrix. Both values must be specified. 

 The accepted values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.709</font>
<dt><b>fcc</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FCC</font>
<dt><b>bt601</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.601</font>
<dt><b>bt470</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470</font>
<dt><b>bt470bg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470BG</font>
<dt><b>smpte170m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-170M</font>
<dt><b>smpte240m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-240M</font>
<dt><b>bt2020</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.2020</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>
 

 For example to convert from <font SIZE="-1">BT.601</font> to <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-240M,</font> use the command: 

 <pre>
        colormatrix=bt601:smpte240m
</pre>

<h3>colorspace</h3>

 Convert colorspace, transfer characteristics or color primaries. Input video needs to have an even size. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>all</b>
<dd> Specify all color properties at once. 

 The accepted values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>bt470m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470M</font>
<dt><b>bt470bg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470BG</font>
<dt><b>bt601-6-525</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.601-6 525</font>
<dt><b>bt601-6-625</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.601-6 625</font>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.709</font>
<dt><b>smpte170m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-170M</font>
<dt><b>smpte240m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-240M</font>
<dt><b>bt2020</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.2020</font></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>space</b>
<dd> Specify output colorspace. 

 The accepted values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.709</font>
<dt><b>fcc</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">FCC</font>
<dt><b>bt470bg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470BG</font> or <font SIZE="-1">BT.601-6 625</font>
<dt><b>smpte170m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-170M</font> or <font SIZE="-1">BT.601-6 525</font>
<dt><b>smpte240m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-240M</font>
<dt><b>ycgco</b>
<dd> YCgCo
<dt><b>bt2020ncl</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.2020</font> with non-constant luminance</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>trc</b>
<dd> Specify output transfer characteristics. 

 The accepted values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.709</font>
<dt><b>bt470m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470M</font>
<dt><b>bt470bg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470BG</font>
<dt><b>gamma22</b>
<dd> Constant gamma of 2.2
<dt><b>gamma28</b>
<dd> Constant gamma of 2.8
<dt><b>smpte170m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-170M, BT.601-6 625</font> or <font SIZE="-1">BT.601-6 525</font>
<dt><b>smpte240m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-240M</font>
<dt><b>srgb</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SRGB</font>
<dt><b>iec61966-2-1</b>
<dd> iec61966-2-1
<dt><b>iec61966-2-4</b>
<dd> iec61966-2-4
<dt><b>xvycc</b>
<dd> xvycc
<dt><b>bt2020-10</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.2020</font> for 10-bits content
<dt><b>bt2020-12</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.2020</font> for 12-bits content</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>primaries</b>
<dd> Specify output color primaries. 

 The accepted values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>bt709</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.709</font>
<dt><b>bt470m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470M</font>
<dt><b>bt470bg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.470BG</font> or <font SIZE="-1">BT.601-6 625</font>
<dt><b>smpte170m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-170M</font> or <font SIZE="-1">BT.601-6 525</font>
<dt><b>smpte240m</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-240M</font>
<dt><b>film</b>
<dd> film
<dt><b>smpte431</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-431</font>
<dt><b>smpte432</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SMPTE-432</font>
<dt><b>bt2020</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">BT.2020</font>
<dt><b>jedec-p22</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">JEDEC P22</font> phosphors</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>range</b>
<dd> Specify output color range. 

 The accepted values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>tv</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">TV</font> (restricted) range
<dt><b>mpeg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">MPEG</font> (restricted) range
<dt><b>pc</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">PC</font> (full) range
<dt><b>jpeg</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">JPEG</font> (full) range</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>format</b>
<dd> Specify output color format. 

 The accepted values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>yuv420p</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:2:0</font> planar 8-bits
<dt><b>yuv420p10</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:2:0</font> planar 10-bits
<dt><b>yuv420p12</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:2:0</font> planar 12-bits
<dt><b>yuv422p</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:2:2</font> planar 8-bits
<dt><b>yuv422p10</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:2:2</font> planar 10-bits
<dt><b>yuv422p12</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:2:2</font> planar 12-bits
<dt><b>yuv444p</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:4:4</font> planar 8-bits
<dt><b>yuv444p10</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:4:4</font> planar 10-bits
<dt><b>yuv444p12</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">YUV 4:4:4</font> planar 12-bits</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>fast</b>
<dd> Do a fast conversion, which skips gamma/primary correction. This will take significantly less <font SIZE="-1">CPU,</font> but will be mathematically incorrect. To get output compatible with that produced by the colormatrix filter, use fast=1.
<dt><b>dither</b>
<dd> Specify dithering mode. 

 The accepted values are:
