<h3>shear</h3>

 Apply shear transform to input video. 

 This filter supports the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>shx</b>
<dd> Shear factor in X-direction. Default value is 0. Allowed range is from -2 to 2.
<dt><b>shy</b>
<dd> Shear factor in Y-direction. Default value is 0. Allowed range is from -2 to 2.
<dt><b>fillcolor, c</b>
<dd> Set the color used to fill the output area not covered by the transformed video. For the general syntax of this option, check the <b>``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. If the special value ``none'' is selected then no background is printed (useful for example if the background is never shown). 

 Default value is ``black''.
<dt><b>interp</b>
<dd> Set interpolation type. Can be <tt>&quot;bilinear&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;nearest&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;bilinear&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>showinfo</h3>

 Show a line containing various information for each input video frame. The input video is not modified. 

 This filter supports the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>checksum</b>
<dd> Calculate checksums of each plane. By default enabled.</dl>
 

 The shown line contains a sequence of key/value pairs of the form <i>key</i>:<i>value</i>. 

 The following values are shown in the output:
<dl>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> The (sequential) number of the input frame, starting from 0.
<dt><b>pts</b>
<dd> The Presentation TimeStamp of the input frame, expressed as a number of time base units. The time base unit depends on the filter input pad.
<dt><b>pts_time</b>
<dd> The Presentation TimeStamp of the input frame, expressed as a number of seconds.
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd> The position of the frame in the input stream, or -1 if this information is unavailable and/or meaningless (for example in case of synthetic video).
<dt><b>fmt</b>
<dd> The pixel format name.
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd> The sample aspect ratio of the input frame, expressed in the form <i>num</i>/<i>den</i>.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> The size of the input frame. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>i</b>
<dd> The type of interlaced mode (``P'' for ``progressive'', ``T'' for top field first, ``B'' for bottom field first).
<dt><b>iskey</b>
<dd> This is 1 if the frame is a key frame, 0 otherwise.
<dt><b>type</b>
<dd> The picture type of the input frame (``I'' for an I-frame, ``P'' for a P-frame, ``B'' for a B-frame, or ``?'' for an unknown type). Also refer to the documentation of the <tt>&quot;AVPictureType&quot;</tt> enum and of the <tt>&quot;av_get_picture_type_char&quot;</tt> function defined in <i>libavutil/avutil.h</i>.
<dt><b>checksum</b>
<dd> The Adler-32 checksum (printed in hexadecimal) of all the planes of the input frame.
<dt><b>plane_checksum</b>
<dd> The Adler-32 checksum (printed in hexadecimal) of each plane of the input frame, expressed in the form &quot;[<i>c0</i> <i>c1</i> <i>c2</i> <i>c3</i>]&quot;.
<dt><b>mean</b>
<dd> The mean value of pixels in each plane of the input frame, expressed in the form &quot;[<i>mean0</i> <i>mean1</i> <i>mean2</i> <i>mean3</i>]&quot;.
<dt><b>stdev</b>
<dd> The standard deviation of pixel values in each plane of the input frame, expressed in the form &quot;[<i>stdev0</i> <i>stdev1</i> <i>stdev2</i> <i>stdev3</i>]&quot;.</dl>

<h3>showpalette</h3>

 Displays the 256 colors palette of each frame. This filter is only relevant for <i>pal8</i> pixel format frames. 

 It accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> Set the size of the box used to represent one palette color entry. Default is <tt>30</tt> (for a <tt>&quot;30x30&quot;</tt> pixel box).</dl>

<h3>shuffleframes</h3>

 Reorder and/or duplicate and/or drop video frames. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>mapping</b>
<dd> Set the destination indexes of input frames. This is space or '|' separated list of indexes that maps input frames to output frames. Number of indexes also sets maximal value that each index may have. '-1' index have special meaning and that is to drop frame.</dl>
 

 The first frame has the index 0. The default is to keep the input unchanged. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Swap second and third frame of every three frames of the input: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf &quot;shuffleframes=0 2 1&quot; OUTPUT
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Swap 10th and 1st frame of every ten frames of the input: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf &quot;shuffleframes=9 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 0&quot; OUTPUT
</pre></dl>

<h3>shufflepixels</h3>

 Reorder pixels in video frames. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>direction, d</b>
<dd> Set shuffle direction. Can be forward or inverse direction. Default direction is forward.
<dt><b>mode, m</b>
<dd> Set shuffle mode. Can be horizontal, vertical or block mode.
<dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>height, h</b>
<dd> Set shuffle block_size. In case of horizontal shuffle mode only width part of size is used, and in case of vertical shuffle mode only height part of size is used.
<dt><b>seed, s</b>
<dd> Set random seed used with shuffling pixels. Mainly useful to set to be able to reverse filtering process to get original input. For example, to reverse forward shuffle you need to use same parameters and exact same seed and to set direction to inverse.</dl>

<h3>shuffleplanes</h3>

 Reorder and/or duplicate video planes. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>map0</b>
<dd> The index of the input plane to be used as the first output plane.
<dt><b>map1</b>
<dd> The index of the input plane to be used as the second output plane.
<dt><b>map2</b>
<dd> The index of the input plane to be used as the third output plane.
<dt><b>map3</b>
<dd> The index of the input plane to be used as the fourth output plane.</dl>
 

 The first plane has the index 0. The default is to keep the input unchanged. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Swap the second and third planes of the input: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf shuffleplanes=0:2:1:3 OUTPUT
</pre></dl>

<h3>signalstats</h3>

 Evaluate various visual metrics that assist in determining issues associated with the digitization of analog video media. 

 By default the filter will log these metadata values:
<dl>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YMIN</b></font>
<dd> Display the minimal Y value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YLOW</b></font>
<dd> Display the Y value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YAVG</b></font>
<dd> Display the average Y value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YHIGH</b></font>
<dd> Display the Y value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YMAX</b></font>
<dd> Display the maximum Y value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UMIN</b></font>
<dd> Display the minimal U value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>ULOW</b></font>
<dd> Display the U value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UAVG</b></font>
<dd> Display the average U value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UHIGH</b></font>
<dd> Display the U value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UMAX</b></font>
<dd> Display the maximum U value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VMIN</b></font>
<dd> Display the minimal V value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VLOW</b></font>
<dd> Display the V value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VAVG</b></font>
<dd> Display the average V value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VHIGH</b></font>
<dd> Display the V value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VMAX</b></font>
<dd> Display the maximum V value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATMIN</b></font>
<dd> Display the minimal saturation value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATLOW</b></font>
<dd> Display the saturation value at the 10% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATAVG</b></font>
<dd> Display the average saturation value within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATHIGH</b></font>
<dd> Display the saturation value at the 90% percentile within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>SATMAX</b></font>
<dd> Display the maximum saturation value contained within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-~181.02].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>HUEMED</b></font>
<dd> Display the median value for hue within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-360].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>HUEAVG</b></font>
<dd> Display the average value for hue within the input frame. Expressed in range of [0-360].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YDIF</b></font>
<dd> Display the average of sample value difference between all values of the Y plane in the current frame and corresponding values of the previous input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UDIF</b></font>
<dd> Display the average of sample value difference between all values of the U plane in the current frame and corresponding values of the previous input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VDIF</b></font>
<dd> Display the average of sample value difference between all values of the V plane in the current frame and corresponding values of the previous input frame. Expressed in range of [0-255].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>YBITDEPTH</b></font>
<dd> Display bit depth of Y plane in current frame. Expressed in range of [0-16].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>UBITDEPTH</b></font>
<dd> Display bit depth of U plane in current frame. Expressed in range of [0-16].
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VBITDEPTH</b></font>
<dd> Display bit depth of V plane in current frame. Expressed in range of [0-16].</dl>
 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>stat</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>out</b>
<dd> <b>stat</b> specify an additional form of image analysis. <b>out</b> output video with the specified type of pixel highlighted. 

 Both options accept the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>tout</b>
<dd> Identify <i>temporal outliers</i> pixels. A <i>temporal outlier</i> is a pixel unlike the neighboring pixels of the same field. Examples of temporal outliers include the results of video dropouts, head clogs, or tape tracking issues.
<dt><b>vrep</b>
<dd> Identify <i>vertical line repetition</i>. Vertical line repetition includes similar rows of pixels within a frame. In born-digital video vertical line repetition is common, but this pattern is uncommon in video digitized from an analog source. When it occurs in video that results from the digitization of an analog source it can indicate concealment from a dropout compensator.
<dt><b>brng</b>
<dd> Identify pixels that fall outside of legal broadcast range.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>color, c</b>
<dd> Set the highlight color for the <b>out</b> option. The default color is yellow.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Output data of various video metrics: 

 <pre>
        ffprobe -f lavfi movie=example.mov,signalstats=&quot;stat=tout+vrep+brng&quot; -show_frames
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Output specific data about the minimum and maximum values of the Y plane per frame: 

 <pre>
        ffprobe -f lavfi movie=example.mov,signalstats -show_entries frame_tags=lavfi.signalstats.YMAX,lavfi.signalstats.YMIN
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Playback video while highlighting pixels that are outside of broadcast range in red. 

 <pre>
        ffplay example.mov -vf signalstats=&quot;out=brng:color=red&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Playback video with signalstats metadata drawn over the frame. 

 <pre>
        ffplay example.mov -vf signalstats=stat=brng+vrep+tout,drawtext=fontfile=FreeSerif.ttf:textfile=signalstat_drawtext.txt
</pre> 

 The contents of signalstat_drawtext.txt used in the command are: 

 
time % {pts : hms} Y(% {metadata : lavfi.signalstats.YMIN} - % {metadata : lavfi.signalstats.YMAX}) U(% {metadata : lavfi.signalstats.UMIN} - % {metadata : lavfi.signalstats.UMAX}) V(% {metadata : lavfi.signalstats.VMIN} - % {metadata : lavfi.signalstats.VMAX}) saturation maximum : %
{
metadata:
    lavfi.signalstats.SATMAX
}
</dl>

<h3>signature</h3>

 Calculates the <font SIZE="-1">MPEG-7</font> Video Signature. The filter can handle more than one input. In this case the matching between the inputs can be calculated additionally. The filter always passes through the first input. The signature of each stream can be written into a file. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>detectmode</b>
<dd> Enable or disable the matching process. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>off</b>
<dd> Disable the calculation of a matching (default).
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd> Calculate the matching for the whole video and output whether the whole video matches or only parts.
<dt><b>fast</b>
<dd> Calculate only until a matching is found or the video ends. Should be faster in some cases.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>nb_inputs</b>
<dd> Set the number of inputs. The option value must be a non negative integer. Default value is 1.
<dt><b>filename</b>
<dd> Set the path to which the output is written. If there is more than one input, the path must be a prototype, i.e. must contain <tt>%d</tt> or <tt>%0nd</tt> (where n is a positive integer), that will be replaced with the input number. If no filename is specified, no output will be written. This is the default.
<dt><b>format</b>
<dd> Choose the output format. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>binary</b>
<dd> Use the specified binary representation (default).
<dt><b>xml</b>
<dd> Use the specified xml representation.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>th_d</b>
<dd> Set threshold to detect one word as similar. The option value must be an integer greater than zero. The default value is 9000.
<dt><b>th_dc</b>
<dd> Set threshold to detect all words as similar. The option value must be an integer greater than zero. The default value is 60000.
<dt><b>th_xh</b>
<dd> Set threshold to detect frames as similar. The option value must be an integer greater than zero. The default value is 116.
<dt><b>th_di</b>
<dd> Set the minimum length of a sequence in frames to recognize it as matching sequence. The option value must be a non negative integer value. The default value is 0.
<dt><b>th_it</b>
<dd> Set the minimum relation, that matching frames to all frames must have. The option value must be a double value between 0 and 1. The default value is 0.5.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> To calculate the signature of an input video and store it in signature.bin: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.mkv -vf signature=filename=signature.bin -map 0:v -f null -
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> To detect whether two videos match and store the signatures in <font SIZE="-1">XML</font> format in signature0.xml and signature1.xml: 

 
ffmpeg - i input1.mkv - i input2.mkv - filter_complex "[0:v][1:v] signature=nb_inputs=2:detectmode=full:format=xml:filename=signature%d.xml" - map : v - f null -
</dl>

<h3>smartblur</h3>

 Blur the input video without impacting the outlines. 

 It accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>luma_radius, lr</b>
<dd> Set the luma radius. The option value must be a float number in the range [0.1,5.0] that specifies the variance of the gaussian filter used to blur the image (slower if larger). Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>luma_strength, ls</b>
<dd> Set the luma strength. The option value must be a float number in the range [-1.0,1.0] that configures the blurring. A value included in [0.0,1.0] will blur the image whereas a value included in [-1.0,0.0] will sharpen the image. Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>luma_threshold, lt</b>
<dd> Set the luma threshold used as a coefficient to determine whether a pixel should be blurred or not. The option value must be an integer in the range [-30,30]. A value of 0 will filter all the image, a value included in [0,30] will filter flat areas and a value included in [-30,0] will filter edges. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>chroma_radius, cr</b>
<dd> Set the chroma radius. The option value must be a float number in the range [0.1,5.0] that specifies the variance of the gaussian filter used to blur the image (slower if larger). Default value is <b>luma_radius</b>.
<dt><b>chroma_strength, cs</b>
<dd> Set the chroma strength. The option value must be a float number in the range [-1.0,1.0] that configures the blurring. A value included in [0.0,1.0] will blur the image whereas a value included in [-1.0,0.0] will sharpen the image. Default value is <b>luma_strength</b>.
<dt><b>chroma_threshold, ct</b>
<dd> Set the chroma threshold used as a coefficient to determine whether a pixel should be blurred or not. The option value must be an integer in the range [-30,30]. A value of 0 will filter all the image, a value included in [0,30] will filter flat areas and a value included in [-30,0] will filter edges. Default value is <b>luma_threshold</b>.</dl>
 

 If a chroma option is not explicitly set, the corresponding luma value is set.

<h3>sobel</h3>

 Apply sobel operator to input video stream. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Set value which will be multiplied with filtered result.
<dt><b>delta</b>
<dd> Set value which will be added to filtered result.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>spp</h3>

 Apply a simple postprocessing filter that compresses and decompresses the image at several (or - in the case of <b>quality</b> level <tt>6</tt> - all) shifts and average the results. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>quality</b>
<dd> Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts an integer in the range 0-6. If set to <tt>0</tt>, the filter will have no effect. A value of <tt>6</tt> means the higher quality. For each increment of that value the speed drops by a factor of approximately 2. Default value is <tt>3</tt>.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd> Force a constant quantization parameter. If not set, the filter will use the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the video stream (if available).
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set thresholding mode. Available modes are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>hard</b>
<dd> Set hard thresholding (default).
<dt><b>soft</b>
<dd> Set soft thresholding (better de-ringing effect, but likely blurrier).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>use_bframe_qp</b>
<dd> Enable the use of the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the B-Frames if set to <tt>1</tt>. Using this option may cause flicker since the B-Frames have often larger <font SIZE="-1">QP.</font> Default is <tt>0</tt> (not enabled).</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl>
<dt><b>quality, level</b>
<dd> Set quality level. The value <tt>&quot;max&quot;</tt> can be used to set the maximum level, currently <tt>6</tt>.</dl>

<h3>sr</h3>

 Scale the input by applying one of the super-resolution methods based on convolutional neural networks. Supported models:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Super-Resolution Convolutional Neural Network model (<font SIZE="-1">SRCNN</font>). See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00092">https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00092</a></b>&gt;.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Efficient Sub-Pixel Convolutional Neural Network model (<font SIZE="-1">ESPCN</font>). See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05158">https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.05158</a></b>&gt;.</dl>
 

 Training scripts as well as scripts for model file (.pb) saving can be found at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/XueweiMeng/sr/tree/sr_dnn_native">https://github.com/XueweiMeng/sr/tree/sr_dnn_native</a></b>&gt;. Original repository is at &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/HighVoltageRocknRoll/sr.git">https://github.com/HighVoltageRocknRoll/sr.git</a></b>&gt;. 

 Native model files (.model) can be generated from TensorFlow model files (.pb) by using tools/python/convert.py 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>dnn_backend</b>
<dd> Specify which <font SIZE="-1">DNN</font> backend to use for model loading and execution. This option accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>native</b>
<dd> Native implementation of <font SIZE="-1">DNN</font> loading and execution.
<dt><b>tensorflow</b>
<dd> TensorFlow backend. To enable this backend you need to install the TensorFlow for C library (see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://www.tensorflow.org/install/install_c">https://www.tensorflow.org/install/install_c</a></b>&gt;) and configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libtensorflow&quot;</tt></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>native</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>model</b>
<dd> Set path to model file specifying network architecture and its parameters. Note that different backends use different file formats. TensorFlow backend can load files for both formats, while native backend can load files for only its format.
<dt><b>scale_factor</b>
<dd> Set scale factor for <font SIZE="-1">SRCNN</font> model. Allowed values are <tt>2</tt>, <tt>3</tt> and <tt>4</tt>. Default value is <tt>2</tt>. Scale factor is necessary for <font SIZE="-1">SRCNN</font> model, because it accepts input upscaled using bicubic upscaling with proper scale factor.</dl>
 

 This feature can also be finished with <b>dnn_processing</b> filter.

<h3>ssim</h3>

 Obtain the <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> (Structural SImilarity Metric) between two input videos. 

 This filter takes in input two input videos, the first input is considered the ``main'' source and is passed unchanged to the output. The second input is used as a ``reference'' video for computing the <font SIZE="-1">SSIM.</font> 

 Both video inputs must have the same resolution and pixel format for this filter to work correctly. Also it assumes that both inputs have the same number of frames, which are compared one by one. 

 The filter stores the calculated <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of each frame. 

 The description of the accepted parameters follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>stats_file, f</b>
<dd> If specified the filter will use the named file to save the <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of each individual frame. When filename equals ``-'' the data is sent to standard output.</dl>
 

 The file printed if <i>stats_file</i> is selected, contains a sequence of key/value pairs of the form <i>key</i>:<i>value</i> for each compared couple of frames. 

 A description of each shown parameter follows:
<dl>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> sequential number of the input frame, starting from 1
<dt><b>Y, U, V, R, G, B</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of the compared frames for the component specified by the suffix.
<dt><b>All</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of the compared frames for the whole frame.
<dt><b>dB</b>
<dd> Same as above but in dB representation.</dl>
 

 This filter also supports the <b>framesync</b> options. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> For example: 

 
movie = ref_movie.mpg, setpts = PTS - STARTPTS[main];
[main][ref] ssim = "stats_file=stats.log"[out]
 

 On this example the input file being processed is compared with the reference file <i>ref_movie.mpg</i>. The <font SIZE="-1">SSIM</font> of each individual frame is stored in <i>stats.log</i>.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Another example with both psnr and ssim at same time: 

 
ffmpeg - i main.mpg - i ref.mpg - lavfi "ssim;[0:v][1:v]psnr" - f null -

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Another example with different containers: 

 
ffmpeg - i main.mpg - i ref.mkv - lavfi "[0:v]settb=AVTB,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[main];[1:v]settb=AVTB,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS[ref];[main][ref]ssim" - f null -
</dl>

<h3>stereo3d</h3>

 Convert between different stereoscopic image formats. 

 The filters accept the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>in</b>
<dd> Set stereoscopic image format of input. 

 Available values for input image formats are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>sbsl</b>
<dd> side by side parallel (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbsr</b>
<dd> side by side crosseye (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2l</b>
<dd> side by side parallel with half width resolution (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2r</b>
<dd> side by side crosseye with half width resolution (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>abl</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tbl</b>
<dd> above-below (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>abr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tbr</b>
<dd> above-below (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>ab2l</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tb2l</b>
<dd> above-below with half height resolution (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>ab2r</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tb2r</b>
<dd> above-below with half height resolution (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>al</b>
<dd> alternating frames (left eye first, right eye second)
<dt><b>ar</b>
<dd> alternating frames (right eye first, left eye second)
<dt><b>irl</b>
<dd> interleaved rows (left eye has top row, right eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>irr</b>
<dd> interleaved rows (right eye has top row, left eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>icl</b>
<dd> interleaved columns, left eye first
<dt><b>icr</b>
<dd> interleaved columns, right eye first 

 Default value is <b>sbsl</b>.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>out</b>
<dd> Set stereoscopic image format of output.
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>sbsl</b>
<dd> side by side parallel (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbsr</b>
<dd> side by side crosseye (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2l</b>
<dd> side by side parallel with half width resolution (left eye left, right eye right)
<dt><b>sbs2r</b>
<dd> side by side crosseye with half width resolution (right eye left, left eye right)
<dt><b>abl</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tbl</b>
<dd> above-below (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>abr</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tbr</b>
<dd> above-below (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>ab2l</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tb2l</b>
<dd> above-below with half height resolution (left eye above, right eye below)
<dt><b>ab2r</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tb2r</b>
<dd> above-below with half height resolution (right eye above, left eye below)
<dt><b>al</b>
<dd> alternating frames (left eye first, right eye second)
<dt><b>ar</b>
<dd> alternating frames (right eye first, left eye second)
<dt><b>irl</b>
<dd> interleaved rows (left eye has top row, right eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>irr</b>
<dd> interleaved rows (right eye has top row, left eye starts on next row)
<dt><b>arbg</b>
<dd> anaglyph red/blue gray (red filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>argg</b>
<dd> anaglyph red/green gray (red filter on left eye, green filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arcg</b>
<dd> anaglyph red/cyan gray (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arch</b>
<dd> anaglyph red/cyan half colored (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arcc</b>
<dd> anaglyph red/cyan color (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>arcd</b>
<dd> anaglyph red/cyan color optimized with the least squares projection of dubois (red filter on left eye, cyan filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmg</b>
<dd> anaglyph green/magenta gray (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmh</b>
<dd> anaglyph green/magenta half colored (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmc</b>
<dd> anaglyph green/magenta colored (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>agmd</b>
<dd> anaglyph green/magenta color optimized with the least squares projection of dubois (green filter on left eye, magenta filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybg</b>
<dd> anaglyph yellow/blue gray (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybh</b>
<dd> anaglyph yellow/blue half colored (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybc</b>
<dd> anaglyph yellow/blue colored (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>aybd</b>
<dd> anaglyph yellow/blue color optimized with the least squares projection of dubois (yellow filter on left eye, blue filter on right eye)
<dt><b>ml</b>
<dd> mono output (left eye only)
<dt><b>mr</b>
<dd> mono output (right eye only)
<dt><b>chl</b>
<dd> checkerboard, left eye first
<dt><b>chr</b>
<dd> checkerboard, right eye first
<dt><b>icl</b>
<dd> interleaved columns, left eye first
<dt><b>icr</b>
<dd> interleaved columns, right eye first
<dt><b>hdmi</b>
<dd> <font SIZE="-1">HDMI</font> frame pack</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>arcd</b>.</dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Convert input video from side by side parallel to anaglyph yellow/blue dubois: 

 <pre>
        stereo3d=sbsl:aybd
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Convert input video from above below (left eye above, right eye below) to side by side crosseye. 

 <pre>
        stereo3d=abl:sbsr
</pre></dl>

<h3>streamselect, astreamselect</h3>

 Select video or audio streams. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>inputs</b>
<dd> Set number of inputs. Default is 2.
<dt><b>map</b>
<dd> Set input indexes to remap to outputs.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 The <tt>&quot;streamselect&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;astreamselect&quot;</tt> filter supports the following commands:
<dl>
<dt><b>map</b>
<dd> Set input indexes to remap to outputs.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Select first 5 seconds 1st stream and rest of time 2nd stream: 

 <pre>
        sendcmd='5.0 streamselect map 1',streamselect=inputs=2:map=0
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but for audio: 

 <pre>
        asendcmd='5.0 astreamselect map 1',astreamselect=inputs=2:map=0
</pre></dl>

<h3>subtitles</h3>

 Draw subtitles on top of input video using the libass library. 

 To enable compilation of this filter you need to configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libass&quot;</tt>. This filter also requires a build with libavcodec and libavformat to convert the passed subtitles file to <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> (Advanced Substation Alpha) subtitles format. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>filename, f</b>
<dd> Set the filename of the subtitle file to read. It must be specified.
<dt><b>original_size</b>
<dd> Specify the size of the original video, the video for which the <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> file was composed. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Due to a misdesign in <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> aspect ratio arithmetic, this is necessary to correctly scale the fonts if the aspect ratio has been changed.
<dt><b>fontsdir</b>
<dd> Set a directory path containing fonts that can be used by the filter. These fonts will be used in addition to whatever the font provider uses.
<dt><b>alpha</b>
<dd> Process alpha channel, by default alpha channel is untouched.
<dt><b>charenc</b>
<dd> Set subtitles input character encoding. <tt>&quot;subtitles&quot;</tt> filter only. Only useful if not <font SIZE="-1">UTF-8.</font>
<dt><b>stream_index, si</b>
<dd> Set subtitles stream index. <tt>&quot;subtitles&quot;</tt> filter only.
<dt><b>force_style</b>
<dd> Override default style or script info parameters of the subtitles. It accepts a string containing <font SIZE="-1">ASS</font> style format <tt>&quot;KEY=VALUE&quot;</tt> couples separated by ``,''.</dl>
 

 If the first key is not specified, it is assumed that the first value specifies the <b>filename</b>. 

 For example, to render the file <i>sub.srt</i> on top of the input video, use the command: 

 <pre>
        subtitles=sub.srt
</pre> 

 which is equivalent to: 

 <pre>
        subtitles=filename=sub.srt
</pre> 

 To render the default subtitles stream from file <i>video.mkv</i>, use: 

 <pre>
        subtitles=video.mkv
</pre> 

 To render the second subtitles stream from that file, use: 

 <pre>
        subtitles=video.mkv:si=1
</pre> 

 To make the subtitles stream from <i>sub.srt</i> appear in 80% transparent blue <tt>&quot;DejaVu Serif&quot;</tt>, use: 

 <pre>
        subtitles=sub.srt:force_style='Fontname=DejaVu Serif,PrimaryColour=&amp;HCCFF0000'
</pre>

<h3>super2xsai</h3>

 Scale the input by 2x and smooth using the Super2xSaI (Scale and Interpolate) pixel art scaling algorithm. 

 Useful for enlarging pixel art images without reducing sharpness.

<h3>swaprect</h3>

 Swap two rectangular objects in video. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd> Set object width.
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> Set object height.
<dt><b>x1</b>
<dd> Set 1st rect x coordinate.
<dt><b>y1</b>
<dd> Set 1st rect y coordinate.
<dt><b>x2</b>
<dd> Set 2nd rect x coordinate.
<dt><b>y2</b>
<dd> Set 2nd rect y coordinate. 

 All expressions are evaluated once for each frame.</dl>
 

 The all options are expressions containing the following constants:
<dl>
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> The input width and height.
<dt><b>a</b>
<dd> same as <i>w</i> / <i>h</i>
<dt><b>sar</b>
<dd> input sample aspect ratio
<dt><b>dar</b>
<dd> input display aspect ratio, it is the same as (<i>w</i> / <i>h</i>) * <i>sar</i>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> The number of the input frame, starting from 0.
<dt><b>t</b>
<dd> The timestamp expressed in seconds. It's <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if the input timestamp is unknown.
<dt><b>pos</b>
<dd> the position in the file of the input frame, <font SIZE="-1">NAN</font> if unknown</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the all above options as <b>commands</b>.

<h3>swapuv</h3>

 Swap U &amp; V plane.

<h3>tblend</h3>

 Blend successive video frames. 

 See <b>blend</b>

<h3>telecine</h3>

 Apply telecine process to the video. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>first_field</b>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>top, t</b>
<dd> top field first
<dt><b>bottom, b</b>
<dd> bottom field first The default value is <tt>&quot;top&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>pattern</b>
<dd> A string of numbers representing the pulldown pattern you wish to apply. The default value is <tt>23</tt>.</dl>
 

 <pre>
        Some typical patterns:
        
        NTSC output (30i):
        27.5p: 32222
        24p: 23 (classic)
        24p: 2332 (preferred)
        20p: 33
        18p: 334
        16p: 3444
        
        PAL output (25i):
        27.5p: 12222
        24p: 222222222223 (&quot;Euro pulldown&quot;)
        16.67p: 33
        16p: 33333334
</pre>

<h3>thistogram</h3>

 Compute and draw a color distribution histogram for the input video across time. 

 Unlike <b>histogram</b> video filter which only shows histogram of single input frame at certain time, this filter shows also past histograms of number of frames defined by <tt>&quot;width&quot;</tt> option. 

 The computed histogram is a representation of the color component distribution in an image. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>width, w</b>
<dd> Set width of single color component output. Default value is <tt>0</tt>. Value of <tt>0</tt> means width will be picked from input video. This also set number of passed histograms to keep. Allowed range is [0, 8192].
<dt><b>display_mode, d</b>
<dd> Set display mode. It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>stack</b>
<dd> Per color component graphs are placed below each other.
<dt><b>parade</b>
<dd> Per color component graphs are placed side by side.
<dt><b>overlay</b>
<dd> Presents information identical to that in the <tt>&quot;parade&quot;</tt>, except that the graphs representing color components are superimposed directly over one another.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;stack&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>levels_mode, m</b>
<dd> Set mode. Can be either <tt>&quot;linear&quot;</tt>, or <tt>&quot;logarithmic&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;linear&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>components, c</b>
<dd> Set what color components to display. Default is <tt>7</tt>.
<dt><b>bgopacity, b</b>
<dd> Set background opacity. Default is <tt>0.9</tt>.
<dt><b>envelope, e</b>
<dd> Show envelope. Default is disabled.
<dt><b>ecolor, ec</b>
<dd> Set envelope color. Default is <tt>&quot;gold&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>slide</b>
<dd> Set slide mode. 

 Available values for slide is:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>frame</b>
<dd> Draw new frame when right border is reached.
<dt><b>replace</b>
<dd> Replace old columns with new ones.
<dt><b>scroll</b>
<dd> Scroll from right to left.
<dt><b>rscroll</b>
<dd> Scroll from left to right.
<dt><b>picture</b>
<dd> Draw single picture.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;replace&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>threshold</h3>

 Apply threshold effect to video stream. 

 This filter needs four video streams to perform thresholding. First stream is stream we are filtering. Second stream is holding threshold values, third stream is holding min values, and last, fourth stream is holding max values. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed.</dl>
 

 For example if first stream pixel's component value is less then threshold value of pixel component from 2nd threshold stream, third stream value will picked, otherwise fourth stream pixel component value will be picked. 

 Using color source filter one can perform various types of thresholding: 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Binary threshold, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=black -f lavfi -i color=white -lavfi threshold output.avi
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Inverted binary threshold, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=white -f lavfi -i color=black -lavfi threshold output.avi
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Truncate binary threshold, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -lavfi threshold output.avi
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Threshold to zero, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -f lavfi -i color=white -i 320x240.avi -lavfi threshold output.avi
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Inverted threshold to zero, using gray color as threshold: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=gray -i 320x240.avi -f lavfi -i color=white -lavfi threshold output.avi
</pre></dl>

<h3>thumbnail</h3>

 Select the most representative frame in a given sequence of consecutive frames. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> Set the frames batch size to analyze; in a set of <i>n</i> frames, the filter will pick one of them, and then handle the next batch of <i>n</i> frames until the end. Default is <tt>100</tt>.</dl>
 

 Since the filter keeps track of the whole frames sequence, a bigger <i>n</i> value will result in a higher memory usage, so a high value is not recommended. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Extract one picture each 50 frames: 

 <pre>
        thumbnail=50
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Complete example of a thumbnail creation with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i in.avi -vf thumbnail,scale=300:200 -frames:v 1 out.png
</pre></dl>

<h3>tile</h3>

 Tile several successive frames together. 

 The <b>untile</b> filter can do the reverse. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>layout</b>
<dd> Set the grid size (i.e. the number of lines and columns). For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.
<dt><b>nb_frames</b>
<dd> Set the maximum number of frames to render in the given area. It must be less than or equal to <i>w</i>x<i>h</i>. The default value is <tt>0</tt>, meaning all the area will be used.
<dt><b>margin</b>
<dd> Set the outer border margin in pixels.
<dt><b>padding</b>
<dd> Set the inner border thickness (i.e. the number of pixels between frames). For more advanced padding options (such as having different values for the edges), refer to the pad video filter.
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> Specify the color of the unused area. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. The default value of <i>color</i> is ``black''.
<dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd> Set the number of frames to overlap when tiling several successive frames together. The value must be between <tt>0</tt> and <i>nb_frames - 1</i>.
<dt><b>init_padding</b>
<dd> Set the number of frames to initially be empty before displaying first output frame. This controls how soon will one get first output frame. The value must be between <tt>0</tt> and <i>nb_frames - 1</i>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Produce 8x8 <font SIZE="-1">PNG</font> tiles of all keyframes (<b>-skip_frame nokey</b>) in a movie: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -skip_frame nokey -i file.avi -vf 'scale=128:72,tile=8x8' -an -vsync 0 keyframes%03d.png
</pre> 

 The <b>-vsync 0</b> is necessary to prevent <b>ffmpeg</b> from duplicating each output frame to accommodate the originally detected frame rate.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Display <tt>5</tt> pictures in an area of <tt>&quot;3x2&quot;</tt> frames, with <tt>7</tt> pixels between them, and <tt>2</tt> pixels of initial margin, using mixed flat and named options: 

 <pre>
        tile=3x2:nb_frames=5:padding=7:margin=2
</pre></dl>

<h3>tinterlace</h3>

 Perform various types of temporal field interlacing. 

 Frames are counted starting from 1, so the first input frame is considered odd. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Specify the mode of the interlacing. This option can also be specified as a value alone. See below for a list of values for this option. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>merge, 0</b>
<dd> Move odd frames into the upper field, even into the lower field, generating a double height frame at half frame rate. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        
        Output:
        11111                           33333
        22222                           44444
        11111                           33333
        22222                           44444
        11111                           33333
        22222                           44444
        11111                           33333
        22222                           44444
</pre>
<dt><b>drop_even, 1</b>
<dd> Only output odd frames, even frames are dropped, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        
        Output:
        11111                           33333
        11111                           33333
        11111                           33333
        11111                           33333
</pre>
<dt><b>drop_odd, 2</b>
<dd> Only output even frames, odd frames are dropped, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        
        Output:
                        22222                           44444
                        22222                           44444
                        22222                           44444
                        22222                           44444
</pre>
<dt><b>pad, 3</b>
<dd> Expand each frame to full height, but pad alternate lines with black, generating a frame with double height at the same input frame rate. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        
        Output:
        11111           .....           33333           .....
        .....           22222           .....           44444
        11111           .....           33333           .....
        .....           22222           .....           44444
        11111           .....           33333           .....
        .....           22222           .....           44444
        11111           .....           33333           .....
        .....           22222           .....           44444
</pre>
<dt><b>interleave_top, 4</b>
<dd> Interleave the upper field from odd frames with the lower field from even frames, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
        11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
        11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
        11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
        
        Output:
        11111                           33333
        22222                           44444
        11111                           33333
        22222                           44444
</pre>
<dt><b>interleave_bottom, 5</b>
<dd> Interleave the lower field from odd frames with the upper field from even frames, generating a frame with unchanged height at half frame rate. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
        11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
        11111           22222&lt;-         33333           44444&lt;-
        11111&lt;-         22222           33333&lt;-         44444
        
        Output:
        22222                           44444
        11111                           33333
        22222                           44444
        11111                           33333
</pre>
<dt><b>interlacex2, 6</b>
<dd> Double frame rate with unchanged height. Frames are inserted each containing the second temporal field from the previous input frame and the first temporal field from the next input frame. This mode relies on the top_field_first flag. Useful for interlaced video displays with no field synchronisation. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111           22222           33333           44444
         11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
         11111           22222           33333           44444
        
        Output:
        11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444   44444
         11111   11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444
        11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444   44444
         11111   11111   22222   22222   33333   33333   44444
</pre>
<dt><b>mergex2, 7</b>
<dd> Move odd frames into the upper field, even into the lower field, generating a double height frame at same frame rate. 

 <pre>
         ------&gt; time
        Input:
        Frame 1         Frame 2         Frame 3         Frame 4
        
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        11111           22222           33333           44444
        
        Output:
        11111           33333           33333           55555
        22222           22222           44444           44444
        11111           33333           33333           55555
        22222           22222           44444           44444
        11111           33333           33333           55555
        22222           22222           44444           44444
        11111           33333           33333           55555
        22222           22222           44444           44444
</pre></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Numeric values are deprecated but are accepted for backward compatibility reasons. 

 Default mode is <tt>&quot;merge&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>flags</b>
<dd> Specify flags influencing the filter process. 

 Available value for <i>flags</i> is:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>low_pass_filter, vlpf</b>
<dd> Enable linear vertical low-pass filtering in the filter. Vertical low-pass filtering is required when creating an interlaced destination from a progressive source which contains high-frequency vertical detail. Filtering will reduce interlace 'twitter' and Moire patterning.
<dt><b>complex_filter, cvlpf</b>
<dd> Enable complex vertical low-pass filtering. This will slightly less reduce interlace 'twitter' and Moire patterning but better retain detail and subjective sharpness impression.
<dt><b>bypass_il</b>
<dd> Bypass already interlaced frames, only adjust the frame rate.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Vertical low-pass filtering and bypassing already interlaced frames can only be enabled for <b>mode</b> <i>interleave_top</i> and <i>interleave_bottom</i>.</dl>
</dl>

<h3>tmedian</h3>

 Pick median pixels from several successive input video frames. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>radius</b>
<dd> Set radius of median filter. Default is 1. Allowed range is from 1 to 127.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set which planes to filter. Default value is <tt>15</tt>, by which all planes are processed.
<dt><b>percentile</b>
<dd> Set median percentile. Default value is <tt>0.5</tt>. Default value of <tt>0.5</tt> will pick always median values, while <tt>0</tt> will pick minimum values, and <tt>1</tt> maximum values.</dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports all above options as <b>commands</b>, excluding option <tt>&quot;radius&quot;</tt>.

<h3>tmidequalizer</h3>

 Apply Temporal Midway Video Equalization effect. 

 Midway Video Equalization adjusts a sequence of video frames to have the same histograms, while maintaining their dynamics as much as possible. It's useful for e.g. matching exposures from a video frames sequence. 

 This filter accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>radius</b>
<dd> Set filtering radius. Default is <tt>5</tt>. Allowed range is from 1 to 127.
<dt><b>sigma</b>
<dd> Set filtering sigma. Default is <tt>0.5</tt>. This controls strength of filtering. Setting this option to 0 effectively does nothing.
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set which planes to process. Default is <tt>15</tt>, which is all available planes.</dl>

<h3>tmix</h3>

 Mix successive video frames. 

 A description of the accepted options follows.
<dl>
<dt><b>frames</b>
<dd> The number of successive frames to mix. If unspecified, it defaults to 3.
<dt><b>weights</b>
<dd> Specify weight of each input video frame. Each weight is separated by space. If number of weights is smaller than number of <i>frames</i> last specified weight will be used for all remaining unset weights.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Specify scale, if it is set it will be multiplied with sum of each weight multiplied with pixel values to give final destination pixel value. By default <i>scale</i> is auto scaled to sum of weights.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Average 7 successive frames: 

 <pre>
        tmix=frames=7:weights=&quot;1 1 1 1 1 1 1&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply simple temporal convolution: 

 <pre>
        tmix=frames=3:weights=&quot;-1 3 -1&quot;
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Similar as above but only showing temporal differences: 

 <pre>
        tmix=frames=3:weights=&quot;-1 2 -1&quot;:scale=1
</pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 This filter supports the following commands:
<dl>
<dt><b>weights</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Syntax is same as option with same name.</dl>

<h3>tonemap</h3>

 Tone map colors from different dynamic ranges. 

 This filter expects data in single precision floating point, as it needs to operate on (and can output) out-of-range values. Another filter, such as <b>zscale</b>, is needed to convert the resulting frame to a usable format. 

 The tonemapping algorithms implemented only work on linear light, so input data should be linearized beforehand (and possibly correctly tagged). 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf zscale=transfer=linear,tonemap=clip,zscale=transfer=bt709,format=yuv420p OUTPUT
</pre> 

 <i>Options</i> 

 The filter accepts the following options.
<dl>
<dt><b>tonemap</b>
<dd> Set the tone map algorithm to use. 

 Possible values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><i>none</i>
<dd> Do not apply any tone map, only desaturate overbright pixels.
<dt><i>clip</i>
<dd> Hard-clip any out-of-range values. Use it for perfect color accuracy for in-range values, while distorting out-of-range values.
<dt><i>linear</i>
<dd> Stretch the entire reference gamut to a linear multiple of the display.
<dt><i>gamma</i>
<dd> Fit a logarithmic transfer between the tone curves.
<dt><i>reinhard</i>
<dd> Preserve overall image brightness with a simple curve, using nonlinear contrast, which results in flattening details and degrading color accuracy.
<dt><i>hable</i>
<dd> Preserve both dark and bright details better than <i>reinhard</i>, at the cost of slightly darkening everything. Use it when detail preservation is more important than color and brightness accuracy.
<dt><i>mobius</i>
<dd> Smoothly map out-of-range values, while retaining contrast and colors for in-range material as much as possible. Use it when color accuracy is more important than detail preservation.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is none.</dl>

<dt><b>param</b>
<dd> Tune the tone mapping algorithm. 

 This affects the following algorithms:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><i>none</i>
<dd> Ignored.
<dt><i>linear</i>
<dd> Specifies the scale factor to use while stretching. Default to 1.0.
<dt><i>gamma</i>
<dd> Specifies the exponent of the function. Default to 1.8.
<dt><i>clip</i>
<dd> Specify an extra linear coefficient to multiply into the signal before clipping. Default to 1.0.
<dt><i>reinhard</i>
<dd> Specify the local contrast coefficient at the display peak. Default to 0.5, which means that in-gamut values will be about half as bright as when clipping.
<dt><i>hable</i>
<dd> Ignored.
<dt><i>mobius</i>
<dd> Specify the transition point from linear to mobius transform. Every value below this point is guaranteed to be mapped 1:1. The higher the value, the more accurate the result will be, at the cost of losing bright details. Default to 0.3, which due to the steep initial slope still preserves in-range colors fairly accurately.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>desat</b>
<dd> Apply desaturation for highlights that exceed this level of brightness. The higher the parameter, the more color information will be preserved. This setting helps prevent unnaturally blown-out colors for super-highlights, by (smoothly) turning into white instead. This makes images feel more natural, at the cost of reducing information about out-of-range colors. 

 The default of 2.0 is somewhat conservative and will mostly just apply to skies or directly sunlit surfaces. A setting of 0.0 disables this option. 

 This option works only if the input frame has a supported color tag.
<dt><b>peak</b>
<dd> Override signal/nominal/reference peak with this value. Useful when the embedded peak information in display metadata is not reliable or when tone mapping from a lower range to a higher range.</dl>

<h3>tpad</h3>

 Temporarily pad video frames. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>start</b>
<dd> Specify number of delay frames before input video stream. Default is 0.
<dt><b>stop</b>
<dd> Specify number of padding frames after input video stream. Set to -1 to pad indefinitely. Default is 0.
<dt><b>start_mode</b>
<dd> Set kind of frames added to beginning of stream. Can be either <i>add</i> or <i>clone</i>. With <i>add</i> frames of solid-color are added. With <i>clone</i> frames are clones of first frame. Default is <i>add</i>.
<dt><b>stop_mode</b>
<dd> Set kind of frames added to end of stream. Can be either <i>add</i> or <i>clone</i>. With <i>add</i> frames of solid-color are added. With <i>clone</i> frames are clones of last frame. Default is <i>add</i>.
<dt><b>start_duration, stop_duration</b>
<dd> Specify the duration of the start/stop delay. See <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. These options override <i>start</i> and <i>stop</i>. Default is 0.
<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> Specify the color of the padded area. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Color'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. 

 The default value of <i>color</i> is ``black''.</dl>

<h3>transpose</h3>

 Transpose rows with columns in the input video and optionally flip it. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>dir</b>
<dd> Specify the transposition direction. 

 Can assume the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0, 4, cclock_flip</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise and vertically flip (default), that is: 

 <pre>
        L.R     L.l
        . . -&gt;  . .
        l.r     R.r
</pre>
<dt><b>1, 5, clock</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise, that is: 

 <pre>
        L.R     l.L
        . . -&gt;  . .
        l.r     r.R
</pre>
<dt><b>2, 6, cclock</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise, that is: 

 <pre>
        L.R     R.r
        . . -&gt;  . .
        l.r     L.l
</pre>
<dt><b>3, 7, clock_flip</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and vertically flip, that is: 

 <pre>
        L.R     r.R
        . . -&gt;  . .
        l.r     l.L
</pre></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 For values between 4-7, the transposition is only done if the input video geometry is portrait and not landscape. These values are deprecated, the <tt>&quot;passthrough&quot;</tt> option should be used instead. 

 Numerical values are deprecated, and should be dropped in favor of symbolic constants.</dl>

<dt><b>passthrough</b>
<dd> Do not apply the transposition if the input geometry matches the one specified by the specified value. It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Always apply transposition.
<dt><b>portrait</b>
<dd> Preserve portrait geometry (when <i>height</i> &gt;= <i>width</i>).
<dt><b>landscape</b>
<dd> Preserve landscape geometry (when <i>width</i> &gt;= <i>height</i>).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;none&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>
 

 For example to rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and preserve portrait layout: 

 <pre>
        transpose=dir=1:passthrough=portrait
</pre> 

 The command above can also be specified as: 

 <pre>
        transpose=1:portrait
</pre>

<h3>transpose_npp</h3>

 Transpose rows with columns in the input video and optionally flip it. For more in depth examples see the <b>transpose</b> video filter, which shares mostly the same options. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>dir</b>
<dd> Specify the transposition direction. 

 Can assume the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>cclock_flip</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise and vertically flip. (default)
<dt><b>clock</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise.
<dt><b>cclock</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees counterclockwise.
<dt><b>clock_flip</b>
<dd> Rotate by 90 degrees clockwise and vertically flip.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>passthrough</b>
<dd> Do not apply the transposition if the input geometry matches the one specified by the specified value. It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>none</b>
<dd> Always apply transposition. (default)
<dt><b>portrait</b>
<dd> Preserve portrait geometry (when <i>height</i> &gt;= <i>width</i>).
<dt><b>landscape</b>
<dd> Preserve landscape geometry (when <i>width</i> &gt;= <i>height</i>).</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<h3>trim</h3>

 Trim the input so that the output contains one continuous subpart of the input. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>start</b>
<dd> Specify the time of the start of the kept section, i.e. the frame with the timestamp <i>start</i> will be the first frame in the output.
<dt><b>end</b>
<dd> Specify the time of the first frame that will be dropped, i.e. the frame immediately preceding the one with the timestamp <i>end</i> will be the last frame in the output.
<dt><b>start_pts</b>
<dd> This is the same as <i>start</i>, except this option sets the start timestamp in timebase units instead of seconds.
<dt><b>end_pts</b>
<dd> This is the same as <i>end</i>, except this option sets the end timestamp in timebase units instead of seconds.
<dt><b>duration</b>
<dd> The maximum duration of the output in seconds.
<dt><b>start_frame</b>
<dd> The number of the first frame that should be passed to the output.
<dt><b>end_frame</b>
<dd> The number of the first frame that should be dropped.</dl>
 

 <b>start</b>, <b>end</b>, and <b>duration</b> are expressed as time duration specifications; see <b>the Time duration section in the <a HREF="/docs/linux/man/1-ffmpeg-utils/">ffmpeg-utils</a>(1) manual</b> for the accepted syntax. 

 Note that the first two sets of the start/end options and the <b>duration</b> option look at the frame timestamp, while the _frame variants simply count the frames that pass through the filter. Also note that this filter does not modify the timestamps. If you wish for the output timestamps to start at zero, insert a setpts filter after the trim filter. 

 If multiple start or end options are set, this filter tries to be greedy and keep all the frames that match at least one of the specified constraints. To keep only the part that matches all the constraints at once, chain multiple trim filters. 

 The defaults are such that all the input is kept. So it is possible to set e.g. just the end values to keep everything before the specified time. 

 Examples:
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Drop everything except the second minute of input: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf trim=60:120
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Keep only the first second: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -vf trim=duration=1
</pre></dl>

<h3>unpremultiply</h3>

 Apply alpha unpremultiply effect to input video stream using first plane of second stream as alpha. 

 Both streams must have same dimensions and same pixel format. 

 The filter accepts the following option:
<dl>
<dt><b>planes</b>
<dd> Set which planes will be processed, unprocessed planes will be copied. By default value 0xf, all planes will be processed. 

 If the format has 1 or 2 components, then luma is bit 0. If the format has 3 or 4 components: for <font SIZE="-1">RGB</font> formats bit 0 is green, bit 1 is blue and bit 2 is red; for <font SIZE="-1">YUV</font> formats bit 0 is luma, bit 1 is chroma-U and bit 2 is chroma-V. If present, the alpha channel is always the last bit.
<dt><b>inplace</b>
<dd> Do not require 2nd input for processing, instead use alpha plane from input stream.</dl>

<h3>unsharp</h3>

 Sharpen or blur the input video. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>luma_msize_x, lx</b>
<dd> Set the luma matrix horizontal size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>luma_msize_y, ly</b>
<dd> Set the luma matrix vertical size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>luma_amount, la</b>
<dd> Set the luma effect strength. It must be a floating point number, reasonable values lay between -1.5 and 1.5. 

 Negative values will blur the input video, while positive values will sharpen it, a value of zero will disable the effect. 

 Default value is 1.0.
<dt><b>chroma_msize_x, cx</b>
<dd> Set the chroma matrix horizontal size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>chroma_msize_y, cy</b>
<dd> Set the chroma matrix vertical size. It must be an odd integer between 3 and 23. The default value is 5.
<dt><b>chroma_amount, ca</b>
<dd> Set the chroma effect strength. It must be a floating point number, reasonable values lay between -1.5 and 1.5. 

 Negative values will blur the input video, while positive values will sharpen it, a value of zero will disable the effect. 

 Default value is 0.0.</dl>
 

 All parameters are optional and default to the equivalent of the string '5:5:1.0:5:5:0.0'. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply strong luma sharpen effect: 

 <pre>
        unsharp=luma_msize_x=7:luma_msize_y=7:luma_amount=2.5
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Apply a strong blur of both luma and chroma parameters: 

 <pre>
        unsharp=7:7:-2:7:7:-2
</pre></dl>

<h3>untile</h3>

 Decompose a video made of tiled images into the individual images. 

 The frame rate of the output video is the frame rate of the input video multiplied by the number of tiles. 

 This filter does the reverse of <b>tile</b>. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>layout</b>
<dd> Set the grid size (i.e. the number of lines and columns). For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Produce a 1-second video from a still image file made of 25 frames stacked vertically, like an analogic film reel: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -r 1 -i image.jpg -vf untile=1x25 movie.mkv
</pre></dl>

<h3>uspp</h3>

 Apply ultra slow/simple postprocessing filter that compresses and decompresses the image at several (or - in the case of <b>quality</b> level <tt>8</tt> - all) shifts and average the results. 

 The way this differs from the behavior of spp is that uspp actually encodes &amp; decodes each case with libavcodec Snow, whereas spp uses a simplified intra only 8x8 <font SIZE="-1">DCT</font> similar to <font SIZE="-1">MJPEG.</font> 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>quality</b>
<dd> Set quality. This option defines the number of levels for averaging. It accepts an integer in the range 0-8. If set to <tt>0</tt>, the filter will have no effect. A value of <tt>8</tt> means the higher quality. For each increment of that value the speed drops by a factor of approximately 2. Default value is <tt>3</tt>.
<dt><b>qp</b>
<dd> Force a constant quantization parameter. If not set, the filter will use the <font SIZE="-1">QP</font> from the video stream (if available).</dl>

<h3>v360</h3>

 Convert 360 videos between various formats. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>input</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>output</b>
<dd> Set format of the input/output video. 

 Available formats:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>e</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>equirect</b>
<dd> Equirectangular projection.
<dt><b>c3x2</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c6x1</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>c1x6</b>
<dd> Cubemap with 3x2/6x1/1x6 layout. 

 Format specific options:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>in_pad</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>out_pad</b>
<dd> Set padding proportion for the input/output cubemap. Values in decimals. 

 Example values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd> No padding.
<dt><b>0.01</b>
<dd> 1% of face is padding. For example, with 1920x1280 resolution face size would be 640x640 and padding would be 3 pixels from each side. (640 * 0.01 = 6 pixels)</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is @samp<b>{0</b>}. Maximum value is @samp<b>{0.1</b>}.</dl>

<dt><b>fin_pad</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>fout_pad</b>
<dd> Set fixed padding for the input/output cubemap. Values in pixels. 

 Default value is @samp<b>{0</b>}. If greater than zero it overrides other padding options.
<dt><b>in_forder</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>out_forder</b>
<dd> Set order of faces for the input/output cubemap. Choose one direction for each position. 

 Designation of directions:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>r</b>
<dd> right
<dt><b>l</b>
<dd> left
<dt><b>u</b>
<dd> up
<dt><b>d</b>
<dd> down
<dt><b>f</b>
<dd> forward
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> back</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is @samp<b>{rludfb</b>}.</dl>

<dt><b>in_frot</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>out_frot</b>
<dd> Set rotation of faces for the input/output cubemap. Choose one angle for each position. 

 Designation of angles:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>0</b>
<dd> 0 degrees clockwise
<dt><b>1</b>
<dd> 90 degrees clockwise
<dt><b>2</b>
<dd> 180 degrees clockwise
<dt><b>3</b>
<dd> 270 degrees clockwise</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is @samp<b>{000000</b>}.</dl>
</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>eac</b>
<dd> Equi-Angular Cubemap.
<dt><b>flat</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gnomonic</b>
<dd>
