<dd> Set spectrogram color scheme. This is list of floating point values with format <tt>&quot;left_r|left_g|left_b|right_r|right_g|right_b&quot;</tt>. The default is <tt>&quot;1|0.5|0|0|0.5|1&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Playing audio while showing the spectrum: 

 
ffplay - f lavfi 'amovie=a.mp3, asplit [a][out1]; [a] showcqt [out0]'

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but with frame rate 30 fps: 

 
ffplay - f lavfi 'amovie=a.mp3, asplit [a][out1]; [a] showcqt=fps=30:count=5 [out0]'

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Playing at 1280x720: 

 
ffplay - f lavfi 'amovie=a.mp3, asplit [a][out1]; [a] showcqt=s=1280x720:count=4 [out0]'

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Disable sonogram display: 

 <pre>
        sono_h=0
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> A1 and its harmonics: A1, A2, (near)E3, A3: 

 
ffplay - f lavfi 'aevalsrc=0.1*sin(2*PI*55*t)+0.1*sin(4*PI*55*t)+0.1*sin(6*PI*55*t)+0.1*sin(8*PI*55*t), asplit[a][out1];
[a] showcqt[out0]'

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Same as above, but with more accuracy in frequency domain: 

 
ffplay - f lavfi 'aevalsrc=0.1*sin(2*PI*55*t)+0.1*sin(4*PI*55*t)+0.1*sin(6*PI*55*t)+0.1*sin(8*PI*55*t), asplit[a][out1];
[a] showcqt = timeclamp = 0.5 [out0]'

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Custom volume: 

 <pre>
        bar_v=10:sono_v=bar_v*a_weighting(f)
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Custom gamma, now spectrum is linear to the amplitude. 

 <pre>
        bar_g=2:sono_g=2
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Custom tlength equation: 

 <pre>
        tc=0.33:tlength='st(0,0.17); 384*tc / (384 / ld(0) + tc*f /(1-ld(0))) + 384*tc / (tc*f / ld(0) + 384 /(1-ld(0)))'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Custom fontcolor and fontfile, C-note is colored green, others are colored blue: 

 <pre>
        fontcolor='if(mod(floor(midi(f)+0.5),12), 0x0000FF, <a HREF="//www.systutorials.com/docs/linux/man/1-g/">g</a>(1))':fontfile=myfont.ttf
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Custom font using fontconfig: 

 <pre>
        font='Courier New,Monospace,mono|bold'
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Custom frequency range with custom axis using image file: 

 <pre>
        axisfile=myaxis.png:basefreq=40:endfreq=10000
</pre></dl>
 <a NAME="lb\P">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>showfreqs</h3>

 Convert input audio to video output representing the audio power spectrum. Audio amplitude is on Y-axis while frequency is on X-axis. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd> Specify size of video. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default is <tt>&quot;1024x512&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set display mode. This set how each frequency bin will be represented. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>line</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bar</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dot</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;bar&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>ascale</b>
<dd> Set amplitude scale. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> Linear scale.
<dt><b>sqrt</b>
<dd> Square root scale.
<dt><b>cbrt</b>
<dd> Cubic root scale.
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> Logarithmic scale.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>fscale</b>
<dd> Set frequency scale. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> Linear scale.
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> Logarithmic scale.
<dt><b>rlog</b>
<dd> Reverse logarithmic scale.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;lin&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>win_size</b>
<dd> Set window size. Allowed range is from 16 to 65536. 

 Default is <tt>2048</tt>
<dt><b>win_func</b>
<dd> Set windowing function. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rect</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bartlett</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hanning</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hamming</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>blackman</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>welch</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>flattop</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bharris</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bnuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bhann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>sine</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>nuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lanczos</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gauss</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tukey</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dolph</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cauchy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>parzen</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>poisson</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bohman</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;hanning&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd> Set window overlap. In range <tt>&quot;[0, 1]&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>1</tt>, which means optimal overlap for selected window function will be picked.
<dt><b>averaging</b>
<dd> Set time averaging. Setting this to 0 will display current maximal peaks. Default is <tt>1</tt>, which means time averaging is disabled.
<dt><b>colors</b>
<dd> Specify list of colors separated by space or by '|' which will be used to draw channel frequencies. Unrecognized or missing colors will be replaced by white color.
<dt><b>cmode</b>
<dd> Set channel display mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>combined</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>separate</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;combined&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>minamp</b>
<dd> Set minimum amplitude used in <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt> amplitude scaler.
<dt><b>data</b>
<dd> Set data display mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>magnitude</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>phase</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>delay</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is <tt>&quot;magnitude&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>
 <a NAME="lb\Q">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>showspatial</h3>

 Convert stereo input audio to a video output, representing the spatial relationship between two channels. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd> Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;512x512&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>win_size</b>
<dd> Set window size. Allowed range is from <i>1024</i> to <i>65536</i>. Default size is <i>4096</i>.
<dt><b>win_func</b>
<dd> Set window function. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rect</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bartlett</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hanning</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hamming</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>blackman</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>welch</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>flattop</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bharris</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bnuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bhann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>sine</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>nuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lanczos</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gauss</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tukey</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dolph</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cauchy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>parzen</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>poisson</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bohman</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;hann&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd> Set ratio of overlap window. Default value is <tt>0.5</tt>. When value is <tt>1</tt> overlap is set to recommended size for specific window function currently used.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb\R">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>showspectrum</h3>

 Convert input audio to a video output, representing the audio frequency spectrum. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd> Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;640x512&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>slide</b>
<dd> Specify how the spectrum should slide along the window. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>replace</b>
<dd> the samples start again on the left when they reach the right
<dt><b>scroll</b>
<dd> the samples scroll from right to left
<dt><b>fullframe</b>
<dd> frames are only produced when the samples reach the right
<dt><b>rscroll</b>
<dd> the samples scroll from left to right</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;replace&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Specify display mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>combined</b>
<dd> all channels are displayed in the same row
<dt><b>separate</b>
<dd> all channels are displayed in separate rows</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>combined</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> Specify display color mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>channel</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed in a separate color
<dt><b>intensity</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the same color scheme
<dt><b>rainbow</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the rainbow color scheme
<dt><b>moreland</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the moreland color scheme
<dt><b>nebulae</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the nebulae color scheme
<dt><b>fire</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the fire color scheme
<dt><b>fiery</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the fiery color scheme
<dt><b>fruit</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the fruit color scheme
<dt><b>cool</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the cool color scheme
<dt><b>magma</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the magma color scheme
<dt><b>green</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the green color scheme
<dt><b>viridis</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the viridis color scheme
<dt><b>plasma</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the plasma color scheme
<dt><b>cividis</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the cividis color scheme
<dt><b>terrain</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the terrain color scheme</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>channel</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Specify scale used for calculating intensity color values. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> linear
<dt><b>sqrt</b>
<dd> square root, default
<dt><b>cbrt</b>
<dd> cubic root
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> logarithmic
<dt><b>4thrt</b>
<dd> 4th root
<dt><b>5thrt</b>
<dd> 5th root</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>sqrt</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>fscale</b>
<dd> Specify frequency scale. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> linear
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> logarithmic</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>lin</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>saturation</b>
<dd> Set saturation modifier for displayed colors. Negative values provide alternative color scheme. <tt>0</tt> is no saturation at all. Saturation must be in [-10.0, 10.0] range. Default value is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>win_func</b>
<dd> Set window function. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rect</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bartlett</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hanning</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hamming</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>blackman</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>welch</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>flattop</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bharris</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bnuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bhann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>sine</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>nuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lanczos</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gauss</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tukey</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dolph</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cauchy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>parzen</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>poisson</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bohman</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;hann&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>orientation</b>
<dd> Set orientation of time vs frequency axis. Can be <tt>&quot;vertical&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;horizontal&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;vertical&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd> Set ratio of overlap window. Default value is <tt>0</tt>. When value is <tt>1</tt> overlap is set to recommended size for specific window function currently used.
<dt><b>gain</b>
<dd> Set scale gain for calculating intensity color values. Default value is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>data</b>
<dd> Set which data to display. Can be <tt>&quot;magnitude&quot;</tt>, default or <tt>&quot;phase&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>rotation</b>
<dd> Set color rotation, must be in [-1.0, 1.0] range. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>start</b>
<dd> Set start frequency from which to display spectrogram. Default is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>stop</b>
<dd> Set stop frequency to which to display spectrogram. Default is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>fps</b>
<dd> Set upper frame rate limit. Default is <tt>&quot;auto&quot;</tt>, unlimited.
<dt><b>legend</b>
<dd> Draw time and frequency axes and legends. Default is disabled.</dl>
 

 The usage is very similar to the showwaves filter; see the examples in that section. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Large window with logarithmic color scaling: 

 <pre>
        showspectrum=s=1280x480:scale=log
</pre>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Complete example for a colored and sliding spectrum per channel using <b>ffplay</b>: 

 
ffplay - f lavfi 'amovie=input.mp3, asplit [a][out1];
             [a] showspectrum = mode = separate : color = intensity : slide = 1 : scale = cbrt[out0]'
</dl>
 <a NAME="lb\S">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>showspectrumpic</h3>

 Convert input audio to a single video frame, representing the audio frequency spectrum. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd> Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;4096x2048&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Specify display mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>combined</b>
<dd> all channels are displayed in the same row
<dt><b>separate</b>
<dd> all channels are displayed in separate rows</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>combined</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>color</b>
<dd> Specify display color mode. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>channel</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed in a separate color
<dt><b>intensity</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the same color scheme
<dt><b>rainbow</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the rainbow color scheme
<dt><b>moreland</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the moreland color scheme
<dt><b>nebulae</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the nebulae color scheme
<dt><b>fire</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the fire color scheme
<dt><b>fiery</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the fiery color scheme
<dt><b>fruit</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the fruit color scheme
<dt><b>cool</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the cool color scheme
<dt><b>magma</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the magma color scheme
<dt><b>green</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the green color scheme
<dt><b>viridis</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the viridis color scheme
<dt><b>plasma</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the plasma color scheme
<dt><b>cividis</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the cividis color scheme
<dt><b>terrain</b>
<dd> each channel is displayed using the terrain color scheme</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>intensity</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Specify scale used for calculating intensity color values. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> linear
<dt><b>sqrt</b>
<dd> square root, default
<dt><b>cbrt</b>
<dd> cubic root
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> logarithmic
<dt><b>4thrt</b>
<dd> 4th root
<dt><b>5thrt</b>
<dd> 5th root</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>log</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>fscale</b>
<dd> Specify frequency scale. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> linear
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> logarithmic</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <b>lin</b>.</dl>

<dt><b>saturation</b>
<dd> Set saturation modifier for displayed colors. Negative values provide alternative color scheme. <tt>0</tt> is no saturation at all. Saturation must be in [-10.0, 10.0] range. Default value is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>win_func</b>
<dd> Set window function. 

 It accepts the following values:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>rect</b>

<dt><b>bartlett</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hanning</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>hamming</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>blackman</b>

<dd>
<dt><b>bnuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bhann</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>sine</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>nuttall</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>lanczos</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>gauss</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>tukey</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>dolph</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>cauchy</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>parzen</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>poisson</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>bohman</b>
<dd></dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;hann&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>orientation</b>
<dd> Set orientation of time vs frequency axis. Can be <tt>&quot;vertical&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;horizontal&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;vertical&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>gain</b>
<dd> Set scale gain for calculating intensity color values. Default value is <tt>1</tt>.
<dt><b>legend</b>
<dd> Draw time and frequency axes and legends. Default is enabled.
<dt><b>rotation</b>
<dd> Set color rotation, must be in [-1.0, 1.0] range. Default value is <tt>0</tt>.
<dt><b>start</b>

</pre></dl>

<h3>showvolume</h3>

 Convert input audio volume to a video output. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd> Set video rate.
<dt><b>b</b>
<dd> Set border width, allowed range is [0, 5]. Default is 1.
<dt><b>w</b>
<dd> Set channel width, allowed range is [80, 8192]. Default is 400.
<dt><b>h</b>
<dd> Set channel height, allowed range is [1, 900]. Default is 20.
<dt><b>f</b>
<dd> Set fade, allowed range is [0, 1]. Default is 0.95.
<dt><b>c</b>
<dd> Set volume color expression. 

 The expression can use the following variables:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>VOLUME</b></font>
<dd> Current max volume of channel in dB.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>PEAK</b></font>
<dd> Current peak.
<dt><font SIZE="-1"><b>CHANNEL</b></font>
<dd> Current channel number, starting from 0.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>t</b>
<dd> If set, displays channel names. Default is enabled.
<dt><b>v</b>
<dd> If set, displays volume values. Default is enabled.
<dt><b>o</b>
<dd> Set orientation, can be horizontal: <tt>&quot;h&quot;</tt> or vertical: <tt>&quot;v&quot;</tt>, default is <tt>&quot;h&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>s</b>
<dd> Set step size, allowed range is [0, 5]. Default is 0, which means step is disabled.
<dt><b>p</b>
<dd> Set background opacity, allowed range is [0, 1]. Default is 0.
<dt><b>m</b>
<dd> Set metering mode, can be peak: <tt>&quot;p&quot;</tt> or rms: <tt>&quot;r&quot;</tt>, default is <tt>&quot;p&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>ds</b>
<dd> Set display scale, can be linear: <tt>&quot;lin&quot;</tt> or log: <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt>, default is <tt>&quot;lin&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>dm</b>
<dd> In second. If set to &gt; 0., display a line for the max level in the previous seconds. default is disabled: <tt>0.</tt>
<dt><b>dmc</b>
<dd> The color of the max line. Use when <tt>&quot;dm&quot;</tt> option is set to &gt; 0. default is: <tt>&quot;orange&quot;</tt></dl>
 <a NAME="lb\U">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>showwaves</h3>

 Convert input audio to a video output, representing the samples waves. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>size, s</b>
<dd> Specify the video size for the output. For the syntax of this option, check the <b>``Video size'' section in the ffmpeg-utils manual</b>. Default value is <tt>&quot;600x240&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set display mode. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>point</b>
<dd> Draw a point for each sample.
<dt><b>line</b>
<dd> Draw a vertical line for each sample.
<dt><b>p2p</b>
<dd> Draw a point for each sample and a line between them.
<dt><b>cline</b>
<dd> Draw a centered vertical line for each sample.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;point&quot;</tt>.</dl>

<dt><b>n</b>
<dd> Set the number of samples which are printed on the same column. A larger value will decrease the frame rate. Must be a positive integer. This option can be set only if the value for <i>rate</i> is not explicitly specified.
<dt><b>rate, r</b>
<dd> Set the (approximate) output frame rate. This is done by setting the option <i>n</i>. Default value is ``25''.
<dt><b>split_channels</b>
<dd> Set if channels should be drawn separately or overlap. Default value is 0.
<dt><b>colors</b>
<dd> Set colors separated by '|' which are going to be used for drawing of each channel.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Set amplitude scale. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> Linear.
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> Logarithmic.
<dt><b>sqrt</b>
<dd> Square root.
<dt><b>cbrt</b>
<dd> Cubic root.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is linear.</dl>

<dt><b>draw</b>
<dd> Set the draw mode. This is mostly useful to set for high <i>n</i>. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Scale pixel values for each drawn sample.
<dt><b>full</b>
<dd> Draw every sample directly.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default value is <tt>&quot;scale&quot;</tt>.</dl>
</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Output the input file audio and the corresponding video representation at the same time: 

 
amovie = a.mp3, asplit[out0], showwaves[out1]

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Create a synthetic signal and show it with showwaves, forcing a frame rate of 30 frames per second: 

 
aevalsrc = sin(1 * 2 * PI * t) * sin(880 * 2 * PI * t)
    : cos(2 * PI * 200 * t),
asplit[out0], showwaves = r = 30 [out1]
</dl>
 <a NAME="lb\V">&nbsp;</a>

<dt><b>colors</b>
<dd> Set colors separated by '|' which are going to be used for drawing of each channel.

<dd> Set amplitude scale. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>lin</b>
<dd> Linear.
<dt><b>log</b>
<dd> Logarithmic.
<dt><b>sqrt</b>
<dd> Square root.
<dt><b>cbrt</b>
<dd> Cubic root.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> 

 Default is linear.</dl>

<dt><b>draw</b>
<dd> Set the draw mode. 

 Available values are:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>scale</b>

 <a NAME="lb\W">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>sidedata, asidedata</h3>

 Delete frame side data, or select frames based on it. 

 This filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>mode</b>
<dd> Set mode of operation of the filter. 

 Can be one of the following:
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt><b>select</b>
<dd> Select every frame with side data of <tt>&quot;type&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>delete</b>
<dd> Delete side data of <tt>&quot;type&quot;</tt>. If <tt>&quot;type&quot;</tt> is not set, delete all side data in the frame.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>type</b>
<dd> Set side data type used with all modes. Must be set for <tt>&quot;select&quot;</tt> mode. For the list of frame side data types, refer to the <tt>&quot;AVFrameSideDataType&quot;</tt> enum in <i>libavutil/frame.h</i>. For example, to choose <tt>&quot;AV_FRAME_DATA_PANSCAN&quot;</tt> side data, you must specify <tt>&quot;PANSCAN&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb\X">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>spectrumsynth</h3>

 Synthesize audio from 2 input video spectrums, first input stream represents magnitude across time and second represents phase across time. The filter will transform from frequency domain as displayed in videos back to time domain as presented in audio output. 

 This filter is primarily created for reversing processed <b>showspectrum</b> filter outputs, but can synthesize sound from other spectrograms too. But in such case results are going to be poor if the phase data is not available, because in such cases phase data need to be recreated, usually it's just recreated from random noise. For best results use gray only output (<tt>&quot;channel&quot;</tt> color mode in <b>showspectrum</b> filter) and <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt> scale for magnitude video and <tt>&quot;lin&quot;</tt> scale for phase video. To produce phase, for 2nd video, use <tt>&quot;data&quot;</tt> option. Inputs videos should generally use <tt>&quot;fullframe&quot;</tt> slide mode as that saves resources needed for decoding video. 

 The filter accepts the following options:
<dl>
<dt><b>sample_rate</b>
<dd> Specify sample rate of output audio, the sample rate of audio from which spectrum was generated may differ.
<dt><b>channels</b>
<dd> Set number of channels represented in input video spectrums.
<dt><b>scale</b>
<dd> Set scale which was used when generating magnitude input spectrum. Can be <tt>&quot;lin&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;log&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>slide</b>
<dd> Set slide which was used when generating inputs spectrums. Can be <tt>&quot;replace&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;scroll&quot;</tt>, <tt>&quot;fullframe&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;rscroll&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;fullframe&quot;</tt>.
<dt><b>win_func</b>
<dd> Set window function used for resynthesis.
<dt><b>overlap</b>
<dd> Set window overlap. In range <tt>&quot;[0, 1]&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>1</tt>, which means optimal overlap for selected window function will be picked.
<dt><b>orientation</b>
<dd> Set orientation of input videos. Can be <tt>&quot;vertical&quot;</tt> or <tt>&quot;horizontal&quot;</tt>. Default is <tt>&quot;vertical&quot;</tt>.</dl>
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> First create magnitude and phase videos from audio, assuming audio is stereo with 44100 sample rate, then resynthesize videos back to audio with spectrumsynth: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i input.flac -lavfi showspectrum=mode=separate:scale=log:overlap=0.875:color=channel:slide=fullframe:data=magnitude -an -c:v rawvideo magnitude.nut
        ffmpeg -i input.flac -lavfi showspectrum=mode=separate:scale=lin:overlap=0.875:color=channel:slide=fullframe:data=phase -an -c:v rawvideo phase.nut
        ffmpeg -i magnitude.nut -i phase.nut -lavfi spectrumsynth=channels=2:sample_rate=44100:win_func=hann:overlap=0.875:slide=fullframe output.flac
</pre></dl>
 <a NAME="lb\Y">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>split, asplit</h3>

 Split input into several identical outputs. 

 <tt>&quot;asplit&quot;</tt> works with audio input, <tt>&quot;split&quot;</tt> with video. 

 The filter accepts a single parameter which specifies the number of outputs. If unspecified, it defaults to 2. 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Create two separate outputs from the same input: 

 
[in] split[out0][out1]

<dt>&bull;
<dd> To create 3 or more outputs, you need to specify the number of outputs, like in: 

 
[in] asplit = 3 [out0][out1][out2]

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Create two separate outputs from the same input, one cropped and one padded: 

 
[in] split[splitout1][splitout2];
[splitout1] crop = 100 : 100 : 0 : 0 [cropout];
[splitout2] pad = 200 : 200 : 100 : 100 [padout];

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Create 5 copies of the input audio with <b>ffmpeg</b>: 

 <pre>
        ffmpeg -i INPUT -filter_complex asplit=5 OUTPUT
</pre></dl>
 <a NAME="lb\Z">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>zmq, azmq</h3>

 Receive commands sent through a libzmq client, and forward them to filters in the filtergraph. 

 <tt>&quot;zmq&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;azmq&quot;</tt> work as a pass-through filters. <tt>&quot;zmq&quot;</tt> must be inserted between two video filters, <tt>&quot;azmq&quot;</tt> between two audio filters. Both are capable to send messages to any filter type. 

 To enable these filters you need to install the libzmq library and headers and configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-libzmq&quot;</tt>. 

 For more information about libzmq see: &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.zeromq.org/">http://www.zeromq.org/</a></b>&gt; 

 The <tt>&quot;zmq&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;azmq&quot;</tt> filters work as a libzmq server, which receives messages sent through a network interface defined by the <b>bind_address</b> (or the abbreviation &quot;<b>b</b>&quot;) option. Default value of this option is <i><a HREF="tcp://localhost:5555">tcp://localhost:5555</a></i>. You may want to alter this value to your needs, but do not forget to escape any ':' signs (see <b>filtergraph escaping</b>). 

 The received message must be in the form: 

 <pre>
        &lt;TARGET&gt; &lt;COMMAND&gt; [&lt;ARG&gt;]
</pre> 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>TARGET</i></font><i></i> specifies the target of the command, usually the name of the filter class or a specific filter instance name. The default filter instance name uses the pattern <b>Parsed_&lt;filter_name&gt;_&lt;index&gt;</b>, but you can override this by using the <b>filter_name@id</b> syntax (see <b>Filtergraph syntax</b>). 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>COMMAND</i></font><i></i> specifies the name of the command for the target filter. 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>ARG</i></font><i></i> is optional and specifies the optional argument list for the given <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>COMMAND</i></font><i></i>. 

 Upon reception, the message is processed and the corresponding command is injected into the filtergraph. Depending on the result, the filter will send a reply to the client, adopting the format: 

 <pre>
        &lt;ERROR_CODE&gt; &lt;ERROR_REASON&gt;
        &lt;MESSAGE&gt;
</pre> 

 <i></i><font SIZE="-1"><i>MESSAGE</i></font><i></i> is optional. 

 <i>Examples</i> 

 Look at <i>tools/zmqsend</i> for an example of a zmq client which can be used to send commands processed by these filters. 

 Consider the following filtergraph generated by <b>ffplay</b>. In this example the last overlay filter has an instance name. All other filters will have default instance names. 

 
ffplay - dumpgraph 1 - f lavfi "
    color = s = 100x100 : c = red[l];
color = s = 100x100 : c = blue[r];
nullsrc = s = 200x100, zmq[bg];
[bg][l] overlay[bg + l];
[bg + l][r] overlay @my = x = 100 "
 

 To change the color of the left side of the video, the following command can be used: 

 <pre>
        echo Parsed_color_0 c yellow | tools/zmqsend
</pre> 

 To change the right side: 

 <pre>
        echo Parsed_color_1 c pink | tools/zmqsend
</pre> 

 To change the position of the right side: 

 <pre>
        echo overlay@my x 150 | tools/zmqsend
</pre> <a NAME="lb]A">&nbsp;</a>

<h2>MULTIMEDIA SOURCES</h2>

 Below is a description of the currently available multimedia sources. <a NAME="lb]B">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>amovie</h3>

 This is the same as <b>movie</b> source, except it selects an audio stream by default. <a NAME="lb]C">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>movie</h3>

 Read audio and/or video stream(s) from a movie container. 

 It accepts the following parameters:
<dl>
<dt><b>filename</b>
<dd> The name of the resource to read (not necessarily a file; it can also be a device or a stream accessed through some protocol).
<dt><b>format_name, f</b>
<dd> Specifies the format assumed for the movie to read, and can be either the name of a container or an input device. If not specified, the format is guessed from <i>movie_name</i> or by probing.
<dt><b>seek_point, sp</b>
<dd> Specifies the seek point in seconds. The frames will be output starting from this seek point. The parameter is evaluated with <tt>&quot;av_strtod&quot;</tt>, so the numerical value may be suffixed by an <font SIZE="-1">IS</font> postfix. The default value is ``0''.
<dt><b>streams, s</b>
<dd> Specifies the streams to read. Several streams can be specified, separated by ``+''. The source will then have as many outputs, in the same order. The syntax is explained in the <b>``Stream specifiers'' section in the ffmpeg manual</b>. Two special names, ``dv'' and ``da'' specify respectively the default (best suited) video and audio stream. Default is ``dv'', or ``da'' if the filter is called as ``amovie''.
<dt><b>stream_index, si</b>
<dd> Specifies the index of the video stream to read. If the value is -1, the most suitable video stream will be automatically selected. The default value is ``-1''. Deprecated. If the filter is called ``amovie'', it will select audio instead of video.
<dt><b>loop</b>
<dd> Specifies how many times to read the stream in sequence. If the value is 0, the stream will be looped infinitely. Default value is ``1''. 

 Note that when the movie is looped the source timestamps are not changed, so it will generate non monotonically increasing timestamps.
<dt><b>discontinuity</b>
<dd> Specifies the time difference between frames above which the point is considered a timestamp discontinuity which is removed by adjusting the later timestamps.</dl>
 

 It allows overlaying a second video on top of the main input of a filtergraph, as shown in this graph: 

 
input-- -- -- -- ---&gt;deltapts0-- &gt; overlay-- &gt; output ^
    |
    movie-- &gt; scale-- &gt; deltapts1-- -- -- -+
 

 <i>Examples</i>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> Skip 3.2 seconds from the start of the <font SIZE="-1">AVI</font> file in.avi, and overlay it on top of the input labelled ``in'': 

 
movie = in.avi : seek_point = 3.2, scale = 180 : -1, setpts = PTS - STARTPTS[over];
[in] setpts = PTS - STARTPTS[main];
[main][over] overlay = 16 : 16 [out]

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Read from a video4linux2 device, and overlay it on top of the input labelled ``in'': 

 
movie = / dev / video0 : f = video4linux2, scale = 180 : -1, setpts = PTS - STARTPTS[over];
[in] setpts = PTS - STARTPTS[main];
[main][over] overlay = 16 : 16 [out]

<dt>&bull;
<dd> Read the first video stream and the audio stream with id 0x81 from dvd.vob; the video is connected to the pad named ``video'' and the audio is connected to the pad named ``audio'': 

 <pre><code>
movie = dvd.vob : s = v : 0 + #0x81 [video][audio]
</code></pre></dl>
 

 <i>Commands</i> 

 Both movie and amovie support the following commands:
<dl>
<dt><b>seek</b>
<dd> Perform seek using ``av_seek_frame''. The syntax is: seek <i>stream_index</i>|<i>timestamp</i>|<i>flags</i>
<dl>
<dt>
<dd>
<dl>
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <i>stream_index</i>: If stream_index is -1, a default stream is selected, and <i>timestamp</i> is automatically converted from <font SIZE="-1">AV_TIME_BASE</font> units to the stream specific time_base.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <i>timestamp</i>: Timestamp in AVStream.time_base units or, if no stream is specified, in <font SIZE="-1">AV_TIME_BASE</font> units.
<dt>&bull;
<dd> <i>flags</i>: Flags which select direction and seeking mode.</dl>
</dl>

<dl>
<dt>
<dd></dl>

<dt><b>get_duration</b>
<dd> Get movie duration in <font SIZE="-1">AV_TIME_BASE</font> units.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb]D">&nbsp;</a>

<h2>EXTERNAL LIBRARIES</h2>

 FFmpeg can be hooked up with a number of external libraries to add support for more formats. None of them are used by default, their use has to be explicitly requested by passing the appropriate flags to <b>./configure</b>. <a NAME="lb]E">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>Alliance for Open Media (<font SIZE="-1">AOM</font>)</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the <font SIZE="-1">AOM</font> library for <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> decoding and encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://aomedia.org/">http://aomedia.org/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libaom&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]F">&nbsp;</a>

<h3><font SIZE="-1">AMD AMF/VCE</font></h3>

 FFmpeg can use the <font SIZE="-1">AMD</font> Advanced Media Framework library for accelerated H.264 and <font SIZE="-1">HEVC</font>(only windows) encoding on hardware with Video Coding Engine (<font SIZE="-1">VCE</font>). 

 To enable support you must obtain the <font SIZE="-1">AMF</font> framework header files(version 1.4.9+) from &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/AMF.git">https://github.com/GPUOpen-LibrariesAndSDKs/AMF.git</a></b>&gt;. 

 Create an <tt>&quot;AMF/&quot;</tt> directory in the system include path. Copy the contents of <tt>&quot;AMF/amf/public/include/&quot;</tt> into that directory. Then configure FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-amf&quot;</tt>. 

 Initialization of amf encoder occurs in this order: 1) trying to initialize through dx11(only windows) 2) trying to initialize through dx9(only windows) 3) trying to initialize through vulkan 

 To use h.264(<font SIZE="-1">AMD VCE</font>) encoder on linux amdgru-pro version 19.20+ and amf-amdgpu-pro package(amdgru-pro contains, but does not install automatically) are required. 

 This driver can be installed using amdgpu-pro-install script in official amd driver archive. <a NAME="lb]G">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>AviSynth</h3>

 FFmpeg can read AviSynth scripts as input. To enable support, pass <tt>&quot;--enable-avisynth&quot;</tt> to configure after installing the headers provided by &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/AviSynth/AviSynthPlus">https://github.com/AviSynth/AviSynthPlus</a></b>&gt;. AviSynth+ can be configured to install only the headers by either passing <tt>&quot;-DHEADERS_ONLY:bool=on&quot;</tt> to the normal CMake-based build system, or by using the supplied <tt>&quot;GNUmakefile&quot;</tt>. 

 For Windows, supported AviSynth variants are &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://avisynth.nl">http://avisynth.nl</a></b>&gt; for 32-bit builds and &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://avisynth.nl/index.php/AviSynth+">http://avisynth.nl/index.php/AviSynth+</a></b>&gt; for 32-bit and 64-bit builds. 

 For Linux, macOS, and <font SIZE="-1">BSD,</font> the only supported AviSynth variant is &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/AviSynth/AviSynthPlus">https://github.com/AviSynth/AviSynthPlus</a></b>&gt;, starting with version 3.5. 

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> In 2016, AviSynth+ added support for building with <font SIZE="-1">GCC.</font> However, due to the eccentricities of Windows' calling conventions, 32-bit <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> builds of AviSynth+ are not compatible with typical 32-bit builds of FFmpeg. 

 By default, FFmpeg assumes compatibility with 32-bit <font SIZE="-1">MSVC</font> builds of AviSynth+ since that is the most widely-used and entrenched build configuration. Users can override this and enable support for 32-bit <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> builds of AviSynth+ by passing <tt>&quot;-DAVSC_WIN32_GCC32&quot;</tt> to <tt>&quot;--extra-cflags&quot;</tt> when configuring FFmpeg. 

 64-bit builds of FFmpeg are not affected, and can use either <font SIZE="-1">MSVC</font> or <font SIZE="-1">GCC</font> builds of AviSynth+ without any special flags.</dl>
 

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> AviSynth(+) is loaded dynamically. Distributors can build FFmpeg with <tt>&quot;--enable-avisynth&quot;</tt>, and the binaries will work regardless of the end user having AviSynth installed. If/when an end user would like to use AviSynth scripts, then they can install AviSynth(+) and FFmpeg will be able to find and use it to open scripts.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb]H">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>Chromaprint</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the Chromaprint library for generating audio fingerprints. Pass <tt>&quot;--enable-chromaprint&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://acoustid.org/chromaprint">https://acoustid.org/chromaprint</a></b>&gt;. <a NAME="lb]I">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>codec2</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the codec2 library for codec2 decoding and encoding. There is currently no native decoder, so libcodec2 must be used for decoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://freedv.org/">http://freedv.org/</a></b>&gt;, download ``Codec 2 source archive''. Build and install using CMake. Debian users can install the libcodec2-dev package instead. Once libcodec2 is installed you can pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libcodec2&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. 

 The easiest way to use codec2 is with .c2 files, since they contain the mode information required for decoding. To encode such a file, use a .c2 file extension and give the libcodec2 encoder the -mode option: <tt>&quot;ffmpeg -i input.wav -mode 700C output.c2&quot;</tt>. Playback is as simple as <tt>&quot;ffplay output.c2&quot;</tt>. For a list of supported modes, run <tt>&quot;ffmpeg -h encoder=libcodec2&quot;</tt>. Raw codec2 files are also supported. To make sense of them the mode in use needs to be specified as a format option: <tt>&quot;ffmpeg -f codec2raw -mode 1300 -i input.raw output.wav&quot;</tt>. <a NAME="lb]J">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>dav1d</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the dav1d library for <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> video decoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav1d">https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav1d</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libdav1d&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]K">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>davs2</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the davs2 library for <font SIZE="-1">AVS2-P2/IEEE1857.4</font> video decoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/pkuvcl/davs2">https://github.com/pkuvcl/davs2</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libdavs2&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. 

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> libdavs2 is under the <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> Public License Version 2 or later (see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html">http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html</a></b>&gt; for details), you must upgrade FFmpeg's license to <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> in order to use it.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb]L">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>uavs3d</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the uavs3d library for <font SIZE="-1">AVS3-P2/IEEE1857.10</font> video decoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/uavs3/uavs3d">https://github.com/uavs3/uavs3d</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libuavs3d&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]M">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>Game Music Emu</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the Game Music Emu library to read audio from supported video game music file formats. Pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libgme&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://bitbucket.org/mpyne/game-music-emu/overview">https://bitbucket.org/mpyne/game-music-emu/overview</a></b>&gt;. <a NAME="lb]N">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>Intel QuickSync Video</h3>

 FFmpeg can use Intel QuickSync Video (<font SIZE="-1">QSV</font>) for accelerated decoding and encoding of multiple codecs. To use <font SIZE="-1">QSV,</font> FFmpeg must be linked against the <tt>&quot;libmfx&quot;</tt> dispatcher, which loads the actual decoding libraries. 

 The dispatcher is open source and can be downloaded from &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/lu-zero/mfx_dispatch.git">https://github.com/lu-zero/mfx_dispatch.git</a></b>&gt;. FFmpeg needs to be configured with the <tt>&quot;--enable-libmfx&quot;</tt> option and <tt>&quot;pkg-config&quot;</tt> needs to be able to locate the dispatcher's <tt>&quot;.pc&quot;</tt> files. <a NAME="lb]O">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>Kvazaar</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the Kvazaar library for <font SIZE="-1">HEVC</font> encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/ultravideo/kvazaar">https://github.com/ultravideo/kvazaar</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libkvazaar&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]P">&nbsp;</a>

<h3><font SIZE="-1">LAME</font></h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the <font SIZE="-1">LAME</font> library for <font SIZE="-1">MP3</font> encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://lame.sourceforge.net/">http://lame.sourceforge.net/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libmp3lame&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]Q">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>libilbc</h3>

 iLBC is a narrowband speech codec that has been made freely available by Google as part of the WebRTC project. libilbc is a packaging friendly copy of the iLBC codec. FFmpeg can make use of the libilbc library for iLBC decoding and encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/TimothyGu/libilbc">https://github.com/TimothyGu/libilbc</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libilbc&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]R">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>libvpx</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the libvpx library for <font SIZE="-1">VP8/VP9</font> decoding and encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.webmproject.org/">http://www.webmproject.org/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libvpx&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]S">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>ModPlug</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of this library, originating in Modplug-XMMS, to read from MOD-like music files. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/Konstanty/libmodplug">https://github.com/Konstanty/libmodplug</a></b>&gt;. Pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libmodplug&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]T">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>OpenCORE, VisualOn, and Fraunhofer libraries</h3>

 Spun off Google Android sources, OpenCore, VisualOn and Fraunhofer libraries provide encoders for a number of audio codecs. 

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> OpenCORE and VisualOn libraries are under the Apache License 2.0 (see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0">http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0</a></b>&gt; for details), which is incompatible to the <font SIZE="-1">LGPL</font> version 2.1 and <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> version 2. You have to upgrade FFmpeg's license to <font SIZE="-1">LGPL</font> version 3 (or if you have enabled <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> components, <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> version 3) by passing <tt>&quot;--enable-version3&quot;</tt> to configure in order to use it. 

 The license of the Fraunhofer <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> library is incompatible with the <font SIZE="-1">GPL.</font> Therefore, for <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> builds, you have to pass <tt>&quot;--enable-nonfree&quot;</tt> to configure in order to use it. To the best of our knowledge, it is compatible with the <font SIZE="-1">LGPL.</font></dl>
 

 <i>OpenCORE </i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AMR</i></font><i></i> 

 FFmpeg can make use of the OpenCORE libraries for AMR-NB decoding/encoding and AMR-WB decoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/">http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the libraries. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libopencore-amrnb&quot;</tt> and/or <tt>&quot;--enable-libopencore-amrwb&quot;</tt> to configure to enable them. 

 <i>VisualOn AMR-WB encoder library</i> 

 FFmpeg can make use of the VisualOn AMR-WBenc library for AMR-WB encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/">http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libvo-amrwbenc&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. 

 <i>Fraunhofer </i><font SIZE="-1"><i>AAC</i></font><i> library</i> 

 FFmpeg can make use of the Fraunhofer <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> library for <font SIZE="-1">AAC</font> decoding &amp; encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/">http://sourceforge.net/projects/opencore-amr/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libfdk-aac&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]U">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>OpenH264</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the OpenH264 library for H.264 decoding and encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.openh264.org/">http://www.openh264.org/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libopenh264&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. 

 For decoding, this library is much more limited than the built-in decoder in libavcodec; currently, this library lacks support for decoding B-frames and some other main/high profile features. (It currently only supports constrained baseline profile and <font SIZE="-1">CABAC.</font>) Using it is mostly useful for testing and for taking advantage of Cisco's patent portfolio license (&lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.openh264.org/BINARY_LICENSE.txt">http://www.openh264.org/BINARY_LICENSE.txt</a></b>&gt;). <a NAME="lb]V">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>OpenJPEG</h3>

 FFmpeg can use the OpenJPEG libraries for decoding/encoding J2K videos. Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.openjpeg.org/">http://www.openjpeg.org/</a></b>&gt; to get the libraries and follow the installation instructions. To enable using OpenJPEG in FFmpeg, pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libopenjpeg&quot;</tt> to <i>./configure</i>. <a NAME="lb]W">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>rav1e</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of rav1e (Rust <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> Encoder) via its C bindings to encode videos. Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/xiph/rav1e/">https://github.com/xiph/rav1e/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions to build the C library. To enable using rav1e in FFmpeg, pass <tt>&quot;--enable-librav1e&quot;</tt> to <i>./configure</i>. <a NAME="lb]X">&nbsp;</a>

<h3><font SIZE="-1">SVT-AV1</font></h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the Scalable Video Technology for <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> library for <font SIZE="-1">AV1</font> encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/OpenVisualCloud/SVT-AV1/">https://github.com/OpenVisualCloud/SVT-AV1/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libsvtav1&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]Y">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>TwoLAME</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the TwoLAME library for <font SIZE="-1">MP2</font> encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.twolame.org/">http://www.twolame.org/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libtwolame&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb]Z">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>VapourSynth</h3>

 FFmpeg can read VapourSynth scripts as input. To enable support, pass <tt>&quot;--enable-vapoursynth&quot;</tt> to configure. Vapoursynth is detected via <tt>&quot;pkg-config&quot;</tt>. Versions 42 or greater supported. See &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.vapoursynth.com/">http://www.vapoursynth.com/</a></b>&gt;. 

 Due to security concerns, Vapoursynth scripts will not be autodetected so the input format has to be forced. For ff* <font SIZE="-1">CLI</font> tools, add <tt>&quot;-f vapoursynth&quot;</tt> before the input <tt>&quot;-i yourscript.vpy&quot;</tt>. <a NAME="lb^A">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>x264</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the x264 library for H.264 encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html">http://www.videolan.org/developers/x264.html</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libx264&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. 

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> x264 is under the <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> Public License Version 2 or later (see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html">http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html</a></b>&gt; for details), you must upgrade FFmpeg's license to <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> in order to use it.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb^B">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>x265</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the x265 library for <font SIZE="-1">HEVC</font> encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://x265.org/developers.html">http://x265.org/developers.html</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libx265&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. 

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> x265 is under the <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> Public License Version 2 or later (see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html">http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html</a></b>&gt; for details), you must upgrade FFmpeg's license to <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> in order to use it.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb^C">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>xavs</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the xavs library for <font SIZE="-1">AVS</font> encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://xavs.sf.net/">http://xavs.sf.net/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libxavs&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb^D">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>xavs2</h3>

 FFmpeg can make use of the xavs2 library for <font SIZE="-1">AVS2-P2/IEEE1857.4</font> video encoding. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="https://github.com/pkuvcl/xavs2">https://github.com/pkuvcl/xavs2</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libxavs2&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. 

<dl>
<dt>
<dd> libxavs2 is under the <font SIZE="-1">GNU</font> Public License Version 2 or later (see &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html">http://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html</a></b>&gt; for details), you must upgrade FFmpeg's license to <font SIZE="-1">GPL</font> in order to use it.</dl>
 <a NAME="lb^E">&nbsp;</a>

<h3><font SIZE="-1">ZVBI</font></h3>

 <font SIZE="-1">ZVBI</font> is a <font SIZE="-1">VBI</font> decoding library which can be used by FFmpeg to decode <font SIZE="-1">DVB</font> teletext pages and <font SIZE="-1">DVB</font> teletext subtitles. 

 Go to &lt;<b><a rel="nofollow" HREF="http://sourceforge.net/projects/zapping/">http://sourceforge.net/projects/zapping/</a></b>&gt; and follow the instructions for installing the library. Then pass <tt>&quot;--enable-libzvbi&quot;</tt> to configure to enable it. <a NAME="lb^F">&nbsp;</a>

<h2>SUPPORTED FILE FORMATS</h2>

 You can use the <tt>&quot;-formats&quot;</tt> and <tt>&quot;-codecs&quot;</tt> options to have an exhaustive list. <a NAME="lb^G">&nbsp;</a>

<h3>File Formats</h3>

 FFmpeg supports the following file formats through the <tt>&quot;libavformat&quot;</tt> library:
<dl>
<dt><b>Name : Encoding </b>@tab<b> Decoding </b>@tab<b> Comments</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>3dostr : </b>@tab<b> X</b>
<dd>
<dt><b>4xm : </b>@tab<b> X</b>
<dd> <pre>
